田舎-
{
田舎 (いなか) - countryside / rural area
A noun referring to a rural area, the country, or one's hometown.
Memory Tip: 田 means rice field and 舎 means cottage/hut. A place with rice fields and huts is the countryside.
Example: 夏休みは田舎に帰る。(なつやすみはいなかにかえる。)
-I will return to the countryside during summer vacation.
}
釣り-
{
釣り (つり) - fishing
A noun derived from the verb 釣る (to fish). It refers to the activity of angling.
Memory Tip: The left side of 釣 is 金 (metal), which looks like a sharp metal fishhook!
Example: 週末は川へ釣りに行きます。(しゅうまつはかわへつりにいきます。)
-With the weekend coming, I am going fishing at the river.
}
照れ屋-
{
照れ屋 (てれや) - a shy person
A noun used to describe someone who gets embarrassed or shy easily.
Memory Tip: 照れる (tereru) means to be shy/bashful, and 屋 (ya) means a shop or person of a certain trait. Literally, a "shy specialist."
Example: 彼は照れ屋だから、褒められると顔が赤くなる。(かれはてれやだから、ほめられるとおかおがあかくなる。)
-Because he is a shy person, his face turns red when he is praised.
}
相変わらず-
{
相変わらず (あいかわらず) - as usual / as always
An adverb meaning that something remains unchanged from its previous state.
Memory Tip: 相 (mutual/state) + 変わらず (without changing). Everything is exactly the same as always.
Example: 彼は相変わらず元気そうだ。(かれはあいかわらずげんきそうだ。)
-He looks energetic, as always.
}
斬新-
{
斬新 (ざんしん) - novel / innovative
A na-adjective used to describe ideas, designs, or concepts that are completely new and original.
Memory Tip: 斬 means to slice/cut, and 新 means new. An idea so sharp and new it "cuts" through the old stuff!
Example: 彼のアイデアはとても斬新だ。(かれのあいであはとてもざんしんだ。)
-His idea is very innovative.
}
感想-
{
感想 (かんそう) - impressions / thoughts / opinion
A noun referring to one's thoughts, feelings, or impressions about a book, movie, or experience.
Memory Tip: 感 means "feeling/emotion" and 想 means "thought/concept." Putting them together gives you your thoughts and feelings about something.
Example: 映画の感想を教えてください。(えいがのかんそうをおしえてください。)
-Please tell me your impressions of the movie.
}
昼間-
{
昼間 (ひるま) - daytime / during the day
A noun referring to the hours of daylight, usually between morning and evening.
Memory Tip: 昼 means "noon/daytime" and 間 means "interval/time." The interval of time during the day.
Example: 昼間は仕事が忙しい。(ひるまはしごとがいそがしい。)
-I am busy with work during the day.
}
急いでいた-
{
急いでいた (いそいでいた) - was hurrying / was in a rush
The past continuous form of the verb 急ぐ (いそぐ - to hurry).
Memory Tip: The kanji 急 has a "heart" (心) on the bottom. When you hurry, your heart beats fast!
Example: 私はとても急いでいたので、傘を忘れた。(わたしはとてもいそいでいたので、かさをわすれた。)
-I was in a big rush, so I forgot my umbrella.
}
伏せる-
{
伏せる (ふせる) - to look down / cast down / hide
A transitive verb meaning to turn something face down, cast one's eyes downward, or conceal information.
Memory Tip: The kanji combines イ (person) and 犬 (dog). Picture a person telling a dog to "lay low" or "down."
Example: 彼女は恥ずかしそうに目を伏せた。(かのじょははずかしそうにめをふせた。)
-She cast her eyes down embarrassedly.
}
何の力もない-
{
何の力もない (なんのちからもない) - completely powerless / helpless
A phrase used to describe having absolutely no power, influence, or strength to change a situation.
Memory Tip: 何の (of what kind) + 力 (power) + もない (does not even exist).
Example: 私は何の力もない一般人です。(わたしはなんのちからもないいっぱんじんです。)
-I am just an ordinary person with absolutely no power.
}
だけ-
{
だけ (だけ) - only / just
A particle limiting things to a specific amount or object.
Memory Tip: Standard grammar particle used directly after nouns or verbs to set a boundary.
Example: １つだけ買いました。(ひとつだけかいました。)
-I bought just one.
}
延ばす-
{
延ばす (のばす) - to postpone / extend / prolong
A transitive verb used when you extend a deadline, postpone an event, or stretch something out.
Memory Tip: The kanji 延 means to prolong or stretch. Think of stretching a rubber band or extending a due date.
Example: 会議の予定を来週に延ばす。(かいぎのよていをらいしゅうにのばす。)
-I will postpone the schedule of the meeting to next week.
}
何歳までに-
{
何歳までに (なんさいまでに) - by what age / by how old
A question phrase asking for a specific deadline or age target.
Memory Tip: 何歳 (how old) + までに (by/before a certain time limit).
Example: 何歳までに結婚したいですか？(なんさいまでにけっこんしたいですか？)
-By what age do you want to get married?
}
うちの店-
{
うちの店 (うちのみせ) - our shop / my store
A casual noun phrase used by an owner or employee to refer to their own workplace.
Memory Tip: うち (our/my house/group) + の + 店 (shop).
Example: うちの店はラーメンが美味しいですよ。(うちのみせはらーめんがおいしいですよ。)
-The ramen at our shop is delicious, you know.
}
連れて来る-
{
連れて来る (つれてくる) - to bring (a person/animal) along
A compound verb used when bringing someone or a pet to a place.
Memory Tip: 連れる means to lead/take along, and くる means to come. "To lead and come."
Example: 明日、友達を連れて来ます。(あした、ともだちをつれてきます。)
-I will bring my friend along tomorrow.
}
思い切って-
{
思い切って (おもいきって) - taking the plunge / boldly
An adverbial phrase used when making a bold decision after hesitant thinking.
Memory Tip: 思い (thoughts) + 切って (cutting off). Cutting off your lingering doubts and just doing it!
Example: 思い切って新しい車を買った。(おもいきってあたらしいくるまをかった。)
-I took the plunge and bought a new car.
}
〜かだら。-
{
〜かだから。 (〜かだから。) - "Is it because...?" / "That's exactly why..."
A conversational phrase pattern typically indicating a specific cause or conclusion.
Memory Tip: A combination of 〜か (question/uncertainty) and だから (therefore/because).
Example: だから言ったじゃない。(だからいったじゃない。)
-That's why I told you so, didn't I?
}
のみ-
{
のみ (のみ) - only / solely
A particle with the same meaning as だけ, but highly formal, written, or restrictive.
Memory Tip: Often found on signs, official notices, or rules.
Example: 会員のみ入場できます。(かいいんのみにゅうじょうできます。)
-Only members can enter.
}
だんだん-
{
だんだん (だんだん) - gradually / step by step
An adverb used to describe a gradual, continuous change over time.
Memory Tip: Think of steps or stairs (段 - dan). You go up them step-by-step.
Example: 英語の生活にだんだん慣れてきた。(えいごのせいかつにだんだんなれてきた。)
-I have gradually gotten used to living in English.
}
前月-
{
前月 (ぜんげつ) - the previous month
A noun referring to the month right before the current one.
Memory Tip: 前 means "before/previous" and 月 means "month."
Example: 前月の売上は好調だった。(ぜんげつのうりあげはこうちょうだった。)
-The sales for the previous month were strong.
}
折られた-
{
折られた (おられた) - was broken / snapped / folded
The passive past-tense form of the verb 折る (おる - to fold/break).
Memory Tip: The left side is 扌 (hand), and the right looks like an axe 斤. Using hands or an axe to break a branch.
Example: 強風で木の枝が折られた。(きょうふうできのえだがおられた。)
-The tree branch was snapped by the strong wind.
}
悩む-
{
悩む (なやむ) - to worry / be troubled
An intransitive verb used when you are deeply troubled or undecided about a problem.
Memory Tip: The radical 忄 represents the "heart." When you are deeply worried, your heart feels heavy.
Example: 進路について悩んでいる。(しんろについてなやんでいる。)
-I am troubled about my future path.
}
建物-
{
建物 (たてもの) - building / structure
A noun for any physical building or structure.
Memory Tip: 建 means "to build" and 物 means "thing." Literally, a "built thing."
Example: その古い建物は美術館です。(そのふるいたてものはびじゅつかんです。)
-That old building is an art museum.
}
自分に言い聞かせる-
{
自分に言い聞かせる (じぶんにいいきかせる) - to tell oneself / persuade oneself
A verb phrase meaning to mentally remind or convince yourself of something.
Memory Tip: 自分 (myself) + 言い聞かせる (to tell/admonish). Telling yourself to stay strong.
Example: 「大丈夫だ」と自分に言い聞かせた。(「だいじょうぶだ」とじぶんにいいきかせた。)
-I told myself, "It's going to be okay."
}
とはいえ-
{
とはいえ (とはいえ) - though / albeit / having said that
A conjunction used to qualify or contrast a previous statement.
Memory Tip: と (quotation) + は (topic) + いえ (say/even if said). "Even if you say that..."
Example: 給料が上がった。とはいえ、物価も高い。(きゅうりょうがあがった。とはいえ、ぶっかもたかい。)
-My salary went up. Having said that, prices are high too.
}
チラシを配る-
{
チラシを配る (ちらしをくばる) - to hand out flyers
A verb phrase meaning to distribute leaflets or flyers.
Memory Tip: チラシ comes from 散らす (to scatter), and 配る means to distribute/hand out.
Example: 駅前でチラシを配るアルバイトをした。(えきまえでちらしをくばるあるばいとをした。)
-I did a part-time job handing out flyers in front of the station.
}
なかなか-
{
なかなか (なかなか) - quite / fairly / (with negative) not easily
An adverb. With a positive verb, it means "quite." With a negative verb, it means "not easily/takes effort."
Memory Tip: Repeat "naka" twice. It adds emphasis to the difficulty or unexpected quality of a situation.
Example: バスがなかなか来ない。(ばすがなかなかこない。)
-The bus is just not coming easily.
}
守る-
{
守る (まもる) - to protect / keep (a promise)
A transitive verb used for guarding something, keeping a secret, or abiding by a rule.
Memory Tip: Under the roof (宀), there is a hand/measurement (寸). Holding something close under your roof to protect it.
Example: 約束は必ず守ります。(やくそくはかならずまもります。)
-I will definitely keep my promise.
}
育ち-
{
育ち (そだち) - upbringing / growth
The noun form of the verb 育つ (to grow up), referring to one's background or environment where they were raised.
Memory Tip: Derived from 育てる/育つ (to raise/grow).
Example: 私は東京生まれ、大阪育ちです。(わたしはとうきょううまれ、おおさかそだちです。)
-I was born in Tokyo and raised in Osaka.
}
団地-
{
団地 (だんち) - public housing complex / apartment complex
A noun referring to a large cluster of apartment buildings, often publicly managed.
Memory Tip: 団 means "group/collective" and 地 means "land/plot." A collective plot of living spaces.
Example: 私は子供の頃、大きな団地に住んでいた。(わたしはこどものころ、おおきなだんちに住んでいた。)
-I lived in a large apartment complex when I was a child.
}
あまり-
{
あまり (あまり) - not very (with negative) / too much (with positive)
An adverb. Most commonly used with negative verbs to mean "not much/not very."
Memory Tip: Think of "remainder/surplus." Doing something past the normal limit, or conversely, barely hitting it.
Example: 今日はあまり寒くない。(きょうはあまりさむくない。)
-It is not very cold today.
}
当たらない-
{
当たらない (あたらない) - doesn't hit / incorrect / doesn't apply
The negative form of 当たる (あたる - to hit/win/apply).
Memory Tip: 当 means to hit the target. 当たらない means missing the mark or a prediction being wrong.
Example: 彼の天気予報はめったに当たらない。(かれのてんきよほうはめったにあたらない。)
-His weather forecasts rarely hit the mark.
}
はっきり-
{
はっきり (はっきり) - clearly / distinctly
An adverb used when something can be seen, heard, or understood clearly without confusion.
Memory Tip: Sounds crisp and sharp, just like seeing something in high definition.
Example: 彼の声ははっきり聞こえます。(かれのこえははっきりきこえます。)
-His voice can be heard clearly.
}
増える-
{
増える (ふえる) - to increase / multiply
An intransitive verb used when numbers, amounts, or quantities go up naturally.
Memory Tip: The left side is 水 (water radical). Think of water levels rising and increasing.
Example: 体重が増えた。(たいじゅうがふえた。)
-My body weight increased.
}
育む-
{
育む (はぐくむ) - to nurture / foster / cultivate
A poetic or deeper transitive verb often used for cultivating love, dreams, trust, or shielding something to help it grow.
Memory Tip: Think of a bird covering its chicks with its wings to protect and nurture them.
Example: 二人は長い時間をかけて愛を育んだ。(ふたりはながいじかんをかけてあいをはぐくんだ。)
-The two of them nurtured their love over a long period of time.
}
墓-
{
墓 (はか) - grave / tomb
A noun referring to a burial site or tombstone.
Memory Tip: Imagine the cross at the top of 墓 sits over the ground, marking a burial plot.
Example: お盆にお墓参りに行きました。(おぼんにおはかまいりにいきました。)
-I went to visit the family grave during Obon.
}
開く-
{
開く (ひらく) - to open / hold (an event)
A verb meaning to physically open (like a book or umbrella) or to host/hold a meeting or party.
Memory Tip: The gate radical 門 contains 开 (two hands sliding a bolt open).
Example: 来週、誕生日パーティーを開きます。(らいしゅう、たんじょうびぱーてぃーをひらきます。)
-I will hold a birthday party next week.
}
育てる-
{
育てる (そだてる) - to raise / bring up / nurture
A transitive verb used for raising children, pets, or growing plants.
Memory Tip: 育 means to grow up. 育てる is the active thing you do to help something grow.
Example: 彼女は３人の子供を育てた。(かのじょはさんにんのこどもをそだてた。)
-She raised three children.
}
こんなことしか-
{
こんなことしか (こんなことしか) - only something small like this / nothing but this
A humble phrase used when you feel your helpful actions are minimal or insufficient.
Memory Tip: こんなこと (a thing like this) + しか (only, used with negative).
Example: こんなことしか出来なくてごめんね。(こんなことしかできなくてごめんね。)
-I'm sorry I can only do a small thing like this for you.
}
従業-
{
従業 (じゅうぎょう) - employment / engagement in work
A noun referring to being engaged in operations or employment.
Memory Tip: 従 means "to follow/subordinate" and 業 means "work." Following a line of work.
Example: 従業時間は午前９時から午後５時までだ。(じゅうぎょうじかんはごぜんくじからごごごじまでだ。)
-The working hours are from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM.
}
歳をとってしまい-
{
歳をとってしまい (としをとってしまい) - ended up growing old
A phrase expressing regret or completion about aging.
Memory Tip: 歳をとる (to take on years/age) + 〜てしまう (regrettable completion).
Example: 私も歳をとってしまいました。(わたしもとしをとってしまいました。)
-I, too, have ended up growing old.
}
からかい-
{
からかい (からかい) - teasing / banter
The noun form of the verb からかう (to tease/banter).
Memory Tip: Think of light-hearted teasing among friends.
Example: 彼の言葉はただのからかいだ。(かれのことばはただのからかいだ。)
-His words are just teasing.
}
なければならない-
{
なければならない (なければならない) - must do / have to do
A high-frequency grammar pattern indicating an absolute obligation.
Memory Tip: なければ (if you don't do it) + ならない (it won't work/it's unacceptable).
Example: 今日は早く寝なければならない。(きょうははやくねなければならない。)
-I must go to sleep early today.
}
衛兵-
{
衛兵 (えいへい) - guard / sentinel
A noun referring to a soldier or guard stationed to protect a specific place.
Memory Tip: 衛 means "defense/protection" and 兵 means "soldier." A defense soldier.
Example: バッキンガム宮殿の衛兵を見た。(バッキンガムきゅうでんのえいへいをみた。)
-I saw the guards at Buckingham Palace.
}
よく-
{
よく (よく) - often / well
An adverb used to describe doing something frequently or doing something thoroughly.
Memory Tip: Sounds like "yoku" which means good; doing something often or well is a good habit.
Example: 彼はよく本を読む。(かれはよくほんをよむ。)
-He often reads books.
}
遊べばよかった-
{
遊べばよかった (あそべばよかった) - I wish I had played / I should have hung out
A conditional grammar phrase expressing regret over an action not taken.
Memory Tip: 遊べば (if I had played) + よかった (it would have been good).
Example: 学生時代にもっと遊べばよかった。(がくせいじだいにもっとあそべばよかった。)
-I wish I had played/hung out more during my student days.
}
授業-
{
授業 (じゅぎょう) - class / lesson
A noun referring to a school class or lesson.
Memory Tip: 授 means "to instruct/confer" and 業 means "work/business." The work of instruction.
Example: 今日の授業は面白かった。(きょうのじゅぎょうはおもしろかった。)
-Today's class was interesting.
}
押し入って-
{
押し入って (おしいって) - to break into / force one's way in
The -te form of the compound verb 押し入る (おしいる), meaning to push past and enter.
Memory Tip: 押す (to push) + 入る (to enter) = pushing your way in forcefully.
Example: 泥棒が家に押し入ってきた。(泥棒がいえにおしいってきた。)
-A thief broke into the house.
}
つもり-
{
つもり (つもり) - intention / plan
A noun used after a verb to express what you intend or plan to do.
Memory Tip: Standard grammar structure: [Verb Plain Form] + つもり.
Example: 明日は勉強するつもりです。(あしたはべんきょうするつもりです。)
-I intend to study tomorrow.
}
〜だと-
{
〜だと (〜だと) - if it's the case that... / rumor has it that...
A particle phrase used to establish a condition or to report something heard.
Memory Tip: だ (copula) + と (conditional/quotation).
Example: 明日だと都合が良いです。(あしただとつごうがよいです。)
-If it's tomorrow, that is convenient for me.
}
〜なんて-
{
〜なんて (〜なんて) - things like... / to think that...
A particle expressing modesty, trivialization, or deep surprise/disbelief about something.
Memory Tip: Used to single out an item with a sense of "such a thing as."
Example: 私が合格するなんて信じられない。(わたしがごうかくするなんてしんじられない。)
-I can't believe that someone like me passed.
}
〜のでしょう-
{
〜のでしょう (〜のでしょう) - probably is / right?
A polite ending pattern used to express a strong conjecture or ask for gentle confirmation.
Memory Tip: の (explanatory) + でしょう (probably/right).
Example: 明日は雨が降るのでしょう。(あしたはあめがふるのでしょう。)
-It will probably rain tomorrow, right?
}
〜たり-
{
〜たり (〜たり) - doing things like X and Y
A grammar particle used in pairs (〜たり、〜たりする) to list examples of activities.
Memory Tip: Attached to past tense ta-forms of verbs to form an open list.
Example: 週末は本を読んだり、映画を見たりします。(しゅうまつはほんをよんだり、えいがをみたりします。)
-On weekends, I do things like reading books and watching movies.
}
〜が、-
{
〜が、 (〜が、) - but / however / although
A conjunction particle placed at the end of a clause to introduce a contrast.
Memory Tip: Functions identically to "but" in English when linking two clauses.
Example: 勉強しましたが、テストは難しかった。(べんきょうしましたが、てすとはむずかしかった。)
-I studied, but the test was difficult.
}
どうなるか-
{
どうなるか (どうなるか) - what will happen / how it will turn out
An embedded question phrase wondering about a future outcome.
Memory Tip: どう (how) + なる (to become) + か (question marker).
Example: これからどうなるか分からない。(これからどうなるかわからない。)
-I don't know what will happen from here on out.
}
やり取り-
{
やり取り (やりとり) - exchange / giving and taking
A noun referring to back-and-forth communication, messages, or exchanges.
Memory Tip: Combined from やる (to give) and 取る (to take). The literal act of giving and taking.
Example: 友達とメールのやり取りをする。(ともだちとめーるのやりとりをする。)
-I exchange emails with my friend.
}
読むうちに-
{
読むうちに (よむうちに) - while reading / in the course of reading
A grammar phrase combining 読む (to read) with 〜うちに (while/in the process of).
Memory Tip: 〜うちに implies that a natural change happens while you are in the middle of doing an action.
Example: 本を読むうちに、眠くなってしまった。(ほんをよむうちに、ねむくなってしまった。)
-While reading the book, I ended up getting sleepy.
}
ただ-
{
ただ (ただ) - just / only / simply
An adverb used to minimize something or indicate a narrow scope.
Memory Tip: Sounds like "ta-da!"—revealing that it's nothing special, just a simple thing.
Example: 私はただの学生です。(わたしはただのがくせいです。)
-I am just a student.
}
おかしい-
{
おかしい (おかしい) - strange / funny / suspicious
An i-adjective used for something amusingly funny, or something weird/out of place.
Memory Tip: If something doesn't make sense or feels out of alignment, it's "okashii."
Example: この機械の動きはおかしい。(このきかいのうごきはおかしい。)
-This machine's movement is strange.
}
寝たきり-
{
寝たきり (ねたきり) - bedridden
A noun indicating a state of being confined to bed, usually due to illness or old age.
Memory Tip: 寝た means slept/laid down, and きり implies "just that" or "entirely." Literally, entirely lying down.
Example: 祖母は寝たきりになっている。(そぼはねたきりになっている。)
-My grandmother is bedridden.
}
明るい-
{
明るい (あかるい) - bright / cheerful
An i-adjective used to describe physical brightness or a person's upbeat, cheerful personality.
Memory Tip: 明 combines the sun (日) and the moon (月). Having both makes things very bright!
Example: 彼女はとても明るい性格だ。(かのじょはとてもあかるいせいかくだ。)
-She has a very cheerful personality.
}
〜たり-
{
〜たり (〜たり) - doing such things as... / sometimes...
A grammatical particle used with verbs to list representative actions or states, usually followed by する.
Memory Tip: Think of "tallying" up different activities. I did this (tally), I did that (tally).
Example: 週末は本を読んだり映画を見たりする。(しゅうまつはほんをよんだりえいがをみたりする。)
-On weekends, I do things like read books and watch movies.
}
苦しい-
{
苦しい (くるしい) - painful / difficult / tough
An i-adjective describing physical or emotional distress, tightness, or financial difficulty.
Memory Tip: The kanji 苦 represents suffering or bitterness (like bitter medicine).
Example: 息をするのが苦しい。(いきをするのがくるしい。)
-It is painful to breathe.
}
〜くて-
{
〜くて (〜くて) - and / because (for i-adjectives)
The te-form connective for i-adjectives, used to link descriptions or indicate a cause.
Memory Tip: Drop the final "i" (い) and add "kute" (くて) to "cut" the word and connect a new one.
Example: このケーキは安くて美味しい。(このけーきはやすくておいしい。)
-This cake is cheap and delicious.
}
気が狂う-
{
気が狂う (きがくるう) - to go mad / lose one's mind
An expression meaning to go crazy, either literally or figuratively from stress/emotion.
Memory Tip: 気 (spirit/mind) + 狂う (to go out of order/go crazy). Your mind goes out of order.
Example: 忙しすぎて気が狂いそうだ。(いそがしすぎてきがくるいそうだ。)
-I'm so busy I feel like I'm going to lose my mind.
}
ある日-
{
ある日 (あるひ) - one day / a certain day
A phrase often used in storytelling to introduce an event that happened on an unspecified day.
Memory Tip: ある means "a certain" or "existing", and 日 is day. "A certain day."
Example: ある日、不思議な手紙が届いた。(あるひ、ふしぎなてがみがとどいた。)
-One day, a mysterious letter arrived.
}
着替え-
{
着替え (きがえ) - change of clothes / changing clothes
A noun (from the verb 着替える) referring to spare clothes or the act of changing attire.
Memory Tip: 着 (wear) + 替え (exchange/swap). Swapping what you wear.
Example: 念のため着替えを持っていく。(ねんのためきがえをもっていく。)
-I'll bring a change of clothes just in case.
}
箪笥-
{
箪笥 (たんす) - chest of drawers / wardrobe
A noun for traditional Japanese cabinetry or any general dresser for clothes.
Memory Tip: Both kanji are complex and contain the bamboo radical (⺮), as old storage items were often crafted from bamboo or wood.
Example: 服を箪笥にしまう。(ふくをたんすにしまう。)
-To put away clothes in the dresser.
}
開きました-
{
開きました (あきました / ひらきました) - opened
The polite past tense of 開く, meaning something opened (intransitive: あく) or someone opened something (transitive: ひらく).
Memory Tip: The kanji 開 has a gate (門) and two hands opening it. ました makes it a polite past action.
Example: ドアが自動で開きました。(どあがじどうであきました。)
-The door opened automatically.
}
奥-
{
奥 (おく) - inner part / back / depths
A noun referring to the deep interior or the back of a space, building, or drawer.
Memory Tip: Sounds like "oak"—imagine walking deep into the inner part of an oak forest.
Example: 箪笥の奥に隠す。(たんすのおくにかくす。)
-To hide it in the back of the dresser.
}
きちんと-
{
きちんと (きちんと) - properly / neatly / accurately
An adverb indicating that an action is done in an exact, orderly, or flawless manner.
Memory Tip: Sounds like "kitchen." You have to keep a kitchen "properly and neatly" clean.
Example: 部屋をきちんと片付ける。(へやをきちんとかたづける。)
-To tidy up the room neatly.
}
まとめてある-
{
まとめてある (まとめてある) - is gathered together / is organized
A grammatical construct using the te-form of まとめる (to collect/summarize) + ある (indicates a resulting state from an intentional action).
Memory Tip: まとめる means to gather. The 〜てある ending shows someone left it gathered for a reason.
Example: 資料は机の上にまとめてある。(しりょうはつくえのうえにまとめてある。)
-The documents have been gathered together on the desk.
}
三十通-
{
三十通 (さんじゅっつう) - 30 letters/documents
A number + counter combination. 通 (つう) is the counter for letters, emails, and documents.
Memory Tip: 通 (pass/commute) is used for letters because they travel and "pass" through the mail to get to you.
Example: 手紙を三十通も書いた。(てがみをさんじゅっつうもかいた。)
-I wrote as many as 30 letters.
}
裏-
{
裏 (うら) - reverse side / back / behind
A noun referring to the back or hidden side of an object, or behind a building.
Memory Tip: It looks similar to 表 (front), but has clothes (衣) at the bottom. The inside of clothes is the reverse side.
Example: 紙の裏に名前を書く。(かみのうらになまえをかく。)
-Write your name on the back of the paper.
}
封筒-
{
封筒 (ふうとう) - envelope
A noun for a paper container used to send letters.
Memory Tip: 封 means seal, and 筒 means tube or cylinder. Before flat envelopes, letters were often sealed in bamboo tubes.
Example: 手紙を封筒に入れる。(てがみをふうとうにいれる。)
-To put a letter in an envelope.
}
恐ろしい-
{
恐ろしい (おそろしい) - terrifying / frightening / dreadful
An i-adjective used to express intense fear or the dreadful nature of something.
Memory Tip: The kanji 恐 contains the heart radical (心) at the bottom. Your heart drops when you see something terrifying.
Example: 恐ろしい夢を見た。(おそろしいゆめをみた。)
-I had a terrifying dream.
}
恋-
{
恋 (こい) - romantic love
A noun representing romantic affection, passion, or longing for someone.
Memory Tip: 恋 has the heart radical (心) at the bottom. It represents the deeply felt, often slightly painful, emotional side of love.
Example: 彼女は恋をしている。(かのじょはこいをしている。)
-She is in love.
}
幸せ-
{
幸せ (しあわせ) - happiness / blessing / good fortune
A noun or na-adjective representing a state of joy, contentment, and well-being.
Memory Tip: The kanji 幸 means fortune. It looks like a person with their arms open wide to receive good luck.
Example: あなたといると幸せだ。(あなたといるとしあわせだ。)
-I am happy when I am with you.
}
焼きました-
{
焼きました (やきました) - baked / grilled / burned
The polite past tense of 焼く (やく), meaning to cook with heat or to burn something down.
Memory Tip: The kanji 焼 contains the fire radical (火). Fire is used to bake or burn.
Example: 庭で古い手紙を焼きました。(にわでふるいてがみをやきました。)
-I burned the old letters in the yard.
}
途中-
{
途中 (とちゅう) - midway / on the way / in the middle of
A noun used to indicate that something happens while en route to a destination or in the middle of an action. (Note: corrected from 途中う)
Memory Tip: 途 (route) + 中 (middle). Literally "middle of the route."
Example: 学校へ行く途中で雨が降った。(がっこうへいくとちゅうであめがふった。)
-It rained on the way to school.
}
痩せる-
{
痩せる (やせる) - to lose weight / to become thin
An ichidan (ru) verb describing the physical act of getting thinner.
Memory Tip: The kanji 痩 contains the sickness radical (疒) because getting dangerously thin was historically associated with illness.
Example: 運動して少し痩せた。(うんどうしてすこしやせた。)
-I exercised and lost a little weight.
}
枕-
{
枕 (まくら) - pillow
A noun for the cushion you rest your head on while sleeping.
Memory Tip: Contains the wood radical (木). In ancient Japan, pillows were often made of carved wood rather than soft fabric.
Example: 枕が変わると眠れない。(まくらがかわるとねむれない。)
-I can't sleep if my pillow changes (if I use a different pillow).
}
つもり-
{
つもり (つもり) - intention / plan / belief
A noun used after a verb to express what someone intends to do, or what they are convinced is true.
Memory Tip: Sounds like "tsunami." When you have a strong intention, it hits you like a tsunami of motivation.
Example: 明日、彼に会うつもりだ。(あした、かれにあうつもりだ。)
-I intend to meet him tomorrow.
}
そのころ-
{
そのころ (そのころ) - around that time / in those days
An expression indicating a specific, approximate time period in the past (or sometimes future).
Memory Tip: その (that) + ころ (around the time of). Very literal translation.
Example: そのころ、私は学生だった。(そのころ、わたしはがくせいだった。)
-Around that time, I was a student.
}
指差して-
{
指差して (ゆびさして) - pointing at
The te-form of 指差す (ゆびさす), meaning to point a finger at someone or something.
Memory Tip: 指 (finger) + 差して (thrust/indicate). Thrusting your finger to point.
Example: 彼は空を指差して叫んだ。(かれはそらをゆびさしてさけんだ。)
-He pointed at the sky and shouted.
}
いつ来たの-
{
いつ来たの (いつきたの) - when did (you) come?
A casual question asking for the time of arrival. The 'の' acts as a casual question marker.
Memory Tip: いつ (when) + 来た (came) + の (question marker).
Example: 部屋にいたんだ。いつ来たの？(へやにいたんだ。いつきたの？)
-You were in the room. When did you get here?
}
変わる-
{
変わる (かわる) - to change / to be altered
An intransitive godan (u) verb meaning something transforms or becomes different.
Memory Tip: 変わる is for when something changes on its own or naturally (intransitive), like the weather or feelings.
Example: 季節が変わる。(きせつがかわる。)
-The seasons change.
}
自分で-
{
自分で (じぶんで) - by oneself / personally
A phrase meaning doing an action without help from others.
Memory Tip: 自分 (oneself) + で (by means of). By means of oneself.
Example: 自分で宿題をやった。(じぶんでしゅくだいをやった。)
-I did my homework by myself.
}
また-
{
また (また) - again / also / moreover
An adverb or conjunction used to indicate repetition or an addition to something just said.
Memory Tip: Think of saying "matter" with a British accent. When things happen again, it becomes a matter of concern.
Example: また明日会いましょう。(またあしたあいましょう。)
-Let's meet again tomorrow.
}
こっそり-
{
こっそり (こっそり) - secretly / stealthily
An adverb describing an action done quietly so others won't notice.
Memory Tip: Sounds like "costly." If you break a costly vase, you secretly hide the pieces.
Example: こっそりケーキを食べた。(こっそりけーきをたべた。)
-I secretly ate the cake.
}
置いておく-
{
置いておく (おいておく) - to put (and leave it) / to leave behind
A grammatical structure: 置く (to put) + 〜ておく (to do in advance or leave in a state).
Memory Tip: 置いて is "put", and おく is "leave it for later." Put it down and leave it for a future purpose.
Example: 鍵を机の上に置いておく。(かぎをつくえのうえにおいとおく。)
-I'll leave the keys on the desk (for later).
}
当時-
{
当時 (とうじ) - at that time / in those days
A noun referring to a specific period in the past that is being discussed.
Memory Tip: 当 (this/that specific) + 時 (time). That specific time.
Example: 当時、インターネットはなかった。(とうじ、いんたーねっとはなかった。)
-At that time, the internet did not exist.
}
～のもの-
{
～のもの (〜のもの) - belonging to... / the property of...
A phrase indicating possession or origin, typically attaching a noun to a pronoun.
Memory Tip: の (possessive) + もの (thing). "The thing of [Subject]."
Example: これは私のものです。(これはわたしのものです。)
-This belongs to me (is my thing).
}
ではなかった-
{
ではなかった (ではなかった) - was not
The formal past negative form of です/だ. It means something wasn't a certain way.
Memory Tip: では (topic of state) + ない (not) -> なかった (was not).
Example: 彼は犯人ではなかった。(かれははんにんではなかった。)
-He was not the culprit.
}
捨て-
{
捨て (すて) - throwing away (continuative form)
The stem (連用形) of 捨てる, meaning to throw away or discard. It connects to other words (like 捨て犬 - abandoned dog).
Memory Tip: The kanji 捨 has the hand radical (扌). You use your hand to toss the trash.
Example: ゴミを捨てに行く。(ごみをすてにいく。)
-I am going to throw away the trash.
}
ですが-
{
ですが (ですが) - however / but
A polite conjunction used at the beginning of a sentence, or attached to a clause, to introduce a contrast.
Memory Tip: です (it is) + が (but). "It is so, but..."
Example: 雨ですが、出かけます。(あめですが、でかけます。)
-It is raining, but I will go out.
}
私には-
{
私には (わたしには) - to me / for me / as far as I am concerned
A combination of 私 (I/me) + に (target/direction) + は (topic marker), emphasizing a perspective or ability.
Memory Tip: Translates clearly: "As for (は) toward (に) me (私)."
Example: 私にはわからない。(わたしにはわからない。)
-It is incomprehensible to me (I don't understand).
}
眩しい-
{
眩しい (まぶしい) - dazzling / radiant / glaring
An i-adjective describing light that is so bright it hurts the eyes, or someone who is radiantly beautiful.
Memory Tip: The kanji 眩 has the eye radical (目). The brightness is blinding your eyes.
Example: 太陽が眩しい。(たいようがまぶしい。)
-The sun is dazzlingly bright.
}
〜すぎる-
{
〜すぎる (〜すぎる) - too much / overly
An auxiliary verb attached to verb stems or adjective roots to indicate an excessive amount or degree.
Memory Tip: Think of "sugary." If a cake is overly sugary, you put too much sugar. すぎる = too much.
Example: ご飯を食べすぎる。(ごはんをたべすぎる。)
-To eat too much rice/food.
}
困る-
{
困る (こまる) - to be troubled / to be bothered / to be in a bind
An intransitive godan verb indicating one is in a difficult situation and doesn't know what to do.
Memory Tip: The kanji 困 shows a tree (木) trapped inside a box (囗). A trapped tree is in a troubled spot!
Example: お金がなくて困る。(おかねがなくてこまる。)
-I am troubled because I have no money.
}
そのことを-
{
そのことを (そのことを) - about that matter (as an object)
A phrase pointing to a specific topic or event previously mentioned, marked as the direct object by を.
Memory Tip: その (that) + こと (intangible thing/matter) + を (object marker).
Example: そのことを彼に話した。(そのことをかれにはなした。)
-I talked to him about that matter.
}
ようにする-
{
ようにする (ようにする) - to make an effort to do / to try to
A grammar point used to express a conscious effort or habit to bring about a certain state or action.
Memory Tip: ように (in a way that) + する (to do). You "do" things "in a way that" achieves the goal.
Example: 毎日野菜を食べるようにする。(まいにちやさいをたべるようにする。)
-I make an effort to eat vegetables every day.
}
しなければなりません-
{
しなければなりません (しなければなりません) - must do / have to do
A highly polite and formal expression indicating obligation or duty.
Memory Tip: しない (not do) + ば (if) + なりません (it won't do/be okay). "If I do not do it, it won't be okay."
Example: 明日早く起きなければなりません。(あしたはやくおきなければなりません。)
-I must wake up early tomorrow.
}
なかった-
{
なかった (なかった) - was not / did not exist
The plain past tense of ない (negative of ある), meaning something wasn't there or didn't happen.
Memory Tip: The past tense of i-adjectives ends in かった. ない becomes なかった.
Example: 質問はなかった。(しつもんはなかった。)
-There were no questions.
}
自信-
{
自信 (じしん) - confidence
A noun referring to a belief in one's own abilities or qualities.
Memory Tip: 自 (self) + 信 (believe). To believe in oneself.
Example: 彼には自信がある。(かれにはじしんがある。)
-He has confidence.
}
間違う-
{
間違う (まちがう) - to make a mistake / to be incorrect
A godan (u) verb meaning to get something wrong or to err.
Memory Tip: 間 (space/interval) + 違う (differ/be wrong). If your spacing is wrong, you make a mistake.
Example: テストの答えを間違う。(てすとのこたえをまちがう。)
-To make a mistake on a test answer.
}
勇気-
{
勇気 (ゆうき) - courage / bravery
A noun for the mental or moral strength to venture, persevere, and withstand danger or fear.
Memory Tip: 勇 (bravery) + 気 (spirit). A brave spirit.
Example: 勇気を出して告白する。(ゆうきをだしてこくはくする。)
-To muster up the courage and confess (one's love).
}
口笛-
{
口笛 (くちぶえ) - whistle (with one's mouth)
A noun for the sound made by forcing breath through a small opening in the lips.
Memory Tip: 口 (mouth) + 笛 (flute). A flute made by your mouth.
Example: 機嫌よく口笛を吹く。(きげんよくくちぶえをふく。)
-To whistle cheerfully.
}
破る-
{
破る (やぶる) - to tear / to break / to defeat
A transitive godan verb used for tearing paper, breaking promises, or defeating an opponent.
Memory Tip: The kanji 破 means "rend/tear" and has the skin/hide radical (皮) next to stone (石). Smashing hide with a stone tears it.
Example: 約束を破る。(やくそくをやぶる。)
-To break a promise.
}
真似して-
{
真似して (まねして) - imitating / copying
The te-form of 真似する, meaning to mimic someone's actions, voice, or style.
Memory Tip: 真 (true) + 似 (resemble). Trying to truly resemble someone else by copying them.
Example: 鳥の鳴き声を真似して。(とりのなきごえをまねして。)
-Imitating the sound of a bird.
}
しなくてもいい-
{
しなくてもいい (しなくてもいい) - do not have to do / it is okay not to do
A grammar structure expressing the absence of obligation.
Memory Tip: しなくて (not doing) + も (even if) + いい (is good). "Even if you don't do it, it is good."
Example: 無理をしなくてもいい。(むりをしなくてもいい。)
-You don't have to push yourself too hard.
}
美しかった-
{
美しかった (うつくしかった) - was beautiful
The past tense of the i-adjective 美しい. (Note: Corrected from your list's "美しいかった", as i-adjectives drop the 'i' before 'katta').
Memory Tip: かった is the time machine for i-adjectives, sending them to the past.
Example: 昨夜の星は美しかった。(さくやのほしはうつくしかった。)
-The stars last night were beautiful.
}
〜のでしょう-
{
〜のでしょう (〜のでしょう) - I guess that... / probably... / isn't it?
A polite conjectural or explanatory ending. It asks for agreement or expresses a deduction.
Memory Tip: の (explanatory) + でしょう (polite "probably"). Seeking a polite confirmation of a situation.
Example: 彼は疲れているのでしょう。(かれはつかれているのでしょう。)
-He is probably tired.
}
一昨年-
{
一昨年 (いっさくねん / おととし) - the year before last
A noun referring to two years ago. "おととし" is the conversational reading, "いっさくねん" is more formal.
Memory Tip: 一 (one) + 昨 (previous) + 年 (year). One year before the previous year.
Example: 一昨年、日本に行きました。(おととし、にほんへいきました。)
-I went to Japan the year before last.
}
〜なんて-
{
〜なんて (〜なんて) - such a thing as... / things like...
A particle used to express surprise, belittlement, or modesty about the preceding noun or phrase.
Memory Tip: Think of it as a dramatic sigh. "Math... nante... I hate it!"
Example: お化けなんていない。(おばけなんていない。)
-There is no such thing as ghosts.
}
もっと-
{
もっと (もっと) - more / longer / further
An adverb used to indicate a higher degree or amount of something.
Memory Tip: When you want more, you want the most-o (motto).
Example: もっと日本語を勉強したい。(もっとにほんごをべんきょうしたい。)
-I want to study Japanese more.
}
もって-
{
もって (もって) - having / by means of / with
Depending on context, it's either the te-form of 持つ (to hold) or the particle 以て (by means of). Let's use the very common "持つ" (to hold/have).
Memory Tip: If derived from 持つ, think of holding a "mote" (moat) to defend a castle. You are holding it.
Example: 自信をもって頑張れ。(じしんをもってがんばれ。)
-Do your best with confidence (holding confidence).
}
〜ことがない-
{
〜ことがない (〜ことがない) - have never done / it never happens
A grammar structure used with a verb to express that an experience has never occurred.
Memory Tip: こと (the event of) + がない (does not exist). The event does not exist.
Example: 納豆を食べたことがない。(なっとうをたべたことがない。)
-I have never eaten natto.
}
死にたくない-
{
死にたくない (しにたくない) - do not want to die
The negative tai-form (desire) of the verb 死ぬ (to die).
Memory Tip: 死に (die) + たく (want - negative stem) + ない (not).
Example: まだ死にたくない。(まだしにたくない。)
-I don't want to die yet.
}
胸がいっぱいになる-
{
胸がいっぱいになる (むねがいっぱいになる) - to be overwhelmed with emotion
An idiom meaning one's heart is full of intense feelings (joy, sadness, gratitude, etc.).
Memory Tip: 胸 (chest/heart) + がいっぱい (is full) + になる (becomes). Your chest becomes physically full of emotion.
Example: 感謝で胸がいっぱいになる。(かんしゃでむねがいっぱいになる。)
-To be overwhelmed with gratitude.
}
涙-
{
涙 (なみだ) - tear(s)
A noun for the liquid that falls from your eyes when crying.
Memory Tip: The kanji has the water radical (氵) on the left, and a shape resembling an eye weeping on the right.
Example: 彼女の目に涙が浮かんだ。(かのじょのめになみだがうかんだ。)
-Tears welled up in her eyes.
}
抱きしめました-
{
抱きしめました (だきしめました) - hugged / embraced
The polite past tense of 抱きしめる, meaning to hold someone tightly in your arms.
Memory Tip: 抱き (hold/hug) + しめる (tighten). To hug someone tightly.
Example: 母親は子供を抱きしめました。(ははおやはこどもをだきしめました。)
-The mother hugged her child.
}
けれど-
{
けれど (けれど) - but / however / although
A conjunction used to connect two contrasting clauses. A slightly less formal version of けれども.
Memory Tip: Functions identically to "but". "I want to go, keredo, I have no time."
Example: 疲れたけれど、楽しかった。(つかれたけれど、たのしかった。)
-I was tired, but it was fun.
}
〜だと-
{
〜だと (〜だと) - if it is... / that it is...
A quotation or conditional marker used after nouns or na-adjectives. だ (copula) + と (quotation/conditional).
Memory Tip: だ states what it is, and と acts like quotation marks or an "if/when" trigger.
Example: 雨だと試合は中止だ。(あめだとしあいはちゅうしだ。)
-If it is rain, the match will be canceled.
}
なさった-
{
なさった (なさった) - did (honorific)
The past tense of なさる, the sonkeigo (respectful) equivalent of する (to do). Used for someone else's actions.
Memory Tip: Sounds like NASA. Astronauts at NASA did great, respectable things.
Example: 先生はどうなさいましたか。(せんせいはどうなさいましたか。)
-[Polite form] What happened to the teacher? / What did the teacher do?
}
厳しい-
{
厳しい (きびしい) - strict / severe / intense
An i-adjective used for strict rules, severe weather, or harsh people.
Memory Tip: The kanji 厳 is complex and sharp-looking, just like a strict teacher grading your test.
Example: 冬の寒さが厳しい。(ふゆのさむさがきびしい。)
-The winter cold is severe.
}
かわいそうだ-
{
かわいそうだ (かわいそうだ) - pitiful / poor thing
A na-adjective expressing sympathy or pity for someone else's unfortunate situation.
Memory Tip: Careful! 可愛い (kawaii) means cute. かわいそう (kawaisou) means pitiful/sad. The "sou" means "seems", so it "seems like a situation requiring pity."
Example: 迷子の子犬がかわいそうだ。(まいごのこいぬがかわいそうだ。)
-The lost puppy is a poor thing (pitiful).
}
と思った-
{
と思った (とおもった) - thought that...
The quotation particle と + the past tense of 思う (to think). Used to state a past thought.
Memory Tip: と quotes your mind's voice, and 思った means "I thought."
Example: 明日は晴れると思った。(あしたははれるとおもった。)
-I thought it would be sunny tomorrow.
}
のかもしれません-
{
のかもしれません (のかもしれません) - might be / perhaps
A polite expression used to state a possibility or conjecture with low certainty.
Memory Tip: の (explanatory) + か (question) + も (also) + しれません (cannot know). "I also cannot know if it is..."
Example: 彼は病気なのかもしれません。(かれはびょうきなのかもしれません。)
-He might be sick.
}
信じたいです-
{
信じたいです (しんじたいです) - want to believe
The polite tai-form (desire) of 信じる (to believe).
Memory Tip: 信じる (to believe) drops the る and adds たい (want to) + です (polite).
Example: 彼の言葉を信じたいです。(かれのことばをしんじたいです。)
-I want to believe his words.
}
思った方がいい-
{
思った方がいい (おもったほうがいい) - had better think... / should consider
A grammar structure giving advice: past tense verb (思った) + 方がいい (it is better to).
Memory Tip: 方 (way/direction) + がいい (is good). "The direction where you thought about it is good."
Example: これはチャンスだと思った方がいい。(これはちゃんすだとおもったほうがいい。)
-You should consider this a chance.
}
移動-
{
移動 (いどう) - movement / transfer / migration
A noun or Suru-verb referring to changing one's position, moving from one place to another, or transferring locations.
Memory Tip: 移 means to shift or move, and 動 means to change position (action). Together, they mean moving from point A to point B.
Example: 電車で次の目的地へ移動する。(でんしゃでつぎのもくてきちへいどうする。)
-We will move to the next destination by train.
}
展開-
{
展開 (てんかい) - development / expansion / unfolding (e.g., plot or map)
A noun or Suru-verb referring to opening up a space, expanding a business, or the unfolding of a story or strategy.
Memory Tip: 展 means to unfold or display, and 開 means to open. Think of unrolling a scroll or expanding a map.
Example: 物語は予想外の展開を迎えた。(ものがたりはよそうがいのてんかいをむかえた。)
-The story took an unexpected turn (unfolding).
}
多彩-
{
多彩 (たさい) - colorful / diverse / variegated
A Na-adjective describing a wide variety of colors, talents, styles, or options.
Memory Tip: 多 means many, and 彩 means colors or brilliance. "Many colors" implies a rich diversity.
Example: 彼は多彩な才能を持っている。(かれはたさいなさいのうをもっている。)
-He possesses a diverse range of talents.
}
異なる-
{
異なる (ことなる) - to differ / to vary / to be different
A formal, literary verb used to state that two or more things are not identical in nature, appearance, or opinion.
Memory Tip: Think of this as the written/formal equivalent of 違う (ちがう).
Example: 二人の意見は大きく異なる。(ふたりのいけんはおおきくことなる。)
-The opinions of the two people differ greatly.
}
全般-
{
全般 (ぜんぱん) - overall / general / across the board
A noun referring to the entirety of a specific subject, field, or situation rather than just a part of it.
Memory Tip: 全 means all or whole, and 般 means variety or category. It covers all categories of a topic.
Example: 彼はゲーム全般に詳しい。(かれはげーむぜんぱんにくわしい。)
-He is knowledgeable about gaming in general.
}
指し-
{
指し (さし) - pointing / indicating / referring to
The continuative/noun form (連用形) of the verb 指す (さす), meaning to point at, direct toward, or refer to something.
Memory Tip: The kanji 指 features the hand radical (扌), which makes sense since you use your finger to point.
Example: 指し示された方向へ進む。(さししめされたほうこうへすすむ。)
-Move in the direction that was pointed out.
}
挑戦-
{
挑戦 (ちょうせん) - challenge / attempt / try
A noun or Suru-verb representing the act of taking on a difficult task, rival, or new endeavor with courage.
Memory Tip: 挑 means to provoke or test, and 戦 means battle. You are psyching yourself up to battle a tough goal.
Example: 新しい記録に挑戦する。(あたらしいきろくにちょうせんする。)
-To challenge a new record.
}
草原-
{
草原 (そうげん) - grassland / prairie / meadow
A noun describing a wide, open field covered primarily with grass.
Memory Tip: 草 means grass, and 原 means field or tundra. Literally, a "grass field."
Example: 馬たちが広い草原を駆け抜けた。(うまたちがひろいそうげんをかけぬけた。)
-The horses dashed through the wide grassland.
}
風景-
{
風景 (ふうけい) - scenery / landscape / view
A noun referring to the visual scenery of nature, a town, or a specific setting.
Memory Tip: 風 means wind/atmosphere, and 景 means view or scene. It's the visual atmosphere of a place.
Example: 窓から美しい山の風景が見える。(まどからうつくしいやまのふうけいがみえる。)
-A beautiful mountain landscape can be seen from the window.
}
飽きる-
{
飽きる (あきる) - to get tired of / to lose interest in / to be fed up with
An intransitive verb indicating that you have had too much of something to the point that it no longer entertains or satisfies you.
Memory Tip: Think of eating your favorite food every single day until you eventually get sick of it (飽きる).
Example: 毎日同じゲームばかりで飽きてしまった。(まいにちおなじげーむばかりであきてしまった。)
-I got tired of it because it's the same game every day.
}
攻略-
{
攻略 (こうりゃく) - capture / conquest / walkthrough (gaming)
A noun or Suru-verb meaning to conquer an enemy castle, or in modern contexts, to beat/complete a difficult video game stage or boss.
Memory Tip: 攻 means to attack, and 略 means strategy or capture. Attacking with a smart strategy to win.
Example: この難関ダンジョンの攻略方法を探す。(このなんかんだんじょんのこうりゃくほうほうをさがす。)
-Search for a strategy/walkthrough to beat this difficult dungeon.
}
関係ない-
{
関係ない (かんけいない) - unrelated / irrelevant / none of one's business
An I-adjective phrase meaning that a certain topic, person, or action has no connection to the matter at hand.
Memory Tip: 関係 (connection/relationship) combined with ない (does not exist). Literally: "No connection."
Example: それは今回の件とは全く関係ない。(それはこんかいのけんとわまったくかんけいない。)
-That is completely unrelated to the current matter.
}
育成-
{
育成 (いくせい) - rearing / training / cultivation (e.g., character leveling)
A noun or Suru-verb meaning to raise, nurture, and develop the skills or growth of children, monsters, or game characters.
Memory Tip: 育 means to raise/grow, and 成 means to become or succeed. Nurturing something so it grows up successfully.
Example: お気に入りのキャラクターを育成する。(おきにいりのきゃらくたーをいくせいする。)
-To raise/level up your favorite character.
}
散策-
{
散策 (さんさく) - stroll / wander / ramble
A noun or Suru-verb meaning to walk around leisurely for relaxation, enjoyment, or exploration.
Memory Tip: 散 means to scatter or stroll, and 策 means a cane or walking path. Stepping out to casually explore.
Example: 天気が良いので近くの公園を散策した。(てんきがよいのでちかくのこうえんをさんさくした。)
-The weather was nice, so I took a stroll through the nearby park.
}
指示-
{
指示 (しじ) - instructions / directions / orders
A noun or Suru-verb referring to the act of pointing out a specific direction or giving an order on what to do next.
Memory Tip: 指 means to point, and 示 means to show. You point your finger to show someone exactly what they need to do.
Example: 隊長の指示に従って行動してください。(たいちょうのしじにしたがっておこなってください。)
-Please act in accordance with the captain's instructions.
}
ひっそり-
{
ひっそり (ひっそり) - quietly / still / silently
An adverb (often used with と or する) written in hiragana. It describes a state of absolute quietness, stillness, or being unnoticed.
Memory Tip: Think of someone making a "Hiss!" sound to tell people to be completely quiet (ひっそり).
Example: 彼女は田舎でひっそりと暮らしている。(かのじょはいなかでひっそりとくらしている。)
-She lives quietly in the countryside.
}
佇んで-
{
佇んで (たたずんで) - standing still / lingering
The te-form of the verb 佇む (たたずむ). It combines the kanji 佇 (stand still/linger) to describe standing in one place for a while, often lost in thought.
Memory Tip: The kanji features a person (亻) standing (立) in a specific spot (宁).
Example: 彼は雨の中、一人で佇んでいた。(かれはあめのなか、ひとりでたたずんでいた。)
-He was standing still alone in the rain.
}
瞬かせた-
{
瞬かせた (まばたかせた) - blinked
The past tense, causative form of the verb 瞬く (まばたく). The kanji 瞬 means "blink" or "twinkle."
Memory Tip: Notice the eye radical (目) indicating an action done with the eyes, like a rapid blink.
Example: 彼女は驚いて目を瞬かせた。(かのじょはおどろいてめをまばたかせた。)
-She blinked her eyes in surprise.
}
鐘の音-
{
鐘の音 (かねのね) - sound of a bell
A noun phrase combining 鐘 (bell), the connecting particle の (of), and 音 (sound).
Memory Tip: A metal (金) object struck by a child (童) makes the heavy bell (鐘) sound (音).
Example: 遠くから教会の鐘の音が聞こえる。(とおくからきょうかいのかねのねがきこえる。)
-The sound of a church bell can be heard from afar.
}
覚ました-
{
覚ました (さました) - woke up / awakened
The past tense of the transitive verb 覚ます (さます). The kanji 覚 means "memorize," "learn," or "awake."
Memory Tip: When you wake up (覚), you suddenly become conscious and aware of your surroundings.
Example: 大きな物音が彼を眠りから覚ました。(おおきなものおとがかれをねむりからさました。)
-A loud noise woke him from his sleep.
}
廊下-
{
廊下 (ろうか) - corridor / hallway
A noun combining 廊 (corridor/gallery) and 下 (below/down). It refers to the passageways connecting rooms in a building.
Memory Tip: A long covered passage (廊) that you walk down (下).
Example: 廊下を走らないでください。(ろうかをはしらないでください。)
-Please do not run in the hallway.
}
飛び出した-
{
飛び出した (とびだした) - jumped out / flew out
The past tense of the compound verb 飛び出す, combining 飛 (fly/jump) and 出 (exit/out).
Memory Tip: Imagine a bird violently flying (飛) out (出) of an open cage.
Example: 子供が急に道路に飛び出した。(こどもがきゅうにどうろにとびだした。)
-A child suddenly jumped out into the road.
}
すると-
{
すると (すると) - thereupon / then / and then
A conjunction formed from the verb する (to do) and the conditional particle と. It connects two consecutive events where the second is an immediate result of the first.
Memory Tip: "When doing (する) that (と)... the next thing instantly happens."
Example: ドアを開けた。すると、彼が立っていた。(どあをあけた。すると、かれがたっていた。)
-I opened the door. Thereupon, he was standing there.
}
大勢-
{
大勢 (おおぜい) - many people / a crowd
A noun combining 大 (big/large) and 勢 (force/power/momentum). It specifically refers to a large number of people.
Memory Tip: A large (大) force (勢) of people moving together forms a crowd.
Example: お祭りには大勢の人が集まった。(おまつりにはおおぜいのひとがあつまった。)
-Many people gathered for the festival.
}
隠れになった-
{
隠れになった (かくれになった) - became hidden / passed away (if お隠れになった)
A phrase combining 隠れ (hiding) and になった (became). In formal contexts, お隠れになった is an honorific phrase meaning royalty or nobility has passed away (hidden behind the clouds).
Memory Tip: Moving to a place where one is permanently hidden (隠) from the mortal world.
Example: 王は静かにお隠れになった。(おうはしずかにおかくれになった。)
-The king peacefully passed away.
}
すぐさま-
{
すぐさま (すぐさま) - immediately / right away
An adverb emphasizing immediate action. It is a more emphatic version of すぐ (soon/immediately).
Memory Tip: Think of it as doing something "immediately" (すぐ) in that exact "state/manner" (さま).
Example: 彼は手紙を読み、すぐさま家を出た。(かれはてがみをよみ、すぐさまいえをでた。)
-He read the letter and immediately left the house.
}
継がれる-
{
継がれる (つがれる) - to be inherited / to be succeeded
The passive form of the verb 継ぐ (つぐ). The kanji 継 means "inherit," "succeed," or "patch."
Memory Tip: A thread (糸) connecting past generations to the present to inherit (継) a legacy.
Example: その伝統は代々受け継がれる。(そのでんとうはだいだいうけつがれる。)
-That tradition is inherited from generation to generation.
}
ことになる-
{
ことになる (ことになる) - it will be decided that / it turns out that
A grammatical phrase combining こと (thing/matter) and になる (to become). It expresses that a decision, rule, or outcome has been settled, often outside of one's direct control.
Memory Tip: "The matter (こと) has become (になる) a reality."
Example: 来月、東京に転勤することになる。(らいげつ、とうきょうにてんきんすることになる。)
-It has been decided that I will transfer to Tokyo next month.
}
いるような気がした-
{
いるような気がした (いるようなきがした) - felt like (someone/something) was there
A phrase combining いる (to exist/be), ような (like/similar to), and 気がした (had a feeling).
Memory Tip: "My mind/spirit (気) did (した) a thing where it felt like (ような) someone was there (いる)."
Example: 後ろに誰かいるような気がした。(うしろにだれかいるようなきがした。)
-I felt like someone was behind me.
}
顎髭-
{
顎髭 (あごひげ) - beard (on the chin) / goatee
A compound noun combining 顎 (chin/jaw) and 髭 (facial hair/beard).
Memory Tip: Hair (髭) that specifically grows on the jaw/chin (顎).
Example: 彼は立派な顎髭を生やしている。(かれはりっぱなあごひげをはやしている。)
-He is growing a fine beard.
}
編み込み-
{
編み込み (あみこみ) - braiding / hair braid
A noun derived from the verb 編み込む (to braid into). It combines 編 (knit/braid) and 込 (include/put in).
Memory Tip: Taking strands of hair and knitting (編) them together into (込) a unified style.
Example: 彼女の髪は綺麗な編み込みだった。(かのじょのかみはきれいなあみこみだった。)
-Her hair was in a beautiful braid.
}
衣-
{
衣 (ころも) - robe / clothing / coating (e.g., batter on fried food)
A noun representing traditional garments, robes, or an outer layer.
Memory Tip: The kanji 衣 visually resembles the folds and collar of a traditional robe.
Example: 僧侶は白い衣を身にまとっていた。(そうりょはしろいころもをみにまとっていた。)
-The monk was clad in a white robe.
}
召しになっていた-
{
召しになっていた (めしになっていた) - was wearing / was eating (honorific)
The past continuous, honorific form (尊敬語) of the verb 着る (to wear) or 食べる (to eat), using お召しになる.
Memory Tip: A high-status person summons (召) an item of clothing to wear or food to consume.
Example: 王妃は美しいドレスをお召しになっていた。(おうひはうつくしいどれすをおめしになっていた。)
-The queen was wearing a beautiful dress.
}
宴-
{
宴 (うたげ) - banquet / feast / party
A formal or literary noun for a festive gathering with food and drink.
Memory Tip: People gathering under a roof (宀) on a relaxing day (日) to have a feast.
Example: 城で盛大な宴が開かれた。(しろでせいだいなうたげがひらかれた。)
-A grand banquet was held at the castle.
}
朗らか-
{
朗らか (ほがらか) - cheerful / bright / clear
An adjectival noun (na-adjective) describing a bright, cheerful personality or clear weather.
Memory Tip: Good (良) weather under the moon (月) makes everyone feel clear and cheerful (朗).
Example: 彼女はいつも朗らかに笑っている。(かのじょはいつもほがらかにわらっている。)
-She is always smiling cheerfully.
}
状-
{
状 (じょう) - letter / condition / shape
A noun/suffix indicating a state of affairs, a shape, or a written document (like an invitation).
Memory Tip: Think of a dog (犬) sitting by a wooden board (爿) waiting for a "letter" or looking at a specific "shape".
Example: 彼から招待状が届いた。(かれからしょうたいじょうがとどいた。)
-An invitation letter arrived from him.
}
王妃-
{
王妃 (おうひ) - queen (consort)
A noun combining 王 (king) and 妃 (queen/princess/wife of a ruler). It refers to the wife of a king.
Memory Tip: The woman (女) who rules alongside the king (王).
Example: 王と王妃はバルコニーに現れた。(おうとおうひはばるこにーにあらわれた。)
-The king and queen appeared on the balcony.

数日前-
{
数日前 (すうじつまえ) - a few days ago
A temporal noun combining 数 (number/several), 日 (day), and 前 (before/ago).
Memory Tip: "Several" (数) "days" (日) "before" (前) today.
Example: 数日前に彼に会いました。(すうじつまえにかれにあいました。)
-I met him a few days ago.

幼い-
{
幼い (おさない) - young / childish / immature
An i-adjective describing someone of a very young age or exhibiting childish behavior.
Memory Tip: The kanji contains the radical for "small/little" (幺) and "strength" (力), indicating a young person with little strength.

身分-
{
身分 (みぶん) - social status / position
A noun combining 身 (body/oneself) and 分 (part/portion). It refers to one's standing or rank in society.
Memory Tip: The "portion" (分) of society that your "body/self" (身) occupies.

天と地-
{
天と地 (てんとち) - heaven and earth
A phrase combining 天 (heaven/sky), と (and), and 地 (earth/ground). Often used metaphorically to describe a massive difference (like "night and day").
Memory Tip: The literal top of the world (天) versus the literal bottom (地).
Example: 彼らの実力は天と地ほど違う。(かれらのじつりょくはてんとちほどちがう。)

隔たり-
{
隔たり (へだたり) - distance / gap / estrangement
A noun derived from the verb 隔たる (to be distant/separated). It denotes physical distance or a metaphorical gap in status, feelings, or opinions.
Memory Tip: A physical wall or hill (阝) separating (隔) two things.
Example: 二人の間には大きな隔たりがある。(ふたりのあいだにはおおきなへだたりがある。)
-There is a wide gap between the two of them.

家臣-
{
家臣 (かしん) - retainer / vassal
A noun combining 家 (house/family) and 臣 (retainer/subject). It refers to a servant who serves a noble household or lord.

相手-
{
相手 (あいて) - opponent / partner / the other party
A noun combining 相 (mutual/together) and 手 (hand/person). It refers to the person you are interacting with, whether fighting, talking, or marrying.

枝垂れた-
{
枝垂れた (しだれた) - drooped / wept (as in a weeping willow)
Note: Corrected from the fragment "枝れたレた". The past tense of 枝垂れる (to droop/hang down), combining 枝 (branch) and 垂 (hang/suspend).
Memory Tip: A branch (枝) that loses its upward strength and hangs down (垂).
Example: 枝垂れた桜が美しく咲いている。(しだれたさくらがうつくしくさいている。)
-The weeping cherry blossoms are blooming beautifully.

わからない-
{
わからない (わからない) - do not understand / do not know
Note: Corrected from the fragment "からない". The negative form of the verb 分かる (to understand).
Memory Tip: When things are not divided/sorted (分) in your brain, you do not understand them.
Example: 彼の言っている意味がわからない。(かれのいっているいみがわからない。)
-I don't understand the meaning of what he is saying.
}
ねだり-
{
ねだり (ねだり) - begging / pleading
A noun derived from the verb ねだる (to beg/plead for something). Often seen in compounds like おねだり (coaxing/begging).
Memory Tip: Think of someone continuously "needling" (ねだり) you until you buy them what they want.
Example: 子供がおもちゃをねだり始めた。(こどもがおもちゃをねだりはじめた。)
-The child started begging for a toy.
}
他にも-
{
他にも (ほかにも) - besides / in addition to / elsewhere
A phrase combining 他 (other), に (particle), and も (also/too).
Memory Tip: "Also" (も) existing in "other" (他) places.
Example: 他にも質問はありますか？ (ほかにもしつもんはありますか？)
-Do you have any other questions?
}
住んでいた-
{
住んでいた (すんでいた) - was living / used to live
The past continuous form of the verb 住む (to live/reside), combining the te-form (住んで) and いた (was).
Memory Tip: The kanji shows a person (亻) acting as the master (主) of a house, meaning they live there.
Example: 私は以前、京都に住んでいた。(わたしはいぜん、きょうとにすんでいた。)
-I used to live in Kyoto.

掟により-
{
掟により (おきてにより) - according to the rules / by the law
Note: Corrected from the fragment "掟によ". A phrase combining 掟 (rule/law) and により (by means of / according to).
Memory Tip: A rule (掟) handed down that must be strictly followed.
Example: 村の掟により、部外者は入れない。(むらのおきてにより、ぶがいしゃはいれない。)

許されない-
{
許されない (ゆるされない) - not permitted / unforgivable
The negative potential or passive form of the verb 許す (to forgive/permit).
Memory Tip: Words (言) spoken to grant approval (許), negated by ない.
Example: そのような行為は決して許されない。(そのようなこういはけっしてゆるされない。)
-Such behavior is absolutely not permitted.
}
さえなかった-
{
さえなかった (さえなかった) - was not clear / was dull / didn't even [verb]
The past negative of 冴える (to be clear/bright) OR the particle さえ (even) combined with なかった (was not). Depends heavily on context.
Memory Tip: Without a clear, bright (冴) outcome, the situation was dull.
Example: 彼の表情は少しもさえなかった。(かれのひょうじょうはすこしもさえなかった。)
-His expression was not bright/cheerful in the slightest.
}
武器-
{
武器 (ぶき) - weapon / arms
A noun combining 武 (military/martial) and 器 (instrument/tool).
Memory Tip: An instrument (器) used for military (武) purposes is a weapon.
Example: 彼は強力な武器を手に入れた。(かれはきょうりょくなぶきをてにいれた。)
-He acquired a powerful weapon.
}
戦-
{
戦 (いくさ) - war / battle
A noun referring to a battle, war, or military campaign. Also read as "たたかい".
Memory Tip: A conflict involving weapons and strategy to achieve victory.
Example: 長い戦がついに終わった。(ながいいくさがついにおわった。)
-The long war finally ended.
}
欲しい-
{
欲しい (ほしい) - want / desire
An i-adjective used to express the desire for a noun.
Memory Tip: When you lack (欠) something, your desire for it breathes heavily out of your mouth (谷).
Example: 私は新しい車が欲しい。(わたしはあたらしいくるまがほしい。)
-I want a new car.
}
揺らす-
{
揺らす (ゆらす) - to shake / to rock / to sway (transitive)
A transitive verb written with the kanji 揺 (shake/sway). It means to physically cause something else to shake.
Memory Tip: Using your hand (扌) to move something back and forth.
Example: 風が木々の枝を揺らす。(かぜがきぎのえだをゆらす。)
-The wind shakes the branches of the trees.
}
煽られる-
{
煽られる (あおられる) - to be fueled / to be fanned / to be swayed
The passive form of the verb 煽る (to fan / to stir up / to instigate).
Memory Tip: The fire (火) is being fanned by a door (扇) opening and closing to stir it up.
Example: 強い風に煽られて火が燃え広がった。(つよいかぜにあおられてひがもえひろがった。)
-Fanned by the strong wind, the fire spread.
}
すれば-
{
すれば (すれば) - if you do / in that case
The conditional (ba-form) of the verb する (to do).
Memory Tip: "If (ば) you do (する) this..."
Example: そうすれば問題は解決する。(そうすればもんだいはかいけつする。)
-If you do that, the problem will be solved.
}
辺り-
{
辺り (あたり) - vicinity / surroundings / nearby
A noun indicating the area around a certain place or person.
Memory Tip: The path (辶) going around the boundary/edge of an area.
Example: この辺りにコンビニはありますか？(このあたりにこんびにはありますか？)
-Is there a convenience store around here?
}
でかい-
{
でかい (でかい) - huge / big
A colloquial i-adjective meaning very large. It is a more casual/slang version of 大きい (おおきい).
Memory Tip: Imagine saying "BIG" but with a heavy, emphatic "DE-kai" sound for exaggeration.
Example: 彼の家はとにかくでかい。(かれのいえはとにかくでかい。)
-His house is just huge.
}
石畳-
{
石畳 (いしだたみ) - stone paving / cobblestone
A noun combining 石 (stone) and 畳 (tatami/folding/paving). It refers to streets paved with flat stones.
Memory Tip: Stones (石) laid out flat on the ground like tatami mats (畳).
Example: ヨーロッパの古い石畳の道を歩く。(よーろっぱのふるいいしだたみのみちをあるく。)
-Walking along an old cobblestone street in Europe.
}
容赦なく-
{
容赦なく (ようしゃなく) - mercilessly / without hesitation / ruthlessly
An adverbial phrase combining 容赦 (pardon/mercy) and なく (without).
Memory Tip: Leaving no room for pardon or mercy when taking action.
Example: 敵は容赦なく攻撃してきた。(てきはようしゃなくこうげきしてきた。)
-The enemy attacked mercilessly.
}
香辛料-
{
香辛料 (こうしんりょう) - spices / condiments
A compound noun combining 香 (fragrance/incense), 辛 (spicy/hot), and 料 (ingredients/materials).
Memory Tip: Ingredients (料) that add fragrance (香) and spice (辛) to your food.
Example: カレーにはたくさんの香辛料が使われている。(かれーにはたくさんのこうしんりょうがつかわれている。)
-Many spices are used in curry.
}
人懐っこい-
{
人懐っこい (ひとなつっこい) - friendly / amiable / sociable
Note: Corrected from the fragment "人懐". An adjective describing someone (or an animal) that easily becomes attached to people. Combines 人 (person) and 懐く (to become emotionally attached).
Memory Tip: A person or pet whose feelings (忄) easily attach to the bosom/pocket (懐) of a person (人).
Example: その犬はとても人懐っこい。(そのいぬはとてもひとなつっこい。)
-That dog is very friendly.
}
敗北-
{
敗北 (はいぼく) - defeat
A noun combining 敗 (defeat/fail) and 北 (north / flee). In ancient Chinese battles, turning one's back to flee was associated with the character for north.
Memory Tip: Fleeing (北) after experiencing failure/defeat (敗).
Example: チームは決勝戦で敗北を喫した。(ちーむはけっしょうせんではいぼくをきっした。)
-The team suffered a defeat in the final match.
}
恐る-
{
恐る (おそる) - to fear / to be afraid of
A verb (often seen as 恐れる) combining the kanji 恐 (fear/dread).
Memory Tip: A work (工) of a mediocre (凡) heart (心) produces fear (恐).
Example: 失敗を恐るな。(しっぱいをおそるな。)
-Do not fear failure.
}
ひまわり-
{
ひまわり (ひまわり) - sunflower
A noun usually written in hiragana or katakana (ヒマワリ), but legally/kanji as 向日葵. It refers to the flower that faces the sun.
Memory Tip: A flower that turns to go around (まわり) following the sun (ひ).
Example: 夏になると、ひまわりが咲く。(なつになると、ひまわりがさく。)
-When summer comes, sunflowers bloom.
}
付き合って-
{
付き合って (つきあって) - accompany me / date / keep company
The te-form of the verb 付き合う (to associate with / to keep company / to date). Combines 付 (attach) and 合う (fit/together).
Memory Tip: Attaching (付) yourself together (合) with someone to spend time with them.
Example: 買い出しに付き合ってくれる？ (かいだしにつきあってくれる？)
-Will you keep me company for shopping?
}

味噌汁-
{
味噌汁 (みそしる) - Miso soup
A compound noun formed by 味噌 (miso paste) and 汁 (soup/broth/juice). It is a staple side dish in traditional Japanese meals.
Memory Tip: Think of it as the "juice" (汁) made from fermented "miso" (味噌).
Example: 朝食に温かい味噌汁を飲む。 (ちょうしょくにあたたかいみそしるをのむ。)
-I drink warm miso soup for breakfast.
}

旅行者-
{
旅行者 (りょこうしゃ) - traveler / tourist
A noun combining 旅行 (travel) and the suffix 者 (person) to denote a person who is traveling.
Memory Tip: A person (者) who goes on a journey (旅) while moving/going (行).
Example: 多くの旅行者が京都を訪れる。 (おおくのりょこうしゃがきょうとをおとずれる)
-Many travelers visit Kyoto.
}

柔道-
{
柔道 (じゅうどう) - Judo
This noun combines 柔 (soft/gentle) and 道 (way/path), representing the martial art focused on yielding to force.
Memory Tip: Think of the "gentle way" where you use an opponent's strength against them.
Example: 彼は柔道を習っています。(かれはじゅうどうをならっています。)
-He is learning judo.
}

体育-
{
体育 (たいいく) - Physical Education
This noun combines the characters for 'body' and 'nurture', referring to physical training or PE classes.
Memory Tip: Focus on nurturing (育) the body (体) through exercise.
Example: 体育の授業は楽しいです (たいいくのじゅぎょうはたのしいです)
-Physical education class is fun.
}

刺身-
{
刺身 (さしみ) - sashimi / sliced raw fish
A traditional Japanese dish of thinly sliced raw seafood or meat.
Memory Tip: 刺 (pierce/stab) + 身 (body). To prepare it, the chef must slice through the body of the fish.
Example: 刺身の盛り合わせを注文した。 (さしみのもりあわせをちゅうもんした。)
-I ordered a sashimi platter.
}

自己紹介-
{
自己紹介 (じこしょうかい) - Self-introduction
A compound word made of 'self' (自己) and 'introduction' (紹介).
Memory Tip: When you 'introduce' (紹介) your own 'self' (自己) to someone new.
Example: クラスで自己紹介をした。 (くらすでじこしょうかいをした。)
-I introduced myself in class.
}

水道-
{
水道 (すいどう) - Water supply, tap water
Literally translated as 'water road,' referring to the infrastructure for water.
Memory Tip: The 'road' or 'way' (道) that 'water' (水) travels through to reach your home.
Example: 水道代が高い。 (すいどうだいがたかい。)
-The water bill is expensive.
}

温める-
{
温める (あたためる) - To warm up (something)
This transitive Ichidan verb is used for heating up physical objects like food or keeping an abstract idea in development.
Memory Tip: Think of 'Atami' (hot spring town) and 'tame' (for the sake of). You warm it for your sake.
Example: スープを温める。 (すーぷをあたためる。)
-Warm up the soup.
}

駅員-
{
駅員 (えきいん) - Station staff/attendant
A straightforward compound of 駅 (station) and 員 (member/employee).
Memory Tip: A 'Member' (in) of the 'Station' (eki) team.
Example: 駅員に道を尋ねました。 (えきいんにみちをたずねました。)
-I asked the station attendant for directions.
}

無料-
{
無料 (むりょう) - Free of charge
A common compound of 無 (none/nothing) and 料 (fee/cost).
Memory Tip: 'Mu' means nothing and 'Ryou' means fee. No fee = Free!
Example: 入場は無料です。 (にゅうじょうはむりょうです。)
-Entrance is free.
}

料理人-
{
料理人 (りょうりにん) - Chef; Cook
Combines 料理 (cooking/cuisine) with the suffix 人 (person) to indicate a professional role.
Memory Tip: A 'person' (人) who makes a career out of 'cooking' (料理).
Example: 彼は有名なフランス料理の料理人です。 (かれはゆうめいなふらんすりょうりのりょうりにんです。)
-He is a famous French cuisine chef.
}

水色-
{
水色 (みずいろ) - light blue; pale blue
Literally 'water color,' it refers to a bright, pale blue similar to a clear sky or shallow water.
Memory Tip: 水 (water) + 色 (color). Think of the clear, light blue color of clean water in a pool.
Example: 彼は水色のシャツを着ている。(かれはみずいろのしゃつをきている。)
-He is wearing a light blue shirt.
}

仮名-
{
仮名 (かな) - kana (Japanese script) / pseudonym
While it usually refers to hiragana and katakana, it literally means a 'provisional name' (borrowed characters used for sound).
Memory Tip: Using a temporary/provisional (仮) name (名) to represent phonetics.
Example: 外国語の名前は仮名で表記される。 (がいこくごのなまえはかなでひょうきされる。)
-Foreign names are written in kana.
}

郵便-
{
郵便 (ゆうびん) - Mail/Post
This noun combines 郵 (post station) and 便 (service/convenience). It refers to the physical mail system and its operations.
Memory Tip: Think of a post station (郵) providing a convenient (便) way to send letters.
Example: 郵便を出す。 (ゆうびんをだす。)
-Send the mail.
}

昔話-
{
昔話 (むかしばなし) - folklore / fairy tale
This word combines 昔 (old times) and 話 (story) to describe traditional oral legends.
Memory Tip: Stories (話) told from the long-ago (昔) past.
Example: 祖母は毎晩昔話を語ってくれた。 (そぼはまいばんむかしばなしをかたってくれた。)
-My grandmother told me folk tales every night.
}

中華-
{
中華 (ちゅうか) - Chinese (style) / China
Literally "Middle Splendor," it is most commonly used in Japan to refer to Chinese cuisine.
Memory Tip: The land in the center (中) of the world with flowery splendor (華).
Example: 今夜は中華を食べに行こう。 (こんやはちゅうかをたべにいこう。)
-Let's go out for Chinese food tonight.
}

毎回-
{
毎回 (まいかい) - Every time
A common adverbial noun used to describe an action that occurs at every instance or turn.
Memory Tip: 毎 (every) plus 回 (times/occurrences). Think of every rotation of a wheel.
Example: 彼は毎回遅刻してくる。 (かれはまいかいちこくしてくる。)
-He comes late every single time.
}

新年-
{
新年 (しんねん) - New Year
A formal compound of 新 (new) and 年 (year), often used in greetings and official contexts.
Memory Tip: 'Shin' (New) like a shiny new object + 'Nen' (Year). The start of a shiny new year.
Example: 新年あけましておめでとう。 (しんねんあけましておめでとう。)
-Happy New Year.
}

花見-
{
花見 (はなみ) - cherry blossom viewing
A compound noun formed from 'flower' (花) and the stem of 'to see' (見). It specifically refers to the Japanese custom of enjoying the blooming sakura.
Memory Tip: Simply 'flower' plus 'see'—looking at flowers.
Example: 公園でお花見をしましょう。(こうえんでおはなみをしましょう。)
-Let's go cherry blossom viewing at the park.
}

バス停-
{
バス停 (ばすてい) - bus stop
A compound of the loanword "basu" (bus) and the kanji for "halt/stop" (停).
Memory Tip: Combining "Bus" with "Tei" from "Teisha" (stopping a vehicle). It is the official place where buses stop.
Example: 次のバス停で降ります。 (つぎのばすていでおります。)
-I will get off at the next bus stop.
}

魚屋-
{
魚屋 (さかなや) - Fish shop, fishmonger
A compound noun combining the word for fish and the suffix for a shop or professional.
Memory Tip: Take "Sakana" (fish) and add "Ya" (the standard suffix for a merchant or store).
Example: 近所の魚屋で新鮮な鯛を買った。 (きんじょのさかなやでしんせんなたいをかった。)
-I bought a fresh sea bream at the local fishmonger.
}

作り方-
{
作り方 (つくりかた) - How to make, way of making
Formed by the stem of the verb 作る (to make) plus the suffix 方 (way/method).
Memory Tip: Tsukuri (make) + Kata (method) = The method of making something.
Example: この料理の作り方を教えてください。 (このりょうりのつくりかたをおしえてください。)
-Please teach me how to make this dish.
}

南米-
{
南米 (なんべい) - South America
Abbreviation of 南 (south) and 米国 (America), specifically the continent.
Memory Tip: Look for South (南) on the map of the Americas (米).
Example: 彼は南米を一人で旅した。(かれはなんべいをひとりでたびした。)
-He traveled through South America alone.
}

水泳-
{
水泳 (すいえい) - Swimming
A formal noun for the sport or act of swimming, often used in educational or competitive contexts.
Memory Tip: Combines 水 (water) and 泳 (swim). It's the literal activity of swimming through water.
Example: 私は水泳が得意です。 (わたしはすいえいがとくいです。)
-I am good at swimming.
}

辞典-
{
辞典 (じてん) - Dictionary
Specifically a dictionary for words and phrases (辞), as opposed to 'jiten' (字典) which is for individual characters.
Memory Tip: 'Ji' (words/expressions) + 'Ten' (standard/canon) = the standard book for words.
Example: 電子辞典で調べる。 (でんしじてんでしらべる。)
-Look it up in an electronic dictionary.
}

作文-
{
作文 (さくぶん) - Essay/composition
A noun that refers to the act of writing or the piece of writing itself, often used for school assignments.
Memory Tip: To make or create (作) a series of sentences/text (文).
Example: 学校で作文を書いた。 (がっこうでさくぶんをかいた。)
-I wrote an essay at school.
}

薬局-
{
薬局 (やっきょく) - Pharmacy
Formed by 'medicine' (薬) and 'bureau/office' (局), it refers to a place where medicine is dispensed or sold.
Memory Tip: The official office (局) where you go to get your medicine (薬).
Example: 薬局で風邪薬を買った。 (やっきょくでかぜぐすりをかった。)
-I bought cold medicine at the pharmacy.

手作り-
{
手作り (てづくり) - Handmade
A simple combination of 手 (hand) and 作り (making/creation).

-This cake is my mother's handmade creation.

四角-
{
四角 (しかく) - Square / Rectangle
Composed of 四 (four) and 角 (angles/corners).

仲良し-
{
仲良し (なかよし) - Close friend, being on good terms
Formed from 仲 (relationship) and 良し (good). It is often used to describe friends, siblings, or couples with a harmonious bond.

忘れ物-

忘れ物 (わすれもの) - Forgotten item / Something left behind
A common noun used for lost property or things one forgets to bring or take away.

次回-
{
次回 (じかい) - Next time

千円札-

千円札 (せんえんさつ) - 1,000 yen bill

留学生-

留学生 (りゅうがくせい) - International student

電池 (でんち) - Battery

運動会 (うんどうかい) - Sports day / Athletic meet

冷房 (れいぼう) - Air conditioning (cooling)

定食-

閉店-
{
閉店 (へいてん) - Shop closing
A noun or suru-verb consisting of 閉 (close) and 店 (shop). It can refer to the daily closing or a business going out of business.

歯医者-
{
歯医者 (はいしゃ) - Dentist
This word combines the kanji for 'tooth' (歯) and 'doctor' (医者). It is the most common term for a dentist in Japan.
Memory Tip: Focus on the 'ha' (tooth) radical; a 'ha' doctor is a dentist.

お待たせしました-
{
お待たせしました (おまたせしました) - Sorry to have kept you waiting
A polite set phrase using the causative form of 'matsu' (to wait). It literally translates to 'I have caused you to wait'.
Memory Tip: 'O' (polite) + 'matase' (made to wait) + 'shimashita' (did).
Example: 大変お待たせしました。(たいへんおまたせしました)
- Thank you very much for waiting.
}

焼肉-
{
焼肉 (やきにく) - grilled meat, BBQ
A noun combining the kanji for grill/burn and meat; refers to the style of cooking meat over a flame.
Memory Tip: Kanji breakdown: Grill (焼) + Meat (肉). It's the ultimate 'burned meat' feast.
Example: 今日の夕食は焼肉です。(きょうのゆうしょくはやきにくです。)
-Tonight's dinner is grilled meat.
}

寝坊-
{
寝坊 (ねぼう) - Oversleeping, late riser
A noun referring to the act of sleeping late or a person who has the habit of doing so.
Memory Tip: A sleepy (寝) boy (坊) who refuses to get out of bed.
Example: 彼は寝坊で遅刻した。 (かれはねぼうでちこくした。)
-He was late because of oversleeping.
}

寝坊する-
{
寝坊する (ねぼうする) - To oversleep
The verb form of the noun 'nebō', used when someone accidentally sleeps past their intended time.
Memory Tip: Just add 'do' (する) to the 'sleepy boy' (寝坊) to describe the action of oversleeping.
Example: 今朝は寝坊した。 (けさはねぼうした。)
-I overslept this morning.
}

靴屋-
{
靴屋 (くつや) - Shoe store
This noun combines 靴 (shoe) and the suffix 屋 (shop/specialist) to indicate a retail store or a cobbler.
Memory Tip: Think of a shop (屋) where you find rows of leather footwear (靴).
Example: 新しい靴を靴屋で買いました。 (あたらしいくつをくつやでかいました。)
-I bought new shoes at the shoe store.
}

蝶々-
{
蝶々 (ちょうちょう) - Butterfly
The kanji for butterfly is doubled, which is common in speech and evocative of flapping wings.
Memory Tip: The repetition in 'ちょうちょう' sounds like the repetitive motion of a butterfly's wings.
Example: 庭に蝶々が飛んでいる。 (にわにちょうちょうがとんでいる。)

冬休み (ふゆやすみ) - Winter vacation

梅干し (うめぼし) - Pickled plum / Dried plum

ご苦労様-
{
ご苦労様 (ごくろうさま) - Good job / Thank you for your effort
A set phrase used by a person of higher status to thank someone of lower status.

{
易しい (やさしい) - Easy / Simple
