Memory Tip: Literally a "nail cutter." 爪 (fingernail) + 切り (cutting tool).
Example: 爪切りを貸してください。 (つめきりをかしてください。)
-Please lend me the nail clippers.
}

照り焼き-
{
照り焼き (てりやき) - Teriyaki
A cooking technique where food is basted with a sweet soy glaze while being grilled.
Memory Tip: Food that is grilled or baked (焼き) until it has a shiny glaze or luster (照り).
Example: 晩御飯に照り焼きチキンを作った。 (ばんごはんにおいてりやきちきんをつくった。)
-I made teriyaki chicken for dinner.
}

親子丼-
{
親子丼 (おやこどん) - Chicken and egg bowl
Literally "parent and child bowl," referring to the chicken (parent) and egg (child) cooked together over rice.
Memory Tip: It is a dark joke in a bowl; the 'parent' (親) chicken and 'child' (子) egg served in a 'bowl' (丼).
Example: お昼ご飯に親子丼を注文した。 (おひるごはんにおやこどんをちゅうもんした。)
-I ordered a chicken and egg bowl for lunch.
}

再来年-
{
再来年 (さらいねん) - The year after next
A common time-related word for two years into the future. It literally means 'again' (再) + 'come' (来) + 'year' (年).
Memory Tip: After next year comes, the cycle happens again (再) to reach the year after next.
Example: 再来年、日本に行きます。 (さらいねん、にほんにいきます。)
-I will go to Japan the year after next.
}

烏龍茶-
{
烏龍茶 (うーろんちゃ) - Oolong tea
This word is a phonetic transliteration from Chinese, using ateji characters to represent the specific variety of tea.
Memory Tip: Dark like a Crow (烏) and twisted like a Dragon (龍) tea (茶).
Example: 食事と一緒に烏龍茶を注文した。(しょくじといっしょにうーろんちゃをちゅうもんした。)
-I ordered oolong tea to go with my meal.
}

切符売り場-
{
切符売り場 (きっぷうりば) - Ticket office / Ticket counter
A compound noun consisting of 切符 (ticket), 売り (selling), and 場 (place).
Memory Tip: A literal "place" (場) for the "selling" (売り) of "tickets" (切符).
Example: 駅の切符売り場はどこですか？ (えきのきっぷうりばはどこですか？)
-Where is the station ticket counter?
}

郵便箱-
{
郵便箱 (ゆうびんばこ) - Mailbox
A compound of 郵便 (mail) and 箱 (box), referring to the container where mail is placed.
Memory Tip: The postal service (郵便) delivers items into this specific box (箱).
Example: 郵便箱に手紙が届いている。 (ゆうびんばこにてがみがとどいている。)
-There is a letter in the mailbox.
}

沖縄県-
{
沖縄県 (おきなわけん) - Okinawa Prefecture
The southernmost prefecture of Japan, consisting of hundreds of the Ryukyu Islands.
Memory Tip: 沖 (offshore) + 縄 (rope) = a "rope" of islands out in the "offshore" ocean.
Example: 沖縄県は観光地として人気がある。(おきなわけんはかんこうちとしてにんきがある。)
-Okinawa Prefecture is popular as a tourist destination.
}

御手洗-
{
御手洗 (おてあらい) - Restroom/Washroom
A polite euphemism used in daily life, combining the honorific prefix 'O' with 'hand wash'.
Memory Tip: Think of the kanji for Hand (手) and Wash (洗) - the place where you honorably wash your hands.
Example: 御手洗を借りてもいいですか？ (おてあらいをかりてもいいですか？)
-May I use the restroom?
}

営業中-
{
営業中 (えいぎょうちゅう) - open for business
Commonly seen on signs to indicate that a shop or restaurant is currently operating.
Memory Tip: Business operations (営業) in the middle (中) of happening.
Example: その店はまだ営業中だ。 (そのみせはまだえいぎょうちゅうだ。)
-That shop is still open for business.
}

着替え-
{
着替え (きがえ) - Change of clothes
Derived from the verbs 着る (to wear) and 替える (to exchange/replace). It can refer to the act of changing or the spare clothes themselves.
Memory Tip: Wear (着) one set, then exchange (替) it for another to change your clothes.
Example: 運動の後に着替えをします。(うんどうのあとにきがえをします。)
-I change my clothes after exercising.
}

ご飯粒-
{
ご飯粒 (ごはんつぶ) - Grain of rice
Combines ご飯 (cooked rice) and 粒 (grain/drop). It specifically refers to an individual grain of cooked rice.
Memory Tip: A single tiny grain (粒) of delicious cooked rice (ご飯) that often sticks to a bowl.
Example: 頬にご飯粒がついているよ。 (ほほにごはんつぶがついているよ。)
-There is a grain of rice on your cheek.
}

痛み-
{
痛み (いたみ) - Pain
The noun form of the i-adjective 'itai' (painful). The 'mi' suffix transforms the state into a concrete noun.
Memory Tip: 'Itai' means 'ouch!', and adding 'mi' makes it 'the pain' itself.
Example: 薬で痛みを和らげる。(くすりでいたみをやわらげる。)
-Ease the pain with medicine.
}

再来月-
{
再来月 (さらいげつ) - The month after next
Formed by adding 再 (again/re-) to 来月 (next month), indicating the month following the upcoming one.
Memory Tip: It is the month that comes 'again' (再) after the 'next' (来) 'month' (月).
Example: 再来月の末に旅行に行きます。 (さらいげつのすえにりょこうにいきます。)
-I am going on a trip at the end of the month after next.
}

春巻き-
{
春巻き (はるまき) - Spring roll
A literal translation of the Chinese dish name, combining 春 (spring) and 巻き (roll).
Memory Tip: A "spring"-time treat that is "rolled" up and fried.
Example: 夕食に春巻きを作った (ゆうしょくにはるまきをつくった)
-I made spring rolls for dinner.
}

目医者-
{
目医者 (めいしゃ) - Eye doctor / Ophthalmologist
A colloquial and common way to refer to an eye doctor. While 'gankai' (眼科医) is the clinical term, 'meisha' is frequently used in daily conversation.
Memory Tip: Simply an 'eye' (目) 'doctor' (医者).
Example: 目が赤いので、目医者に行った。 (めがあかいので、めいしゃにいった。)
-My eyes were red, so I went to the eye doctor.
}

叫び-
{
叫び (さけび) - Shout, cry, or scream
This is the nominalized (noun) form of the verb "sakebu" (to shout).
Memory Tip: The mouth radical (口) in the kanji indicates a loud sound coming from the mouth.
Example: 彼は恐怖で叫び声を上げた。 (かれはきょうふでさけびごえをあげた。)
-He let out a scream of terror.
}

うなぎ丼-
{
うなぎ丼 (うなぎどん) - Eel bowl
A compound noun consisting of うなぎ (eel) and 丼 (bowl of rice with toppings). It is a popular Japanese summer dish.
Memory Tip: Imagine an eel (unagi) diving into a giant bowl (don) of rice.
Example: お昼ご飯にうなぎ丼を食べる。 (おひるごはんにはうなぎどんをたべる。)
-I eat an eel bowl for lunch.
}

残り-
{
残り (のこり) - Remainder; leftover; balance
The noun form of the verb 残る (to remain). It refers to whatever is left over after a part has been used or removed.
Memory Tip: The kanji 残 shows bones (歹) and a spear (戈) - what is left after a battle.
Example: 残りのケーキを食べる。 (のこりのけーきをたべる。)
-Eat the remaining cake.
}

笑い-
{
笑い (わらい) - Laughter; smile
The noun form of the verb 笑う (to laugh/smile). It can refer to the sound of laughter or the act of smiling.
Memory Tip: The top of the kanji 笑 represents bamboo (竹) swaying like it's laughing in the wind.
Example: 彼の話で笑いが起きた。 (かれのはなしでわらいがおきた。)
-His story caused laughter.
}

動き-
{
動き (うごき) - movement/motion/trend
The noun form of the verb 動く, used for physical motion or abstract changes in market trends.
Memory Tip: A 'heavy' (重) thing moved by 'power' (力) creates action or movement.
Example: 素早い動きを見せる。 (すばやいうごきをみせる。)
-Show a quick movement.
}

怒り-
{
怒り (いかり) - Anger
The noun form of the verb 怒る (okoru), describing a state of rage or resentment.
Memory Tip: The kanji has 'heart' (心) at the bottom; imagine your heart is enslaved (奴) to a hot temper.
Example: 彼は激しい怒りを感じた。 (かれははげらしいいかりをかんじた。)
-He felt a fierce anger.
}

匂い-
{
匂い (におい) - Smell/Scent
Refers generally to a neutral or pleasant scent, as opposed to 臭い (kusai) which implies a bad odor.
Memory Tip: Think of a "new" (ni) "oil" (oi) that has a very distinct, fresh scent.
Example: バラのいい匂いがする。 (ばらのいいにおいがする。)
-It smells like roses.
}

握り-
{
握り (にぎり) - Grip/Grasp/Handful
The noun form of 握る (nigiru), often used to describe the handle of a tool or hand-pressed sushi.
Memory Tip: The 'hand' radical (扌) on the left shows you are using your hand to squeeze or hold something tightly.
Example: 彼はナイフの握りを確かめた。 (かれはないふのにぎりをたしかめた。)
-He checked the grip of the knife.
}

驚き-
{
驚き (おどろき) - Surprise / astonishment
The noun form of the verb 驚く (to be surprised). It expresses the state of being startled or amazed.
Memory Tip: Odoroki sounds like "Oh! Door! Key!"; finding a surprise key in your door causes astonishment.
Example: その知らせは大きな驚きだった。(そのしらせはおおきなおどろきだった。)
-That news was a big surprise.
}

間違い-
{
間違い (まちがい) - mistake / error
The noun form of the verb 間違う (machigau). It is used for both simple errors and more serious misunderstandings.
Memory Tip: Think of crossing paths (the 'X' nuance of chigau) in the 'interval' (間) of a task.
Example: その答えは間違いです。 (そのこたえはまちがいです。)
-That answer is a mistake.
}

乗り換え-
{
乗り換え (のりかえ) - transfer / changing vehicles
A compound noun/verb-base of 乗り (riding) and 換え (exchanging). Used for trains, planes, and buses.
Memory Tip: You are 'exchanging' (換え) the thing you are currently 'riding' (乗り).
Example: 新宿駅で乗り換えが必要だ。 (しんじゅくえきでのりかえがひつようだ。)
-A transfer is necessary at Shinjuku Station.
}

踊り-
{
踊り (おどり) - Dance, dancing
The noun form of the verb 踊る, referring to rhythmic movement, traditional Japanese folk dances, or any performed dance.
Memory Tip: It takes courage (勇) to use your feet (⻊) to perform a dance in front of others.
Example: 彼女は盆踊りが上手だ。 (かのじょはぼんおどりがじょうずだ)
-She is good at the Bon dance.
}

違い-
{
違い (ちがい) - difference, mistake
This is the noun form of the verb 違う (chigau), used to describe a discrepancy, distinction, or error between two or more things.
Memory Tip: Think of the verb 'chigau' (to be different/wrong). The 'i' ending turns the action into a thing—a difference.
Example: 意見に違いがある。 (いけんにちがいがある。)
-There is a difference in opinion.
}

使える-
{
使える (つかえる) - to be useful, to be able to use
The potential form of the verb 使う (tsukau - to use). It indicates either the capability of the user or the utility of an object.
Memory Tip: Take the root 'tsukau' (to use) and change it to the 'e' row to add the meaning of 'can'.
Example: この道具はまだ使える。 (このどうぐはまだつかえる。)
-This tool is still usable.
}

失礼しました-
{
失礼しました (しつれいしました) - I am sorry / Excuse me (past)
The past tense of 'shitsurei suru' (to be rude). Used to apologize after a mistake or when finishing an interaction.
Memory Tip: 'Shitsu' (Lose) + 'Rei' (Etiquette). You literally 'lost your etiquette' in the past and are now acknowledging it.
Example: お待たせして失礼しました。 (おまたせしてしつれいしました。)
-I am sorry for keeping you waiting.
}

凄く-
{
凄く (すごく) - Extremely, very
Adverbial form of the adjective 'sugoi'. It is used to emphasize the intensity of an adjective or verb in a sentence.
Memory Tip: Think of 'sugoi' (amazing); changing the 'i' to 'ku' turns it into an adverb meaning 'amazingly' or 'very'.
Example: 昨日は凄く暑かったです。(きのうはすごくあつかったです)
-It was extremely hot yesterday.
}

田-
{
田 (た) - Rice field
This pictographic kanji represents a field divided into sections and is a primary component of many common Japanese surnames.
Memory Tip: The character is a literal drawing of a bird's-eye view of a grid-like rice paddy.
Example: 田んぼに水があります。 (たんぼにみずがあります。)
-There is water in the rice field.
}

じゃが芋-
{
じゃが芋 (じゃがいも) - Potato
Named after "Jagatara" (Jakarta), the port from which it was introduced to Japan. It refers specifically to the common white/Irish potato.
Memory Tip: Jaga (Jakarta) + Imo (tuber). Imagine a potato wearing a souvenir hat from its trip to Jakarta.
Example: じゃが芋の皮をむいてください。 (じゃがいものかわをむいてください。)
-Please peel the potatoes.
}

お城-
{
お城 (おしろ) - Castle
A noun typically used with the honorific prefix 'o' to refer to traditional Japanese fortifications.
Memory Tip: 'O' (honorific) + 'Shiro' (white)—Japanese castles are famous for their brilliant white plastered walls.
Example: お城を見学する。 (おしろをけんがくする。)
-To tour a castle.
}

不味い-
{
不味い (まずい) - Bad-tasting / Awkward
Combines "not" (不) and "flavor" (味), used for bad food or problematic situations.
Memory Tip: This food has "No" (不) "Taste" (味), it's mazu-i (must be bad).
Example: このスープは不味いです。(このすーぷはまずいです)
-This soup tastes bad.
}

池-
{
池 (いけ) - Pond
A noun representing a small body of water, often artificial.
Memory Tip: The left side is the water radical (氵) and the right side (也) can be seen as a funnel holding water in place.
Example: 池の周りを歩く。 (いけのまわりをあるく。)
-I walk around the pond.
}

巻きずし-
{
巻きずし (まきずし) - Rolled sushi
Formed from the verb 巻く (to roll) and sushi; the 's' becomes 'z' due to rendaku.
Memory Tip: Think of 'maki' as a 'making' a roll of seaweed and rice.
Example: 昼休みに巻きずしを食べた (ひるやすみにまきずしをたべた)
-I ate rolled sushi during my lunch break.
}

名古屋-
{
名古屋 (なごや) - Nagoya
The capital city of Aichi Prefecture, known as a major industrial and transit hub.
Memory Tip: A city with a Famous (名) Old (古) Roof/House (屋).
Example: 来週、名古屋へ行きます。 (らいしゅう、なごやへいきます。)
-I am going to Nagoya next week.
}

又-
{
又 (また) - again, or, also
A conjunction or adverb used to indicate repetition or an alternative choice.
Memory Tip: The kanji looks like a hand reaching out to grab something 'again.'
Example: 又、会いましょう。 (また、あいましょう。)
-Let's meet again.
}

お持ち帰り-
{
お持ち帰り (おもちかえり) - Takeout / To go
A polite construction using 'muchi' (holding/carrying) and 'kaeri' (returning). Literally 'polite carrying-return'.
Memory Tip: You Carry (持ち) the food and Return (帰り) home with it.
Example: お持ち帰りでお願いします。(おもちかえりでおねがいします。)
-To go, please.
}

具合が悪い-
{
具合が悪い (ぐあいがわるい) - Feeling unwell / out of order
A set phrase combining 具合 (condition/state) and 悪い (bad).
Memory Tip: Think of 'Gooy-ai' (guai) - if your condition feels gooey and messy, you are feeling unwell.
Example: 今日は具合が悪いです。 (きょうはぐあいがわるいです。)
-I feel unwell today.
}

混む-
{
混む (こむ) - To be crowded
This verb is typically used to describe places like trains or restaurants being packed with people. It is often used as 混んでいる to describe the current state.
Memory Tip: Think of a "comb" (sounding like 'komu') with many teeth close together, just like a crowd.
Example: 電車がとても混んでいる。(でんしゃがとてもこんでいる)
-The train is very crowded.
}

〜のに-
{
〜のに (のに) - Even though, despite
A conjunctive particle used to express contrast or frustration when a result differs from expectation.
Memory Tip: Think 'No' (the fact) + 'Ni' (at). Looking 'at' the 'fact' that X happened, it is strange Y occurred.
Example: 練習したのに負けました。(れんしゅうしたのにまけました。)
-Despite practicing, I lost.
}

向かい-
{
向かい (むかい) - Opposite / Across from
The noun/adverbial form of 'mukau' (to face), used to describe locations.
Memory Tip: The kanji (向) looks like a window you look through to see who is facing you.
Example: 郵便局は銀行の向かいにあります。 (ゆうびんきょくはぎんこうのむかいにあります。)
-The post office is opposite the bank.
}

棚-
{
棚 (たな) - Shelf
A common noun for furniture used to hold or display items.
Memory Tip: The left side is 'wood' (木) and the right side looks like a frame with items aligned on it.
Example: 棚に本を並べる。 (たなにほんをならべる。)
-I arrange books on the shelf.
}

火事-
{
火事 (かじ) - Fire (accident)
A noun referring to a destructive fire or conflagration, combining "fire" (火) and "thing/incident" (事).
Memory Tip: Think of a fire being a very serious event or "matter" (事) to attend to.
Example: 近所で火事があった。 (きんじょでかじがあった。)
-There was a fire in the neighborhood.
}

持ち帰り-
{
持ち帰り (もちかえり) - Takeout, takeaway
The noun form of the verb 'mochikaeru'. It combines 'motsu' (to hold/carry) and 'kaeru' (to return).
Memory Tip: Mochi (carry) + Kaeri (return) = Carrying food while returning home.
Example: 持ち帰りでお願いします。(もちかえりでおねがいします。)
-Takeout, please.
}

力-
{
力 (ちから) - power, strength, ability
Refers to physical muscle power as well as metaphorical capability or effort.
Memory Tip: This kanji looks like a muscular arm flexing or a hand-drawn plow indicating hard work.
Example: 彼の力はすごい。 (かれのちからはすごい。)
-His strength is amazing.
}

背-
{
背 (せ) - Height / Back
Refers to the physical height of a person or the upper part of the back.
Memory Tip: North (北) people standing back-to-back over a body part (月/肉).
Example: 彼の背は高い。(かれのせはたかい)
-His height is tall.
}

祭り-
{
祭り (まつり) - 
A noun referring to a traditional Japanese festival or celebration.
Memory Tip: A 'mass' of people gathering 'to see' (ri) the decorations at a shrine.
Example: 夏祭りに行きます。(なつまつりにいきます。)
-I will go to a summer festival.
}

若い-
{
若い (わかい) - Young
An i-adjective used to describe someone of low age or youthful appearance.
Memory Tip: The top radical is grass 艹, like a young green sprout coming from the ground.
Example: 彼はまだ若いです。(かれはまだわかいです)
-He is still young.
}

もし-
{
もし (もし) - If / Supposing
A conjunction used at the start of a sentence to signal a conditional 'if' scenario.
Memory Tip: It sounds like 'Moshi moshi' on the phone, where you check 'if' someone is there.
Example: もし雨なら、行きません。 (もしあめなら、いきません。)
-If it rains, I won't go.
}

道に迷う-
{
道に迷う (みちにまよう) - To get lost
A verb phrase consisting of 'road' and the verb 'to be puzzled' or 'to wander'.
Memory Tip: You are 'puzzled' (迷う) about which 'road' (道) to take.
Example: 帰り道に迷いました。 (かえりみちにまよいました。)
-I got lost on the way home.
}

辞書形-
{
辞書形 (じしょけい) - Dictionary form
Composed of 辞書 (dictionary) and 形 (form). It is the base/plain form of Japanese verbs.
Memory Tip: The 'Ji-sho' (Dictionary) 'Kei' (Key) is the form you use to look words up.
Example: 動詞を辞書形で覚える。 (どうしをじしょけいでおぼえる。) -[Memorize verbs in their dictionary form.]
}

鼻の穴-
{
鼻の穴 (はなのあな) - Nostril
A compound noun literally meaning 'hole of the nose' (鼻 hana + の no + 穴 ana).
Memory Tip: Simply combine the kanji for 'nose' (鼻) with the kanji for 'hole/cave' (穴).
Example: 鼻の穴が大きいです。 (はなのあながおおきいです。)
-My nostrils are large.
}

竹の子-
{
竹の子 (たけのこ) - Bamboo shoot
Literally 'bamboo's child.' It refers to the edible young shoots of the bamboo plant.
Memory Tip: Bamboo (竹) + 's (の) + child (子). The small child of the tall bamboo plant.
Example: 竹の子が旬です (たけのこがしゅんです)
-Bamboo shoots are in season.
}

逃げる-
{
逃げる (にげる) - To escape, run away, or flee
An intransitive verb indicating movement away from danger, capture, or responsibility.
Memory Tip: The 'road' radical (辶) on the left shows someone hitting the road to get away.
Example: 犯人は逃げた。 (はんにんはにげた。)
-The criminal escaped.
}

言われる-
{
言われる (いわれる) - To be told / To be called
This is the passive form of the verb 言う (to say). It indicates that someone else is speaking to the subject.
Memory Tip: Use the 'say' radical (言) plus the passive 'wa-re-ru' suffix to remember the action is received.
Example: 先生に言われる。 (せんせいにいわれる。)
-To be told by the teacher.
}

頼む-
{
頼む (たのむ) - To request/To ask a favor
A common verb used for asking someone for help or for ordering items at a restaurant.
Memory Tip: "Ta-nomu" sounds like you are "asking" for a "drink" (nomu).
Example: 手伝ってくれるよう頼んだ。 (てつだってくれるようたのんだ。)
-I asked him to help me.
}

酷い-
{
酷い (ひどい) - Terrible; cruel; severe
An i-adjective used to describe something very bad in quality, or a person who is acting mean/cruel.
Memory Tip: The radical for sake (酉) suggests that a 'severe' hangover or bad alcohol makes you feel 'terrible'.
Example: 酷い雨だ (ひどいあめだ)
-It is a terrible rain
}

どういう-
{
どういう (どういう) - What kind of / What sort of
A pre-noun adjectival phrase derived from 'dou' (how) and 'iu' (to say).
Memory Tip: Literally "How is it said?" It is used to ask for clarification or deeper meaning.
Example: どういう意味ですか？(どういういみですか？) - What does that mean?
}

眠る-
{
眠る (ねむる) - To sleep
This verb refers to the physiological state of being asleep or unconscious.
Memory Tip: Combines 'eye' (目) and 'civilian' (民). Imagine a civilian closing their eyes to sleep.
Example: 彼は静かに眠っている。 (かれはしずかにねむっている。)
-He is sleeping quietly.
}

冷やす-
{
冷やす (ひやす) - To cool, to chill
A transitive verb indicating an intentional action taken to lower the temperature of something.
Memory Tip: Focus on the 'Hiya' sound—like 'Hiya!' a cold wind hits you as you chill something.
Example: ビールを冷蔵庫で冷やす。(びーるをれいぞうこでひやす。)
-Chill the beer in the refrigerator.
}

不思議-
{
不思議 (ふしぎ) - wonderful, strange, mysterious
A na-adjective describing something that is mysterious or defies normal explanation.
Memory Tip: It literally means 'not' (不) 'think' (思) 'discussion' (議) — something beyond thought or talk.
Example: 彼は不思議な力を持っている。 (かれはふしぎなちからをもっている。)
-He has a mysterious power.
}

床-
{
床 (ゆか) - floor
Refers specifically to the indoor floor of a building or room.
Memory Tip: Under the roof (广) of the house, the wood (木) boards form the floor.
Example: 床を掃除します。 (ゆかをそうじします。)
-I will clean the floor.
}

死-
{
死 (し) - death
A noun or root indicating the end of life or a state of being dead.
Memory Tip: The left side of the kanji (歹) represents skeletal remains or broken bones, symbolizing death.
Example: 死を恐れません。 (しをおそれません。)
-I do not fear death.
}

疲れ-
{
疲れ (つかれ) - Tiredness / Fatigue
The noun form of the verb 疲れる, indicating a state of being worn out.
Memory Tip: The sickness radical (疒) on top suggests that being extremely tired feels like being ill.
Example: 疲れが溜まっている (つかれがたまっている)
-Fatigue is building up.
}

返る-
{
返る (かえる) - To return / To go back
An intransitive verb meaning something returns to its original state or owner. It is often used for abstract items like consciousness or seasons.
Memory Tip: The 'movement' radical (辶) combined with 'anti/return' (反) suggests moving back to a previous point.
Example: 意識が返る。 (いしきがかえる。)
-Consciousness returns.
}

昔-
{
昔 (むかし) - Old times / Long ago
A noun indicating the distant past. It is famously used in the opening phrase 'Mukashi mukashi' (Once upon a time).
Memory Tip: The top part represents many 'days' or 'layers' stacked above the sun (日), indicating time from long ago.
Example: 昔、ここに川があった。 (むかし、ここにかわがあった。)
-Long ago, there was a river here.
}

〜みたいな-
{
〜みたいな (〜みたいな) - Like, similar to
A colloquial expression used to describe something by comparing it to something else. It functions as a 'na-adjective' when modifying nouns.
Memory Tip: Think of it as 'me-tai-na' - 'I want to be like that' (informally).
Example: 夢みたいな話だ。(ゆめみたいなはなしだ。)
-It's like a dream story.
}

いつ頃-
{
いつ頃 (いつごろ) - About when
Combines the question word 'いつ' (when) with '頃' (approximate time), making the inquiry less precise and softer.
Memory Tip: 'Itsu' (when) plus 'Goro' (approximate goal) equals asking for the ballpark time.
Example: いつ頃出発しますか？ (いつごろしゅっぱつしますか？)
-About when will you depart?
}

髪-
{
髪 (かみ) - Hair (on the head)
Refers specifically to human head hair; the kanji includes the radical for long hair (彡).
Memory Tip: 'Kami' is also the word for God; imagine gods have majestic, flowing hair.
Example: 彼は髪を短く切った。 (かれはかみをみじかくきった。)
-He cut his hair short.
}

髪の毛-
{
髪の毛 (かみのけ) - Hair (strands), head hair
Combines '髪' (head hair) and '毛' (fur/hair/bristle) to refer to the collective hair or individual strands on the head.
Memory Tip: 'Kami' (head hair) + 'no' (possessive) + 'ke' (fur) = The fur of the head.
Example: 髪の毛が一本落ちている。 (かみのけがいっぽんおちている。)
-There is a single strand of hair lying there.
}

回る-
{
回る (まわる) - To turn, revolve
An intransitive godan verb describing circular motion, spinning, or making a round of visits.
Memory Tip: The kanji 回 looks like a smaller box rotating inside a larger box, like a wheel or a revolving door.
Example: 地球は太陽の周りを回る。 (ちきゅうはたいようのまわりをまわる。)
-The Earth revolves around the sun.
}

先-
{
先 (さき) - Tip, ahead, future, previous
A noun and adverbial noun that refers to either the point of something or a point in time (either past or future depending on context).
Memory Tip: The bottom part (儿) represents legs moving forward, putting you 'ahead' of others.
Example: お先に失礼します。 (おさきにしつれいします。)
-Excuse me for leaving before you.
}

数-
{
数 (かず) - Number, amount
A noun used to describe a quantity of items. It forms the base of the verb 数える (to count).
Memory Tip: The left side has rice (米) and woman (女); imagine someone counting every single grain of rice.
Example: 数を数えてください。 (かずをかぞえてください。)
-Please count the number.
}

偉い-
{
偉い (えらい) - Great / Admirable / High-ranking
An i-adjective used to praise someone's status, character, or diligent effort.
Memory Tip: Someone "E-rai" is a "great guy" who is high in status.
Example: 毎日勉強して偉いですね。(まいにちべんきょうしてえらいですね)
-You are admirable for studying every day.
}

指-
{
指 (ゆび) - Finger, toe
A general term for the digits on hands and feet. It is often combined with other nouns, like '親指' for thumb.
Memory Tip: Hand (扌) radical + delicious (旨); you use your finger to taste if something is delicious.
Example: 指で指す。 (ゆびでさす。)
-To point with a finger.
}

お釣り-
{
お釣り (おつり) - Change (money)
Derived from 'tsuru' (to fish or hang), referring to the balance 'hanging' back after a payment. 'O' is the honorific prefix.
Memory Tip: You are 'fishing' (釣り) for the honorific (お) change left in your pocket after shopping.
Example: お釣りを忘れないでください。(おつりをわすれないでください。)
-Please don't forget your change.
}

〜部-
{
〜部 (〜ぶ) - department/club/copy
A suffix used for organizational sections, school clubs, or as a counter for newspapers and books.
Memory Tip: The radical 阝 on the right represents a division or walled town, signifying that the 'part' (部) belongs to a larger whole.
Example: 彼はテニス部に所属している。 (かれはてにすぶにしょぞくしている。)
-He belongs to the tennis club.
}

生まれ-
{
生まれ (うまれ) - 
Refers to one's birth, origin, or lineage; it is the noun form of the verb 生まれる.
Memory Tip: The radical 生 represents a plant sprouting from the ground, symbolizing life and birth.
Example: 私は東京生まれです。 (わたしはとうきょううまれです。)
-I was born in Tokyo.
}

玄関-
{
玄関 (げんかん) - Entrance / Foyer
Composed of 'mysterious' (玄) and 'gateway' (関). In Japan, it's the designated area to remove shoes.
Memory Tip: The 'mysterious' (玄) 'gate' (関) where you leave the outside world and enter the home.
Example: 玄関で靴を脱ぐ。(げんかんでくつをぬぐ。)
-Take off your shoes at the entrance.
}

喉-
{
喉 (のど) - Throat
A noun referring to the throat. It is commonly used in phrases related to thirst or soreness.
Memory Tip: The left radical (月) means body part, and the right side features a mouth (口) where the throat is located.
Example: 喉が痛いです。 (のどがいたいです。)
-My throat hurts.
}

痩せる-
{
痩せる (やせる) - To lose weight, to get thin
An intransitive verb. When describing someone as 'thin', the continuous form 痩せている is used.
Memory Tip: The radical 疒 refers to sickness, suggesting someone who has become thin or frail.
Example: ダイエットで痩せました。(だいえっとでやせました)
-I lost weight on a diet.
}

見える-
{
見える (みえる) - To be visible, to be seen
An intransitive verb used when something naturally comes into view without the observer's active effort.
Memory Tip: It is the spontaneous form of 'miru' (to see); it just 'appears' or 'is seen'.
Example: 富士山が見えます。(ふじさんがみえます。)
-Mount Fuji is visible.
}

参る-
{
参る (まいる) - To go; to come (humble)
A humble (kenjougo) verb used when the speaker is lowering themselves while interacting with a superior.
Memory Tip: The kanji 参 looks like someone bowing low while walking toward a destination.
Example: 明日、参ります。 (あした、まいります。)
-I will come tomorrow.
}

変-
{
変 (へん) - Strange, odd, unusual
A na-adjective used to describe something that feels off, weird, or eccentric.
Memory Tip: The kanji is associated with 'change.' If something has changed from the norm, it's 'strange.'
Example: 彼の様子が変だ。 (かれのようすがへんだ。)
-His behavior is strange.
}

普通-
{
普通 (ふつう) - Normal, ordinary
A noun and na-adjective describing something standard. 'Fu' means general/universal and 'tsu' means to pass through.
Memory Tip: 'Fu' (Few) things are 'tsu' (too) normal; it's the standard path everyone passes through.
Example: 彼は普通の学生です (かれはふつうのがくせいです)
-He is an ordinary student.
}

両手-
{
両手 (りょうて) - Both hands
A compound noun consisting of 両 (both/pair) and 手 (hand).
Memory Tip: Think of 'both' (両) as a pair of items held in the 'hands' (手).
Example: 両手で持つ (りょうでもつ)
-To hold with both hands
}

命-
{
命 (いのち) - Life
A noun referring to physical life or the vital force of living things.
Memory Tip: Imagine the kanji as a person (人) under a roof (亼) receiving a command (卩) or mouth (口) to live.
Example: 命は大切です。(いのちはたいせつです。)
-Life is precious.
}

打つ-
{
打つ (うつ) - 
A versatile Godan verb meaning to hit, strike, or type (as in a keyboard or email).
Memory Tip: 'U' (You) 'tsu' (strike) the keys to type a message.
Example: メールを打つ。(めーるをうつ。)
-To type/send an email.
}

運ぶ-
{
運ぶ (はこぶ) - 
A transitive Godan verb meaning to transport or carry something from one place to another.
Memory Tip: Use the 'box' (hako) logic again—to 'hako-bu' is to move boxes to another location.
Example: 荷物を二階へ運ぶ。(にもつをにかいへはこぶ。)
-Carry the luggage to the second floor.
}

特に-
{
特に (とくに) - Especially / Particularly
An adverb formed by 'special' (特) and the particle 'ni'. It highlights one item or reason above others.
Memory Tip: TOKyio is UNique (ni), especially the food.
Example: 特に寿司が好きです。 (とくにすしがすきです。)
-I especially like sushi.
}

〜室-
{
〜室 (〜しつ) - Room suffix
A suffix added to nouns to designate a specific type of room or indoor space.
Memory Tip: This kanji shows a 'roof' over a 'base'; it's a specific 'room' for a dedicated purpose.
Example: 会議室で待っています。(かいぎしつでまっています。)
-I am waiting in the meeting room.
}

捨てる-
{
捨てる (すてる) - To throw away
A transitive verb used for discarding physical trash or metaphorical things like pride.
Memory Tip: Stop TErrible RUbbish—throw it away.
Example: ゴミを捨てないで。 (ごみをすてないで。)
-Please don't throw away trash.
}

急ぐ-
{
急ぐ (いそぐ) - To hurry / To rush
An intransitive verb used to indicate haste or performing an action quickly due to urgency.
Memory Tip: I SO Gushed out the door because I had to hurry.
Example: 学校へ急ぐ。 (がっこうへいそぐ。)
-I hurry to school.
}

段々-
{
段々 (だんだん) - Gradually / Step by step
An adverb formed by repeating the kanji for 'step' or 'stair' (段).
Memory Tip: Visualize someone climbing stairs (dan-dan) one step at a time.
Example: 段々寒くなってきました。 (だんだんさむくなってきました。)
-It has gradually become colder.

図-
{
図 (ず) - Diagram/Figure/Illustration
A noun used for visual representations, maps, or charts in books and manuals.

Example: この図を見てください。 (このずをみてください。)
-Please look at this diagram.
}

お手拭き-
{
お手拭き (おてふき) - Wet towel
A polite noun combining honorific お, 手 (hand), and the stem of 拭く (to wipe). It is the standard term for a moist towel provided at restaurants.
Memory Tip: It literally means "hand-wiping" with a polite prefix; the radicals are 'hand' and 'wipe'.
Example: お手拭きをいただけますか？ (おてふきをいただけますか？)
-May I have a wet towel?
}

気分-
{
気分 (きぶん) - Feeling, mood
Refers to one's internal emotional or physical state. Combines 'ki' (spirit/energy) and 'bun' (part/portion).
Memory Tip: Your mood is the specific 'portion' (分) of your 'spirit' (気) at a given moment.
Example: 今日は気分がいい。(きょうはきぶんがいい。)
-I feel good today.
}

合う-
{
合う (あう) - To fit, to match, to suit
An intransitive verb used for compatibility between things, sizes, or people's opinions.
Memory Tip: The kanji shows a lid (top) and a mouth (bottom) fitting together perfectly.
Example: この靴は私に合う。(このくつはわたしにあう。)
-These shoes fit me.
}

無理-
{
無理 (むり) - Impossible, unreasonable, overdoing it
Combines 'mu' (none) and 'ri' (reason/logic). Literally means something that lacks logical feasibility.
Memory Tip: If there is 'no' (無) 'reason' (理) to attempt it, it is 'impossible'.
Example: 無理をしないでください。(むりをしないでください。)
-Please don't overdo it.
}

二杯-
{
二杯 (にはい) - Two cups/glasses
Uses the counter "-hai" for liquid-filled containers. The reading of the counter changes to "hai" after the number two.
Memory Tip: Two (二) units of a liquid container (杯).
Example: コーヒーを二杯ください (こーひーをにはいください)
-Two cups of coffee, please.
}

渡る-
{
渡る (わたる) - To cross over
An intransitive verb used to describe moving across a boundary such as a bridge, road, or ocean.
Memory Tip: The 'water' radical (氵) on the left reminds you that you are crossing over a body of water.
Example: 橋を渡る (はしをわたる)
-To cross a bridge
}

勝つ-
{
勝つ (かつ) - To win
An intransitive verb meaning to gain victory; it usually takes the particle 'ni' to mark the person or game won.
Memory Tip: You need 'strength' (力) at the bottom of the kanji to 'win' the prize.
Example: 試合に勝つ (しあいにかつ)
-To win the match
}

変える-
{
変える (かえる) - To change something
A transitive verb used when a person actively alters the state or nature of an object.
Memory Tip: The kanji features the 'strange' radical; when you change things, they look strange at first.
Example: 予定を変える。 (よていをかえる。)
-I will change the schedule.
}

森-
{
森 (もり) - Forest
Refers to a large, dense forest or grove with many trees.
Memory Tip: The kanji is made of three tree (木) radicals clumped together to make a thick forest.
Example: 森を歩く。 (もりをあるく。)
-To walk through the forest.
}

息子-
{
息子 (むすこ) - Son
A noun specifically used for one's own male offspring.
Memory Tip: A 'child' (子) who is as precious as your own 'breath' (息).
Example: 私の息子は五歳です。 (わたしのむすこはごさいです。)
-My son is five years old.
}

決まる-
{
決まる (きまる) - To be decided
An intransitive verb used when something gets settled or determined.
Memory Tip: Imagine the flow of water (氵) being set into a fixed path.
Example: 予定が決まった。 (よていがきまった。)
-The schedule has been decided.
}

喜ぶ-
{
喜ぶ (よろこぶ) - To be happy
A verb used to express joy or gratitude in response to something good.
Memory Tip: Ten (十) mouths (口) celebrating with a drum (壴) in the middle.
Example: 彼女はプレゼントを喜んだ。 (かのじょはぷれぜんとをよろこんだ。)
-She was happy with the gift.
}

観る-
{
観る (みる) - To watch/view
Unlike the general 'miru' (見る), this kanji is reserved for intentional viewing, such as movies, plays, or sightseeing.
Memory Tip: Using your eyes (見) to observe a grand scene like a stork (雚) on a mountaintop.
Example: 映画を観るのが好きだ。 (えいがをみるのがすきだ。)
-I like watching movies.
}

階段-
{
階段 (かいだん) - Stairs/Staircase
Combines 'story/floor' (階) and 'step/grade' (段).
Memory Tip: Use the 'Kai' (climb) to get the 'Dan' (done).
Example: 階段を上る。 (かいだんをのぼる。)
-To go up the stairs.
}

起こる-
{
起こる (おこる) - To occur/happen
An intransitive verb used for events, incidents, or natural phenomena taking place.
Memory Tip: Things 'rise' (oko) up into reality when they happen.
Example: 事件が起こった。 (じけんがおこった。)
-An incident occurred.
}

登る-
{
登る (のぼる) - To climb
An intransitive verb used for ascending mountains, stairs, or the sun rising.

-To climb a mountain.

倒れる-
{
倒れる (たおれる) - To fall down/collapse
An intransitive verb describing a person fainting or a vertical object falling over.

Example: 木が倒れた。 (きがたおれた。)
-The tree fell down.

危険-
{
危険 (きけん) - Danger
Composed of 'peril' (危) and 'narrow/stiff' (険), functioning as a na-adjective or noun.
Memory Tip: Finding a 'ki' (key) in a lion's 'ken' (kennel) is 'danger'.
Example: ここは危険です。 (ここはきけんです。)
-This place is dangerous.
}

結局-
{
結局 (けっきょく) - After all/In the end
Literally 'the conclusion of the game,' used to describe the ultimate result.
Memory Tip: A 'kek' (cake) served at the 'kyoku' (bureau) was the 'end' result.
Example: 結局、彼は来なかった。 (けっきょく、かれはこなかった。)
-In the end, he didn't come.

腹-
{
腹 (はら) - Belly, stomach
A noun for the abdomen, frequently used in idioms regarding emotions or hidden intentions.
Memory Tip: The radical 月 (body part) plus 複 (complex) represents the complexity of the gut.
Example: 腹が痛いです。 (はらがいたいです。)
-My stomach hurts.

腹が減った-
{
腹が減った (はらがへった) - I'm hungry
A casual, often masculine expression combining 'belly' and the verb 'to decrease'.
Memory Tip: Hara (belly) + Hetta (decreased) = My belly's contents have decreased.
Example: 腹が減ったから、ラーメンを食べよう。 (はらがへったから、らーめんをたべよう。)
-I'm hungry, so let's eat ramen.
}

苛める-
{
苛める (いじめる) - To bully, to tease
An ichidan verb used to describe picking on or mistreating someone. It conveys a sense of cruelty toward a weaker subject.
Memory Tip: It sounds like 'iji' (easy) — don't bully people just because it's easy!
Example: 弱い者を苛めてはいけない (よわいものをいじめてはいけない)
-You must not bully the weak.

〜ようと思ってる-
{
〜ようと思ってる (〜ようとおもってる) - I am thinking of (doing)
Uses the volitional form (~ou) plus the continuous form of 'think' to show an intention formed in the past that continues.
Memory Tip: Volitional (~ou) + 'to' (quote) + 'omou' (think). I am currently carrying the thought of doing it.
Example: 留学しようと思ってる。 (りゅうがくしようとおもってる。)
-I am thinking of studying abroad.
