串焼き-
{
串焼き (くしやき) - Skewer grilling
A combination of 串 (skewer) and 焼き (grilling/roasting).
Memory Tip: The kanji 串 literally looks like two pieces of food on a stick! 焼き means heat or fire.
Example: 居酒屋で串焼きを注文した。 (いざかやでくしやきをちゅうもんした。)
-I ordered some grilled skewers at the izakaya.
}

梅酒-
{
梅酒 (うめしゅ) - Plum wine, plum liqueur
A Japanese alcoholic drink made by steeping green plums in liquor and sugar.
Memory Tip: 梅 (plum) + 酒 (alcohol). Simply 'plum alcohol'.
Example: 食前に自家製の梅酒を飲んだ。 (しょくぜんにじかせいのうめしゅをのんだ。)
-I drank some homemade plum wine before the meal.
}

再来週-
{
再来週 (さいらいしゅう) - the week after next
Combines 再 (again), 来 (coming), and 週 (week) to skip one week ahead.
Memory Tip: The "again" (再) coming week refers to the one after the next immediate week.
Example: 再来週の月曜日に会いましょう。 (さいらいしゅうのげつようびにあいましょう。)
-Let's meet on the Monday after next.
}

ばい菌-
{
ばい菌 (ばいきん) - Bacteria/germs
A common word for harmful microbes. While 'baikin' is used colloquially, 'saikin' (細菌) is the more scientific term.
Memory Tip: Harmful 'Fungi/Germs' (菌) that 'Multiply' or act like mold (ばい/黴).
Example: 手を洗わないとばい菌がつくよ。 (てをあらわないとばいきんがつくよ。)
-If you don't wash your hands, you'll get germs on them.
}

腹切り-
{
腹切り (はらきり) - Harakiri
A descriptive noun for ritual suicide; it is more literal and colloquial than the formal term "seppuku."
Memory Tip: To literally cut (切り) the belly (腹).
Example: 侍は腹切りを命じられた。 (さむらいははらきりをめいじられた。)
-The samurai was ordered to commit harakiri.
}

割り算-
{
割り算 (わりざん) - Division
A math term combining the stem of the verb 割る (to split) and 算 (calculation).
Memory Tip: A calculation (算) where you split or divide (割り) a whole number into parts.
Example: 割り算は少し難しいです。 (わりざんはすこしむずかしいです。)
-Division is a little difficult.
}

戻り道-
{
戻り道 (もどりみち) - Way back
Combines the noun form of 戻る (to return) with 道 (path) to describe the journey home or return route.
Memory Tip: The path (道) you take while you are on the way back (戻り) to where you started.
Example: 戻り道で雨が降ってきた。 (もどりみちであめがふってきた。)
-It started raining on the way back.
}

雄犬-
{
雄犬 (おすいぬ) - Male dog
A literal compound of 雄 (male/masculine) and 犬 (dog).
Memory Tip: Combine the character for male/hero (雄) with the character for dog (犬) to distinguish it from a female dog (雌犬).
Example: うちの犬は雄犬です。 (うちのいぬはおすいぬです。)
-My dog is a male dog.
}

福袋-
{
福袋 (ふくぶくろ) - lucky bag / mystery bag
Formed from 福 (luck/fortune) and 袋 (bag), these are bags sold at New Year's with unknown contents worth more than the price.
Memory Tip: A "bag" (袋) full of "good fortune" (福) grabbed during New Year sales.
Example: 初売りで福袋を買った。 (はつうりでふくぶくろをかった。)
-I bought a lucky bag at the first sale of the year.
}

お会計-
{
お会計 (おかいけい) - The bill / Check / Payment
A polite term using the prefix お with 会計 (accounting/finance), commonly used in restaurants and shops.
Memory Tip: You are 'meeting' (会) with the 'calculation' (計) to settle your debt.
Example: お会計をお願いします。 (おかいけいをおねがいします。)
-Check, please.
}

喉飴-
{
喉飴 (のどあめ) - Throat Lozenge / Cough Drop
A compound noun consisting of 'throat' and 'candy'. It refers to medicated or soothing candy for throat irritation.
Memory Tip: 喉 (throat) + 飴 (candy). Candy you take specifically for your throat.
Example: 喉が痛いので喉飴をなめる。 (のどがいたいのでのどあめをなめる。)
-I'll suck on a throat lozenge because my throat hurts.
}

待たせる-
{
待たせる (またせる) - To keep someone waiting
This is the causative form of the verb "matsu" (to wait).
Memory Tip: "Matsu" (wait) + the causative "-seru" (to make/let) = to make someone wait.
Example: 友達を駅で一時間も待たせてしまった。 (ともだちをえきでいちじかんもまたせてしまった。)
-I ended up keeping my friend waiting at the station for a whole hour.
}

望み-
{
望み (のぞみ) - Hope, wish, or prospect
The noun form of the verb "nozomu," meaning to desire or look forward to something.
Memory Tip: The kanji depicts someone standing on the ground looking (目) at the distant moon (月) with hope.
Example: 私たちの望みは世界平和です。 (わたしたちののぞみはせかいへいわです。)
-Our wish is for world peace.
}

頼み-
{
頼み (たのみ) - Request; favor; reliance
The noun form of the verb 頼む (to ask/request). It signifies a plea for help or something entrusted to another.
Memory Tip: The kanji 頼 shows a head (頁) looking for someone to rely on for support.
Example: 一つ頼みがあります。 (ひとつたのみがあります。)
-I have one request.
}

思える-
{
思える (おもえる) - to seem/to appear/to look like
The potential or spontaneous form of 思う, indicating an impression that comes to mind naturally.
Memory Tip: Think of it as 'it can be thought,' suggesting a situation naturally leads to a certain conclusion.
Example: それは本当のように思える。 (それはほんとうのようにおもえる。)
-That seems to be true.
}

呼ばれる-
{
呼ばれる (よばれる) - To be called
The passive form of the verb 呼ぶ (yobu), used for names, titles, or being summoned.
Memory Tip: "Yo!" is what you yell to call someone; add "-bareru" to make it the passive "being called."
Example: 彼は親しい友人に「ケン」と呼ばれている。 (かれはしたしいゆうじんに「けん」とよばれている。)
-He is called "Ken" by his close friends.
}

回転ずし-
{
回転ずし (かいてんずし) - conveyor belt sushi
A combination of 回転 (kaiten - rotation/turning) and sushi. It refers to the popular dining style where plates move on a belt.
Memory Tip: 'Kai' (circle) + 'ten' (turn) = rotation. Sushi that turns in a circle around the restaurant!
Example: 回転ずしに行こう。 (かいてんずしにいこう。)
-Let's go to a conveyor belt sushi restaurant.
}

押し-
{
押し (おし) - pushing, pressure, weight
The noun form of the verb 押す (osu), used to mean physical pressure or social influence.
Memory Tip: The hand radical (扌) combined with armor (甲) suggests applying force with your palm.
Example: 最後に一押しが必要です。 (さいごにひとおしがひつようです。)
-One last push is necessary.
}

要る-
{
要る (いる) - To need
A common Godan (u-verb) used with the particle が to mark the object that is necessary. Unlike the homophone 'iru' (to exist), this verb conjugates as 'irimasu' in polite form.
Memory Tip: The kanji 要 looks like a person with their hands on their hips standing over a woman (女); imagine them pointing out what is 'essential' for the household.
Example: 助けが要りますか。 (たすけがいりますか。)
-Do you need help?
}

役に立つ-
{
役に立つ (やくにたつ) - to be useful, to be helpful
A common verb phrase where "役" means role/service and "立つ" means to stand. It literally translates to "to stand in a role," indicating something serves a purpose.
Memory Tip: Think of a tool "standing" (立つ) ready in its "role" (役). If it's standing there ready to work, it is being useful!
Example: この本はとても役に立つ。 (このほんはとてもやくにたつ。)
-This book is very useful.
}

〜って-
{
〜って (って) - Quoting particle; topic marker; says; is called
A versatile casual contraction of particles like と, という, or は, used to relay information, define a subject, or report speech.
Memory Tip: Think of the small 'っ' as a verbal 'hook' that catches someone else's words or a specific topic to bring it into the conversation.
Example: 彼は来ないって。 (かれはこないって。)
-He says he isn't coming.
}

仕方がない-
{
しかたがない (しかたがない) - It can't be helped / There's no other way
This phrase combines 'shikata' (way of doing) and 'nai' (none), indicating a situation is outside of one's control. It is a core concept in Japanese culture representing resilient acceptance.
Memory Tip: 'Shikata' means 'way to do'; if there is 'nai' (no) 'way to do' it, you must accept the outcome.
Example: 負けてしまったのは仕方がない。(まけてしまったのはしかたがない。)
-It can't be helped that we lost.
}

興味がない-
{
きょうみがない (きょうみがない) - Not interested / Have no interest
This common expression combines the noun '興味' (interest) with the negative adjective 'ない' (none). It is used to express a complete lack of curiosity or concern toward a specific subject.
Memory Tip: 'Kyomi' (興味) literally means 'interest-taste'. If you have no 'taste' for something, you have 'Kyomi ga nai'.
Example: 彼はそのゲームに全く興味がない。 (かれはそのゲームにまったくきょうみがない。)
-He has absolutely no interest in that game.
}

〜ながら-
{
〜ながら (ながら) - While / Although
Attached to the stem of a verb to indicate that two actions are performed simultaneously by the same person, or to show a contrast between two states.
Memory Tip: Think of "naga-i" (long); you are stretching one action out "alongside" another.
Example: 音楽を聴きながら勉強します。 (おんがくをききながらべんきょうします。)
-I study while listening to music.
}

〜し-
{
〜し (し) - ...and; besides; what's more
This conjunctive particle lists multiple reasons or qualities that support a specific conclusion or situation, often implying that more reasons could exist. It attaches to the plain/casual form of verbs and adjectives.
Memory Tip: Think of 'shi' as 'Sharing' a 'series' of points or reasons.
Example: 安いし、おいしいです。(やすいし、おいしいです)
-It's cheap, and besides, it's delicious.
}

〜んだ-
{
〜んだ (んだ) - Explaining context or seeking clarification
A casual contraction of the explanatory particle "〜のだ," used to provide a reason, emphasize a fact, or seek background information. It connects the statement to a specific context or shared situation.
Memory Tip: Think of the 'n' as "Notice"—you use it when there is a reason or context you want the listener to notice behind your statement.
Example: 忙しいんだ。 (いそがしいんだ。)
-It's that I'm busy. / (The reason is) I'm busy.
}

開館時間-
{
開館時間 (かいかんじかん) - Opening hours
A compound noun typically used for public buildings like libraries or museums.
Memory Tip: Combine 'Open' (開), 'Building' (館), and 'Time Interval' (時間).
Example: 図書館の開館時間を教えてください。 (としょかんのかいかんじかんをおしえてください。)
-Please tell me the library's opening hours.
}

診る-
{
診る (みる) - To examine (medically)
A specific verb used for a doctor's medical inspection or diagnostic checkup.
Memory Tip: Combining 'words' and 'take'—the doctor takes your words and symptoms to diagnose you.
Example: 医者に診てもらいなさい。 (いしゃにみてもらいなさい。)
-Please have a doctor examine you.
}

〜的-
{
〜的 (〜てき) - -ish / -like / -al (suffix)
A suffix that transforms nouns into na-adjectives, similar to the English suffix "-ic."
Memory Tip: The kanji shows a "target." It targets a specific quality of the preceding word.
Example: それは世界的な問題だ。 (それはせかいてきなもんだいだ。)
-That is a global problem.
}

人間-
{
人間 (にんげん) - Human Being
This noun combines 'person' (人) and 'between/space' (間), suggesting that humans are defined by their social connections.
Memory Tip: A person needs the space between others to be a human.
Example: 人間は社会的な動物だ。 (にんげんはしゃかいてきなどうぶつだ。)
-Humans are social animals.
}

〜まま-
{
〜まま (まま) - As it is / leaving it in a state
Indicates a state that remains unchanged from a previous action or condition.
Memory Tip: Think of "mama" (mother) - staying exactly as you were when you were a baby with your mama.
Example: 靴を履いたまま部屋に入った。 (くつをはいたままへやにはいった。)
-I entered the room with my shoes still on.
}

〜ばかり-
{
〜ばかり (ばかり) - Only / nothing but / just finished
Indicates that something is the exclusive focus or that an action just occurred.
Memory Tip: "Bakari" sounds like "battery" - you only have one battery left for your remote.
Example: 彼は寝てばかりいる。 (かれはねてばかりいる。)
-He does nothing but sleep.
}

感じ-
{
感じ (かんじ) - Feeling, impression
The noun form of the verb "kanjiru" (to feel), referring to an atmosphere or sensation.
Memory Tip: The kanji features the heart radical (心) at the bottom, where all feelings are centered.
Example: 良い感じです。 (いいかんじです)
-It's a good feeling.
}

〜気がする-
{
〜気がする (きがする) - To have a feeling / to have a hunch
Expresses a subjective intuition or a vague feeling that something might be the case.
Memory Tip: "Ki" (spirit/air) + "suru" (to do). Your inner spirit is "doing" or signaling a feeling.
Example: 雨が降る気がする。 (あめがふるきがする。)
-I have a feeling it will rain.
}

気がする-
{
気がする (きがする) - To feel that / to have a sense
Similar to its grammar form, it indicates an internal hunch or an impression.
Memory Tip: Your "inner air" (ki) is making a move (suru) to give you a specific sensation.
Example: どこかで会った気がする。 (どこかであったきがする。)
-I feel like I've met you somewhere before.
}

麺つゆ-
{
麺つゆ (めんつゆ) - Noodle soup base
A common Japanese seasoning made from dashi, soy sauce, and mirin used for dipping noodles.
Memory Tip: 麺 (Noodle) plus つゆ (Soup/Dew). It is the 'dew' for your noodles.
Example: 麺つゆを作る。 (めんつゆをつくる。)
-I will make noodle soup base.
}

細かい-
{
細かい (こまかい) - Fine / Small / Detailed
This adjective describes small physical particles or very detailed, meticulous points.
Memory Tip: The 'thread' radical (糸) suggests a thin, fine thread of detail.
Example: 細かいお金がありますか。 (こまかいおかねがありますか。)
-Do you have any small change?
}

立派-
{
立派 (りっぱ) - Splendid / Fine / Admirable
A na-adjective meaning something stands out as excellent, dignified, or praiseworthy.
Memory Tip: If your 'group' (派) can 'stand' (立) tall, they are truly 'splendid'.
Example: 彼は立派な医者になった。(かれはりっぱないしゃになった。)
-He became a fine doctor.
}

戻る-
{
戻る (もどる) - to return, to go back
Used when returning to a previous location or state. It is an intransitive verb emphasizing the destination reached again.
Memory Tip: The radical 戶 represents a door; imagine returning through your front door to where you belong.
Example: 家に戻る。 (いえにもどる。)
-I will return home.
}

付ける-
{
付ける (つける) - to attach, to turn on, to apply
A transitive verb used for joining one thing to another or activating electrical devices.
Memory Tip: "Tsukeru" sounds like "sticking" something onto a surface.
Example: 電気を付ける。 (でんきをつける。)
-To turn on the light.
}

お前-
{
お前 (おまえ) - You (informal/blunt)
A casual and sometimes rough second-person pronoun used by men or superiors to subordinates.
Memory Tip: O (prefix) + Mae (in front), meaning "the person in front of me."
Example: お前、何をしているんだ？(おまえ、なにもしているんだ？)
-You, what are you doing?
}

側-
{
側 (そば) - Side / Vicinity
A noun referring to the area nearby or immediately next to someone or something.
Memory Tip: A person (亻) standing by a cliff/rule marker (則) is at the "side" of it.
Example: 彼の側にいます。 (かれのそばにいます。)
-I am by his side.
}

必要-
{
必要 (ひつよう) - Necessary, essential
A na-adjective or noun denoting something that is required or unavoidable.
Memory Tip: It combines 'certainly' (必) and 'important/need' (要).
Example: 水は生命に必要です。 (みずはせいめいにひつようです。)
-Water is necessary for life.
}

〜以上-
{
〜以上 (〜いじょう) - ...or more, more than, that's all
A suffix used for quantities or to indicate the conclusion of a statement or speech.
Memory Tip: From (以) the specified point and upwards (上).
Example: 18歳以上です。 (じゅうはっさいいじょうです。)
-18 years old or older.
}

乗り換える-
{
乗り換える (のりかえる) - To transfer (trains), to switch over
Combination of 乗り (riding) and 換える (exchanging/switching). Used for changing transport or methods.
Memory Tip: Ride (乗) one thing, then change (換) it for something new.
Example: 新宿駅で山手線に乗り換える (しんじゅくえきでやまのてせんにのりかえる)
-I will transfer to the Yamanote Line at Shinjuku Station.
}

区-
{
区 (く) - Ward / District
An administrative division used in large cities, like the 23 wards of Tokyo.
Memory Tip: A box (匚) containing a mark (メ) to divide land into separate sections.
Example: 私は新宿区に住んでいます。 (わたしはしんじゅくくにすんでいます)
-I live in Shinjuku Ward.
}

作品-
{
作品 (さくひん) - Work / Piece of art / Opus
Combines 'make' (作) and 'item/goods' (品). Specifically refers to creative productions like art or literature.
Memory Tip: An 'item' (品) that was 'made' (作) with creativity is an 'artwork'.
Example: 彼の作品はどれも素晴らしい。(かれのさくひんはどれもすばらしい。)
-Every one of his works is wonderful.
}

〜度-
{
〜度 (ど) - Counter for occurrences/degrees
A suffix used to count the number of times (frequency) or to measure units like temperature and angles.
Memory Tip: The kanji depicts a hand measuring inside a building; think of measuring the 'degree' of heat.
Example: もう一度言ってください。 (もういちどいってください。)
-Please say it one more time.
}

濃い-
{
濃い (こい) - Dark/Thick/Strong
An i-adjective used for colors (dark), liquids (thick), or flavors (strong/rich).
Memory Tip: Includes the water radical (氵); think of a liquid being so 'thick' or 'strong' it barely flows.
Example: このコーヒーは少し濃すぎる。 (このこーひーはすこしこすぎる。)
-This coffee is a bit too strong.
}

門-
{
門 (もん) - Gate
A noun referring to a formal gate or entrance to a building, school, or estate.
Memory Tip: The kanji is a literal pictograph of a pair of large swinging double doors.
Example: 彼は校門の前に立っている。 (かれはこうもんのまえにたっている。)
-He is standing in front of the school gate.
}

下がる-
{
下がる (さがる) - To hang down, to step back, to drop
An intransitive verb used for something moving downwards or decreasing in value, temperature, or rank.
Memory Tip: Combines the kanji for 'under' (下) with the movement suffix 'garu' to indicate a process of going down.
Example: 気温が下がりました。 (きおんがさがりました。)
-The temperature dropped.
}

教え-
{
教え (おしえ) - Teaching / lesson / doctrine
The noun form derived from the verb 教える (oshieru - to teach).
Memory Tip: The kanji shows a child (子) being guided/hit (攵) into learning filial piety (孝).
Example: 彼の教えは厳しい。 (かれのおしえはきびしい。)
-His teachings are strict.
}

〜てて-
{
〜てて (〜てて) - Contraction of 〜ていて (continuous state)
A colloquial contraction used in informal speech to indicate an ongoing action or a state that remains.
Memory Tip: The double 'te' sounds like a heartbeat, representing an action that keeps 'be-ing'.
Example: そこで座ってて。 (そこですわってて。)
-Stay sitting there.
}

振る-
{
振る (ふる) - To shake / to wave / to dump
A versatile verb used for physical shaking, waving hands, or rejecting a romantic partner.
Memory Tip: The left side is the hand radical (扌), showing it is an action performed with the hand.
Example: 手を振る (てをふる)
-To wave one's hand.
}

迎え-
{
迎え (むかえ) - Meeting, greeting, picking someone up
The noun form of the verb 'mukaeru'. It is most commonly used in the phrase 'mukae ni iku' (to go pick someone up).
Memory Tip: The radical on the left represents 'movement,' used when you move towards someone to greet them.
Example: 駅まで迎えに行く。 (えきまでむかえにいく。)
-I'll go to the station to pick you up.
}

首になる-
{
首になる (くびになる) - To be fired/dismissed
A common idiom meaning to lose one's job, referencing the concept of losing one's 'head' or position.
Memory Tip: Imagine the 'neck' (首) being metaphorically cut off from the company body.
Example: 先週、彼は首になった。 (せんしゅう、かれはくびになった。)
-He was fired last week.
}

〜とか言って-
{
〜とか言って (〜とかいって) - Saying something like...
Used to quote something vaguely or suggest that the reason given might be an excuse or just one of many.
Memory Tip: 'Toka' (etc.) + 'itte' (saying) = "Saying things like..."
Example: 忙しいとか言って、来なかった (いそがしいとかいって、こなかった)
-Saying he was busy or something, he didn't come.
}

下駄-
{
下駄 (げた) - Geta (wooden clogs)
A traditional Japanese footwear noun consisting of a wooden base held by cloth straps to keep the kimono away from the ground.
Memory Tip: Think of 'down' (下) on the feet, made of 'clogs' (駄) or wood.
Example: 祭りに下駄を履いて行く。 (まつりにげたをはいていく。)
-I will wear geta to the festival.

その他-
{
その他 (そのた) - Others / Miscellaneous / And so on
A phrase combining 'sono' (that) and 'ta' (other), used to categorize remaining items in a list.
Memory Tip: Literally translates to 'that other'; used for the 'extra' category in forms or lists.
Example: その他に質問はありますか？ (そのたにしつもんはありますか？)
-Are there any other questions?

深い-
{
深い (ふかい) - Deep
An i-adjective used for physical depth, complexity, or intense emotions.
Memory Tip: The water (氵) radical combined with the tree/depth elements suggests a deep, dark forest pool.

-This river is very deep.

場合-
{
場合 (ばあい) - Case, situation, or occasion
A compound of 'place' (場) and 'join/match' (合), used to describe specific circumstances or conditions.
Memory Tip: Think of it as the 'place' where conditions 'join' together to form a situation.
Example: 雨の場合、中止です。 (あめのばあい、ちゅうしです。)
-In case of rain, it will be canceled.

それでも-
{
それでも (それでも) - Nevertheless, even so, or despite that
A conjunction used to contrast a new statement with a previously mentioned fact.
Memory Tip: Literally 'sore' (that) + 'de' (by/at) + 'mo' (even)—'even with that' being the case.
Example: 難しいが、それでもやる。 (むずかしいが、それでもやる。)
-It's difficult, but I'll do it anyway.

思い出す-

思い出す (おもいだす) - To remember/recall
This is a compound verb combining 思う (to think) and 出す (to put out/surface), signifying bringing a thought back to the conscious mind.

しばらく (しばらく) - For a while / A moment

点-

点 (てん) - Point; mark; dot

当たり-
{
当たり (あたり) - Success / Hit / Per (unit)
The noun form of the verb 'ataru'. It can mean a literal hit, a winning lottery ticket, or a rate per person/item.
Memory Tip: Focus on the 'hit' kanji (当) becoming a noun (り) to represent the 'result' of the hit.

-The cost per person.

説明-
{
説明 (せつめい) - explanation
A noun combining 'theory/opinion' (説) and 'bright/clear' (明).

-A detailed explanation is necessary.

説明する-
{
説明する (せつめいする) - to explain
The verb form of 'explanation' created by adding the auxiliary verb 'suru' (to do).

〜ようになる-
{
〜ようになる (〜ようになる) - to reach the point where, to come to
Indicates a gradual change in ability, habit, or state over time, moving from one condition to another.

奥-
{
奥 (おく) - Inner part / Back
This word refers to the interior or deepest part of a space, like a room or a forest, or even one's heart.

-There is a desk in the back of the room.

たしか-
{
たしか (たしか) - If I remember correctly, certain
Used as an adverb to express a vague recollection or as a Na-adjective for certainty.
Memory Tip: Sounds like 'Teacher.' The teacher knows for 'certain' (if I remember correctly).
Example: たしか、彼は学生だ。 (たしか、かれはがくせいだ。)
-If I remember correctly, he is a student.

結構-
{
結構 (けっこう) - Fine, good, okay; quite
An adjective or adverb used to express satisfaction or to decline an offer politely.
Memory Tip: Combining 結 (tie) and 構 (structure), it implies a well-composed or 'fine' state.
Example: いいえ、結構です。 (いいえ、けっこうです。)
-No, I am fine (no thank you).

〜ことになる-
{
〜ことになる (〜ことになる) - It has been decided that; it turns out that
A grammar structure where a situation (こと) becomes (なる) a reality, often due to external factors or decisions.
Memory Tip: The "matter" (koto) has "become" (naru) a rule or a settled outcome.
Example: 来月、日本へ行くことになった。 (らいげつ、にほんへいくことになった。)
-It has been decided that I will go to Japan next month.
}

に対して-
{
に対して (にたいして) - Towards / Against / Regarding
A particle phrase used to indicate a target of an action or a contrast between two things.
Memory Tip: Combine に (to/at) + 対して (facing/opposite). You are 'facing' something directly.
Example: 先生に対して失礼です。(せんせいにたいしてしつれいですよ。) - That is rude toward the teacher.
}

とにかく-
{
とにかく (とにかく) - anyway, at any rate
An adverb used to set aside other details and focus on the main point or next action.
Memory Tip: Sounds like 'Tony-kaku'—tell Tony to do it 'at any rate'.
Example: とにかく、やってみよう。 (とにかく、やってみよう。)
-Anyway, let's give it a try.
}

暫く-
{
暫く (しばらく) - For a while / a moment
This adverb refers to an unspecified but relatively short duration of time. It is often used in polite requests to wait.
Memory Tip: The kanji contains 'sun/day' (日) and 'cut' (斤). Think of a 'cut' or small slice of the day spent waiting.
Example: 暫くお待ちください。 (しばらくおまちください。)
-Please wait for a while.
}

〜と思ったら-
{
〜と思ったら (〜とおもったら) - Just when I thought...
A grammar point used when something unexpected happens immediately after a specific action or state.
Memory Tip: "To omotta" (thought that) + "ra" (if/when) creates the sense of "The moment I thought X, Y happened."
Example: 晴れたと思ったら、また雨が降り出した。 (はれたとおもったら、またあめがふりだした。)
-Just when I thought it cleared up, it started raining again.
}

可燃ゴミ-
{
可燃ゴミ (かねんごみ) - Burnable trash
A compound noun: 可 (possible) + 燃 (burn) + ゴミ (trash).
Memory Tip: Think 'Can' (Ka) I 'burn' (nen) this trash?
Example: 可燃ゴミは月曜日に出します。(かねんごみはげつようびにだします。)
-Put out the burnable trash on Monday.
}

朝食付き-
{
朝食付き (ちょうしょくつき) - Breakfast included
A common compound found in hotel listings. 'Tsuki' means attached or included.
Memory Tip: Morning (朝) + Food (食) + Attached (付き) equals breakfast provided.
Example: このホテルは朝食付きです (このほてるはちょうしょくつきです)
-This hotel includes breakfast.
}

用-
{
用 (よう) - task; business; use
Refers to errands or matters to attend to, or the specific purpose/utility of an object.
Memory Tip: Looks like a grid or a bucket; think of it as a bucket list of tasks to complete.
Example: 今日は急な用ができた。 (きょうはきゅうなようができた。)
-I have some urgent business to attend to today.

第一-
{
第一 (だいいち) - first / number one / most important
Uses the prefix 第 (ordinal indicator) and 一 (one) to indicate the very first item or the top priority.
Memory Tip: The 第 radical looks like bamboo; the 'one' (一) bamboo shoot is the first one to grow.

-Health is the top priority.

東京弁-

東京弁 (とうきょうべん) - Tokyo dialect
A compound noun referring to the specific dialect spoken in the Tokyo region.

ちゃんと-

ちゃんと (ちゃんと) - Properly, reliably, correctly

長靴-
{
長靴 (ながぐつ) - Boots, rain boots

泊まり-

泊まり (とまり) - Staying (overnight)
The noun form of 'tomaru' (to stay overnight), often used in travel contexts or work shifts.

壊す-

壊す (こわす) - To break
A transitive verb used for physically breaking objects or metaphorically damaging health or atmosphere.

助ける-

似る-

〜かどうか-
{
〜かどうか (〜かどうか) - Whether or not
A grammatical structure used to embed a yes/no question within a sentence.

暮らす-

-I live in the city.

周り-
{
周り (まわり) - surroundings/around
The noun form of the verb 'mawaru' (to go around), referring to the perimeter or vicinity of a point.

無し-
{
無し (なし) - None / Without
A word meaning 'nothing' or 'not existing'. It is often used as a suffix to indicate a lack of something.

アメリカ製-

アメリカ製 (アメリカせい) - Made in USA

途中-
{
途中 (とちゅう) - On the way/In the middle of
Combines 'route/road' (途) and 'middle' (中) to describe an action occurring mid-transit.

少々お待ちください-
{
少々お待ちください (しょうしょうおまちください) - Please wait a moment
A very polite, formal expression often used in business or retail settings.

〜付き-

〜付き (〜つき) - with, including, attached

高級-
{
高級 (こうきゅう) - high-class, luxury
Combines "high" (高) and "rank/class" (級). Describes expensive, high-quality items.

口笛を吹く-
{
口笛を吹く (くちぶえをふく) - To whistle
A verb phrase literally meaning "to blow a mouth-flute." It specifically describes the act of whistling.

Example: 彼は口笛を吹きながら歩いた (かれはくちぶえをふきながらあるいた)

膝-
{
膝 (ひざ) - Knee
A noun identifying the joint in the middle of the human leg; it contains the 'flesh' radical (月).
Memory Tip: The body part (月) that allows you to fold your leg like a tree (木) branch.
Example: 膝を怪我しました。 (ひざをけがしました。)
-I injured my knee.
}

端-
{
端 (はし) - Edge/End
Refers to the physical limit, border, or tip of an object or space. It is a common word for giving directions.
Memory Tip: Imagine someone standing (立) at the very edge (端) of a high mountain ledge.
Example: 道の端を歩いてください。(みちのはしをあるいてください)
-Please walk on the edge of the road.
}

昭和-
{
昭和 (しょうわ) - Showa era (1926–1989)
A proper noun referring to the reign of Emperor Hirohito. It means 'Enlightened Harmony'.
Memory Tip: 'Shining' (昭) 'Harmony' (和) was the goal of this long historical era.
Example: 昭和時代は長かった。 (しょうわじだいはながかった。)
-The Showa era was long.
}

お握り-
{
お握り (おにぎり) - rice ball
Derived from the polite prefix 'o' and the verb 'nigiru' (to grasp/squeeze) describing how the rice is formed.
Memory Tip: You 'nigiru' (squeeze) the rice firmly in your palms to make this snack.
Example: お昼にお握りを食べた。 (おひるにおにぎりをたべた。)
-I ate a rice ball for lunch.
}

落とす-
{
落とす (おとす) - To drop / To lose
A transitive verb used when one lets something fall or accidentally loses an object.
Memory Tip: Grass (艹) falling into water (氵) depicts things dropping down.
Example: 道で鍵を落としました。 (みちでかぎをおとしました。)
-I dropped my keys on the street.
}

踏む-
{
踏む (ふむ) - To step on/tread
A verb used for physical stepping or following a process/procedure.
Memory Tip: The left radical '𠮛' represents a foot, which is what you use to step (fumu).
Example: 誰かに足を踏まれた。 (だれかにあしをふまれた。)
-Someone stepped on my foot.
}

別れる-
{
別れる (わかれる) - To separate, break up
An intransitive verb used for people parting ways physically or ending a romantic relationship.
Memory Tip: Use a knife (刂) to separate or divide things into different parts.
Example: 駅で友達と別れた。 (えきでともだちとわかれた。)
-I parted ways with my friend at the station.
}

騒ぐ-
{
騒ぐ (さわぐ) - To make noise, be rowdy
A verb describing loud behavior, making a commotion, or causing a public disturbance.
Memory Tip: Imagine a horse (馬) acting up again and again (又) causing a loud scene.
Example: 教室で騒がないで。 (きょうしつでさわがないで。)
-Don't be rowdy in the classroom.
}

起こす-
{
起こす (おこす) - To wake someone up / To cause
The transitive version of 起きる, used when an external force initiates an action or state.
Memory Tip: The kanji suggests 'running' (走) to get someone 'up' (己/stand).
Example: 毎朝六時に母を起こす (まいあさろくじにははをおこす)
-I wake my mother up at 6:00 every morning.
}

知り合い-
{
知り合い (しりあい) - acquaintance
A noun formed from the stem of 'shiru' (to know) and 'au' (to meet/reciprocate).
Memory Tip: It refers to two people who 'know' (shiri) 'each other' (ai) but aren't necessarily close friends.
Example: 彼は私の古い知り合いです。 (かれはわたしのふるいしりあいです。)
-He is an old acquaintance of mine.
}

空く-
{
空く (あく) - To become empty / To be free
An intransitive verb used when a space becomes vacant or a seat becomes available.
Memory Tip: Think of the kanji for sky (空) – when a seat is 'aku,' it has as much open space as the sky.
Example: この席は空いていますか？ (このせきはあいていますか？)
-Is this seat vacant?
}

集まる-
{
集まる (あつまる) - To gather / To assemble
An intransitive verb describing people or things coming together in one location.
Memory Tip: Birds (隹) gathering together on a tree (木).
Example: 広場に多くの人が集まった。 (ひろばにおおくのひとがあつまった。)
-Many people gathered in the square.
}

丁度いい-
{
丁度いい (ちょうどいい) - Just right / perfect
This phrase combines the adverb 丁度 (exactly) with the adjective いい (good) to describe a perfect fit in size, time, or quality.
Memory Tip: The character 丁 looks like a T-junction or a nail; hitting the nail 'exactly' makes it 'just right.'
Example: このサイズは丁度いいです。 (このさいずはちょうどいいです。)
-This size is just right.
}

元-
{
元 (もと) - Origin, former, source
This noun refers to the beginning of something or its previous state. It is often used to describe foundations or ex-titles.
Memory Tip: The kanji shows a person (儿) with a foundation (二) above their head, marking the start or origin.
Example: 元の場所に戻す。 (もとのばしょにもどす。)
-Return it to its original place.
}

下る-
{
下る (くだる) - To descend, to go down, to be handed down
An intransitive verb used for physical movement downward or abstract things like a judgment or command being issued.
Memory Tip: The kanji 下 clearly features a line pointing down from a horizontal level.
Example: 山を下る。 (やまをくだる。)
-To go down the mountain.
}

煮る-
{
煮る (にる) - To boil, to simmer, to cook
A transitive Ichidan verb specifically used for cooking food in a liquid, like water or broth.
Memory Tip: Look at the four dots (灬) at the bottom; they represent the 'fire' used to boil the pot.
Example: 野菜を煮る。 (やさいをにる。)
-To boil vegetables.
}

向く-
{
向く (むく) - To face / To turn toward
Used for physical direction or to indicate suitability (e.g., being 'suited' for a job).
Memory Tip: The kanji resembles a person's face looking out from an opening or window.
Example: 彼は窓の方を向いた。(かれはまどのほうをむいた)
-He turned toward the window.
}

秘密-
{
秘密 (ひみつ) - Secret
Formed by 'secret/conceal' and 'dense/hidden'. It refers to information not to be shared.
Memory Tip: Think of keeping things hidden (必) in a very quiet or dense (密) place.
Example: 秘密を守ってください。(ひみつをまもってください)
-Please keep the secret.
}

〜ほど-
{
〜ほど (ほど) - To the extent of, about
A particle indicating the degree, limit, or a relative amount of something.
Memory Tip: Think 'Hold' - how much can you 'hold' in your hand? That is the 'extent'.
Example: 死ぬほど疲れました。(しぬほどつかれました。)
-I'm tired to the point of dying.
}

いきなり-
{
いきなり (いきなり) - Suddenly/abruptly
An adverb used for events that happen without any warning or preparation.
Memory Tip: It sounds like "Iki" (breath) – something that happens in the space of a single breath.
Example: いきなり電気が消えた。 (いきなりでんきがきえた。)
-The lights suddenly went out.
}

最も-
{
最も (もっとも) - Most, extremely
An adverb used before adjectives to create the superlative degree (the "most").
Memory Tip: It sounds like "motto" (more) taken to the extreme limit.
Example: これが最も重要です。 (これがもっともじゅうようです)
-This is the most important.
}

〜うちに-
{
〜うちに (うちに) - while; before
Indicates that an action should be taken during a current state before that state changes.
Memory Tip: 'Uchi' means inside; perform the task while you are still 'inside' the opportunity.
Example: 温かいうちに食べてください。 (あたたかいうちにたべてください。)
-Please eat while it is still warm.
}

〜毎に-
{
〜毎に (〜ごとに) - Every time, each, at intervals of
A suffix added to nouns or dictionary form verbs to indicate frequency or repeating intervals.
Memory Tip: Go-to-ni: You 'go to' do it 'every' single time.
Example: 三日毎に掃除する。 (みっかごとにそうじする。)
-I clean every three days.
}

ご自由にどうぞ-
{
ご自由にどうぞ (ごじゆうにどうぞ) - Please help yourself / Feel free
A polite invitation to do something freely. 'Jiyuu' means freedom or liberty.
Memory Tip: 'Jiyuu' sounds like 'Free-you'; you are giving the person freedom to choose.
Example: サンプルを、ご自由にどうぞ。(さんぷるを、ごじゆうにどうぞ。)
-Please help yourself to a sample.
}

燃える-
{
燃える (もえる) - To burn, to get fired up
An intransitive verb used for physical fire or metaphorical passion and enthusiasm.
Memory Tip: Think of 'Moe' (passion for a character) to remember it means to burn.
Example: 紙が燃える。(かみがもえる。)
-Paper burns.
}

大きい順-
{
大きい順 (おおきいじゅん) - In descending order; largest first
A compound phrase combining the adjective "big" with the noun for "order" or "sequence."
Memory Tip: Think of it as "Large (大きい) + Sequence (順)" to remember it means biggest to smallest.
Example: 大きい順に並べてください。 (おおきいじゅんにならべてください。)
-Please arrange them in descending order.
}

味-
{
味 (あじ) - taste, flavor
Used for physical flavor but also metaphorically to describe style or 'savoring' an experience.
Memory Tip: Mouth (口) plus not yet (未). You haven't tasted it with your mouth yet.
Example: この料理はいい味がする。(このりょうりはいいあじがする。)
-This dish has a good taste.
}

脱ぐ-
{
脱ぐ (ぬぐ) - to take off (clothes, shoes)
A transitive verb used for removing any item that covers or wraps the body.
Memory Tip: Flesh (月) plus the part for 'removal' (兌). Removing things from your flesh.
Example: 靴を脱いでください。(くつをぬいでください。)
-Please take off your shoes.
}

雲-
{
雲 (くも) - cloud
A common noun used in weather descriptions and poetry.
Memory Tip: Rain (雨) radical over 'clouds/speaking' (云). Rain comes from the clouds.
Example: 空に白い雲がある。(そらにしろいくもがある。)
-There are white clouds in the sky.
}

直す-
{
直す (なおす) - To fix/To repair/To correct
A transitive verb that means to restore something to its original or proper state. It can apply to objects or mistakes.
Memory Tip: To make something straight (直) again after it has been bent or broken.
Example: 壊れた時計を直す。(こわれたとけいをなおす。)
-To fix a broken watch.
}

文-
{
文 (ぶん) - Sentence/Text/Literature
A foundational kanji representing patterns, writing, or refined culture. It is a single unit of written thought.
Memory Tip: Think of it as a person with markings or a tattoo, representing the first written patterns.
Example: この文を読んでください。(このぶんをよんでください。)
-Please read this sentence.
}

寺-
{
寺 (てら) - Temple
Specifically refers to a Buddhist temple. It is distinct from 'jinja' (Shinto shrine).
Memory Tip: Imagine 'earth' or 'soil' (土) at a place where 'measures/rules' (寸) are kept; a sacred foundation.
Example: 京都には古い寺が多い。 (きょうとにわふるいてらがおおい。)
-There are many old temples in Kyoto.
}

考え-
{
考え (かんがえ) - Thought, idea, or opinion
The noun form of the verb 'kangaeru' (to think), referring to the result of mental effort.
Memory Tip: This is the 'thinking' noun—what stays in your head after you ponder.
Example: いい考えがあります。 (いいかんがえがあります。)
-I have a good idea.
}

切れる-
{
切れる (きれる) - To be cut, to snap, to run out
An intransitive Ichidan verb meaning something physically breaks or a supply/time limit reaches its end.
Memory Tip: The passive form of 'kiru' (to cut); it's when something 'gets cut' or finishes on its own.
Example: 電池が切れました。 (でんちがきれました。)
-The battery has run out.
}

横-
{
横 (よこ) - Side, horizontal, beside
Refers to the horizontal direction or the immediate area beside an object.
Memory Tip: Tree (木) radical + yellow (黄); imagine a yellow tree log lying horizontally on its side.
Example: 彼は私の横に座った。 (かれはわたしのよこにすわった。)
-He sat beside me.
}

相談-
{
相談 (そうだん) - Consultation/Advice
This noun combines characters for mutual interaction and talking, implying seeking counsel or discussing a matter with someone.
Memory Tip: Think of two people mutually (相) talking (談) to solve a specific problem.
Example: 先生に相談しました。 (せんせいにそうだんしました。)
-I consulted with my teacher.
}

厳しい-
{
厳しい (きびしい) - Strict / Severe
An i-adjective used for strict people, harsh weather, or difficult circumstances.
Memory Tip: The kanji (厳) resembles a stern face or a rocky cliff – a cold, hard, and unyielding presence.
Example: 先生はとても厳しい (せんせいはとてもきびしい)
-The teacher is very strict
}

案内-
{
案内 (あんない) - Guidance; information
A noun or suru-verb meaning to lead the way or provide a tour.
Memory Tip: Showing someone the plan (案) for what is inside (内) a building.
Example: 街を案内しましょう。 (まちをあんないしましょう。)
-Let me show you around the town.
}

注意-
{
注意 (ちゅうい) - Caution; attention; warning
A noun/verb used to tell someone to be careful or to pay focus to something.
Memory Tip: Pour (注) your mind and intent (意) into the task to stay safe.
Example: 足元に注意してください。 (あしもとにちゅういしてください。)
-Please watch your step.
}

〜ように見える-
{
〜ように見える (ようにみえる) - To look like, to appear to be
A grammar structure combining 'you' (resemblance) and 'mieru' (to be seen) to express a subjective impression.
Memory Tip: 'You' means 'manner/way'. An object is 'seen' (mieru) in a certain 'way' (you).
Example: 彼は疲れているように見える。(かれはつかれているようにみえる。)
-He looks tired.
}

反対-
{
反対 (はんたい) - opposite, opposition
Used to describe the reverse side of something or to express disagreement.
Memory Tip: Han (anti) and Tai (versus) - standing against the current view.
Example: 案に反対する。 (あんにはんたいする。)
-To oppose the plan.
}

一時-
{
一時 (いちじ) - One o'clock / A short time
A noun that can refer to the specific time of 1:00 or a temporary/brief duration.
Memory Tip: 一 (one) + 時 (time). Think of the 'first' unit of time or a single moment.
Example: 一時、雨が降った。 (いちじ、あめがふった。)
-It rained for a short time.
}

拾う-
{
拾う (ひろう) - To pick up
This verb describes picking something up from the ground or gathering items that are scattered.
Memory Tip: Use your HAND (扌) to gather things TOGETHER (合) to pick them up.
Example: 道で財布を拾った (みちでさいふをひろった)
-I picked up a wallet on the street
}

広げる-
{
広げる (ひろげる) - To spread out; to widen
A transitive verb used when an actor extends, unfolds, or expands the physical size of something.
Memory Tip: To make something WIDE (広) by actively opening it up.
Example: 地図を机の上に広げる (ちずをつくえのうえにひろげる)
-To spread a map out on the desk
}

地球-
{
地球 (ちきゅう) - Earth
A noun specifically referring to the planet Earth as a celestial body.
Memory Tip: The GROUND (地) of our world is shaped like a giant SPHERE (球).
Example: 地球は太陽の周りを回る (ちきゅうはたいようのまわりをまわる)
-The Earth rotates around the sun
}

植える-
{
植える (うえる) - To plant
A transitive verb used for putting plants, trees, or seeds into the ground to grow.
Memory Tip: You set a TREE (木) STRAIGHT (直) into the soil to plant it.
Example: 庭にバラを植える (にわにばらをうえる)
-To plant roses in the garden
}

辺-
{
辺 (へん) - Area; vicinity; side
A noun used to indicate a general location or the side of a geometric shape like a triangle.
Memory Tip: The radical on the bottom-left means 'road/path' (⻌). It represents the area or space along a path.
Example: この三角形の辺の長さは等しい。 (このさんかっけいのへんのながさはひとしい。)
-The sides of this triangle are equal in length.
}

降ろす-
{
降ろす (おろす) - To take down; to unload; to drop off
A transitive u-verb used for moving something from a high place to a low place or letting a passenger out of a vehicle.
Memory Tip: The kanji 降 means 'descend'. Think of 'lowering' cargo from a truck or 'descending' a person from a car.
Example: 荷物を棚から降ろしてください。 (にもつをたなからおろしてください。)
-Please take the luggage down from the shelf.
}

〜ないと-
{
〜ないと (ないと) - Must / have to
This is a casual contraction of "〜ないと いけない", expressing obligation through a conditional "if not..."
Memory Tip: Think of "night" — I "must" get home before "night" falls.
Example: 早く行かないと。 (はやく いかないと。)
-I must go quickly.
}

出発-
{
出発 (しゅっぱつ) - Departure
Formed by "exit" (出) and "emit/start" (発), used for starting a journey or leaving a place.
Memory Tip: "Shu" (Shoot) out of the station to "Patsu" (Pass) the starting line.

-I will depart tomorrow.
}

飾る-
{
飾る (かざる) - To decorate
A Godan verb used for physical decoration or figurative embellishment. It implies making something look more attractive.

真っ直ぐ-
{
真っ直ぐ (まっすぐ) - Straight ahead
Used as an adverb or na-adjective for physical direction or as a metaphor for an honest, direct personality.

今回-
{
今回 (こんかい) - This time
A common temporal noun used to distinguish the current occurrence from previous or future ones. It is slightly more formal than 'kondo'.
Memory Tip: Now (今) + Rotation/Times (回) = the time that is happening right now.

-I will pay this time.

男性-
{
男性 (だんせい) - Male / man
A formal noun used to refer to the male gender in general.

-He is a young man.

失敗-
{
失敗 (しっぱい) - failure, mistake
'Shitsu' (lose/miss) + 'hai' (defeat). It refers to an unsuccessful attempt or an error made during a task.
Memory Tip: You lose (shitsu) the game and face defeat (hai) - that is a failure.
Example: 失敗を恐れてはいけない。 (しっぱいをおそれてはいけない。)

失敗する-
{
失敗する (しっぱいする) - To fail
This is a suru-verb formed by the noun 失敗 (failure) combined with する (to do). It describes failing a task, exam, or goal.
Memory Tip: Combine 失 (loss) and 敗 (defeat) to remember the feeling of losing due to a defeat.
Example: 彼は試験に失敗した。 (かれはしけんにしっぱいした。)
-He failed the exam.
}

枝-
{
枝 (えだ) - Branch, twig
A noun referring to the woody parts of a tree that grow out from the trunk.
Memory Tip: The tree radical (木) is on the left, and the right side (支) means to support or branch out.
Example: 木の枝が折れた。 (きのえだがおれた。)
-The tree branch broke.
}

骨-
{
骨 (ほね) - Bone
A noun referring to the skeletal structure of a body or the core framework of something.
Memory Tip: Think of 'honey' (hone) helping your bones grow strong; the kanji shows a bone structure inside flesh.

具合-
{
具合 (ぐあい) - Condition/Health
Refers to the physical condition of a person or the operational state of a machine.
Memory Tip: 'Gu' (ingredients) 'ai' (match) – when the ingredients match well, the condition is good.
Example: 体の具合はどうですか？(からだのぐあいはどうですか？)

旗-
{
旗 (はた) - Flag
A noun for a banner or flag. The kanji includes the radical for 'direction/banner' (方).

-The flag is swaying in the wind.

人形-
{
人形 (にんぎょう) - Doll; figure
Literally "person" (人) plus "shape" (形).

恥ずかしい-
{
恥ずかしい (はずかしい) - Embarrassed / Shy
An i-adjective used for social discomfort, shyness, or a sense of shame.
Memory Tip: The kanji for shame (恥) combines ear (耳) and heart (心); your ears feel your heartbeat when you are embarrassed.
Example: 恥ずかしくて顔が赤くなった。 (はずかしくてかおがあかくなった。)
-I was embarrassed and my face turned red.

予定-
{
予定 (よてい) - Schedule / Plan
A noun referring to a pre-determined arrangement or an expected event.
Memory Tip: Deciding (定) things beforehand (予) creates your schedule.

-What is your schedule for tomorrow?
}

慣れる-
{
慣れる (なれる) - To get used to / To become accustomed
An intransitive Ichidan verb used when someone becomes familiar with a situation or environment.
Memory Tip: Your heart (忄) becomes pierced (貫) by a habit until it feels natural.
Example: 新しい仕事に慣れました。 (あたらしいしごとになれました。)
-I got used to my new job.
}

届ける-
{
届ける (とどける) - To deliver, to notify
A transitive verb used for physical delivery of items or the formal reporting of information to authorities.
Memory Tip: The radical for 'corpse/house' (尸) over 'arrival' (至). You ensure an item arrives at its house.
Example: 荷物を家に届ける。 (にもつをいえにとどける。)
-Deliver the package to the house.

機械-
{
機械 (きかい) - Machine
A noun used for mechanical devices or apparatus. Both kanji include the 'wood' radical, hinting at historical wooden machinery.
Memory Tip: A mechanism (機) and a contraption (械) combined create a machine.
Example: この機械は故障している。 (このきかいはこしょうしている。)
-This machine is broken.

発表-
{
発表 (はっぴょう) - Announcement / Presentation
Combines 'emit/start' (発) with 'surface/table' (表). It means to bring information to the public surface.
Memory Tip: 'Emitting' (発) information onto a 'table' (表) for everyone to see.
Example: 明日、クラスで発表をします。(あした、くらすではっぴょうをします。)
-I will give a presentation in class tomorrow.
}

矢-
{
矢 (や) - Arrow
A pictographic kanji that represents a traditional arrow. It is often used in metaphors for speed.
Memory Tip: The character 矢 literally looks like an arrow with a head and fletching.
Example: 矢のように月日が過ぎ去る。 (やのようにつきひがすぎさる。)

高校-
{
高校 (こうこう) - High school
A common noun that is an abbreviation of the full term 高等学校 (koutougakkou).
Memory Tip: High (高) level School (校). It is the school building that represents the high level of basic education.
Example: 彼は高校に通っている。 (かれはこうこうにかよっている。)
-He is attending high school.
}

工場-
{
工場 (こうじょう) - Factory, workshop
A noun referring to a site where manufacturing or industrial production takes place.
Memory Tip: The place (場) where manual work or construction (工) is performed.
Example: 父は自動車工場で働いている。 (ちちはじどうしゃこうじょうではたらいています。)
-My father works at a car factory.
}

聴く-
{
聴く (きく) - To listen (attentively)
Unlike 聞く (to hear), this version implies active, focused listening like to music or a lecture.
Memory Tip: This complex kanji for 聴 contains the radicals for "ear" (耳) and "heart" (心).
Example: 音楽を聴く。 (おんがくをきく。)
-Listen to music.
}

育つ-
{
育つ (そだつ) - To grow up / be raised
An intransitive verb; the transitive counterpart is 育てる (そだてる) which means "to raise."
Memory Tip: The top part of 育 looks like a child (子) being held or flipped during growth.
Example: 田舎で育つ。 (いなかでそだつ。)
-Grow up in the countryside.
}

明かり-
{
明かり (あかり) - Light / Lamplight
A noun referring to physical light coming from a source like a lamp, or the state of being lit.
Memory Tip: Formed from the kanji for bright (明) which combines the sun (日) and the moon (月).
Example: 部屋の明かりを消す。 (へやのあかりをけす。)
-Turn off the light in the room.
}

勤める-
{
勤める (つとめる) - to work (for), to be employed
Used when referring to employment at a specific organization, typically followed by the particle 'ni'.
Memory Tip: The right side is 'power/effort' (力), needed to work your job every day.
Example: 兄はIT企業に勤めています。 (あにはあいてぃーきぎょうにつとめています。)
-My older brother works for an IT company.
}

課長-
{
課長 (かちょう) - Section manager
This noun combines 課 (section) and 長 (head/chief). It is a common middle-management rank in Japanese corporate hierarchy.
Memory Tip: The head (長) of the specific department section (課) is your manager.
Example: 課長に書類を提出しました。(かちょうにしょるいをていしゅつしました。)
-I submitted the documents to the section manager.
}

風景-
{
風景 (ふうけい) - Scenery/Landscape
A noun used to describe visible natural or urban scenes, often with an aesthetic focus.
Memory Tip: 'Wind' (風) and 'View/Bright' (景). Think of a scenery so vast you can feel the wind moving through the view.
Example: 窓からの風景は美しい。 (まどからのふうけいはうつくしい。)
-The scenery from the window is beautiful.
}

幽霊-
{
幽霊 (ゆうれい) - Ghost, phantom
Refers to the spirits of the dead that remain in this world due to strong emotions like grudge or love.
Memory Tip: 幽 (faint/dark) + 霊 (spirit). A dark spirit that is barely visible.
Example: 幽霊なんて信じない。 (ゆうれいなんてしんじない。)
-I don't believe in ghosts.
}

癖-
{
癖 (くせ) - Habit, quirk
Usually refers to negative, peculiar, or unconscious personal habits and mannerisms.
Memory Tip: Includes the sickness radical (疒), suggesting a habit is like a small recurring 'affliction' of the body.
Example: 爪を噛む癖がある。 (つめをかむくせがある。)
-I have a habit of biting my nails.
}

太鼓-
{
太鼓 (たいこ) - Drum
A noun specifically referring to traditional Japanese drums, though it can apply to drums in general.
Memory Tip: A 'thick' (太) sound made by striking a 'drum' (鼓) skin.
Example: 祭りで太鼓を叩く。(まつりでたいこをたたく。)
-I play the drum at the festival.
}

体験-
{
体験 (たいけん) - Personal experience
A noun or suru-verb that emphasizes first-hand, physical experience rather than theoretical knowledge.
Memory Tip: Using your own body (体) to test or verify (験) the world.
Example: 留学は良い体験だ。(りゅうがくはよいたいけんだ。)
-Studying abroad is a good experience.
}

お嬢さん-
{
お嬢さん (おじょうさん) - Young lady / Someone's daughter
A polite way to refer to another person's daughter or a well-bred young woman.
Memory Tip: The honorific "O" and suffix "san" sandwich the core word for a refined daughter.
Example: 綺麗なお嬢さんですね。 (きれいなおじょうさんですね。)
-What a beautiful young lady.
}

侍-
{
侍 (さむらい) - Samurai
Refers to the ancient Japanese warrior class. The verb root means "to serve."
Memory Tip: A person (亻) standing by a temple (寺) to serve their lord.
Example: 侍は刀を持っている。 (さむらいはかたなをもっている。)
-The samurai has a sword.
}

種類-
{
種類 (しゅるい) - Variety, kind, type
Used to categorize objects or concepts based on shared traits.
Memory Tip: Seeds (種) are organized into different classes or categories (類).
Example: 公園には多くの種類の花がある。 (こうえんにはおおくのしゅるいのはながある。)
-There are many kinds of flowers in the park.
}

故郷-
{
故郷 (こきょう) - Hometown, birthplace
A formal term for one's native place; it carries a nuance of nostalgia.
Memory Tip: The old (故) village (郷) that you call home.
Example: 彼は十数年ぶりに故郷に帰った。 (かれはじゅうすうねんぶりにこきょうにかえった。)
-He returned to his hometown for the first time in over ten years.
}

帯-
{
帯 (おび) - belt, sash
Refers primarily to the wide sash worn with a kimono, but also used for zones or bands of data.
Memory Tip: The kanji looks like layers of cloth or a long belt being wrapped around a waist.
Example: 帯を締める。 (おびをしめる。)
-To tie a sash.
}

学ぶ-
{
学ぶ (まなぶ) - To learn/study
A Godan verb that implies taking lessons or acquiring knowledge through experience, often more formal than 'benkyou suru'.
Memory Tip: The kanji shows a child (子) under a roof, representing a school environment for learning.
Example: 経験から多くのことを学ぶ。 (けいけんからおおくのことをまなぶ。)
-I learn many things from experience.
}

会議-
{
会議 (かいぎ) - Meeting/Conference
This noun combines 'meeting' (会) and 'deliberation' (議). It is used for formal discussions in business or politics.
Memory Tip: A 'gathering' (会) specifically held to 'discuss' (議) important matters.
Example: 会議は午後三時に始まる。 (かいぎはごごさんじにはじまる。)
-The meeting starts at 3:00 PM.
}

建てる-
{
建てる (たてる) - To build/construct
A transitive Ichidan verb specifically used for constructing large structures like houses, buildings, or monuments.
Memory Tip: The 'brush' radical (聿) inside suggests drawing up architectural plans before building.
Example: 彼は新しい家を建てた。 (かれはあたらしいいえをたてた。)
-He built a new house.
}

思い出-
{
思い出 (おもいで) - Memory, recollection
A noun derived from the compound verb 'omoidasu' (to recall), referring to an event remembered.
Memory Tip: Thought (思い) + Coming out (出). A thought that comes out from your past.
Example: 夏休みのいい思い出。 (なつやすみのいいおもいで。)
-A good memory of summer vacation.
}

布団-
{
布団 (ふとん) - Futon/Bedding
A compound of 'cloth' (布) and 'group/round' (団). It refers to the traditional Japanese style of bedding consisting of a mattress and duvet.
Memory Tip: A large piece of 'cloth' (布) folded into a 'grouping' (団) or pile for sleeping.
Example: 毎朝、布団を畳みます。(まいあさ、ふとんをたたみます。)
-I fold the futon every morning.
}

高さ-
{
高さ (たかさ) - Height
The noun form of the i-adjective 'takai' (high/tall), created by replacing the final 'i' with the suffix '-sa' to indicate degree.
Memory Tip: Start with 'Takai' (High) and add '-sa' to turn the description into a measurable quality.
Example: この山の高さはどのくらいですか？(このやまのたかさはどのくらいですか？)
-How high is this mountain?
}

無くす-
{
無くす (なくす) - To lose something
A transitive verb used when you physically lose an object or cause something to disappear. It is the active counterpart to the intransitive "nakunaru."
Memory Tip: You might cry (naku) because you "lost" (nakusu) something important.
Example: 鍵を無くした (かぎをなくした)
-I lost my keys.
}

まずい-
{
まずい (まずい) - Bad-tasting, awkward, problematic
An i-adjective most commonly used for unpleasant food, but also figuratively for situations that have gone wrong. It is the opposite of "oishii."
Memory Tip: If the food is so bad you "must" spit it out, it is "mazui."
Example: このスープはまずい (このすーぷはまずい)
-This soup tastes bad.
}

港-
{
港 (みなと) - Port/Harbor
A noun for a place where ships dock, containing the water radical (氵).
Memory Tip: Look for the water (氵) on the left of a busy area where ships gather.
Example: 船が港に入ってきた。 (ふねがみなとにはいってきた。)
-The ship entered the port.
}

決定-
{
決定 (けってい) - Decision, determination
This is a noun used to describe a final decision or a settled matter. It combines 'decide' (決) and 'fix/settle' (定).
Memory Tip: To decide (決) and then fix (定) it in place means a final decision is made.
Example: 新しい計画の決定が遅れている。 (あたらしいけいかくのけっていがおくれている。)
-The decision on the new plan is being delayed.
}

決定する-
{
決定する (けっていする) - To decide, to determine
This is the verb form of 決定, created by adding the helper verb 'suru'. It is used for formal or firm decisions.
Memory Tip: Take the noun for decision (決定) and 'do' (する) it to make it an active choice.
Example: 卒業旅行の行き先を決定する。 (そつぎょうりょこうのいきさきをけっていする。)
-We will decide the destination for the graduation trip.
}

赤ん坊-
{
赤ん坊 (あかんぼう) - Baby; infant
A common noun for a baby, named after the flushed red color typical of a newborn's skin.
Memory Tip: Red (赤) baby boy (坊) - newborns are often red in the face when crying.
Example: 赤ん坊が泣いている (あかんぼうがないている)
-The baby is crying.
}

使用-
{
使用 (しよう) - Use; application; employment
A formal word meaning to put something to use, such as tools, rooms, or equipment.
Memory Tip: Using (使) for a specific task or business (用).
Example: 携帯電話の使用は禁止です (けいたいでんわのしようはきんしです)
-Use of mobile phones is prohibited.
}

感動-
{
感動 (かんどう) - Deep emotion/Impression
A noun representing being moved emotionally, combining "feeling" and "movement."
Memory Tip: Your "feelings" (感) are physically "moving" (動) within you because you are touched.
Example: その映画は多くの人に感動を与えた。 (そのえいがはおおくのひとにかんどうをあたえた。)
-That movie moved many people.
}

湖-
{
湖 (みずうみ) - Lake
A noun referring to a large body of water, often surrounded by land.
Memory Tip: Visualize "water" (氵) reflecting the "old" (古) "moon" (月) over a quiet lake.
Example: 湖のほとりを歩いた。 (みずうみのほとりをあるいた。)
-I walked along the shore of the lake.
}

感動する-
{
感動する (かんどうする) - To be moved/touched
The suru-verb form of the noun 感動, used to describe the act of experiencing a strong emotional impact.
Memory Tip: Simply add "to do" (する) to the idea of "moving feelings" (感動).
Example: 彼のスピーチに感動した。 (かれのすぴーちにかんどうした。)
-I was moved by his speech.
}

得意-
{
得意 (とくい) - To be good at/One's forte
Refers to a skill one excels in and feels confident or prideful about.
Memory Tip: To obtain (得) your own idea/meaning (意) is to be naturally good at it.
Example: 料理が得意です。 (りょうりがとくいです。)
-I am good at cooking.
}

たまに-
{
たまに (たまに) - Occasionally/Once in a while
An adverb used for events that happen with very low frequency.
Memory Tip: Think of a rare "gem" (玉 - tama) that you only find once in a while.
Example: たまに映画を見ます。 (たまにえいがをみます。)
-I occasionally watch movies.
}

生える-
{
生える (はえる) - To grow, to sprout
An intransitive verb used for natural growth like hair, teeth, or plants emerging from a surface.
Memory Tip: Think of life (生) springing up from the ground like a sprout.
Example: ひげが生える。 (ひげがはえる。)
-A beard grows.
}

次々-
{
次々 (つぎつぎ) - One after another, in succession
An adverbial phrase used to indicate a continuous and rapid sequence of events.
Memory Tip: The kanji for 'next' (次) is doubled with (々) to show a sequence.
Example: 次々と問題が起こる。 (つぎつぎともんだいがおこる。)
-Problems occur one after another.
}

小声-
{
小声 (こごえ) - Whisper, low voice
A compound noun consisting of 'small' (小) and 'voice' (声).
Memory Tip: When you keep your voice (声) very small (小), it becomes a whisper.
Example: 小声で話してください。 (こごえではなしてください。)
-Please speak in a low voice.
}

〜病-
{
〜病 (〜びょう) - ...disease, ...illness
A suffix added to a noun to specify a particular sickness or condition.
Memory Tip: The kanji contains the sickness radical (疒); it's the specific type of illness someone has.
Example: 彼は心臓病を患っている。 (かれはしんぞうびょうをわずらっている。)
-He is suffering from heart disease.
}

宝石-
{
宝石 (ほうせき) - Gem, jewel
A compound of 宝 (treasure) and 石 (stone), literally meaning a 'treasure stone'.
Memory Tip: A treasure (宝) that is also a stone (石) is a sparkling gem.
Example: 彼女は宝石を集めている。 (かのじょはほうせきをあつめている)
-She collects jewels.
}

場面-
{
場面 (ばめん) - Scene, setting
Used for a specific scene in a play or movie, or a particular situation or context in real life.

-It was a moving scene.

褒める-
{
褒める (ほめる) - To praise, to compliment
A transitive verb used when an equal or superior expresses admiration for someone's actions.

-The teacher praised the child.

奴ら-
{
奴ら (やつら) - They / Those guys
A casual, often derogatory plural pronoun. '奴' (guy) combined with the pluralizer 'ら'.

Example: 奴らを信じるな。(やつらをしんじるな。)
-Don't trust those guys.

嫁-
{
嫁 (よめ) - Bride / Daughter-in-law
Refers to a woman who has married into a family or a son's wife.

数字-
{
数字 (すうじ) - number / digit
Combines 'count/number' (数) and 'character' (字), referring to the symbols used for counting.

-Write down the numbers.

拭く-
{
拭く (ふく) - to wipe, to dry
A transitive godan verb. It uses the hand radical (扌), indicating physical action.
Memory Tip: You use your hand (扌) to wipe (拭く) the dust off a surface.

〜倍-
{
〜倍 (〜ばい) - ...times (multiplier), double/triple
A counter suffix used to indicate multiplication or an increase in quantity. 二倍 (nibai) means double, while 三倍 (sanbai) means triple.
Memory Tip: Look at the radical for 'person' (亻) standing next to 'mouth' (口) - a person announcing things are being multiplied.
Example: 値段が二倍になった。(ねだんがにばいになった。)
-The price has doubled.

大体-
{
大体 (だいたい) - Mostly, roughly, outline
Literally meaning "big body," this adverb/noun refers to the gist or the majority of something.

世話-
{
世話 (せわ) - Care, looking after
A noun often used with the verb 'suru' (to take care of) or 'ni naru' (to be cared for).

直前-

直前 (ちょくぜん) - Just before

枕-

運-

〜鍋-

〜鍋 (〜なべ) - ...pot / ...stew (suffix)

鍋-
{
鍋 (なべ) - Pot / pan / hot pot
Refers to the cooking vessel itself or the communal meal cooked inside it.

臭い-
{
臭い (くさい) - Stinky / smelly
An adjective used for unpleasant odors or, metaphorically, for something suspicious.

松-

松 (まつ) - pine tree
A noun for the evergreen tree that is a symbol of longevity and the New Year in Japan.

-There is a magnificent pine tree.

強力-
{
強力 (きょうりょく) - Powerful/Strong
A na-adjective combining 強 (strong) and 力 (power), used for intensity, effectiveness, or physical strength.
Memory Tip: Imagine a bow (強) combined with pure muscle power (力) to create something unstoppable.

名刺-
{
名刺 (めいし) - Business card
This is a formal noun essential for professional introductions in Japan.
Memory Tip: 名 (name) + 刺 (to pierce/thorn). Think of a card that "stabs" your name into someone's memory.

封筒-
{
封筒 (ふうとう) - Envelope
A common noun for the paper container used to send letters.
Memory Tip: 封 (seal) + 筒 (tube/cylinder). Long ago, messages were sealed inside bamboo tubes.

携帯-
{
携帯 (けいたい) - Portable/Mobile phone
Originally meaning "to carry on one's person," it is now the standard shorthand for a cell phone.

-I forgot my mobile phone at home.

選択-
{
選択 (せんたく) - selection, choice
A noun meaning a choice between multiple options, often in formal or technical contexts.

選択する-
{
選択する (せんたくする) - to choose, to select
The verb form of 選択, used for making a formal choice between items or paths.

都会-
{
都会 (とかい) - City/Urban area
Refers to large, bustling metropolitan areas. It combines 都 (capital/metropolis) and 会 (meeting place).

毛布-
{
毛布 (もうふ) - Blanket
A noun composed of 毛 (hair/fur/wool) and 布 (cloth). Usually refers to thick, warm blankets.

羊-
{
羊 (ひつじ) - Sheep
A simple noun. The kanji is a pictograph of a sheep's head with horns and a snout.

親友-
{
親友 (しんゆう) - Best friend
Combines 'intimacy/parent' (親) and 'friend' (友) to describe a very close, platonic bond.

粉-
{
粉 (こな) - Powder/Flour
Refers to fine particles, commonly used for wheat flour or dust. It is a common noun in culinary and industrial contexts.
Memory Tip: Rice (米) is split into many parts (分) until it becomes fine powder.
Example: 小麦粉を使ってパンを焼く。 (こむぎこをつかってぱんをやく。)
-Use wheat flour to bake bread.
}

跳ぶ-
{
跳ぶ (とぶ) - To jump/To leap
Specifically used for jumping off the ground using legs, as opposed to 飛ぶ which usually means flying.
Memory Tip: The leg radical (⻊) on the left shows this 'tobu' is done with your feet.
Example: 彼は柵を軽々と跳んだ。 (かれはさくをかるがるととんだ。)
-He jumped over the fence lightly.
}

下着-
{
下着 (したぎ) - Underwear
A compound noun literally meaning "below" (下) and "wearing/clothes" (着).
Memory Tip: It is the clothing (着) that you wear below (下) your main outfit.
Example: 下着を買いに行きました。 (したぎをかいにいきました。)
-I went to buy underwear.
}

指輪-
{
指輪 (ゆびわ) - Ring (jewelry)
A compound noun combining "finger" (指) and "hoop/circle" (輪).
Memory Tip: A simple hoop (輪) specifically designed to go on your finger (指).
Example: 綺麗な指輪をはめている。 (きれいなゆびわをはめている。)
-She is wearing a beautiful ring.
}

用事-
{
用事 (ようじ) - Errand, business, things to do
Combines 用 (use/task) and 事 (matter/thing). It is used for general chores or appointments.
Memory Tip: These are matters (事) that use (用) up your schedule.
Example: 今日は用事があります。(きょうはようじがあります)
-I have things to do today.
}

銀色-
{
銀色 (ぎんいろ) - Silver (color)
A compound noun made of 'silver' and 'color', specifically describing the metallic silver hue.
Memory Tip: The 'metal' radical (金) in the character for silver (銀) identifies its origin.
Example: 彼女は銀色の車を選んだ。 (かのじょはぎんいろのくるまをえらんだ。)
-She chose a silver car.
}

九州-
{
九州 (きゅうしゅう) - Kyushu
The name of the southernmost of Japan's four main islands, literally meaning 'nine provinces'.
Memory Tip: Combine the number 'nine' (九) with the character for 'province' or 'state' (州).
Example: 九州は温泉で有名です。 (きゅうしゅうはおんせんでゆうめいです。)
-Kyushu is famous for its hot springs.
}

人数-
{
人数 (にんずう) - Number of people
Combines 人 (person) and 数 (number). Note the irregular reading "ninzuu" instead of "nin-suu."
Memory Tip: Count the "nin" (person) to get the total "suu" (number).
Example: 参加者の人数を確認してください。 (さんかしゃのにんずうをかくにんしてください。)
-Please confirm the number of participants.
}

昼食-
{
昼食 (ちゅうしょく) - Lunch
A formal word combining 昼 (midday/noon) and 食 (meal/food).
Memory Tip: Midday (昼) eating (食) is the definition of lunch.
Example: 一緒に昼食を食べませんか。 (いっしょにちゅうしょくをたべませんか。)
-Won't you have lunch with me?
}

勧める-
{
勧める (すすめる) - To recommend
Used when suggesting an action or item to someone because you think it is beneficial.
Memory Tip: Use your 'power' (力) to help a 'bird' (隹) decide which way to fly.
Example: 先生がこの本を勧めました。 (せんせいがこのほんをすすめました。)
-The teacher recommended this book.
}

芋-
{
芋 (いも) - Potato/Tuber
A general term for starchy root vegetables like potatoes, yams, and taro.
Memory Tip: The top is 'grass' (艹) and the bottom represents a bulbous root growing underground.
Example: 焼き芋を食べたい (やきいもをたべたい)
-I want to eat a roasted sweet potato.
}

駐車場-
{
駐車場 (ちゅうしゃじょう) - Parking lot
This noun combines 駐 (parking/staying), 車 (car), and 場 (place). It describes a designated area where vehicles are kept.
Memory Tip: A place (場) where cars (車) stay (駐) while you shop.
Example: 駐車場はどこですか？ (ちゅうしゃじょうはどこですか？)
-Where is the parking lot?
}

建つ-
{
建つ (たつ) - To be built/To stand
An intransitive verb describing a building or structure that has been erected or is currently standing.
Memory Tip: Once a building is built (建つ), it stands tall on the ground.
Example: 新しい家が建った。 (あたらしいいえがたった。)
-A new house was built.
}

苦手-
{
苦手 (にがて) - Poor at/Dislike
This na-adjective refers to something one is not good at or finds hard to deal with.
Memory Tip: When your "Hand" (手) touches something "Bitter" (苦), you naturally become poor at handling it.
Example: 私は数学が苦手です。 (わたしはすうがくがにがてです。)
-I am bad at math.
}

腕時計-
{
腕時計 (うでどけい) - Wristwatch
A compound noun joining 'ude' (arm) and 'tokei' (clock).
Memory Tip: A literal "Time-measurer" (時計) worn on the "Arm/Wrist" (腕).
Example: 新しい腕時計を買いました。 (あたらしいうでどけいをかいました。)
-I bought a new wristwatch.
}

辞める-
{
辞める (やめる) - To quit / To resign
Specifically used when leaving a job, position, or official role.
Memory Tip: You use 'words' (辞) to formally resign from your duties.
Example: 彼は来月会社を辞める。 (かれはらいげつかいしゃをやめる。)
-He is quitting the company next month.
}

温泉-
{
温泉 (おんせん) - Hot spring
A noun referring to natural hot springs, a staple of Japanese relaxation culture.
Memory Tip: Think of "Warm" (温) water bubbling from a "Spring/Fountain" (泉).
Example: 温泉でゆっくり休む。 (おんせんでゆっくりやすむ。)
-Relax and rest at a hot spring.
}

主婦-
{
主婦 (しゅふ) - Housewife
A noun referring to a woman whose main occupation is managing the home.
Memory Tip: The "Main/Master" (主) "Woman/Lady" (婦) of the household.
Example: 私の母は専業主婦です。 (わたしのはははせんぎょうしゅふです。)
-My mother is a full-time housewife.
}

叔母-
{
叔母 (おば) - Aunt (younger than parent)
Specifically used for an aunt who is the younger sister of one's parent; for an older sister, use 伯母.
Memory Tip: The "junior" (叔) mother (母) figure.
Example: 私の叔母は看護師です。 (わたしのおばはかんごしです。)
-My aunt is a nurse.
}

奥様-
{
奥様 (おくさま) - (Someone else's) wife
An honorific term literally meaning 'person in the inner part' of the house.
Memory Tip: The 'sama' (polite) person in the 'inner' (oku) room.
Example: 田中さんの奥様は親切です (たなかさんのおくさまはしんせつです)
-Mr. Tanaka's wife is kind.
}

締める-
{
締める (しめる) - To tie, to tighten
An Ichidan verb used for fastening belts, neckties, or tightening one's focus.
Memory Tip: Think of 'tightening' a 'sheet' (shi) over a 'mesh' (me).
Example: ネクタイを締める (ねくたいをしめる)
-To tie a necktie.
}

配る-
{
配る (くばる) - To distribute, to hand out
Explanation: Used for the physical act of handing things out to multiple people, or figuratively like in 'attention' (気配り).
Memory Tip: Imagine a cook (配 contains the radical for wine/jar) handing out drinks to everyone.
Example: 先生がプリントを配る。 (せんせいがぷりんとをくばる。)
-The teacher hands out the handouts.
}

大統領-
{
大統領 (だいとうりょう) - President
The title for the head of state in a republic. It consists of 'Big', 'Command', and 'Territory'.
Memory Tip: The 'Big' (大) leader who 'Commands' (統) the 'Territory' (領) is the President.
Example: アメリカの大統領が演説した。(あめりかのだいとうりょうがえんぜつした。)
-The President of the United States gave a speech.

手帳-
{
手帳 (てちょう) - Notebook / Planner
A pocket-sized personal organizer. It combines 'hand' (手) and 'ledger/curtain' (帳).
Memory Tip: A Hand (手) sized Ledger (帳) used to record your schedule.
Example: 手帳に予定を書く。 (てちょうによていをかく。)
-Write a schedule in the notebook.
}

番組-
{
番組 (ばんぐみ) - TV program
Refers to a broadcast show or program. '番' indicates a turn or number, and '組' means a set or group.
Memory Tip: A Group (組) of segments that take their Numbered Turn (番) on screen.

-Watch an interesting program.

家具-
{
家具 (かぐ) - Furniture
A general term for household items like tables and chairs. It literally translates to 'house tools'.

-Buy new furniture.

上司-
{
上司 (じょうし) - Boss / Superior
Refers to someone in a higher rank at a company. '上' means above and '司' means to administer.

Example: 上司に報告する。 (じょうしにほうこくする。)

祝う-
{
祝う (いわう) - To celebrate, to congratulate
A transitive verb. The kanji contains the radical for deity (示) and the radical for older brother (兄).
Memory Tip: The older brother (兄) prays to a deity (示) to celebrate a special occasion.
Example: 友達の誕生日を祝う。(ともだちのたんじょうびをいわう。)
-Celebrate a friend's birthday.

怖がる-
{
怖がる (こわがる) - To be afraid, to show fear
Combines the adjective "kowai" (scary) with "-garu," a suffix for describing someone else's outward feelings.
Memory Tip: Use "garu" when you see someone else "acting" scared.
Example: 妹は暗闇を怖がる。 (いもうとはくらやみをこわがる。)
-My younger sister is afraid of the dark.

刃物-
{
刃物 (はもの) - Edged tool/Cutlery
A general noun encompassing any tool with a blade, such as knives or scissors.

照明-
{
照明 (しょうめい) - Lighting, illumination
Refers to the equipment or the light used to illuminate a space.

地理-
{
地理 (ちり) - Geography
Combines the kanji for earth/ground (地) and logic/reason (理).

傾ける-
{
傾ける (かたむける) - To tilt / To lean
A transitive verb used for physical tilting or figuratively for 'listening intently' (leaning one's ear).
Memory Tip: The right side of the kanji looks like a head (頁), which you tilt when you are thinking or listening.
Example: 彼は首を傾けた。(かれはくびをかたむけた。)
-He tilted his head.
}

境-
{
境 (さかい) - Border / Boundary
A noun referring to a physical boundary, a border between regions, or a psychological turning point.
Memory Tip: Combines 'earth' (土) and 'region' (竟); a boundary is where the earth of one region ends.
Example: 川が二つの町の境になっている。(かわがふたつのまちのさかいになっている。)

歓迎-
{
歓迎 (かんげい) - Welcome, reception
A noun or Suru-verb used to express a warm greeting to a guest or newcomer.
Memory Tip: To greet (迎) someone with a feeling of joy and pleasure (歓) is to welcome them.
Example: 新入生を歓迎するパーティーを開いた。 (しんにゅうせいをかんげいするぱーてぃーをひらいた。)
-We held a party to welcome the new students.
}

〜宅-
{
〜宅 (たく) - House, home, residence
A formal or polite suffix attached to a name to refer to someone's home.
Memory Tip: The roof radical (宀) over a person represents their dwelling or residence.
Example: 田中さんの宅を訪問した。 (たなかさんのたくをほうもんした。)
-I visited Mr. Tanaka's house.

演技-
{
演技 (えんぎ) - Acting, performance
A noun describing the display of skill in a play, movie, or sporting event.

-His acting was wonderful.
}

大気-
{
大気 (たいき) - Atmosphere
Refers to the large body of air or gas surrounding the Earth or another planet.

-Air pollution is becoming a problem.

正義-
{
正義 (せいぎ) - Justice
This noun combines 'correct' (正) and 'righteousness' (義) to describe moral uprightness.
Memory Tip: True justice happens when people are 'Correct' (正) and 'Righteous' (義).
Example: 正義のために戦う。 (せいぎのためにたたかう。)
-Fight for justice.
}

大会-
{
大会 (たいかい) - Convention, tournament, rally
A noun used for large-scale gatherings, ranging from sports competitions to large political meetings.
Memory Tip: Big (大) + Meeting (会). Literally a 'big meeting' or gathering.
Example: 水泳大会に出場する (すいえいたいかいにしゅつじょうする)
-Participate in a swimming tournament
}

国内の-
{
国内の (こくないの) - Domestic/Internal
Combines 国 (country) and 内 (inside) with the possessive particle の.
Memory Tip: Anything located 'inside' (内) the borders of the 'country' (国).
Example: 国内の需要が高まっている。(こくないのじゅようがたかまっている。)
-Domestic demand is increasing.

治る-
{
治る (なおる) - To be cured/to get well
An intransitive verb specifically used for recovery from sickness or injury.
Memory Tip: When your sickness (疒) is governed/controlled (治), you get well.
Example: 風邪がようやく治った。(かぜがようやくなおった。)
-The cold finally got better.
}

体重-
{
体重 (たいじゅう) - Body weight
Combines 体 (body) and 重 (heavy/weight).
Memory Tip: The 'heavy' (重) measure of your physical 'body' (体).
Example: 毎朝、体重を測ります。(まいあさ、たいじゅうをはかります。)
-I measure my body weight every morning.
}

凍る-
{
凍る (こおる) - To freeze
An intransitive verb describing the process of a liquid turning solid due to cold.
Memory Tip: "Kooru" sounds like "cool"—when it gets extremely cool, things freeze.
Example: 湖が厚く凍っている。(みずうみがあつくこおっている。)
-The lake is frozen thick.
}

悪口-
{
悪口 (わるぐち) - Bad-mouthing/Abuse
A compound word of 悪 (bad) and 口 (mouth) used for speaking ill of someone.
Memory Tip: Very literal: using your "mouth" (口) to say "bad" (悪) things.
Example: 人の悪口を言ってはいけない。(ひとをわるぐちをいってはいけない。)
-You shouldn't speak ill of others.

出張-
{
出張 (しゅっちょう) - Business trip
A compound of 'going out' (出) and 'stretching/expanding' (張). It refers to leaving one's main office to conduct work elsewhere.
Memory Tip: Exit (出) the office to extend (張) your business reach.

-I will go on a business trip to Osaka next week.

引っ越す-
{
引っ越す (ひっこす) - To move (house/office)
A compound verb consisting of 'pull' (引く) and 'cross over' (越す). It describes the physical act of changing residences.
Memory Tip: Pull (引) your belongings to cross (越) over into a new home.

-I am moving to Tokyo next month.

昨年-
{
昨年 (さくねん) - Last year
A formal version of 'kyonen,' frequently used in writing and polite speech.
Memory Tip: The 'Previous' (昨) 'Year' (年) that has already passed.
Example: 昨年、日本へ行った。 (さくねんにほんへいった。)
-I went to Japan last year.

車内-
{
車内 (しゃない) - Inside the car/train
Combines 'vehicle' (車) and 'inside' (内).
Memory Tip: Simply the space located inside (内) a vehicle (車).

終了-
{
終了 (しゅうりょう) - End / Completion / Termination
A formal noun or suru-verb used for the end of events, tasks, or programs.

主に-
{
主に (おもに) - Mainly
An adverb derived from the adjective '主' (main/principal), used to indicate the primary focus of an action.

印刷-
{
印刷 (いんさつ) - Printing
A noun or suru-verb referring to the mechanical reproduction of text/images. 'In' means seal/stamp and 'satsu' means to brush or print.
Memory Tip: Visualize a seal (印) being brushed (刷) onto paper in an old printing press.

替える-
{
替える (かえる) - To replace/exchange/substitute
An Ichidan transitive verb specifically used for swapping one thing for another of the same type (like batteries or lightbulbs).
Memory Tip: Look at the two people at the top of 替; they are swapping places under the sun.
Example: 電池を替える。 (でんちをかえる。)
-Replace the batteries.

本社-
{
本社 (ほんしゃ) - Head office/Main office
A noun used to identify the primary office or headquarters of a corporation.
Memory Tip: "Main/Origin" (本) "Company" (社). The original location where the company is based.

-I'm going to the head office next week.

最低-
{
最低 (さいてい) - Lowest / Worst
Combines 最 (most) and 低 (low). It can describe physical height, values, or moral character (scum).
Memory Tip: When something is at the most (最) low (低) point, it is the absolute worst.
Example: 今日の気分は最低だ。(きょうのきぶんはさいていだ。)
-I feel terrible today.

応援-
{
応援 (おうえん) - Support / Cheering
A noun consisting of 応 (respond) and 援 (help/assist). It refers to rooting for a team or supporting a cause.

応援する-
{
応援する (おうえんする) - To support / To cheer for
The verb form of 応援, created by adding the auxiliary verb する (to do).
Memory Tip: Take the concept of support (応援) and put it into action (する).
Example: 私はあなたを応援する。(わたしはあなたをおうえんする。)
-I will support/cheer for you.

保存-
{
保存 (ほぞん) - preservation, storage, conservation
Combines 保 (keep/hold) and 存 (exist). Used for saving data, preserving food, or protecting nature.
Memory Tip: Ho (Hold) + Zon (Zone) — Hold something in the storage zone to "preserve" it.
Example: このファイルを保存してください。 (このふぁいるを ほぞんしてください。)

見方-
{
見方 (みかた) - Viewpoint, way of seeing
Combines the verb stem of "to see" (見) with the suffix "way/method" (方).

頭痛-
{
頭痛 (ずつう) - Headache
A common noun formed by combining 'head' (頭) and 'pain' (痛).

扇子-
{
扇子 (せんす) - Folding fan
A noun for the traditional folding fan, distinguished from the non-folding 'uchiwa.'

双子-

双子 (ふたご) - Twins

人口-
{
人口 (じんこう) - Population
A compound noun literally translated as 'person-mouth,' referring to the number of people in a region.

縦-
{
縦 (たて) - Vertical/Lengthwise
This word describes vertical orientation, the opposite of 'yoko' (horizontal/sideways).

増やす-
{
増やす (ふやす) - To increase (something)
This is a transitive verb. The intransitive counterpart (something increases on its own) is 'fueru'.
Memory Tip: The kanji contains elements for 'earth' and 'sun'; imagine more land being added under the sun every day.
Example: 貯金を増やしたい。 (ちょきんをふやしたい。)

俳優-
{
俳優 (はいゆう) - Actor, actress
A general term for a performer in plays or movies. It combines 'performer' (俳) with 'excellent/gentle' (優), which is also the kanji for 'actor' in ancient contexts.
Memory Tip: An "Excellent" (優) person who performs in a "Haiku-like" (俳) dramatic art.
Example: 彼は有名な俳優だ。 (かれはゆうめいなはいゆうだ。)
-He is a famous actor.
