楽器-
{
楽器 (がっき) - Musical instrument
A general term for any device used to produce music. It combines 'music/comfort' (楽) with 'vessel/tool' (器).
Memory Tip: A "Tool" (器) used for creating "Music" (楽).
Example: 彼は色々な楽器を弾ける。 (かれはいろいろながっきをひける。)
-He can play various musical instruments.
}

救急車-
{
救急車 (きゅうきゅうしゃ) - Ambulance
A compound noun consisting of rescue (救), urgent (急), and vehicle (車).
Memory Tip: Think of 'QQ' (kyu-kyu) as the sound of the siren on a rescue vehicle.
Example: 救急車を呼んでください！ (きゅうきゅうしゃをよんでください！)
-Please call an ambulance!
}

血液-
{
血液 (けつえき) - Blood
A formal or medical term for blood, combining 'blood' (血) and 'liquid' (液).
Memory Tip: It combines the kanji for blood (ketsu) and liquid (eki); literally 'blood liquid'.
Example: 血液検査を受けました。 (けつえきけんさをうけました。)
-I had a blood test.
}

線路-
{
線路 (せんろ) - Railway track
A compound noun consisting of 線 (line) and 路 (road). It specifically refers to the tracks on which trains run.
Memory Tip: Think of it as the "line road" for trains.
Example: 電車が線路を走っている。 (でんしゃがせんろをはしっている。)
-The train is running on the tracks.
}

泣き声-
{
泣き声 (なきごえ) - Crying voice, sob
A compound noun formed from the verb 'naku' (to cry) and 'koe' (voice).
Memory Tip: Cry (泣き) + Voice (声). The literal sound or voice of someone crying.
Example: 隣の部屋から泣き声がする。 (となりのへやからなきごえがする。)
-There is a sound of crying from the next room.
}

発明-
{
発明 (hatsumei) - Invention
A noun/suru-verb referring to the creation of something entirely new.
Memory Tip: To emit/start (発) something that brings light and clarity (明) to the world.
Example: 彼は新しい調理器具を発明した。 (かれはあたらしいちょうりきぐをはつめいした。)
-He invented a new cooking utensil.
}

最終-
{
最終 (さいしゅう) - Final, last
A noun/no-adjective that indicates the absolute end of a sequence or process.
Memory Tip: The most (最) extreme end (終) of a series.
Example: 最終的な結論を出す。 (さいしゅうてきなけつろんをだす。)
-Reach a final conclusion.
}

日光-
{
日光 (にっこう) - Sunlight/Sunshine
Combines 日 (sun) and 光 (light). It is also the name of a famous historical city in Japan.
Memory Tip: Quite literally the "light" (光) emanating from the "sun" (日).
Example: 日光を浴びて歩く。 (にっこうをあびてあるく。)
-To walk while basking in the sunlight.
}

自動-
{
自動 (じどう) - Automatic
Consists of the kanji for 'self' (自) and 'movement' (動). It refers to machines or processes that act on their own.
Memory Tip: When something moves (動) by itself (自), it is automatic.
Example: このドアは自動です。(このどあはじどうです。)
-This door is automatic.
}

見直す-
{
見直す (みなおす) - To look again / To re-evaluate
A compound verb consisting of "to see" (見る) and "to fix/redo" (直す). It implies checking for errors or changing one's opinion.
Memory Tip: To see (見) something again to fix (直) its potential mistakes.
Example: 計画を見直す必要がある (けいかくをみなおすひつようがある)
-It is necessary to re-evaluate the plan.
}

教わる-
{
教わる (おそわる) - To be taught, to learn
A godan verb that focuses on the recipient of the instruction. It is the passive-leaning counterpart to 教える (to teach).
Memory Tip: When you are the one receiving the 'Oso' (lesson), you are 'osowaru' (taught).
Example: 私は母から料理を教わった。 (わたしはははからりょうりをおそわった。)
-I was taught cooking by my mother.
}

委員-
{
委員 (いいん) - Committee member
A noun identifying a person who has been selected to serve on a committee or board.
Memory Tip: One who is 'entrusted' (委) with a duty as a 'member' (員).
Example: 彼は実行委員の一人だ。 (かれはじっこういいんのひとりだ。)
-He is one of the executive committee members.
}

拝見する-
{
拝見する (はいけんする) - To see/look at (humble)
A humble (kenjougo) verb used when referring to your own action of seeing something belonging to a superior.
Memory Tip: You show 'worship/honor' (拝) while 'looking' (見) at something provided to you.
Example: お手紙を拝見しました。 (おてがみをはいけんしました。)
-I have read (seen) your letter.
}

商店街-
{
商店街 (しょうてんがい) - Shopping district
This word refers to a commercial street or mall area. It is composed of 商 (trade), 店 (shop), and 街 (street).
Memory Tip: A street (街) lined with many trading (商) shops (店).
Example: 商店街で夕食の買い物をした。 (しょうてんがいでゆうしょくのかいものをした。)
-I did some grocery shopping for dinner at the shopping district.
}

測る-
{
測る (はかる) - To measure
Used for measuring physical dimensions like depth, length, or time with instruments. The water radical suggests measuring water levels.
Memory Tip: Measure the water level (water radical) next to the rule.
Example: 池の深さを測る (いけのふかさをはかる)
-Measure the depth of the pond.
}

国際-
{
国際 (こくさい) - International
A prefix or noun describing relations between countries. 'Koku' (country) + 'sai' (edge/boundary/between).
Memory Tip: Going between the borders (sai) of different countries (koku) makes it international.
Example: 国際会議に出席する (こくさいかいぎにしゅっせきする)
-Attend an international conference.
}

鳴き声-
{
鳴き声 (なきごえ) - Animal cry / Chirp / Roar
Formed from the verb 鳴く (to cry/make a sound for animals) and 声 (voice).
Memory Tip: This is the literal "voice" of an animal's "cry."
Example: 庭で鳥の鳴き声がする。 (にわでとりのなきごえがする。)
-I hear the chirping of birds in the garden.
}

観光-
{
観光 (かんこう) - Sightseeing / Tourism
Combines 観 (to observe/view) and 光 (light/glory). It literally means "viewing the glory (of a place)."
Memory Tip: Going to "view" (観) the "highlights" or "light" (光) of a new city.
Example: 明日は京都を観光する。 (あしたはきょうとかんこうする。)
-I will go sightseeing in Kyoto tomorrow.
}

後輩-
{
後輩 (こうはい) - Junior (at school, work, etc.)
Composed of "behind/after" (後) and "fellow/companion" (輩). The opposite of 先輩 (senpai).
Memory Tip: A fellow companion (輩) who entered the organization after (後) you.
Example: 彼は私の高校の後輩だ。(かれはわたしのこうこうのこうはいだ。)
-He is my junior from high school.
}

宝物-
{
宝物 (たからもの) - Treasure / Prized possession
A compound of 'takara' (treasure) and 'mono' (thing).
Memory Tip: Imagine a house (宀) with a piece of jade (玉) inside: that is a treasure (宝).
Example: これは私の宝物です。 (これはわたしのたからものです。)
-This is my treasure.
}

前回-
{
前回 (ぜんかい) - Last time, previous time
A noun referring to the most recent previous instance of a recurring event.
Memory Tip: Literally 'the time' (回) that occurred 'before' (前).
Example: 前回のテストは難しかった。 (ぜんかいのてすとをむずかしかった。)
-The previous test was difficult.
}

優勝-
{
優勝 (ゆうしょう) - Victory, championship
Combines 優 (superior/gentle) and 勝 (win). To be 'superior at winning,' meaning to take first place.
Memory Tip: The most superior (優) athlete wins (勝) the championship.
Example: 私たちのチームが優勝した。(わたしたちのチームがゆうしょうした)
-Our team won the championship.
}

台風-
{
台風 (たいふう) - Typhoon
Combines 台 (pedestal/platform) and 風 (wind). In modern usage, 台 is used as a phonetic/simplified kanji for the original 'big' wind.
Memory Tip: A massive typhoon is like a giant platform (台) of wind (風) moving across the sea.
Example: 台風が接近している。(たいふうがせっきんしている)
-A typhoon is approaching.
}

迷路-
{
迷路 (めいろ) - Maze, labyrinth
Formed by the kanji for 'to get lost' and 'road/path'.
Memory Tip: A road (路) that is designed to make you feel perplexed or lost (迷).
Example: 迷路で出口を探す。 (めいろででぐちをさがす。)
-To look for the exit in a maze.
}

泊める-
{
泊める (とめる) - To lodge (someone) / To give someone a place to stay
This is the transitive form of 泊まる (to stay). It means providing accommodation to another person.
Memory Tip: Think of "To-me-ru" as bringing someone "to me" at my house to stay over.
Example: 今夜は友達を家に泊める。 (こんやはともだちをうちにとめる。)
-I will let my friend stay at my house tonight.
}

お守り-
{
お守り (おまもり) - Amulet / Charm / Protection
A noun referring to small lucky charms sold at Shinto shrines and Buddhist temples.
Memory Tip: The honorific 'o' plus 'mamori' (protection); an object that protects you.
Example: 神社でお守りを買った。(じんじゃでおまもりをかった)
-I bought a charm at the shrine.
}

刺さる-
{
刺さる (ささる) - To be stuck, to be pierced
An intransitive verb used for physical objects or metaphorical words that resonate deeply.
Memory Tip: The kanji 刺 looks like a cactus spike sticking into a surface.
Example: その言葉が心に刺さった。 (そのことばがこころにささった。)
-Those words pierced my heart.
}

居酒屋-
{
居酒屋 (いざかや) - Japanese pub
A casual place for drinking and snacks, very common in Japanese social life.
Memory Tip: A shop (屋) where you stay (居) to drink sake (酒).
Example: 仕事の後に居酒屋へ行く。(しごとのあとにいざかやへいく。)
-Go to an izakaya after work.

注射-

注射 (ちゅうしゃ) - Injection
Medical term for giving a shot.

-The nurse gives an injection.

訳す-
{
訳す (やくす) - To translate
A verb indicating the conversion of text or speech from one language to another.

将棋-
{
将棋 (しょうぎ) - Shogi (Japanese chess)
A strategic board game. 将 means commander and 棋 refers to a game piece.

交通-
{
交通 (こうつう) - Traffic, transportation
Consists of 交 (intersect/exchange) and 通 (pass through). It describes the general movement of vehicles and people.

Example: この道は交通量が多い。(このみちはこうつうりょうがおおい。)

醤油-
{
醤油 (しょうゆ) - Soy sauce
Combines 醤 (miso/fermented paste) and 油 (oil/liquid). It refers to the liquid extracted from fermented soybeans.

牧場-
{
牧場 (ぼくじょう) - Farm/Ranch
Combines 'pasturing' and 'place.' It refers to a large area for breeding and raising livestock like cattle or horses.
Memory Tip: A 'place' (場) where the 'shepherd' (牧) manages the grazing animals.
Example: 牧場で牛に餌をやる。(ぼくじょうでうしにえさをやる。)

休憩-
{
休憩 (きゅうけい) - Rest/Break
A noun referring to a short period of rest during work, a journey, or an activity.
Memory Tip: 休 (rest) + 憩 (relax/rest). Both kanji involve the heart and breath, signaling recovery.
Example: 十分間の休憩をとる (じゅっぷんかんのきゅうけいをとる)
-I will take a ten-minute break.

休憩する-
{
休憩する (きゅうけいする) - To take a rest
The verb form of the noun 'kyuukei', meaning to pause an activity to recover energy.
Memory Tip: Combining 'rest' and 'relax' with the active 'suru' (to do).
Example: 近くのカフェで休憩しよう (ちかくのかふぇできゅうけいしよう)
-Let's take a break at a nearby cafe.

博物館-

博物館 (はくぶつかん) - Museum
Composed of 博 (wide/broad), 物 (thing), and 館 (building).

農場-

農場 (のうじょう) - Farm
Combines 農 (agriculture) and 場 (place).

宇宙人-

宇宙人 (うちゅうじん) - Alien/Extraterrestrial

入社-
{
入社 (にゅうしゃ) - Joining a company
A compound of 入 (enter) and 社 (company), used for the act of starting employment at a firm.

花びら-
{
花びら (花びら) - Flower petal
A compound of 'flower' (花) and 'hira' (flake/leaf), which softens to 'bira'. It evokes the delicate nature of petals.
Memory Tip: Picture 'flowers' (花) breaking into small 'flakes' (びら) that flutter in the wind.
Example: 桜の花びらが舞っている。 (さくらのはなびらがまっている。)
-Cherry blossom petals are dancing in the air.

小指-
{
小指 (こゆび) - Little finger / pinky
A noun for the smallest finger on the hand. '小' means small and '指' means finger.
Memory Tip: Simply the small (小) finger (指).
Example: 小指をぶつけて痛い。 (こゆびをぶつけていたい。)
-I hit my pinky and it hurts.

口紅-
{
口紅 (くちべに) - Lipstick
Literally "mouth" (口) "crimson" (紅).
Memory Tip: Applying crimson (紅) color to your mouth (口).

-She applied lipstick.

家賃-
{
家賃 (やちん) - rent
家 (house) and 賃 (fare/fee). The specific word for the monthly cost of a home.

Example: 今月の家賃を払った。(こんげつのやちんをはらった。)
-I paid this month's rent.

順番-
{
順番 (じゅんばん) - turn, order
順 (order/obey) and 番 (number/turn). It indicates the sequence in which things happen.

Example: 順番を待ってください。(じゅんばんをまってください。)
-Please wait for your turn.

炭-
{
炭 (すみ) - Charcoal
Refers to the black carbon residue produced by heating wood without air.
Memory Tip: Imagine a mountain (山) of wood being turned into coal by fire (火).
Example: バーベキューのために炭を買った。 (ばーべきゅーのためにすみをかった)
-I bought charcoal for the barbecue.

洗面所-

洗面所 (せんめんじょ) - Washroom, lavatory
A place specifically designated for washing the face and hands.

一泊-
{
一泊 (いっぱく) - One night stay

登山-

登山 (とざん) - Mountain climbing
A compound noun consisting of 登 (climb) and 山 (mountain), often used as a suru-verb.

真似-

真似 (まね) - Imitation

乾かす-
{
乾かす (かわかす) - To dry (something)
This is a transitive verb used when you act upon an object to remove moisture. Its intransitive partner is 乾く (kawaku).

〜放題-
{
〜放題 (〜ほうだい) - All-you-can..., unlimited
Attached to the stem of a verb or a noun, this suffix indicates doing something without restriction.
Memory Tip: 'Ho (放)' means to release; 'dai (題)' means topic. Release the limits on the topic!
Example: 食べ放題のレストランに行く。 (たべほうだいのれすとらんにいく。)
-I'm going to an all-you-can-eat restaurant.

受かる-
{
受かる (うかる) - To pass (an exam); to be accepted
An intransitive Godan verb specifically used for passing tests or being accepted into an institution like a school or company. Use the particle 'ni' for the exam.

Example: 試験に受かりました。 (しけんにうかりました。)
-I passed the exam.

走り回る (はしりまわる) - To run around

一周 (いっしゅう) - One lap, one circuit

痒い-

痒い (かゆい) - Itchy
An i-adjective used for physical skin irritation.

炊く-
{
炊く (たく) - To cook (rice/grains)
This is a specific transitive verb used for boiling grains (usually rice) until the liquid is fully absorbed.

掃く-
{
掃く (はく) - to sweep
A godan verb specifically used for cleaning a surface using a broom or brush.
Memory Tip: The left side is the hand radical 扌. You use your hand to sweep away dust with a tool.
Example: ほうきで玄関をきれいに掃く。 (ほうきでげんかんをきれいにはく。)
-Sweep the entrance clean with a broom.
}

星空-
{
星空 (ほしぞら) - Starry sky
A compound of 星 (star) and 空 (sky), describing the visual state of the night sky.
Memory Tip: It's simply the sky (空) when it is full of stars (星).
Example: 満天の星空を眺める。 (まんてんのほしぞらをながめる。)
-To gaze at a sky full of stars.
}

夕焼け-
{
夕焼け (ゆうやけ) - Sunset / Afterglow
A noun describing the red glow of the evening sky as the sun goes down.
Memory Tip: Evening (夕) + Burning (焼け) = the sky looks like it is on fire in the evening.
Example: 今日の夕焼けはとても綺麗だ。 (きょうのゆうやけはとてもきれいだ。)
-Today's sunset is very beautiful.
}

お盆-
{
お盆 (おぼん) - Obon Festival/Tray
This word refers to both the Buddhist festival for ancestors and a serving tray; the 'o' is a polite prefix.
Memory Tip: A tray (皿) is used for offerings during the Obon festival season.
Example: お盆に帰省する。 (おぼんにきせいする。)
-Go back to one's hometown for Obon.
}

童話-
{
童話 (どうわ) - fairy tale, children's story
Combines 'child' (童) and 'story/talk' (話). It refers specifically to stories written or intended for young children.
Memory Tip: A story (話) designed to be told to a child (童).
Example: 母が寝る前に童話を読んでくれた。 (ははがねるまえにどうわをよんでくれた。)
-My mother read me a fairy tale before I went to sleep.
}

万年筆-
{
万年筆 (まんねんひつ) - fountain pen
Literally translated as 'ten-thousand-year brush'. It refers to a pen that lasts a long time compared to disposable options.
Memory Tip: A pen meant to last for 'ten thousand' (万) 'years' (年) instead of a simple 'brush' (筆).
Example: 父から万年筆をもらった。 (ちちからまんねんひつをもらった。)
-I received a fountain pen from my father.
}

田んぼ-
{
田んぼ (たんぼ) - Rice field
Usually written with 田 (field) plus 'nbo'. The kanji 田 reflects the grid layout of a paddy field.
Memory Tip: The kanji 田 is a perfect picture of a subdivided rice field seen from above.
Example: 田んぼに苗を植える。 (たんぼになえをうえる。)
-Plant seedlings in the rice field.
}

中指-
{
中指 (なかゆび) - Middle finger
A simple compound noun used to identify the finger between the index and ring finger.
Memory Tip: 中 (middle) + 指 (finger). It is literally the middle finger.
Example: 彼は中指を怪我した。 (かれはなかゆびをけがした。)
-He injured his middle finger.
}

苗字-
{
苗字 (みょうじ) - Surname
Also commonly written as 名字, it refers to a person's family name.
Memory Tip: Your family name is the seedling (苗) or root of your personal characters (字).
Example: 私の苗字は佐藤です。 (わたしのみょうじはさとうです。)
-My surname is Sato.
}

髪型-
{
髪型 (かみがた) - hairstyle
This word combines 髪 (hair) with 型 (model/shape/style) to describe how one's hair is arranged.
Memory Tip: Focus on the 'shape' (型) of the 'hair' (髪) on someone's head.
Example: 彼女の新しい髪型は似合っている。 (かのじょのあたらしいかみがたはにあっている。)
-Her new hairstyle suits her.
}

日時-
{
日時 (にちじ) - Date and time
A compound noun combining day and time, frequently used when scheduling events or appointments.
Memory Tip: Combine the kanji for Sun/Day (日) and Time/Hour (時) to specify the exact when.
Example: 会議の日時を変更する。 (かいぎのにちじをへんこうする。)
-Change the date and time of the meeting.
}

新品-
{
新品 (しんぴん) - Brand new article
Used to describe an object that is completely new and has never been used.
Memory Tip: 新 (new) plus 品 (article/goods) literally translates to a "new item."
Example: これはまだ新品の靴です。 (これはまだしんぴんのくつです。)
-These are still brand new shoes.
}

召し上がる-
{
召し上がる (めしあがる) - To eat/drink (honorific)
The honorific (keigo) equivalent of 食べる or 飲む, used to show respect toward the person performing the action.
Memory Tip: Think of a noble "summoning" (召し) food "up" (上がる) to their mouth.
Example: どうぞ、召し上がってください。 (どうぞ、めしあがってください。)
-Please, help yourself and eat.
}

零時-
{
零時 (れいじ) - Midnight, zero hours
A noun indicating 12:00 AM, using the kanji for zero and time.
Memory Tip: "Rei" means zero; it is the specific hour when the clock resets to start a new day.
Example: 零時に花火が上がった。 (れいじにはなびがあがった。)
-Fireworks went off at midnight.
}

お見舞い-
{
お見舞い (おみまい) - Visiting a sick person, get-well inquiry
A noun (often with the polite 'o') referring to visiting or sending a gift to someone ill or injured.
Memory Tip: You go to "see" (見) someone so they will be happy enough to "dance" (舞) again.
Example: 友達の家にお見舞いに行く。 (ともだちのいえにおみまいにいく。)
-I am going to visit a sick friend.
}

一人暮らし-
{
一人暮らし (ひとりぐらし) - Living alone
A compound of 'one person' (一人) and the nominalized form of the verb 'to live' (暮らす).
Memory Tip: One (一) person (人) making a living (暮らし).
Example: 来月から一人暮らしを始める。 (らいげつからひとりぐらしをはじめる。)
-I will start living alone next month.
}

客室-
{
客室 (きゃくしつ) - guest room
Combined from 'guest' (客) and 'room' (室), commonly used in hotels or large homes.
Memory Tip: Think of a Guest occupying a Room in a castle.
Example: 客室を予約しました。(きゃくしつをよやくしました)
-I booked a guest room.
}

時刻表-
{
時刻表 (じこくひょう) - Timetable
Composed of 時刻 (specific time/moment) and 表 (table/chart/list).
Memory Tip: A chart (表) that shows the exact time (時刻) the train arrives.
Example: 駅で時刻表を確認した。(えきでじこくひょうをかくにんした。)
-I checked the timetable at the station.
}

北風-
{
北風 (きたかぜ) - north wind
A compound of 北 (north) and 風 (wind). In Japan, this wind is synonymous with the arrival of cold winter weather.
Memory Tip: Simply the wind (風) coming from the north (北).
Example: 北風が強く吹いている。 (きたかぜがつよくふいている。)
-The north wind is blowing hard.
}

敬語-
{
敬語 (けいご) - Honorific language
Consisting of 'respect' (敬) and 'language' (語), this system is essential for formal social interactions in Japan.
Memory Tip: The specific language (語) used to express respect (敬) to someone of higher status.
Example: 上司には敬語を使うべきだ。 (じょうしにはけいごをつかうべきだ。)
-You should use polite language with your boss.
}

蛇口-
{
蛇口 (じゃぐち) - Faucet, tap
A common household noun. It literally translates to 'snake mouth,' as early water taps were often shaped like dragons or snakes.
Memory Tip: Think of water flowing out of the mouth (口) of a long, thin pipe like a snake (蛇).
Example: 蛇口から水が漏れている。 (じゃぐちからみずがもれている。)
-Water is leaking from the faucet.
}

怠け者-
{
怠け者 (なまけもの) - Lazy person / Idler
A combination of the verb 怠ける (to be idle/neglect) and 者 (person).
Memory Tip: Someone who lets their heart (the bottom of 怠) get lazy and neglects their duties.
Example: 彼はクラスで一番の怠け者だ。 (かれはクラスでいちばんのなまけものだ。)
-He is the biggest slacker in the class.
}

代わり-
{
代わり (かわり) - Substitute / Replacement
Derived from the verb 代わる, meaning to take the place of something or someone.
Memory Tip: The kanji 代 shows a person (亻) taking a turn or place (represented by the stake symbol).
Example: コーヒーの代わりに茶を飲んだ。 (コーヒーのかわりにちゃをのんだ。)
-I drank tea instead of coffee.
}

暖房-
{
暖房 (だんぼう) - Heating
This noun refers to indoor heating systems or the act of warming a room. It combines 'warm' (暖) and 'chamber/room' (房).
Memory Tip: To make a room (房) warm (暖), you need to turn on the heating.
Example: 寒いので暖房を入れました。 (さむいのでだんぼうをいれました。)
-It was cold, so I turned on the heating.
}

串-
{
串 (くし) - Skewer
A pictographic kanji representing a stick passing through two pieces of food.
Memory Tip: The character itself looks exactly like a stick piercing two squares of meat or vegetables.
Example: 焼き鳥を串から外す。 (やきとりをくしからはずす。)
-Remove the yakitori from the skewer.
}

鮭-
{
鮭 (さけ) - salmon
A noun for the specific type of fish, commonly eaten in Japan.
Memory Tip: The fish (魚) whose meat looks like the layered lines of earth (圭).
Example: 彼は朝食に鮭を食べた。 (かれはちょうしょくにさけをたべた。)
-He ate salmon for breakfast.
}

本館-
{
本館 (ほんかん) - Main building
Combines "main/origin" (本) with "large building/hall" (館) to designate the central structure of a facility.
Memory Tip: The "book" (本) building is usually the original or Main building (館).
Example: 本館はあちらにあります。(ほんかんはあちらにあります。)
-The main building is over there.
}

締まる-
{
締まる (しまる) - To be tight / To be closed
An intransitive verb indicating that something is firmly fastened, tightened, or securely locked.
Memory Tip: If something is 'tight' (shimaru), you cannot 'shimmy' it loose.
Example: この瓶の蓋はきつく締まっている。(このびんのふたはきつくしまっている。)
-The lid of this bottle is tightly closed.
}

空席-
{
空席 (くうせき) - vacant seat
Combines 'empty' (空) and 'seat' (席) to indicate availability in a venue or transportation.
Memory Tip: An empty (空) space where a seat (席) is waiting for someone.
Example: 予約がいっぱいで、空席がありません (よやくがいっぱいで、くうせきがありません)
-It is fully booked and there are no vacant seats.
}

南東-
{
南東 (なんとう) - southeast
A compound noun indicating the cardinal direction between south and east.
Memory Tip: Simply combine the kanji for South (南) and East (東).
Example: 風は南東から吹いている。 (かぜはなんとうからふいている。)
-The wind is blowing from the southeast.
}

稲田-
{
稲田 (いなだ) - Rice field; paddy
A specific term for a field where rice plants (稲) are grown.
Memory Tip: 稲 means rice plant and 田 means field; together they form a literal rice-plant field.
Example: 黄金色の稲田が広がる。 (こがねいろのいなだがひろがる。)
-Golden rice fields stretch out.
}

停電-
{
停電 (ていでん) - Power outage
Combines 'halt/stop' (停) and 'electricity' (電). It describes a sudden loss of electrical power.
Memory Tip: "Stopping the Electricity" leaves everyone in the dark during a storm.
Example: 昨夜、近所で停電があった。(さくや、きんじょでていでんがあった。)
-There was a power outage in the neighborhood last night.
}

日本的-
{
日本的 (にほんてき) - Typically Japanese
Uses the suffix '-teki' (的), which functions like '-ish' or '-like' in English to create an adjective from a noun.
Memory Tip: Adding "-teki" to Japan turns it into a description of a style or mood.
Example: それはとても日本的な考え方だ。(それはとてもにほんてきなかんがえかただ。)
-That is a very Japanese way of thinking.
}

鍛冶-
{
鍛冶 (かじ) - Blacksmithing/Metalworking
A noun referring to the craft of forging and shaping metal, especially iron and steel.
Memory Tip: 'Kaji' sounds like 'carve' + 'ji' — someone who carves and shapes metal by fire.
Example: 鍛冶の技術は古くから受け継がれてきた。 (かじのぎじゅつはふるくからうけつがれてきた。)
-The art of blacksmithing has been passed down since ancient times.
}

乳母-
{
乳母 (うば) - Wet nurse/Nanny
A noun for a woman who raises and nurses a child that is not her own, common in noble households.
Memory Tip: 'Uba' sounds like 'oo-bah' — the soothing sound a nurse makes to calm a baby.
Example: 王子は乳母に育てられた。 (おうじはうばにそだてられた。)
-The prince was raised by a wet nurse.
}

王位を継ぐ-
{
王位を継ぐ (おういをつぐ) - To inherit/succeed the throne
A verb phrase describing the act of officially taking over the position of king or queen.
Memory Tip: 'Tsugu' means to 'connect' — you connect yourself to the royal line by inheriting the throne.
Example: 長男が王位を継ぐことになった。 (ちょうなんがおういをつぐことになった。)
-The eldest son was to inherit the throne.
}

命を落とす-
{
命を落とす (いのちをおとす) - To lose one's life/To die
A formal or literary phrase used to describe death, especially in dramatic or solemn contexts.
Memory Tip: 'Otоsu' means 'to drop' — you 'drop' your life, letting it fall away.
Example: 多くの兵士が戦場で命を落とした。 (おおくのへいしがせんじょうでいのちをおとした。)
-Many soldiers lost their lives on the battlefield.
}

必死で-
{
必死で (ひっしで) - Desperately/With all one's might
An adverbial phrase expressing total effort driven by urgency or survival instinct.
Memory Tip: 'Hisshi' literally means 'certain death' — you act desperately when death is certain.
Example: 彼は必死で助けを求めた。 (かれはひっしでたすけをもとめた。)
-He desperately called for help.
}

うろ-
{
うろ - Hollow/Cavity (in a tree)
A noun for a hollow space or hole inside a tree trunk, often used as a hiding spot in stories.
Memory Tip: Imagine an animal going 'uro-uro' (wandering) until it finds a hollow to hide in.
Example: リスがうろの中に木の実を隠した。 (りすがうろのなかにきのみをかくした。)
-The squirrel hid nuts inside the hollow of the tree.
}

こずえ-
{
こずえ - Treetop/Tips of branches
A noun referring to the very top or outermost tips of a tree's branches, often used in poetic language.
Memory Tip: 'Ko' (small) + 'zue' (staff tip) — the tiny tips of branches reaching to the sky like small staffs.
Example: 小鳥がこずえで歌っていた。 (ことりがこずえでうたっていた。)
-A small bird was singing at the treetop.
}

うたげ-
{
うたげ - Banquet/Feast
A poetic or classical noun for a grand celebratory gathering with food, drink, and entertainment.
Memory Tip: 'Utage' sounds like 'uta' (song) + 'ge' — a feast so joyful everyone breaks into song.
Example: 城でうたげが開かれた。 (しろでうたげがひらかれた。)
-A banquet was held at the castle.
}

起床-
{
起床 (きしょう) - Getting out of bed, rising
Combining "rise/wake up" (起) and "bed/floor" (床), this is a formal way to describe getting up in the morning.
Memory Tip: To rise (起) up out of your bed (床) to start the day.
Example: 私は毎朝六時に起床する。 (わたしはまいあさろくじにきしょうする。)
-I get out of bed at six every morning.
}

入国-
{
入国 (にゅうこく) - Entry into a country / Immigration
A formal term used for crossing national borders. It combines 'enter' (入) and 'country' (国).
Memory Tip: Simply the act of 'entering' (入) a 'country' (国).
Example: 空港で入国審査を受ける。 (くうこうでにゅうこくしんさをうける。)
-Go through immigration at the airport.
}

大学院-
{
大学院 (だいがくいん) - Graduate school
Comprised of 'university' (大学) and 'institution/hall' (院). It refers to the level of education beyond the undergraduate degree.
Memory Tip: The 'big learning' (大学) 'institution' (院) where experts are made.
Example: 彼は大学院で経済を学んでいる。 (かれはだいがくいんでけいざいをまなんでいる。)
-He is studying economics at graduate school.
}

遠足-
{
遠足 (えんそく) - Excursion/Field trip
A noun usually referring to a school trip that involves walking to a scenic or educational spot.
Memory Tip: Traveling a 'far' (遠) distance on 'foot' (足) for a fun day out.
Example: 明日は遠足です。 (あしたはえんそくです)
-Tomorrow is the field trip.
}

いい加減にしろ-
{
いい加減にしろ (いいかげんにしろ) - Cut it out! Enough already!
An imperative expression used to express annoyance or to tell someone to stop acting foolishly.
Memory Tip: いい加減 (moderate/right amount) + しろ (do it). Command someone to finally act with some "moderation."
Example: 冗談もいい加減にしろ！(じょうだんもいいかげんにしろ！)
-Enough with the jokes!
}

快速-
{
快速 (かいそく) - High-speed/Express
This word describes a high speed, most commonly used to denote 'Rapid' train services that skip certain stations.
Memory Tip: 快 (pleasant) + 速 (fast) = A pleasantly fast journey on an express train.
Example: 快速列車で駅に向かった。 (かいそくれっしゃでえきにむかった。)
-I headed to the station on the rapid train.
}

漬物-
{
漬物 (つけもの) - Pickles
A general term for Japanese preserved vegetables, which are often soaked in brine, vinegar, or sake lees.
Memory Tip: 漬 (soak) + 物 (thing) = A vegetable that has been soaked.
Example: 祖母が作った漬物は美味しい。 (そぼがつくったつけものはおいしい。)
-The pickles my grandmother made are delicious.
}

食料品-
{
食料品 (しょくりょうひん) - Groceries/Foodstuffs
A compound noun consisting of eat (食), materials (料), and goods (品). It refers to products for consumption.
Memory Tip: Think of goods (品) that serve as the materials (料) for eating (食).
Example: 食料品店で野菜を買う (しょくりょうひんてんでやさいをかう)
-Buying vegetables at the grocery store.
}

書き直す-
{
書き直す (かきなおす) - To rewrite
A compound verb combining '書く' (to write) and the auxiliary '直す' (to redo or fix).
Memory Tip: 'Writing' it over to 'fix' it equals 'rewriting'.
Example: 作文を書き直しました。 (さくぶんをかきなおしました。)
-I rewrote the essay.
}

泥水-
{
泥水 (どろみず) - Muddy water
A straightforward combination of 'mud' (泥) and 'water' (水).
Memory Tip: This is simply 'water' (水) that has been mixed with 'mud' (泥).
Example: 大雨で川が泥水になった。(おおあめでかわがどろみずになった)
- The river turned into muddy water due to the heavy rain.
}

落ち葉-
{
落ち葉 (おちば) - Fallen leaves
A compound of the verb stem 落ち (from 落ちる, to fall) and the noun 葉 (leaf).
Memory Tip: Literally 'falling/fallen leaves' lying on the ground.
Example: 公園で落ち葉を拾った。 (こうえんでおちばをひろった。)
-I picked up fallen leaves in the park.
}

北極-
{
北極 (ほっきょく) - North Pole
Composed of 北 (North) and 極 (Extremity/Pole), referring to the northernmost point of the Earth's axis.
Memory Tip: The absolute northern (北) extreme (極) of the entire planet.
Example: 北極にはシロクマが住んでいる。(ほっきょくにはしろくまがすんでいる。)
-Polar bears live at the North Pole.
}

枚数-
{
枚数 (まいすう) - Number of sheets/pages
A compound of the counter for flat objects (枚) and the word for number or count (数).
Memory Tip: Counting (数) how many trees (木) were turned into sheets (枚) of paper.
Example: コピーの枚数を確認してください。 (こぴーのまいすうをかくにんしてください。)
-Please check the number of copies.
}

逆さま-
{
逆さま (さかさま) - Upside down, inverted
Used to describe things that are inverted or in a reversed state, both physically and conceptually.
Memory Tip: The state or appearance (さま) of being in reverse (逆).
Example: 地図を逆さまに持っている。 (ちずをさかさまにもっている。)
-You are holding the map upside down.
}

桜色-
{
桜色 (さくらいろ) - Cherry blossom color
A compound word representing the iconic light pink color of Japan's cherry blossoms.
Memory Tip: It is the 'color' (色) of the 'cherry tree' (桜).
Example: 彼女の頬が桜色に染まった (かのじょのほほがさくらいろにそまった)
-Her cheeks turned a cherry blossom pink.
}

神奈川県-
{
神奈川県 (かながわけん) - Kanagawa Prefecture
A proper noun for the prefecture south of Tokyo, containing the cities of Yokohama and Kamakura.
Memory Tip: It means 'God' (神) 'Apple-tree/Nara' (奈) 'River' (川) 'Prefecture' (県).
Example: 私は神奈川県に住んでいます。(わたしはかながわけんにすんでいます。)
-I live in Kanagawa Prefecture.
}

温まる-
{
温まる (あたたまる) - To get warm
An intransitive verb used for physical temperature increases (bodies, rooms, soup) or feelings.
Memory Tip: Look at the 'Sun' (日) and 'Water' (氵) radicals in the kanji to imagine soup getting warm under the sun.
Example: お風呂に入ると体が温まる。(おふろにはいるとからだがあたたまる。)
-Entering a bath makes your body get warm.
}

洋食-
{
洋食 (ようしょく) - Western-style food
Refers to Japanese-style adaptations of Western cuisine common in Japan.
Memory Tip: 洋 (ocean/Western) + 食 (food) = food from across the ocean.
Example: 今夜は洋食が食べたい気分だ (こんやはようしょくがたべたいきぶんだ)
-I feel like eating Western-style food tonight.
}

禁煙-
{
禁煙 (きんえん) - No smoking, quitting smoking
Combines 禁 (prohibit) and 煙 (smoke). It can mean a location where smoking is banned or the personal act of quitting.
Memory Tip: Prohibiting (禁) the smoke (煙) from your lungs or the room.
Example: 室内は禁煙です。 (しつないはきんえんです。)
-Smoking is prohibited indoors.
}

動詞-
{
動詞 (どうし) - Verb
Grammatical term formed by the kanji for 'move' and 'word/part of speech.' It encompasses all action, state, and existence words.
Memory Tip: Literally 'moving word.' If the word represents an action or movement, it is a 動詞.
Example: この動詞の活用を覚えなさい。 (このどうしのかつようをおぼえなさい。)
-Please memorize the conjugation of this verb.
}

人込み-
{
人込み (ひとごみ) - Crowd of people
This noun combines 人 (person) and 込み (packed/full), referring specifically to a dense gathering of people.
Memory Tip: Imagine 'people' (人) 'stuffed' (込み) into a small space until it's crowded.
Example: 人込みを避けて歩く。 (ひとごみをさけてあるく。)
-I walk avoiding the crowds.
}

判子-
{
判子 (はんこ) - personal seal / stamp
Common noun used for official signatures or bank accounts in Japan; often synonymous with 'inkan'.
Memory Tip: Think of it as a small tool used to make a 'judgment' (判) on a document by a 'child' (子) sized object.
Example: 契約書に判子を押す。 (けいやくしょにはんこをおす)
-To press a seal on a contract.
}

祭日-
{
祭日 (さいじつ) - National holiday/Festival day
A noun describing a day set aside for rituals or national celebration. '祭' means festival and '日' means day.
Memory Tip: A 'day' (日) dedicated to a 'festival' (祭).
Example: 明日は祭日でお休みだ。 (あしたはさいじつでおやすみだ。)
-Tomorrow is a holiday, so we are off.
}

予報-
{
予報 (よほう) - Forecast
Combines 予 (in advance) and 報 (report/news) to describe a prediction of future events.
Memory Tip: A report (報) that comes beforehand (予) is a forecast.
Example: 天気予報をチェックする。 (てんきよほうをチェックする。)
-To check the weather forecast.
}

南風-
{
南風 (みなみかぜ) - South wind
A compound word of 南 (south) and 風 (wind). In certain contexts, it can also be read as "minami" or "hae".
Memory Tip: A warm wind (風) blowing up from the south (南).
Example: 南風が心地よい。 (みなみかぜがここちよい。)
-The south wind is pleasant.
}

記念日-
{
記念日 (きねんび) - Anniversary / Memorial Day
A compound word consisting of record (記), thought (念), and day (日).
Memory Tip: A Day (日) to Record (記) your Thoughts (念) about a past event.
Example: 今日は結婚記念日だ。 (きょうはけっこんきねんびだ。)
-Today is our wedding anniversary.
}

枯れ木-
{
枯れ木 (かれき) - Dead tree / Withered tree
A compound noun formed from the verb 枯れる (to wither) and the noun 木 (tree). It describes a tree that has lost its life or leaves.
Memory Tip: A 'tree' (木) that has 'withered' (枯れ) is a 'dead tree'.
Example: 枯れ木に花が咲く。 (かれきにはながさく。)
-Flowers bloom on a dead tree.
}

男優-
{
男優 (だんゆう) - Actor
Formed from 'man' (男) and 'excel/actor' (優). While '俳優' (haiyuu) is gender-neutral, '男優' specifically refers to a male performer.
Memory Tip: A 'man' (男) who is an 'actor' (優) is a 'male actor'.
Example: 彼は有名な男優だ。 (かれはゆうめいなだんゆうだ。)
-He is a famous actor.
}

必勝-
{
必勝 (ひっしょう) - Certain victory
Combining 'certainly' (必) and 'win' (勝), this word expresses an absolute determination or a guaranteed outcome of winning.
Memory Tip: If you 'must' (必) 'win' (勝), you are aiming for 'certain victory'.
Example: 必勝を期して練習する。 (ひっしょうをきしてれんしゅうする。)
-We practice with a determination for certain victory.
}

心配事-
{
心配事 (しんぱいごと) - Worries, cares, troubles
A noun combining worry (心配) and thing/matter (事).
Memory Tip: These are the literal "worry things" that keep you up at night.
Example: 彼は心配事が重なって元気がなかった。(かれはしんぱいごとがかさなってげんきがなかった)
-He was discouraged because his worries were piling up.
}

船酔い-
{
船酔い (ふなよい) - seasickness
A compound noun formed from 船 (ship) and 酔い (drunkenness/motion sickness).
Memory Tip: Feeling "drunk" (酔い) because you are on a "ship" (船).
Example: 船酔いがひどい。 (ふなよいがひどい。)
-I have terrible seasickness.
}

出国-
{
出国 (しゅっこく) - departure from a country
A formal term often used in airport contexts, combining 出 (exit) and 国 (country).
Memory Tip: Exiting (出) the borders of a country (国).
Example: 明日出国します。 (あしたしゅっこくします。)
-I will leave the country tomorrow.

盆栽-
{
盆栽 (ぼんさい) - bonsai
A traditional art form involving 盆 (tray/shallow pot) and 栽 (planting).
Memory Tip: A tree that is planted (栽) and styled within a shallow tray (盆).
Example: 盆栽の手入れをする。 (ぼんさいのていれをする。)
-Pruning/taking care of a bonsai.

書き入れる-
{
書き入れる (かきいれる) - To fill in, to write in, to enter
A compound verb: 書く (to write) + 入れる (to put in). Used for filling out forms or adding notes.
Memory Tip: You 'Write' (書) the information and 'Put it in' (入れ) the empty space.
Example: 手帳に予定を書き入れる。 (てちょうによていをかきいれる。)
-I write my schedule in my notebook.

早退-
{
早退 (そうたい) - leaving early
A suru-verb specifically used for leaving school or work before the scheduled finishing time.
Memory Tip: 早 (early) + 退 (retreat/leave). A "premature retreat" from one's duties.
Example: 体調が悪くて早退した。 (たいちょうがわるくてそうたいした。)
-I felt unwell and left early.
}

喫煙-
{
喫煙 (きつえん) - Smoking
Formed by 喫 (consume/eat) and 煙 (smoke), it is the formal term for the act of smoking.
Memory Tip: You are 'consuming' (喫) the 'smoke' (煙) from a cigarette.
Example: ここは喫煙所です。 (ここはきつえんじょです。)
-This is a smoking area.
}

英訳-
{
英訳 (えいやく) - English translation
Specifically refers to translating a text from another language into English.
Memory Tip: Combine "English" (英) with the kanji for "translation/reasoning" (訳).

空車-
{
空車 (くうしゃ) - Empty car/Available taxi
Specifically used as a sign on taxis indicating they have no passengers and are available. Combines 'empty' (空) and 'car' (車).
Memory Tip: An empty (空) car (車) waiting for a passenger.
Example: 空車のタクシーを探す。(くうしゃのたくしーをさがす。)
-Look for an available taxi.

海藻-
{
海藻 (かいそう) - Seaweed
A noun referring generally to aquatic plants and marine algae found in the ocean.
Memory Tip: 海 (sea) + 藻 (algae/seaweed). Think of "sea algae" to remember the kanji components.
Example: 海藻にはミネラルが豊富に含まれている。 (かいそうにはみねらるがほうふにふくまれている。)

文房具-
{
文房具 (ぶんぼうぐ) - Stationery
A collective noun encompassing writing materials like pens, paper, and other office supplies.

一覧-
{
一覧 (いちらん) - list; summary; glance
Formed by 一 (one) and 覧 (look/view), implying everything can be seen in one glance.

-Look at a list of products.

防水-
{
防水 (ぼうすい) - Waterproof
Composed of 防 (prevent/defend) and 水 (water), used to describe materials that resist water penetration.

始発-
{
始発 (しはつ) - First train/bus, starting station

Example: 始発列車に乗る。 (しはつれっしゃにのる。)

説明書-
{
説明書 (せつめいしょ) - Instruction manual
A written document that explains how to use a product or perform a process. It is composed of the words for 'explanation' and 'document'.

入場料-
{
入場料 (にゅうじょうりょう) - entrance fee, admission fee
A logical compound: 'enter' (入) + 'place' (場) + 'fee/material' (料).
Memory Tip: Simply the fee (料) you pay to enter (入) the place (場).

電卓-
{
電卓 (でんたく) - Calculator
An abbreviation of 'electronic desktop calculator' using the kanji for electricity and table/desk.

駅弁-

駅弁 (えきべん) - Railway station boxed lunch

山登り-
{
山登り (やまのぼり) - Mountain climbing
A straightforward combination of 山 (mountain) and the noun form of the verb 登る (to climb). It encompasses everything from casual hiking to serious climbing.

お邪魔します-
{
お邪魔します (おじゃまします) - Excuse me for disturbing you / Hello (entering a home)
A polite set phrase used when entering someone's home or office to acknowledge you are an interruption.
Memory Tip: 邪魔 (jama) means "hindrance" or "obstacle." You are literally saying "I am being a hindrance."

-Excuse me, I'm coming in.

洋室-

全日本 (ぜんにほん) - All-Japan

第一位-
{
第一位 (だいいちい) - First place, top rank
A numerical ranking term. 第 (ordinal indicator) + 一 (one) + 位 (rank).

{
名曲 (めいきょく) - Famous piece of music, masterpiece
This noun combines 名 (name/reputation) and 曲 (composition/tune) to describe a well-known, classic song.

A grammatical term combining past (過去) and form (形).

〜しすぎる-
{
〜しすぎる (〜しすぎる) - To do too much, to overdo
An auxiliary verb attached to the masu-stem of a verb. It indicates that an action has exceeded a healthy or normal limit.
Memory Tip: Sugiru (すぎる) means "to pass/go beyond"; you have passed the limit of the action.
Example: 昨日はお酒を飲みすぎた。 (きのうはおさけをのみすぎた。)
-I drank too much alcohol yesterday.

大阪弁-
{
大阪弁 (おおさかべん) - Osaka dialect
Formed from the city name 大阪 (Osaka) and 弁 (dialect/speech). It is one of the most famous regional dialects in Japan.
Memory Tip: Just add 'ben' (dialect) to the location 'Osaka' to identify its speech style.
Example: 彼はたまに大阪弁で話す。 (かれはたまにおおさかべんではなす。)
-He occasionally speaks in the Osaka dialect.

日光浴-
{
日光浴 (にっこうよく) - Sunbathing
This noun/verb combines 日光 (sunlight) and 浴 (bathe), describing the act of exposing the body to the sun.

下書き-
{
下書き (したがき) - Draft, rough sketch

不合格 (ふごうかく) - Failure, rejection

お構いなく (おかまいなく) - Don't go to any trouble / Please don't bother
A polite phrase used to tell a host not to fuss over preparations or hospitality for the speaker.

一気 (いっき) - In one go / At once / Chug

A compound noun combining 'ni' (luggage/load) and 'fuda' (tag/ticket/label).
Memory Tip: It is the 'tag' (札) you attach to your 'luggage' (荷) when traveling.
Example: スーツケースに荷札を付けてください。 (すーつけーすににふだをつけてください。)
-Please attach a luggage tag to your suitcase.
}

各駅停車-
{
各駅停車 (かくえきていしゃ) - Local train / Stopping at every station
A compound noun describing a train service that makes a stop at every single station on its route.
Memory Tip: A vehicle stopping (停車) at each (各) and every station (駅).
Example: 各駅停車でゆっくり行く。 (かくえきていしゃでゆっくりいく。)
-I will go slowly by local train.
}

縄跳び-
{
縄跳び (なわとび) - Jump rope
A compound noun made of 縄 (rope) and the noun form of the verb 跳ぶ (to jump).
Memory Tip: The act of using a 'rope' (縄) for 'jumping' (跳び) as a game or exercise.
Example: 毎日、健康のために縄跳びをする。 (まいにち、けんこうのためになわとびをする。)
-I jump rope every day for my health.
}

花粉症-
{
花粉症 (かふんしょう) - Hay fever / Pollen allergy
A specific medical condition caused by an allergic reaction to pollen from trees or flowers.
Memory Tip: A sickness (症) caused by flower (花) powder (粉), which is pollen.
Example: 毎年、春になると花粉症がひどい。(まいとし、はるになるとかふんしょうがひどい。)
-Every year, my hay fever gets bad when spring arrives.

肩こり-
{
肩こり (かたこり) - Stiff shoulders / Stiff neck
A common ailment in Japan describing tension and discomfort in the shoulder and neck area.
Memory Tip: Your shoulders (肩) becoming stiff or frozen (こり).
Example: パソコンの使いすぎで肩こりがする。(ぱそこんのつかいすぎでかたこりがする。)
-I have stiff shoulders from using the computer too much.
}

不人気-
{
不人気 (ふにんき) - Unpopularity
This word combines the negative prefix 不 (not) with 人気 (popularity) to describe something that lacks favor or fans.
Memory Tip: Simply combine 'Not' (不) and 'Popularity' (人気) to remember this concept.
Example: その映画は不人気だった。 (そのえいがはふにんきだった。)
-That movie was unpopular.
}

飲み放題-
{
飲み放題 (のみほうだい) - All-you-can-drink
This noun combines the stem of 飲む (to drink) with 放題 (as much as one likes), common in Japanese restaurants and bars.
Memory Tip: Think of a "Ho-down" where drinks are served "freely" (放題) without limits.
Example: 飲み放題のコースを選びました。 (のみほうだいのコースをえらびました。)
-I chose the all-you-can-drink course.
}

履き物-
{
履き物 (はきもの) - Footwear
A general term for things worn on the feet, combining 履く (to wear on feet) and 物 (thing).
Memory Tip: A "thing" (物) that you "put on your feet" (履く).
Example: ここで履き物を脱いでください。 (ここではきものをぬいでください。)
-Please take off your footwear here.
}

偶に-
{
偶に (たまに) - Occasionally, once in a while
An adverb written with the kanji for 'accident' or 'even number,' indicating something that happens infrequently.
Memory Tip: Even (偶) numbers appear only half the time; things happen only 'occasionally' compared to 'always.'
Example: 偶に故郷を思い出す。 (たまにこきょうをおもいだす。)
-I occasionally think of my hometown.
}

食べ放題-
{
食べ放題 (たべほうだい) - All-you-can-eat
Combines the verb stem of 食べる (to eat) with 放題 (as much as one likes/no limit).
Memory Tip: Eat (食べ) with total freedom (放題) and no limits.
Example: 焼肉の食べ放題コースを選ぶ。 (やきにくのたべほうだいコースをえらぶ。)
-Choose the all-you-can-eat grilled meat course.

洗車-
{
洗車 (せんしゃ) - Car wash
A simple compound of 洗 (wash) and 車 (car).
Memory Tip: Use water (the three drops on the left of 洗) to clean your car (車).
Example: 週末はガソリンスタンドで洗車をした。 (しゅうまつはガソリンスタンドでせんしゃをした。)
-I washed my car at the gas station over the weekend.
}

残額-
{
残額 (ざんがく) - Balance/Remaining amount
Formed by 残 (remain/leftover) and 額 (amount/sum). It is commonly used in banking and retail contexts.
Memory Tip: The total amount (額) that remains (残) in your account.
Example: 通帳の残額を確認する。 (つうちょうのざんがくをかくにんする。)
-Check the remaining balance in the bankbook.

掛け算-
{
掛け算 (かけざん) - Multiplication
This is the mathematical term for multiplication, derived from the verb kakeru (to multiply/apply).
Memory Tip: 掛ける (apply/multiply) + 算 (calculation) = The process of applying one number to another through multiplication.
Example: 子供は九九の掛け算を覚えている。(こどもはくくのかけざんをおぼえている。)
-The child is memorizing the multiplication tables.
}

副詞-
{
副詞 (ふくし) - adverb
A grammatical term for a part of speech that modifies verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs.
Memory Tip: A secondary (副) word (詞) that adds extra detail to the main action or quality.
Example: 「ゆっくり」や「とても」は副詞です。 (「ゆっくり」や「とても」はふくしです。)
-"Yukkuri" and "totemo" are adverbs.
}

立ち飲み-
{
立ち飲み (たちのみ) - Standing while drinking
Refers to the culture of drinking at bars (tachinomiyah) where there are no seats to maximize space and lower prices.
Memory Tip: The act of drinking (飲み) while standing (立ち).
Example: 立ち飲み屋で一杯飲んだ。 (たちのみやでいっぱいのんだ。)
-I had a drink at a standing bar.
}

音読み-
{
音読み (おんよみ) - On'yomi
The Chinese-derived reading of a kanji, based on its original "sound" rather than its Japanese meaning.
Memory Tip: The "sound" (音) reading (読み) of the character.
Example: この漢字の音読みは何ですか？ (このかんじのおんよみはなんですか？)
-What is the on'yomi of this kanji?
}

無糖-
{
無糖 (むとう) - sugar-free / unsweetened
Combines 無 (none/without) and 糖 (sugar), frequently seen on coffee and tea labels.
Memory Tip: "No" (無) "sugar" (糖) added to your drink.
Example: 無糖のコーヒーを注文した。 (むとうのこーひーをちゅうもんした。)
-I ordered a sugar-free coffee.
}

五十音順-
{
五十音順 (ごじゅうおんじゅん) - Alphabetical order
Literally 'fifty sounds' (五十音) plus 'order' (順). It refers to the standard sorting order of the Japanese syllabary.
Memory Tip: Think of the 50-sound chart (go-juu-on) and the character for 'order' (jun).
Example: 名簿は五十音順に並んでいる。(めいぼはごじゅうおんじゅんにならんでいる。)
-The name list is arranged in kana order.
}

否定形-
{
否定形 (ひていけい) - Negative form
A grammatical term combining 否定 (negation/denial) and 形 (form/shape).
Memory Tip: The specific "shape" a verb or adjective takes when you are "denying" (negating) an action.
Example: 動詞を否定形に変える (どうしをひていけいにかえる)
-Change the verb into the negative form.
}

携帯ストラップ-
{
携帯ストラップ (けいたいストラップ) - Cell phone strap
A combination of "keitai" (portable/mobile) and the katakana loanword for "strap."
Memory Tip: Think of a "keitai" (mobile) being held safe by a "strap" (ストラップ).
Example: 可愛い携帯ストラップを買いに行こう。 (かわいいけいたいストラップをかいにいこう。)
-Let's go buy a cute cell phone strap.

迷惑メール-
{
迷惑メール (めいわくメール) - Spam or junk mail
Combines "meiwaku" (nuisance/trouble) and "mēru" (email).
Memory Tip: It's email (メール) that causes a nuisance (迷惑) by filling up your inbox.
Example: 迷惑メールのフィルターを設定した。 (めいわくメールのフィルターをせっていした。)
-I set up a spam mail filter.

〜抜き-
{
〜抜き (〜ぬき) - without/omitting
A suffix attached to nouns to indicate that something which is normally included has been left out.
Memory Tip: Derived from the verb 抜く (to extract/pull out), suggesting something has been pulled out of the whole.
Example: 冗談抜きで話そう。 (じょうだんぬきではなそう。)
-Let's talk without jokes.

税込-
{
税込 (ぜいこみ) - tax included
A compound word used in commerce to show that the consumption tax is included in the price.
Memory Tip: Combining 税 (tax) and 込み (including/inside), meaning the tax is already 'inside' the total.
Example: この本は千円、税込です。 (このほんはせんえん、ぜいこみです。)
-This book is 1,000 yen, tax included.

百均-
{
百均 (ひゃっきん) - 100-yen shop
This is an abbreviation for 百円均一 (hyaku-en kin'itsu), meaning '100-yen uniform pricing.' It functions as a noun describing discount stores.
Memory Tip: Focus on '100' (百) and the character for 'uniform/equal' (均), meaning everything is the same price.
Example: 百均でペンを買った。 (ひゃっきんでぺんをかった。)
-I bought a pen at a 100-yen shop.

貸し〜-
{
貸し〜 (かし) - Lending, for hire, for rent
A prefix or noun stem derived from 貸す (to lend). It indicates that the associated object is available for lease or rental.
Memory Tip: Using money (貝) to pay for a substitute (代) item is the essence of renting or lending.
Example: この辺りに貸し自転車はありますか？ (このあたりにかしじてんしゃはありますか)
-Are there rental bicycles around here?

飛ばす-
{
飛ばす (とばす) - To let fly, to skip/omit, to speed
The transitive form of 飛ぶ; it can describe making an object fly, skipping pages in a book, or driving a car at high speeds.
Memory Tip: The kanji 飛 looks like a bird with wings outstretched; tobasu is the action of making those wings move.
Example: 彼は高速道路で車を飛ばした。 (かれはこうそくどうろでくるまをとばした)
-He sped his car on the highway.

確かに-
{
確かに (たしかに) - surely, certainly, for sure
An adverb derived from the adjective 確か (tashika), used to express agreement or confirmation.
Memory Tip: 確 means "certain" and features the stone radical (石), implying a rock-solid truth.
Example: 確かに彼が言った通りだ。 (たしかにかれがいったとおりだ。)
-It is certainly as he said.
}

戦い-
{
戦い (たたかい) - Battle, fight, struggle
The noun form of the verb 'tatakau'. It can refer to physical combat, sports matches, or internal personal struggles.
Memory Tip: The kanji contains radicals for 'single' and 'spear', representing a single combatant holding a weapon.
Example: 激しい戦いが続いている。(はげしいたたかいがつづいている)
-The fierce battle is continuing.
}

怒らせる-
{
怒らせる (おこらせる) - To make someone angry
The causative form of the verb 'okoru' (to get angry). It describes an action that triggers anger in another person.
Memory Tip: 'Okoru' is to be mad; the 'seru' suffix indicates causing that emotion to happen to someone else.
Example: 彼を怒らせるつもりはなかった。(かれをおこらせるつもりはなかった)
-I didn't mean to make him angry.
}

払い-
{
払い (はらい) - Payment
The noun form of 'harau' (to pay or clear away). It specifically refers to the act of settling a debt or bill.
Memory Tip: The hand radical (扌) suggests the action of 'handing over' money to complete a transaction.
Example: お支払いは現金ですか？(おしはらいはげんきんですか)
-Is the payment in cash?
}

磨き-
{
磨き (みがき) - Polishing / Brushing / Refinement
This is the noun form of the verb 磨く (migaku), which means to polish, scour, or brush. It is commonly used in compound words like 歯磨き (tooth brushing) or to describe refining one's character or skills.
Memory Tip: The kanji 磨 contains stone (石) at the bottom. Imagine rubbing a stone over and over to make it smooth and shiny.
Example: 彼は靴磨きを仕事にしている。 (かれはくつみがきをしごとにしている。)
-He polishes shoes for a living.
}

板-
{
板 (いた) - Board, plank, sheet
A common noun used for flat, rigid pieces of material, typically wood. It forms the basis for many everyday objects like blackboards (黒板) and cutting boards (まな板).
Memory Tip: Combining 'tree' (木) and 'return/opposite' (反), imagine a tree being processed into a flat board that looks nothing like its original round form.
Example: 彼は木の板を二枚に割った。(かれはきのいたをにまいにわった。)
-He split the wooden board in two.
}

鳴る-
{
鳴る (なる) - To sound, ring, or echo
An intransitive verb used for sounds produced by objects like bells and clocks, or natural phenomena like thunder and stomach rumbles.
Memory Tip: The kanji combines 'mouth' (口) and 'bird' (鳥)—imagine a bird opening its mouth to make a sound.
Example: 雷が遠くで鳴っている。 (かみなりがとおくでなっている。)
-Thunder is rumbling in the distance.
}

酔う-
{
酔う (よう) - To get drunk, to feel motion sick, or to be captivated
An intransitive verb used for physical intoxication (alcohol), motion sickness (cars/boats), or metaphorical intoxication (beauty/success).
Memory Tip: The left side of the kanji (酉) represents a sake jar. Imagine a Yo-yo (よう) spinning so fast it makes you feel dizzy and drunk.
Example: 彼はすぐにお酒に酔ってしまいます。 (かれはすぐにおさけによってしまいます。)
-He gets drunk on alcohol very quickly.

世の中-
{
世の中 (よのなか) - The world / society
Composed of 世 (world/generation) and 中 (inside), this term refers to human society, the public, or the state of life in general.
Memory Tip: Imagine being right in the "middle" (中) of the "world" (世)—this is the society you interact with every day.
Example: 世の中には色々な人がいる。(よのなかにはいろいろなひとがいる。)
-There are all kinds of people in the world.
}

もしかして-
{
もしかして (もしかして) - Perhaps, by any chance, could it be that
This adverb is used to express a speaker's conjecture or hunch, often appearing at the beginning of a sentence to seek confirmation for a suspicion.
Memory Tip: Connect 'Moshi' (if) with 'shite' (doing). If someone is 'doing' something unexpected, you ask: 'If it's [doing] this, could it be...?'
Example: もしかして、道に迷ったの？ (もしかして、みちにまよったの？)
-By any chance, did you get lost?

恥ずかしがる-
{
恥ずかしがる (はずかしがる) - to feel shy; to show embarrassment
This verb attaches the suffix '~garu' (to appear/behave as if) to the adjective 'hazukashii' to describe a third party's visible shyness.
Memory Tip: 'Hazukashii' is the feeling; adding 'garu' makes it an observable action—like a 'girl' (garu) acting 'shy' (hazukashii).
Example: 妹は知らない人の前で恥ずかしがる。(いもうとはしらないひとのまえではずかしがる)
-My younger sister gets shy in front of strangers.
}

気に入る-
{
気に入る (きにいる) - To like; to be pleased with
This common phrase literally means "to enter one's spirit." It is used when an object or situation makes a favorable impression on you.
Memory Tip: Imagine a gift literally "entering" (入る) your "heart/spirit" (気) because you find it so appealing.
Example: このデザインがとても気に入りました。 (このデザインがとてもきにいりました。)
-I really liked this design.

舌-
{
舌 (した) - Tongue
A noun referring to the muscular organ in the mouth, used for tasting and speaking.

-Stick out one's tongue

いい加減-
{
いい加減 (いいかげん) - Irresponsible, half-baked
Combines 'good' (ii) and 'degree' (kagen); while it can mean 'just right', it usually implies a careless or random attitude.

苛々する-

苛々する (いらいらする) - To get irritated / To be annoyed

飽き-
{
飽き (あき) - Boredom; weariness

だいたい-

折る-

A transitive verb used for folding paper (origami) or snapping long objects like branches.
Memory Tip: You use your hand (扌 radical) to fold an axe (斤 radical) handle.
Example: 紙を半分に折ってください。(かみをはんぶんにおってください)
-Please fold the paper in half.
}

〜様-
{
〜様 (〜さま) - Mr./Ms. (polite) / State or appearance
A respectful honorific for people or a suffix indicating the state of something.
Memory Tip: Use "sama" when the person is "some-a" (someone) very important.
Example: お客様、こちらへどうぞ。(おきゃくさま、こちらへどうぞ)
-Customer, this way please.
}

〜の様に-
{
〜の様に (〜のように) - Like / In the manner of
Used to create a simile or describe how an action is performed relative to a noun.
Memory Tip: "You knee" (youni) down "like" a pro when acting like something else.
Example: 彼は鳥のように飛びたい。(かれはとりのようにとびたい)
-He wants to fly like a bird.
}

集まり-
{
集まり (あつまり) - Gathering
The noun form of the verb 'atsumaru', used to describe a meeting, assembly, or social get-together.
Memory Tip: Many 'birds' (隹) on a 'tree' (木) create a 'gathering' (集).
Example: 今夜は友人たちの集まりがある。 (こんやはゆうじんたちのあつまりがある。)
-There is a gathering of friends tonight.
}

項目-
{
項目 (こうもく) - Item, heading, entry
Consists of 項 (paragraph/item) and 目 (eye/look), referring to specific points in a list or document.
Memory Tip: Think of "looking" (目) at each specific "item" (項) on a checklist.
Example: このリストには５つの項目があります。(このりすとにはいつつのこうもくがあります。)
-There are five items on this list.
}

彼ら-
{
彼ら (かれら) - They
The plural form of "he" (彼). It is used for a group of men or a mixed-gender group.
Memory Tip: Take "him" (彼) and add the pluralizing suffix "ra" (ら) to get "them."
Example: 彼らは大学生です。 (かれらはだいがくせいです。)
-They are university students.
}

日-
{
日 (ひ) - Day, sun
A basic pictographic kanji representing the sun; it can refer to the celestial body or a 24-hour period.
Memory Tip: It looks like a window with a horizontal bar, through which you can see the sun during the day.
Example: 暑い日ですね。(あついひですね。)
-It is a hot day, isn't it?
}

見せる-
{
見せる (みせる) - To show
A transitive ru-verb that is the causative-adjacent form of 見る (to see).
Memory Tip: You are causing something to be in front of someone's eye (見) so they see it.
Example: 写真を見せる。(しゃしんをみせる。)
-To show a photo.
}

控え-
{
控え (ひかえ) - Note / Copy / Reserve
Derived from the verb 'hikaeru', meaning to hold back or to make a record of.
Memory Tip: Use your hand (扌) to hold onto a copy or keep a spare on the side.
Example: 領収書の控えをもらった (りょうしゅうしょのひかえをもらった)
-I received a copy of the receipt.
}

全て-
{
全て (すべて) - All, everything
An adverb or noun indicating the entirety of a group or the whole of a situation.
Memory Tip: Under the roof (top part), the king (王) rules over everything and everyone.
Example: 全て終わりました。(すべておわりました。)
-Everything has finished.
}

外れ-
{
外れ (はずれ) - A miss, failure
A noun indicating that something missed the target, such as a losing lottery ticket or a wrong guess.
Memory Tip: When something lands outside (外) the mark, it is a total miss.
Example: このクジは外れだ。 (このクジははずれだ。)
-This lottery ticket is a loss.
}

全く-
{
全く (まったく) - Entirely; not at all
An adverb used to emphasize the totality of a statement. It is frequently used with negative verbs to mean "not at all."
Memory Tip: The kanji 全 means "all" or "whole," indicating a state is 100% complete.
Example: 全く知りませんでした。 (まったくしりませんでした。)
-I didn't know at all.
}

眺め-
{
眺め (ながめ) - View / Scene / Outlook
The noun form of the verb 'nagameru' (to gaze). It is often used for beautiful scenery.
Memory Tip: 'Naga' sounds like 'long'; you take a 'long' look at a beautiful 'view'.
Example: 窓からの眺めがいい。(まどからのながめがいい。)
-The view from the window is good.
}

底-
{
底 (そこ) - Bottom / Sole
Refers to the lowest part of a container, body of water, or even a person's feelings.
Memory Tip: Radical 广 (cliff/building) over 氐 (low/base). Think of the base of the building floor.
Example: 海の底に沈む。 (うみのそこにしずむ。)
-Sink to the bottom of the sea.
}

口にする-
{
口にする (くちにする) - To eat / To mention
An idiomatic expression meaning to either physically consume food/drink or to voice a thought.
Memory Tip: Literally "to put into the mouth" (to eat) or "to use the mouth for" (to speak).
Example: 彼はそのことを二度と口にしなかった。 (かれはそのことをにどとくちにしなかった。)
-He didn't mention that thing ever again.
}

舐める-
{
舐める (なめる) - To lick, taste, or underestimate
Commonly written in kana, it means to use the tongue or, figuratively, to look down on someone.
Memory Tip: The kanji contains the radical for 'tongue' (舌), essential for licking.
Example: 飴を舐める。 (あめをなめる。)
-To lick a candy.
}

〜ところで-
{
〜ところで (〜ところで) - Just as / Even if
Used after a verb to indicate the moment an action finishes or to show a futile condition (even if).
Memory Tip: "Tokoro" means place or moment. "De" is the particle. "At the moment of..."
Example: 料理ができたところで客が来た。 (りょうりができたところできゃくがきた。)
-Just as the food was ready, the guest arrived.
}

ところで-
{
ところで (ところで) - By the way
A conjunction used to shift the conversation to a completely new or related topic.
Memory Tip: Literally "at the place where we are," let's jump to another point.
Example: ところで、お腹は空いてる？ (ところで、おなかはすいてる？)
-By the way, are you hungry?
}

〜はず-
{
〜はず (〜はず) - expected to, ought to be
A noun-like grammar point used to express a strong expectation or logical conclusion based on facts.
Memory Tip: Think of "hazu" as "has to be" the result because of the evidence available.
Example: 彼は来るはずだ。 (かれはくるはずだ。)
-He is expected to come.
}

神-
{
神 (かみ) - God / Deity
Refers to Shinto gods, the monotheistic God, or slang for someone with "god-tier" skill.
Memory Tip: The left side 礻 represents an altar, and the right side 申 represents a lightning bolt or stretching spirit.
Example: 日本にはたくさんの神がいます。(にほんにはたくさんのかみがいます)
-There are many gods in Japan.
}

〜側-
{
〜側 (〜がわ) - Side / Team
A suffix added to nouns to indicate a specific side, direction, or faction.
Memory Tip: Think of it as a person (亻) standing near a rule-bound area (則) to mark a boundary.
Example: 窓側に座ります。 (まどがわにすわります。)
-I will sit on the window side.
}

内-
{
内 (うち) - Inside / Within
Refers to the interior of a space or the "in-group" (family, company) in Japanese culture.
Memory Tip: It looks like a person walking into a gate or a box to go inside.
Example: 家の内に入る。 (いえのうちにはいる。)
-Go inside the house.
}

〜とかで-
{
〜とかで (〜とかで) - Due to something like; because of hearing that
A casual grammar structure used to state a reason that is either indirect, based on hearsay, or one of several possibilities.
Memory Tip: Combination of "toka" (listing/vague) and "de" (cause) creates "due to X or something."
Example: 風邪とかで休みました。 (かぜとかでやすみました。)
-I took a day off due to a cold or something.
}

残る-
{
残る (のこる) - To remain / To be left over
An intransitive verb describing something that stays behind after others have gone or been used.
Memory Tip: The left radical (歹) means death/bones; what "remains" after life.
Example: ご飯が少し残った。 (ごはんがすこしのこった。)
-A little rice was left over.
}

生きる-
{
生きる (いきる) - To live
This verb focuses on the state of being alive or the act of living one's life.
Memory Tip: The kanji 生 represents a sprout emerging from the ground, symbolizing life growing.
Example: 強く生きる。 (つよくいきる。)
-To live strongly.
}

胸-
{
胸 (むね) - Chest / Heart / Feelings
Refers to the physical chest area or the metaphorical seat of one's deep emotions.
Memory Tip: The radical 月 (flesh) plus a part that looks like a person's frame holding their heart.
Example: 胸が痛い。 (むねがいたい。)
-My chest hurts / My heart aches.
}

驚く-
{
驚く (おどろく) - To be surprised
An intransitive Godan verb used when someone is startled, amazed, or shocked by something unexpected.
Memory Tip: Oh! (O) The door (doro) shook (ku)! I'm so surprised!
Example: その知らせに驚いた。 (そのしらせにおどろいた。)
-I was surprised by that news.
}

自撮り-
{
自撮り (じどり) - 
A modern compound noun meaning 'selfie'.
Memory Tip: Combines 自 (self) and 撮 (taking a photo). It literally means 'self-capturing'.
Example: 友達と一緒に自撮りをした。 (ともだちといっしょにじどりをした。)
-I took a selfie with my friend.
}

〜道-
{
〜道 (〜どう) - Way of... (arts/discipline)
A suffix used to denote a traditional path, martial art, or spiritual discipline.
Memory Tip: Like Judo or Kendo, it represents the 'path' to mastery.
Example: 彼は茶道を習っています。 (かれはさどうをならっています。)
-He is practicing the way of tea (tea ceremony).
}

洗濯粉-
{
洗濯粉 (せんたくこ) - Laundry powder
A compound noun combining 'laundry' (洗濯) and 'powder' (粉).
Memory Tip: Laundry (洗濯) plus 'flour-like powder' (粉), which contains the 'rice' radical.
Example: 洗濯粉を買い忘れました。 (せんたくこをかいわすれました。)
-I forgot to buy laundry powder.
}

叫ぶ-
{
叫ぶ (さけぶ) - To shout / To cry out
A verb describing the act of making a loud vocal sound due to emotion or to call for help.
Memory Tip: A mouth (口) wide open to let out a sharp cry.
Example: 彼は助けてと叫んだ。 (かれはたすけてとさけんだ)
-He shouted for help.
}

様子-
{
様子 (ようす) - Appearance/State/Situation
A noun used to describe the outward look of someone or the current state of an affair.
Memory Tip: 様 (manner) + 子 (aspect). Look at the 'manner' of a 'thing' to understand its situation.
Example: 彼女の様子がおかしい。 (かのじょのようすがおかしい。)
-Something is strange about her appearance/behavior.
}

揚げ-
{
揚げ (あげ) - Fried, deep-fried
Derived from the verb 'ageru' (to lift), referring to lifting food out of hot oil after frying.
Memory Tip: When you deep fry something, you have to 'lift' it up from the pot when it is done.
Example: 鶏の揚げ物が好きです。 (とりのあげものがすきです。)
-I like fried chicken dishes.
}

受ける-
{
受ける (うける) - To receive, to take (an exam), to undergo
A versatile transitive verb used for receiving physical items or taking abstract things like tests or challenges.
Memory Tip: The top part of the kanji looks like a hand reaching down to 'catch' or 'receive' an object.
Example: 明日、試験を受けます。 (あした、しけんをうけます。)
-I will take an exam tomorrow.
}

〜ばかりで-
{
〜ばかりで (〜ばかりで) - Only... and / just... and
Used to express that someone is doing nothing but one specific action, often with a nuance of dissatisfaction.
Memory Tip: 'Bakari' sounds like 'Back' - you keep going back to the same single action.
Example: 彼は寝てばかりで手伝わない。 (かれはねてばかりでてつだわない。) -[He does nothing but sleep and won't help.]
}

染み-
{
染み (しみ) - Stain, spot, blot
A noun referring to a mark left by liquid. It is the nominal form of the verb 染みる (to soak in).
Memory Tip: The kanji contains water (氵) and wood (木). Imagine water/ink staining a piece of wood.
Example: シャツに染みがついた。 (しゃつにしみがついた。)
-A stain got on the shirt.
}

余る-
{
余る (あまる) - To remain / to be left over
Describes when a quantity, amount, or time exceeds what is needed or used.
Memory Tip: A-maru - 'Ah, a whole Maru (circle/pizza) is left over!'
Example: 時間が十分余った。 (じかんがじゅうぶんあまった。) -[There was plenty of time left over.]
}

生む-
{
生む (うむ) - To give birth / to produce
A godan verb referring to biological birth or the metaphorical creation of something new.
Memory Tip: The kanji 生 represents a plant growing out of the ground, symbolizing life.
Example: 彼女は女の子を生んだ (かのじょはおんなのこをうんだ)
-She gave birth to a girl.
}

暮らし-
{
暮らし (くらし) - Living/Life
This is the noun form of the verb 暮らす (kurasu), referring to one's daily life, lifestyle, or livelihood.
Memory Tip: Imagine the sun (日) setting behind the grass (艹) as your daily life cycle repeats at the end (莫) of the day.
Example: 都会の暮らしに慣れた。 (とかいのくらしになれた。)
-I got used to city life.
}

素早さ-
{
素早さ (すばやさ) - Quickness, agility, speed
Derived from the adjective 素早い (quick), with the suffix -さ added to turn it into a noun describing degree or quality.
Memory Tip: 'Su' (pure/basic) + 'Baya' (fast) + 'Sa' (suffix) = The pure state of being fast.
Example: このポケモンの素早さは非常に高い。 (このぽけもんのすばやさはひじょうにたかい。)
-This Pokémon's speed is extremely high.
}

努力-
{
努力 (どりょく) - Effort / Hard work
Consists of 'do' (strive) and 'ryoku' (power), indicating the application of strength toward a goal.
Memory Tip: The first kanji 'do' (努) contains components for a 'woman/slave' and 'power', suggesting intense, submissive labor.
Example: 彼は努力家です。 (かれはどりょくかです。)
-He is a hard worker.
}

続く-
{
続く (つづく) - To continue / To last
An intransitive Godan verb used to indicate that a state or action is ongoing.
Memory Tip: The thread (糸) radical suggests things being tied together in a continuous line.
Example: 雨が三日続く。 (あめがみっかつづく。)
-The rain continues for three days.
}

地-
{
地 (ち) - Earth/ground
A noun often used in compound words (like 地下 or 地図) to refer to the land, soil, or earth.
Memory Tip: The soil (土) on the ground winds like a snake (也) across the world.
Example: 地に落ちる。 (ちにおちる。)
-To fall to the ground.
}

離れる-
{
離れる (はなれる) - To separate/be apart
An intransitive verb describing the state of being physically distant or moving away from a person or location.
Memory Tip: Imagine a bird (隹) flying away from a container (凵) to become 'separated' (離) from it.
Example: 家族と離れて暮らす。 (かぞくとはなれてくらす。)
-To live apart from one's family.
}

敵-
{
敵 (てき) - Enemy / Rival
Used to describe an opponent in sports, a competitor in business, or a literal enemy in conflict.
Memory Tip: The right side looks like a person striking; they are the enemy attacking your position.
Example: 敵を倒す必要があります。 (てきをたおすひつようがあります。)
-It is necessary to defeat the enemy.
}

頂く-
{
頂く (いただく) - To receive / To eat / To drink
This is the humble (kenjougo) form of 'morau', 'taberu', or 'nomu', used to show respect to the provider.
Memory Tip: The kanji contains the radical for 'head'; imagine receiving a gift and bowing your head in thanks.
Example: お土産を頂きました。 (おみやげをいただきました。)
-I received a souvenir.
}

痛める-
{
痛める (いためる) - To hurt; to cause pain
A transitive verb used when causing physical injury or emotional distress to someone or something.
Memory Tip: The radical for 'sickness' (疒) encloses a character representing the source of pain.
Example: 足を痛める (あしをいためる)
-To hurt one's foot.
}

叱る-
{
叱る (しかる) - To scold
To reprimand someone, typically from a position of authority like a parent or teacher.
Memory Tip: 'She' (shi) 'car' (karu) got hit, so she was scolded.
Example: 先生は生徒を叱った。(せんせいはせいとをしかった。)
-The teacher scolded the student.
}

転がる-
{
転がる (ころがる) - To roll / To tumble
An intransitive verb used to describe an object rotating or falling over and over.
Memory Tip: The kanji (転) features the car/wheel radical (車), which is the ultimate symbol for rolling movement.
Example: 石が坂を転がる。 (いしがさかをころがる。)
-A stone rolls down the hill.
}

消える-
{
消える (きえる) - To disappear, go out, or vanish
An intransitive verb used for lights being extinguished, fire going out, or objects vanishing.
Memory Tip: The water radical (氵) on the left 'extinguishes' the flame of presence.
Example: 電気が消えました。 (でんきがきえました。)
-The light went out.
}

関係-
{
関係 (かんけい) - Relationship, connection, or involvement
Combines 'barrier/gate' (関) and 'system/lineage' (係) to describe how things are linked.
Memory Tip: A connection through the 'family gate' shows a 'relationship' or lineage.
Example: 彼とは何の関係もありません。 (かれとはなんのかんけいもありません。)
-I have no relation to him at all.
}

巣-
{
巣 (す) - Nest / Den / Hive
Refers to the home or habitat built by an animal, bird, or insect.
Memory Tip: Imagine three birds (⺍) sitting in a nest on top of a tree (木).
Example: 鳥が巣を作っています (とりがすをつくっています)
-A bird is building a nest.
}

似合う-
{
似合う (にあう) - To suit/To look good on
A compound verb from 似る (to resemble) and 会う (to meet/fit), describing how an item harmonizes with a person.
Memory Tip: When a piece of clothing "meets" (au) your style and "resembles" (ni) your personality, it suits you.
Example: その帽子、似合いますね。 (そのぼうし、にあいますね。)
-That hat suits you, doesn't it?
}

理由-
{
理由 (りゆう) - Reason/Motive
A noun composed of 理 (logic/principle) and 由 (cause/whereabouts).
Memory Tip: Think of it as the "logical" (ri) "origin" (yuu) of why something happened.
Example: 遅れた理由を教えてください。 (おくれたりゆうをおしえてください。)
-Please tell me the reason why you were late.
}

糸-
{
糸 (いと) - Thread
This is a basic noun referring to thread or string, often used in metaphors about fate.
Memory Tip: The kanji depicts a bundle of silk threads tied together at the top.
Example: 糸で布を縫う (いとでぬのをぬう)
-Sew cloth with thread
}

申す-
{
申す (もうす) - To say (humble)
This is the humble equivalent of 'iu', used when speaking formally about one's own speech to show respect.
Memory Tip: The kanji looks like a sprout coming out of the ground, symbolizing a humble message growing upward.
Example: 田中と申します (たなかともうします)
-My name is Tanaka
}

作業-
{
作業 (さぎょう) - Work / Operation / Task
Combines 'work/make' (sa) and 'business/deed' (gyō), typically used for manual or physical tasks.
Memory Tip: Making (sa) something as your professional business (gyō) constitutes a task or operation.
Example: 作業を分担しましょう。 (さぎょうをぶんたんしましょう。)
-Let's divide the work.
}

悲しみ-
{
悲しみ (かなしみ) - Sadness; sorrow
A noun derived from the i-adjective 'kanashii' by replacing the final 'i' with 'mi' to denote a state or quality.
Memory Tip: The top of the kanji means 'wrong' and the bottom is 'heart'; your heart feels wrong when you are sad.
Example: 悲しみを乗り越える。 (かなしみをのりこえる。)
-To overcome sadness.
}

流れる-
{
流れる (ながれる) - To flow / To stream
An intransitive verb used for liquids, air, or the passage of time and information.
Memory Tip: The water radical (氵) on the left clearly indicates the liquid nature of flowing.
Example: 川が海へ流れる (かわがうみへながれる)
-The river flows to the sea
}

与える-
{
与える (あたえる) - To give; to bestow
Used for providing abstract things like influence or damage, or giving to those of lower status.
Memory Tip: Think of the shape as a simple tray holding something to be handed over.
Example: 彼にチャンスを与える (かれにちゃんすをあたえる)
-Give him a chance.
}

再び-
{
再び (ふたたび) - Again / once more
A formal adverb used to indicate the repetition of an action. It is more literary than the common phrase 'mou ichido.'
Memory Tip: The kanji 再 looks like a gate being re-entered for a second time.
Example: 彼に再び会う機会があった。 (かれにふたたびあうきかいがあった。)
-I had the opportunity to meet him again.

編集する-
{
編集する (へんしゅうする) - To edit
The verb form used for modifying or compiling text, films, or data into a final version.
Memory Tip: Use the thread (糸) of a story to tie together gathered (集) ideas.
Example: 原稿を短く編集する。 (げんこうをみじかくへんしゅうする。)
-I will edit the manuscript to make it shorter.
}

捕まる-
{
捕まる (つかまる) - To be caught / arrested
This is an intransitive verb indicating that someone has been captured or held. It is the passive state of being 'caught.'
Memory Tip: The left side is the 'hand' radical (扌). Someone's hand reaches out to grab you, and you are 'caught.'
Example: 泥棒が捕まった。 (どろぼうがつかまった。)
-The thief was caught.
}

輝き-
{
輝き (かがやき) - Radiance/Shine
The noun form of the verb 'kagayaku' (to shine), often used for light or talent.
Memory Tip: 'Kaga' (Kagawa) has a special 'yaki' (grilled) glow or 'shine'.
Example: 星の輝きが美しい。 (ほしのかがやきがうつくしい。)
-The shine of the stars is beautiful.
}

丸ごと-
{
丸ごと (まるごと) - Whole, entirely, in its entirety
An adverbial phrase meaning to take or do something in its complete, undivided state.
Memory Tip: 'Maru' means circle or round. A circle is 'whole' and complete.
Example: リンゴを丸ごと食べる。 (りんごをまるごとたべる。)
-I eat the apple whole.
}

黙る-
{
黙る (だまる) - to be silent, to say nothing
An intransitive verb describing the act of stopping talking or remaining quiet.
Memory Tip: The kanji contains 'black' (黒) and 'dog' (犬); imagine a black dog sitting perfectly silent.
Example: 彼は黙って頷いた。 (かれはだまってうなずいた。)
-He nodded silently.
}

改善-
{
改善 (かいぜん) - Improvement
Combines 改 (reform/change) and 善 (good). Widely used in business to describe continuous improvement.
Memory Tip: Change (Kai) for the Better/Good (Zen).
Example: 業務の効率を改善する。 (ぎょうむのこうりつをかいぜんする。) -[To improve work efficiency.]
}

〜形-
{
〜形 (〜けい / 〜がた) - Shape / Form / Model (suffix)
A suffix used to categorize types or describe grammatical conjugations (like the te-form).
Memory Tip: The three strokes on the right look like hairs or patterns that define the specific form of an object.
Example: 動詞のて形を勉強する (どうしのてけいをべんきょうする)
-I will study the te-form of verbs.
}

抱く-
{
抱く (だく / いだく) - To hold / To embrace / To harbor
'Daku' usually refers to physical hugging, while 'idaku' often refers to harboring feelings or dreams.
Memory Tip: The hand radical (扌) is combined with the 'wrap' radical (包), showing hands wrapping around something.
Example: 赤ん坊を抱く (あかんぼうをだく)
-To hold a baby.
}

まったく-
{
まったく (まったく) - Entirely, completely, (not) at all
An adverb used for emphasis. In negative sentences, it means "not at all"; in positive ones, it means "truly."
Memory Tip: When Matt talks (Mat-taku), he is *completely* and *entirely* honest.
Example: 全く知りませんでした。(まったくしりませんでした。)
-I didn't know at all.
}

病む-
{
病む (やむ) - To fall ill; to suffer from
A godan verb used for being sick, often implying a chronic condition or a state of mental suffering.
Memory Tip: If you are ill, you might say "Yum, no" to food because you are feeling yamu.
Example: 心が病む。 (こころがやむ。)
-To be heartsick.
}

どうせ-
{
どうせ (どうせ) - Anyway / At any rate / After all
An adverb often used to express a sense of resignation or a negative outcome that was expected.
Memory Tip: Think 'dō' (how) + 'se' (even so) — 'no matter how it goes, it's even so/already decided.'
Example: どうせ失敗する。 (どうせしっぱいする。)
-I'll fail anyway.
}

解説-
{
解説 (かいせつ) - explanation, commentary
Combination of "unravel" (解) and "speak" (説). Used for technical explanations or sports commentary.
Memory Tip: Talking (説) to untie (解) a mystery.
Example: 彼はそのニュースについて詳しく解説した。(かれはそのにゅーすについてくわしくかいせつした。)
-He gave a detailed explanation about the news.

揚げる-
{
揚げる (あげる) - To deep-fry / To raise
This is a transitive verb specifically used for frying food or hoisting things like flags.
Memory Tip: You 'raise' the food out of the bubbling oil once it's finished frying.
Example: 天ぷらを揚げる。 (てんぷらをあげる。)
-To fry tempura.
}

用意-
{
用意 (ようい) - Preparation / Readiness
Uses 'use' (用) and 'intention/mind' (意). It implies setting your mind on the use of something beforehand.
Memory Tip: Set your 'mind' (意) on what you will 'use' (用) to be 'ready'.
Example: 食事の用意ができました。(しょくじのよういができました。)
-Dinner is ready.
}

敷く-
{
敷く (しく) - To spread / to lay out
This is a transitive Godan verb used for spreading flat items like futons, rugs, or gravel.

Example: 布団を敷く。 (ふとんをしく。)
-To lay out the futon.

叶える-
{
叶える (かなえる) - To fulfill / To grant
A transitive verb used when making a wish, goal, or dream come true through effort or luck.
Memory Tip: Use your mouth (口) to say a wish ten (十) times until it comes true.
Example: 努力して夢を叶えた。 (どりょくしてゆめをかなえた。)
-I worked hard and fulfilled my dream.
}

致す-
{
致す (いたす) - to do (humble)
The humble (kenjougo) form of the verb 'suru,' used to show respect by lowering the speaker's status.
Memory Tip: Think of it as 'reaching out' (至) with effort to perform a task for someone.
Example: 私がいたします。 (わたくしがいたします。)
-I will do it (humbly).
}

犯人-
{
犯人 (はんにん) - criminal, culprit
A noun combining 'offense/crime' (犯) and 'person' (人) to describe the perpetrator.
Memory Tip: Simply the 'person' (人) who committed the 'crime' (犯).
Example: 犯人が捕まりました。 (はんにんがつかまりました。)
-The criminal was caught.

訪ねる-
{
訪ねる (たずねる) - To visit / To call on
This transitive verb is used for visiting people or places. It is distinct from 尋ねる (to ask/inquire) despite the identical reading.
Memory Tip: The kanji combines 'say' (言) and 'side' (方), implying you talk to someone when you are by their side during a visit.
Example: 友人の家を訪ねる。 (ゆうじんのいえをたずねる。)
-To visit a friend's house.
}

老人-

老人 (ろうじん) - Old person / The elderly
A formal compound noun made of 'old' (老) and 'person' (人).
Memory Tip: Think of a person (人) who is old (老), where the top of the 'old' kanji looks like a person with long hair or a cane.
Example: 老人を大切にする。 (ろうじんをたいせつにする。)
-To treat the elderly with care.

一瞬-
{
一瞬 (いっしゅん) - A moment / Instant

以外-
{
以外 (いがい) - Except for / With the exception of
A noun/suffix used to specify things outside of a particular scope or category.

許す-

許す (ゆるす) - To forgive / Permit

迷い-
{
迷い (まよい) -

戦う (たたかう) - To fight / struggle

瞬間-
{
瞬間 (しゅんかん) - Moment, instant
This noun refers to a very short period of time, essentially a split second. It is composed of 瞬 (wink/blink) and 間 (interval).

限る-
{
限る (かぎる) - To restrict, to limit
A godan verb indicating boundaries. The phrase '~ ni kagiru' is commonly used to say 'there is nothing better than ~'.

食う (くう) - To eat (informal/masculine)
