焦点-
{
焦点 (しょうてん) - Focus/Focal point
Used both for optical focus and the center of attention. It combines 焦 (scorch/burn) and 点 (point).
Memory Tip: Like using a magnifying glass to burn (焦) a single point (点) with concentrated light.
Example: 議論の焦点がずれている。 (ぎろんのしょうてんがずれている。)
-The focus of the discussion is off-track.

圧力-
{
圧力 (あつりょく) - Pressure
A noun describing physical or social/psychological force. It combines 'atsu' (to press) and 'ryoku' (power/force).
Memory Tip: A heavy weight (pressure) combined with physical strength (力).
Example: 強い圧力を感じる (つよいあつりょくをかんじる)
-Feel strong pressure.
}

完了-
{
完了 (かんりょう) - Completion
This noun/suru-verb combines 完 (perfect) and 了 (finish) to describe finishing a process or task.
Memory Tip: A perfect (完) finish (了) means the task is done.
Example: 準備が完了しました。(じゅんびがかんりょうしました。)
-Preparation is complete.
}

食器-

食器 (しょっき) - Tableware/Dishes

Example: 食器を洗う。(しょっきをあらう。)
-To wash the dishes.

人差し指-
{
人差し指 (ひとさしゆび) - Index finger
A compound noun formed by 人 (person), 差し (pointing), and 指 (finger).

故障-

故障 (こしょう) - Breakdown / Out of order
Consists of 故 (cause/old) and 障 (hinder/block). It describes a mechanical failure or malfunction.
Memory Tip: A "cause" that creates a "hindrance" or block in the machine's operation.
Example: 私の車は故障している。 (わたしのくるまはこしょうしている。)
-My car is broken down.

住宅-
{
住宅 (じゅうたく) - Residence / Housing
A noun referring to buildings used as dwellings, often used in the context of urban planning or real estate.

太平洋-
{
太平洋 (たいへいよう) - Pacific Ocean
A proper noun meaning the 'Great Peaceful Ocean,' using the characters for big, peace, and ocean.

経済的-
{
経済的 (けいざいてき) - Economical / Financial
An adjective formed by adding the suffix 'teki' (target/type) to the noun 'keizai' (economy).
Memory Tip: Focus your 'target' (的) on 'economy' (経済) to be efficient with money.

訂正-
{
訂正 (ていせい) - Correction / Revision
Used specifically for fixing errors in documents, text, or spoken statements.
Memory Tip: 'Tei' (訂 - revise/say + nail) + 'Sei' (正 - correct). Nail down what you said to make it correct.
Example: 誤字を訂正してください。 (ごじをていせいしてください。)
-Please correct the typos.

温度-
{
温度 (おんど) - Temperature
Refers to the degree of heat or coldness of air, water, or general objects.

Example: 部屋の温度を下げる。 (へやのおんどをさげる。)

石油-
{
石油 (せきゆう) - Petroleum/Oil
This noun combines the kanji for stone (石) and oil (油) to describe crude mineral oil.

Example: 石油の価格が上がった。(せきゆのかかくがあがった)
-The price of oil went up.

平ら-

平ら (たいら) - Flat, level

Example: 彼は平らな道を選んだ。 (かれはたいらなみちをえらんだ。)

書き込む-

書き込む (かきこむ) - To fill in, to write into
A compound verb: 書く (to write) + 込む (to move inward). It refers to adding text into a form, book, or digital field.
Memory Tip: You are 'writing' (書き) so that the ink goes 'into' (込む) the empty spaces.

退院する-
{
退院する (たいいんする) - To be discharged from the hospital
This verb combines 退 (retreat/leave) and 院 (institution/hospital). It is the antonym of 入院する (to be hospitalized).

Example: 来週退院する予定です。(らいしゅうたいいんするよていです)

人工-
{
人工 (じんこう) - Artificial, man-made

Example: 人工知能が進化している。(じんこうちのうがしんかしている)

無力-
{
無力 (むりょく) - Powerless, helpless

悪人-

悪人 (あくにん) - Bad person / Villain

美術-

茶屋-

茶屋 (ちゃや) - Teahouse

Memory Tip: Imagine walking (left radical) toward something that gives you a benefit or profit.
Example: 安く買えて得をした。 (やすくかえてとくをした。)
-I got a good deal by buying it cheaply.
}

社内-
{
社内 (しゃない) - Within the company/In-house
Common business term referring to internal matters. Breakdown: 社 (company) + 内 (inside).
Memory Tip: Anything that stays inside (内) the company (社) walls is in-house.
Example: 社内規定を確認する。 (しゃないきていをかくにんする。)
-Check the in-house regulations.

店舗-
{
店舗 (てんぽ) - Store, shop, establishment
A formal word for a physical shop or outlet. It combines the kanji for 'shop' (店) and 'paved shop/store' (舗).
Memory Tip: A 'shop' (店) that is firmly 'established' (舗) on the street.
Example: 新しい店舗をオープンする。 (あたらしいてんぽをオープンする。)
-We will open a new store.

切腹-
{
切腹 (せっぷく) - Ritual suicide
This noun refers to the formal ritual disembowelment practiced by samurai to preserve honor. It combines 'cut' (切) and 'belly' (腹).
Memory Tip: Think of cutting (切) the belly (腹) to prove one's inner sincerity.
Example: 侍は切腹によって名誉を守った。 (さむらいはせっぷくによってめいよをまもった。)

株式会社-

株式会社 (かぶしきがいしゃ) - Public company / Co., Ltd.

背丈-
{
背丈 (せたけ) - Stature / height
A noun referring specifically to the height of a person or plant. '背' is back and '丈' is length/measure.

Example: 彼と私は背丈が同じだ。 (かれとわたしはせたけがおなじだ。)

花壇-

花壇 (かだん) - Flower bed

正座-

正座 (せいざ) - Formal sitting (kneeling)

合計-

合計 (ごうけい) - Total / sum

躍り-

躍り (おどり) - Leaping / jump

窓口 (まどぐち) - Service counter / Contact person
Literally 'window mouth,' it refers to a physical ticket window or a specific department for inquiries.
Memory Tip: Think of the 'Mouth' (口) of the building where you talk through a 'Window' (窓) for help.
Example: 問い合わせは窓口で受け付けています。 (といあわせはまどぐちでうけつけています。)
-Inquiries are accepted at the service counter.
}

居眠り-
{
居眠り (いねむり) - Dozing off
Specifically refers to falling asleep while you are sitting or supposed to be awake.
Memory Tip: Existing/being present (居) but sleeping (眠り) at the same time.
Example: 電車で居眠りをしてしまった (でんしゃでいねむりをしてしまった)
-I accidentally dozed off on the train.
}

娯楽-
{
娯楽 (ごらく) - Entertainment, amusement
娯楽 consists of 娯 (recreation) and 楽 (pleasure), referring to leisure activities used for fun.
Memory Tip: 'Go (娯)' out to have some 'raku (楽)' (easy/pleasurable) fun.
Example: この町には娯楽施設が少ない。 (このまちにはごらくしせつがすくない。)
-There are few entertainment facilities in this town.

地蔵-
{
地蔵 (じぞう) - Jizo (stone statue/Bodhisattva)
These are stone statues of a Bodhisattva often found on roadsides, acting as protectors of children and travelers. The kanji mean 'earth' (地) and 'storehouse' (蔵).
Memory Tip: He is the guardian of the 'earth' (地) who 'stores' (蔵) his compassion for travelers and children.
Example: 道端に地蔵が並んでいる。 (みちばたにじぞうがならんでいる。)
-Jizo statues are lined up by the roadside.
}

貯金-
{
貯金 (ちょきん) - Savings
A noun or suru-verb referring to saving money. It combines 'store/save' (貯) and 'money/gold' (金).
Memory Tip: To 'save' (貯) your 'money' (金) safely in a bank or piggy bank.
Example: 旅行のために貯金をする。 (りょこうのためにちょきんをする。)
-I save money for a trip.
}

公衆電話-
{
公衆電話 (こうしゅうでんわ) - Public telephone
A four-kanji compound: 'public' (公衆) and 'telephone' (電話).
Memory Tip: A 'telephone' (電話) intended for the general 'public' (公衆) to use.
Example: 公衆電話はどこにありますか。 (こうしゅうでんわはどこにありますか。)
-Where is a public telephone?

保険-
{
保険 (ほけん) - insurance
A noun covering health, life, or property protection. Often used with the verb 入る (to join/enter).

Example: 海外旅行の前に保険に入る。 (かいがいりょこうのまえにほけんにはいる。)
-I will take out insurance before traveling abroad.

貧乏人-
{
貧乏人 (びんぼうにん) - Poor person
This word describes someone living in poverty. While descriptive, it can be blunt or derogatory depending on the context.

Example: 彼はかつて貧乏人だった。 (かれはかつてびんぼうにんだった。)

殺人者-
{
殺人者 (さつじんしゃ) - Murderer / Killer
A combination of 殺 (kill), 人 (person), and 者 (suffix for person), literally meaning a person who kills people.

名物-
{
名物 (めいぶつ) - Famous product / Specialty

Example: この町の名物は何ですか？ (このまちのめいぶつはなんですか？)

学期-
{
学期 (がっき) - School term, semester
Combines the kanji for 'study' (学) and 'period of time' (期).

馬鹿らしい-
{
馬鹿らしい (ばからしい) - Absurd, ridiculous
An i-adjective formed by adding the suffix "-rashii" (seeming/typical of) to "baka" (fool).
Memory Tip: "Baka" (fool) + "rashii" (seems like) = It seems like a fool's idea, hence it is absurd.
Example: そんな馬鹿らしい話は聞いたことがない。(そんなばからしいはなしはきいたことがない。)

丼-
{
丼 (どんぶり) - bowl / bowl of food
Refers to a large ceramic bowl or a dish served with meat/vegetables over rice in that bowl.

開放する-
{
開放する (かいほうする) - to open up / to liberalize

眉毛 (まゆげ) - eyebrows

募集 (ぼしゅう) - Recruitment, taking applications, invitation

力いっぱい (ちからいっぱい) - With all one's might
A compound noun often used adverbially, combining 'power' (力) with 'fullness' (いっぱい). It describes an action performed with 100% effort.

Formed by 下 (lower/end) and 旬 (10-day period). It specifically refers to the last third of a month (the 21st to the end).

Refers to institutions like schools established by private individuals rather than the state.

Example: 娘は私立の小学校に通っている。(むすめはしりつのしょうがっこうにかよっている。)
-My daughter attends a private elementary school.
}

目次-
{
目次 (もくじ) - Table of contents
A list of the parts of a book or document organized in order.

岐阜 (ぎふ) - Gifu Prefecture

電柱 (でんちゅう) - Utility pole

雑巾-

怠ける-

怠ける (なまける) - To be lazy / To neglect

地中-

A combination of 悪 (bad) and 気 (feeling/spirit). It is most commonly used in the negative form 'warugi wa nai' to mean 'no harm intended.'
Memory Tip: Think of 'Bad' (悪) 'Vibes' (気). If you have no bad vibes, you have no 悪気.
Example: 悪気はなかったんだ。 (わるぎはなかったんだ。)
-I didn't mean any harm.
}

略す-
{
略す (りゃくす) - to abbreviate; to omit; to shorten
A verb used to describe shortening a word, phrase, or action. It is a more casual version of the verb 略する.
Memory Tip: Think of the kanji 略 which means 'abbreviation' or 'summary'. You are 'cutting' the length to make it brief.
Example: 「スマートフォン」を「スマホ」と略す。 (「スマートフォン」を「スマホ」とりゃくす。)
-"Smartphone" is abbreviated to "sumaho."

Example: 風邪の予防に手洗いをする。 (かぜのよぼうにてあらいをする。)
-Wash hands to prevent a cold.

Example: 子供に童謡を歌ってあげる。 (こどもにどうようをうたってあげる。)
-To sing nursery rhymes to a child.
}

間接-
{
間接 (かんせつ) - Indirect
Formed by 間 (interval/space) and 接 (touch/contact), it refers to something that does not involve a direct connection.
Memory Tip: There is a space in-between (間) the contact (接), so it is not direct.
Example: 彼は間接的にそのニュースを聞いた。 (かれはかんせつてきにそのにゅーすをきいた。)

{
薄める (うすめる) - to dilute, to water down
This is a transitive verb derived from the adjective 薄い (thin). It describes the action of making a liquid less concentrated.
Memory Tip: Think of 薄 (thin) plus the transitive suffix める to mean 'making something thin' (less thick).
Example: スープが濃いので、お湯で薄める。 (すーぷがこいので、おゆでうすめる。)

白旗 (はっき) - White flag, surrender

{
短期 (たんき) - Short term

友好-
{
友好 (ゆうこう) - Friendship / Amity
This refers to friendly relations, often in a formal or international context. It combines 'friend' (友) and 'favorable/like' (好).

品質 (ひんしつ) - Quality

岡山県 (おかやまけん) - Okayama Prefecture
A prefecture in the Chūgoku region of Japan, famous for its history and peach production.
Memory Tip: Oka (hill) + Yama (mountain) + Ken (prefecture). It is the prefecture of hills and mountains.
Example: 岡山県は桃で有名です。(おかやまけんはももでゆうめいです。)
-Okayama Prefecture is famous for peaches.
}

指定席-
{
指定席 (していせき) - Reserved seat
Formed by combining 'shitei' (designation) and 'seki' (seat), used commonly on trains and at events.
Memory Tip: You designate (指定) your specific seat (席) to avoid the rush.
Example: 新幹線の指定席を予約しました。 (しんかんせんのしていせきをよやくしました。)
-I reserved a seat on the Shinkansen.
}

消防署-
{
消防署 (しょうぼうしょ) - Fire station
Combines 'shoubou' (firefighting) with 'sho' (government office/station).
Memory Tip: The station (署) dedicated to preventing (防) and extinguishing (消) fire.
Example: 消防署の近くに住んでいます。 (しょうぼうしょのちかくにすんでいます。)
-I live near a fire station.

秒針-
{
秒針 (びょうしん) - Second hand
Formed from 秒 (second) and 針 (needle/pin). This refers specifically to the hand on a clock that tracks seconds.
Memory Tip: The fast-moving needle (針) that tracks every single second (秒).
Example: 秒針がカチカチと動く。 (びょうしんがかちかちとうごく。)
-The second hand moves with a tick-tock.

自炊-
{
自炊 (じすい) - Cooking for oneself, self-catering
Composed of 自 (self) and 炊 (cook/boil rice). It refers to the habit of preparing one's own meals rather than eating out.

中級-
{
中級 (ちゅうきゅう) - Intermediate level

見返る-
{
見返る (みかえる) - To look back, to look over one's shoulder
A godan verb combining 'to see' (見) and 'to return' (返る). It implies physically turning your head to see what is behind you.
Memory Tip: You 'see' (見) by 'returning' (返) your gaze to where you just were.
Example: 誰かに呼ばれた気がして後ろを見返った。 (だれかによばれたきがしてうしろをみかえった。)

{
追い付く (おいつく) - To catch up with, to reach
A compound verb consisting of 'to chase' (追う) and 'to attach/reach' (付く). It describes reaching the same level or physical position as someone ahead.
Memory Tip: You 'chase' (追) someone until you 'stick' (付) to them in rank or distance.
Example: 前を走るランナーにようやく追い付いた。 (まえをはしるランナーにようやくおいついた。)

Memory Tip: Finding a great 'place' hidden in a 'hole' in the wall.
Example: ここは地元の人しか知らない穴場だ。 (ここはじもとのひとしかしらないあなばだ。)
-This is a hidden gem known only to locals.
}

応援団-
{
応援団 (おうえんだん) - Cheering squad / rooters
Combines 応援 (support/cheer) and 団 (group). Specifically refers to the traditional Japanese style of organized cheering groups often seen at schools.
Memory Tip: A 'support group' that uses loud voices and synchronized movements to aid their team.
Example: 私たちの学校の応援団はとても元気だ。 (わたしたちのがっこうのおうえんだんはとてもげんきだ。)
-Our school's cheering squad is very energetic.
}

水彩画-
{
水彩画 (すいさいが) - Watercolor painting
Constructed from 水 (water), 彩 (coloring/hue), and 画 (picture/painting).

Example: 彼女は趣味で水彩画を描く。(かのじょはしゅみですいさいがをえがく。)

副題 (ふくだい) - Subtitle / Subheading

薄まる (うすまる) - To become diluted; to fade

首位 (しゅい) - First place; top position

Consists of 'datsu' (to shed/remove) and 'i' (clothing). Used formally or in compound words like 'datsuijo' (changing room).

-Kagawa Prefecture is famous for udon.

〜ような気がする-
{
〜ような気がする (〜ようなきがする) - Have a feeling that..., I feel like...
A grammar structure using ような (like/as if) and 気がする (to have a feeling). It expresses a vague intuition or impression without certainty.
Memory Tip: I have the "spirit" (ki) that things are "like" (youna) this.
Example: どこかで会ったような気がする。(どこかであったようなきがする。)
-I feel like we've met somewhere before.
}

増税-
{
増税 (ぞうぜい) - Tax increase
Formed by 増 (increase) and 税 (tax). It is the standard term used in news and politics regarding raising taxes.
Memory Tip: 増 (increase) + 税 (tax). Simply adding more to the tax total.
Example: 政府は来年の増税を検討している。 (せいふはらいねんのぞうぜいをけんとうしている。)
-The government is considering a tax increase next year.
}

余震-
{
余震 (よしん) - Aftershock
Combines 余 (surplus/remaining) and 震 (shake/quake) to describe the tremors that follow a large earthquake.
Memory Tip: The remaining (余) shaking (震) that occurs after the main quake.
Example: 大きな地震の後は余震に注意してください。 (おおきなじしんのあとはよしんにちゅういしてください。)
-Please be careful of aftershocks after a large earthquake.
}

徳島県-
{
徳島県 (とくしまけん) - Tokushima Prefecture
A prefecture located on the island of Shikoku, known for the Awa Odori dance. 徳 (virtue) + 島 (island) + 県 (prefecture).
Memory Tip: Think of an island (島) of high virtue (徳) that exists as a prefecture (県).
Example: 私は徳島県に住んでいます。 (わたしはとくしまけんにすんでいます。)
-I live in Tokushima Prefecture.
}

壊れ物-
{
壊れ物 (こわれもの) - fragile item, breakables
A noun formed from the potential/passive form of 壊す (to break) combined with 物 (thing).
Memory Tip: Literally a "broken thing" (壊れ物), which describes items that break easily.
Example: この箱には壊れ物が入っています。(このはこにはこわれものがはいっています)
-This box contains fragile items.
}

胃痛-
{
胃痛 (いつう) - Stomachache / Gastralgia
A formal compound noun joining 胃 (stomach) and 痛 (pain/ache).
Memory Tip: Combine "Stomach" (胃) with "Pain" (痛) for a direct medical description of the ache.
Example: ストレスで胃痛がする。 (ストレスでいつうがする。)
-I have a stomachache due to stress.
}

畜産-
{
畜産 (ちくさん) - Livestock industry
This noun combines 畜 (livestock) and 産 (production/yield) to describe animal husbandry.
Memory Tip: The kanji 畜 looks like a field 田 where animals are raised to produce 産 meat and dairy.
Example: 祖父は北海道で畜産を営んでいる。 (そふはほっかいどうでちくさんをいとなんでいる。)
-My grandfather runs a livestock business in Hokkaido.
}

及び-
{
及び (および) - And; as well as
A formal conjunction used in written Japanese to connect nouns or phrases.
Memory Tip: It is the formal cousin of "to" (と); think of it as "extending to" including another item.
Example: 氏名及び住所を記入してください。 (しめいおよびじゅうしょをきにゅうしてください。)
-Please fill in your name and address.
}

沸点-
{
沸点 (ふってん) - Boiling point
A compound noun consisting of 沸 (boil) and 点 (point). It specifically refers to the temperature at which a liquid turns to vapor.
Memory Tip: Think of the water radical (氵) in 沸 hitting a specific point (点) on the thermometer.
Example: 水の沸点は100度です。 (みずのふってんは100どです。)
-The boiling point of water is 100 degrees.
}

席順-
{
席順 (せきじゅん) - Seating order
A compound of 席 (seat) and 順 (order). It describes the specific sequence or arrangement in which people sit.
Memory Tip: Follow the order (順) to find your assigned seat (席).
Example: 席順はあいうえお順です。 (せきじゅんはあいうえおじゅんです。)
-The seating order is in alphabetical (aiueo) order.
}

部首-
{
部首 (ぶしゅ) - Kanji radical
Combines 部 (part/section) and 首 (head/leader). In linguistics, it refers to the element used to categorize kanji in dictionaries.
Memory Tip: The "head" (首) or leading part (部) of a kanji character.
Example: この漢字の部首は何ですか？ (このかんじのぶしゅはなんですか？)
-What is the radical of this kanji?
}

巻尺-
{
巻尺 (まきじゃく) - Tape measure
A tool used to measure length consisting of a flexible strip that can be wound into a case.
Memory Tip: 巻 (roll/wind) + 尺 (traditional unit of length/ruler) = A ruler that can be rolled up.
Example: 巻尺を使って家具の大きさを測った。(まきじゃくをつかってかぐのおおきさをはかった。)
-I measured the size of the furniture using a tape measure.
}

偏食-
{
偏食 (へんしょく) - Picky eating, unbalanced diet
Refers to the habit of only eating certain foods and avoiding others based on preference.
Memory Tip: 偏 (bias/lean) + 食 (eat). Eating with a heavy bias toward specific foods.
Example: 子供の偏食を直すのは大変だ。 (こどものへんしょくをなおすのはたいへんだ。)
-It is difficult to correct a child's picky eating.
}

猫舌-
{
猫舌 (ねこじた) - Inability to eat or drink hot things
An idiomatic expression describing someone sensitive to high temperatures in food or drink.
Memory Tip: 猫 (cat) + 舌 (tongue). Imagine a cat's sensitive tongue that cannot handle hot soup.
Example: 私は猫舌なので熱いお茶が苦手だ。 (わたしはねこじたなのであついおちゃがにがてだ。)
-I have a 'cat tongue', so I'm not good with hot tea.
}

略語-
{
略語 (りゃくご) - abbreviation/acronym
A compound noun formed by 'abbreviate' (略) and 'word/language' (語).
Memory Tip: A word (語) that has been shortened or abbreviated (略) for efficiency.
Example: 「スマホ」はスマートフォンという言葉の略語です。 (「すまほ」はすまーとふぉんということばのりゃくごです。)
-"Sumaho" is an abbreviation for the word "smartphone."
}

菜食-
{
菜食 (さいしょく) - vegetarian diet
This word describes the practice of eating vegetables or a plant-based diet.
Memory Tip: It is the simple combination of vegetables/greens (菜) and eating (食).
Example: 彼女は健康のために菜食を続けている。 (かのじょはけんこうのためにさいしょくをつづけている。)
-She follows a vegetarian diet for her health.
}

皮膚科-
{
皮膚科 (ひふか) - dermatology
Composed of the formal words for skin (皮膚) and the suffix for a medical or academic department (科).
Memory Tip: The first two kanji both mean skin (皮 and 膚), leading you straight to the skin department.
Example: 湿疹ができたので、皮膚科へ行った。(しっしんができたので、ひふかへいった。)
-I went to the dermatology clinic because I got a rash.
}

賀状-
{
賀状 (がじょう) - New Year's card
A formal abbreviation of 年賀状 (nengajo), used to express congratulations or season's greetings.
Memory Tip: 賀 means congratulations and 状 means a letter or document; literally a congratulatory letter.
Example: 毎年、恩師に賀状を送っている。(まいとし、おんしにがじょうをおくっている。)
-I send a New Year's card to my former teacher every year.
}

無税-
{
無税 (むぜい) - tax-free / duty-free
A compound noun describing the state of being exempt from taxes or customs duties.
Memory Tip: Combine "nothing/without" (無) with "tax" (税) to get the state of having no tax.
Example: この商品は無税で輸入できる。(このしょうひんはむぜいでゆにゅうできる。)
-This product can be imported tax-free.
}

山中湖-
{
山中湖 (やまなかこ) - Lake Yamanaka
Proper noun for the largest of the Fuji Five Lakes, located in Yamanashi Prefecture.
Memory Tip: The lake (湖) in the middle (中) of the mountains (山).
Example: 山中湖から富士山が見える。 (やまなかこからふじさんがみえる。)
-Mount Fuji can be seen from Lake Yamanaka.
}

新発売-
{
新発売 (しんはつばい) - new release / newly launched
Used for products that have just been put on sale for the first time.
Memory Tip: A new (新) start (発) of a sale (売).
Example: 新発売のスマホを買う。 (しんはつばいのすまほをかう。)
-I will buy the newly released smartphone.
}

免税-
{
免税 (めんぜい) - Tax exemption/Duty-free
Composed of 免 (escape/exemption) and 税 (tax). It indicates that the standard tax usually applied to goods has been removed.
Memory Tip: You are excused (免) from the burden of the tax (税).
Example: 免税店で香水を買った。 (めんぜいてんでこうすいをかった。)
-I bought perfume at a duty-free shop.
}

汁物-
{
汁物 (しるもの) - soup; broth-based dish
汁 (soup/juice) and 物 (thing). It is a general term for soup dishes in a Japanese meal.
Memory Tip: The water radical in 汁 indicates a liquid "thing" (物) to be eaten.
Example: 今日は温かい汁物が飲みたい。 (きょうはあたたかいしるものがのみたい。)
-I want to drink some warm soup today.
}

日替わり-
{
日替わり (ひがわり) - Daily special / changing daily
This word combines 日 (day) and 替わり (replacement/change) to describe things that vary day by day.
Memory Tip: Imagine the sun (日) changing (替) the menu every morning.
Example: 今日の日替わりランチを注文した。 (きょうのひがわりらんちをちゅうもんした。)
-I ordered today's daily special lunch.
}

中欧-
{
中欧 (ちゅうおう) - Central Europe
A geographical term combining 中 (middle) and 欧 (short for 欧州 - Europe).
Memory Tip: Right in the middle (中) of Europe (欧).
Example: 中欧の歴史的な街並みを歩く。 (ちゅうおうのれきしてきなまちなみをあるく。)
-To walk through the historical streets of Central Europe.
}

哺乳瓶-
{
哺乳瓶 (ほにゅうびん) - Baby bottle
A specific noun for the container used to feed milk to infants.
Memory Tip: 哺乳 (nursing/lactation) + 瓶 (bottle); a bottle used for nursing.
Example: 赤ちゃんが哺乳瓶でミルクを飲む。 (あかちゃんがほにゅうびんでみるくをのむ。)
-The baby drinks milk from a baby bottle.
}

常勤-
{
常勤 (じょうきん) - Full-time employment
Composed of 常 (constant) and 勤 (work). It refers to a regular, full-time work schedule as opposed to part-time or temporary work.
Memory Tip: If you are constantly (常) at your workplace (勤), you are a full-time employee.
Example: 彼は病院で常勤の医師として働いています。(かれはびょういんでじょうきんのいしとしてはたらいています。)
-He works as a full-time doctor at the hospital.
}

相図-
{
相図 (あいず) - Signal / Sign
A variation of 合図, focusing on the "mutual" (相) aspect of a plan or map (図) used to communicate non-verbally.
Memory Tip: A mutual (相) plan or diagram (図) used to send a secret sign.
Example: 目で相図を送った。(めであいずをおくった。)
-I sent a signal with my eyes.
}

加湿器-
{
加湿器 (かしつき) - Humidifier
A compound noun consisting of 加 (addition), 湿 (moisture), and 器 (device/tool).
Memory Tip: A device (器) that adds (加) wetness (湿) to the dry winter air.
Example: 冬は加湿器を使います。 (ふゆはかしつきをつかいます。)
-I use a humidifier in winter.
}

乾季-
{
乾季 (かんき) - Dry season
A compound of 乾 (dry) and 季 (season), used specifically to refer to the arid period in tropical climates.
Memory Tip: It is the season (季) where everything is dry (乾).
Example: サバンナには乾季がある。 (さばんなにはかんきがある。)
-The savanna has a dry season.
}

虫除け-
{
虫除け (むしよけ) - Insect repellent
A compound noun referring to substances or devices used to keep bugs away.
Memory Tip: Using something to make sure 'insects' (虫) are 'excluded' (除).
Example: 庭いじりの前に虫除けスプレーを使う。 (にわいじりのまえにむしよけすぷれーをつかう。)
-Use insect repellent spray before gardening.
}

海鮮-
{
海鮮 (かいせん) - Seafood
A noun commonly used in culinary contexts to describe fresh products harvested from the sea.
Memory Tip: These are 'fresh' (鮮) ingredients taken straight from the 'sea' (海).
Example: 市場で新鮮な海鮮丼を食べた。 (いちばでしんぜんなかいせんどんをたべた。)
-I ate a fresh seafood bowl at the market.
}

定額-
{
定額 (ていがく) - fixed amount / flat rate
Combining 定 (fix/determine) and 額 (amount/sum), this is commonly used for fixed prices or subscription fees.
Memory Tip: A "fixed" (定) "sum of money" (額) that doesn't change.
Example: 定額制のサービスを利用する。 (ていがくせいのさーびすをりようする。)
-I use a flat-rate service.
}

他動詞-
{
他動詞 (たどうし) - Transitive verb
A grammatical term for verbs that take a direct object (marked by 'wo'). It literally means 'other-moving-word'.
Memory Tip: The verb moves the action onto 'others' (他) or objects, unlike intransitive verbs which focus on self.
Example: 「作る」は典型的な他動詞です。 (「つくる」はてんけいてきなたどうしです。)
-'To make' is a typical transitive verb.
}

閉館時間-
{
閉館時間 (へいかんじかん) - Closing time
A compound noun combining 閉 (close), 館 (building/hall), and 時間 (time), typically used for public facilities like libraries or museums.
Memory Tip: Imagine a 館 (building) where the 時間 (time) has come to 閉 (close) the doors.
Example: この図書館の閉館時間は午後八時です。 (このとしょかんのへいかんじかんはごごはちじです。)
-The closing time of this library is 8 PM.
}

無休-
{
無休 (むきゅう) - No holidays / Open every day
A noun formed by combining 無 (none/without) and 休 (rest/holiday). It is commonly used in the phrase 年中無休 (open year-round).
Memory Tip: A business with 無 (zero) 休 (rest days) is always open for customers.
Example: そのレストランは年中無休で営業している。 (そのれすとらんはねんじゅうむきゅうでえいぎょうしている。)
-That restaurant is open all year round without any holidays.
}

給油所-
{
給油所 (きゅうゆじょ) - Gas station / Filling station
A formal term combining 給 (supply), 油 (oil/fuel), and 所 (place). It is the technical equivalent of the common loanword "gasoline stand."
Memory Tip: A 所 (place) that specializes in 給 (supplying) 油 (oil/gas) to vehicles.
Example: 最寄りの給油所まであと五キロだ。 (もよりのきゅうゆじょまであとごきろだ。)
-It's another five kilometers to the nearest gas station.
}

数詞-
{
数詞 (すうし) - Numeral / Number word
A linguistic category combining 数 (number) and 詞 (word/part of speech), used to express quantities or positions in a series.
Memory Tip: A 詞 (word) used to express a 数 (number).
Example: 多くの言語で、数詞は名詞の前に置かれる。 (おおくのげんごで、すうしはめいしのまえにおかれる。)
-In many languages, numerals are placed before nouns.
}

音訓-
{
音訓 (おんくん) - On and Kun readings
This term refers collectively to the On-yomi (Sino-Japanese) and Kun-yomi (Native Japanese) readings of kanji.
Memory Tip: A compound of the first characters of the two systems: 'Sound' (音) and 'Instruction/Reading' (訓).
Example: 漢字の音訓を一つずつ確認する。 (かんじのおんくんをひとつずつかくにんする。)
-Check the On and Kun readings of the kanji one by one.
}

字典-
{
字典 (じてん) - Character dictionary
A dictionary that focuses on individual characters (kanji), providing their readings, meanings, and origins. It differs from 'jiten' (辞典), which focuses on words.
Memory Tip: A 'canon' or 'law' (典) of individual 'characters' (字).
Example: 漢和字典で熟語を調べる。 (かんわじてんでじゅくごをしらべる。)
-I look up idioms in the Kanji-Japanese dictionary.
}

前売り券-
{
前売り券 (まえうりけん) - Advance ticket
A compound of 前 (before), 売り (selling), and 券 (ticket). It refers to tickets purchased in advance of a performance or event.
Memory Tip: Buy the ticket (券) before (前) the selling (売り) counter gets crowded on the day.
Example: 前売り券を二枚買いました。 (まえうりけんをにまいかいました。)
-I bought two advance tickets.
}

誤り-
{
誤り (あやまり) - error; mistake
The noun form of the verb 誤る (to err). It is used for formal mistakes in logic, calculations, or writing.
Memory Tip: The kanji 誤 combines 'words' (言) and 'give' (呉). Giving the wrong words leads to a mistake.
Example: 記述に誤りがありました。 (きじゅつにあやまりがありました。)
-There was an error in the description.
}

訓読み-
{
訓読み (くんよみ) - native Japanese reading
Refers to the reading of a kanji based on the original Japanese word, rather than the Chinese-derived reading.
Memory Tip: 'Kun' is the 'kindly' local Japanese reading, while 'Yomi' simply means reading.
Example: この漢字の訓読みは何ですか？ (このかんじのくんよみはなんですか？)
-What is the Kun-yomi of this kanji?
}

溶かす-
{
溶かす (とかす) - To melt / To dissolve
A transitive verb used for melting a solid into liquid (like ice) or dissolving a substance into a liquid (like sugar in water).
Memory Tip: The water radical (氵) on the left indicates the involvement of liquid in the process of melting or dissolving.
Example: 砂糖を水に溶かす。 (さとうをみずにとかす。)
-Dissolve sugar in water.
}

従業-
{
従業 (じゅうぎょう) - Employment / Engagement in work
Combines 'follow/accompany' (従) with 'business/work' (業), describing the act of being employed.
Memory Tip: To 'follow' (従) the 'occupation' (業) means you are actively working in a job.
Example: 彼は長年その仕事に従業している。 (かれはながねんそのしごとにじゅうぎょうしている。)
-He has been engaged in that work for many years.

海水魚-
{
海水魚 (かいすいぎょ) - saltwater fish
A biological classification for fish that live in the ocean rather than freshwater.
Memory Tip: A simple combination of Sea (海) + Water (水) + Fish (魚).
Example: 彼は海水魚を飼っている。 (かれはかいすいぎょをかっている。)
-He keeps saltwater fish.

恨み-
{
恨み (うらみ) - Grudge/Resentment
The noun form of 恨む (uramu), referring to a deep-seated feeling of malice or bitterness toward someone.
Memory Tip: A heart (忄) that has reached its limit (艮) results in a long-lasting grudge.
Example: 彼は過去の恨みを忘れていない。 (かれはかこのうらみをわすれていない。)
-He has not forgotten past grudges.

彩り-
{
彩り (いろどり) - Coloring/Color scheme
Refers to the arrangement of colors or adding color to something to make it more appealing.
Memory Tip: Start with "Iro" (color) and imagine "drawing" (dori) a beautiful landscape with many shades.
Example: 料理に彩りを添えるためにパセリを散らす。 (りょうりにいろどりをそえるためにぱせりをちらす。)
-Sprinkle parsley to add color to the dish.

照らす-
{
照らす (てらす) - To illuminate / to shine on
A transitive verb used when a light source shines upon an object or area. It can also mean to compare against a standard.
Memory Tip: Tera sounds like "terra" (earth); imagine the sun shining down to illuminate the earth.
Example: 月が海面を照らしている。(つきがかいめんをてらしている。)
-The moon is illuminating the surface of the sea.

揚げ出し-
{
揚げ出し (あげだし) - deep-fried food served in broth
A compound noun consisting of 揚げ (deep-fried) and 出し (stock/broth), typically referring to tofu or eggplant.

裏切り-
{
裏切り (うらぎり) - betrayal / treachery
Formed from 裏 (back/reverse) and 切り (cutting), implying a strike from behind.
Memory Tip: It is literally 'cutting' (切り) someone's 'back' (裏), the ultimate act of bad faith.
Example: 友人の裏切りは悲しい。 (ゆうじんのうらぎりはかなしい。)

縦書-
{
縦書 (たてがき) - vertical writing
Composed of 縦 (vertical/height) and 書 (writing). It refers to the traditional Japanese style of writing from top to bottom.
Memory Tip: Focus on the 'vertical' (縦) direction of the 'writing' (書).
Example: 日本の小説は縦書が多い。 (にほんのしょうせつはたてがきがおおい。)
-Many Japanese novels use vertical writing.

入館料-
{
入館料 (にゅうかんりょう) - admission fee
A compound of 入 (enter), 館 (building/hall), and 料 (fee/charge).
Memory Tip: Think of it as the fee for Entering (入) the Hall (館).
Example: 入館料は千円です。 (にゅうかんりょうはせんえんです。)
-The admission fee is 1,000 yen.
}

減らす-
{
減らす (へらす) - to reduce, to decrease
The transitive verb meaning to make something smaller in quantity, size, or number.
Memory Tip: The water radical (氵) suggests a liquid level lowering or being subtracted.
Example: 支出を減らす必要があります。 (ししゅつをへらすひつようがあります。)
-It is necessary to reduce expenses.
}

香り-
{
香り (かおり) - scent, aroma, fragrance
This noun is typically used to describe pleasant smells like those from flowers, food, or perfume.
Memory Tip: The kanji combines 'grain' (禾) and 'sun' (日). Imagine the sweet scent of grain drying in the warm sun.
Example: コーヒーの良い香りがする。 (こーひーのよいかおりがする。)
-There is a nice aroma of coffee.

伺い-
{
伺い (うかがい) - inquiry, humble visit
The noun form of the humble verb 'ukagau', used when visiting or asking someone of higher status.
Memory Tip: It sounds like 'You-go-guy' - you are the guy going to visit a boss to ask for advice.
Example: お伺いを立てる。 (おうかがいをたてる。)
-To make an inquiry (to a superior).

支払い-
{
支払い (しはらい) - payment
Derived from the verb 'shiharau', combining 'support/branch' (支) and 'sweep/pay' (払).
Memory Tip: You 'sweep' (払) your money away to 'support' (支) the store; that is a payment.
Example: 支払いは現金ですか？ (しはらいはげんきんですか？)
-Is the payment in cash?

傷つける-
{
傷つける (きずつける) - to hurt, to damage
A transitive verb used for both physical injuries and hurting someone's feelings.
Memory Tip: 'Kizu' (wound/scar) + 'Tsukeru' (to attach). You are literally 'attaching a wound' to someone.
Example: 誰の心も傷つけたくない。 (だれのこころもきずつけたくない。)
-I don't want to hurt anyone's feelings.
}

悩み-
{
悩み (なやみ) - Worry, trouble, distress
Noun form of 'nayamu', describing a mental burden, internal conflict, or a problem one is brooding over.
Memory Tip: The heart radical (忄) in the verb form shows that this 'trouble' is something felt deeply within the mind.
Example: 彼は仕事の悩みを抱えている。(かれはしごとのなやみをかかえている)
-He is carrying worries about his work.
}

だからこそ-
{
だからこそ (だからこそ) - Precisely because; for that very reason
It combines the conjunction だから (so) with the emphatic particle こそ (precisely) to highlight a specific reason as the primary motivation.
Memory Tip: Think of it as 'Therefore (だから) + EXACTLY (こそ)'—it puts a spotlight on the reason rather than just stating a result.
Example: 失敗した。だからこそ、次は絶対に勝ちたい。 (しっぱいした。だからこそ、つぎはぜったいにかちたい。)
-I failed. That is exactly why I want to win next time.
}

〜わけにはいかない-
{
〜わけにはいかない (〜わけにはいかない) - Cannot afford to / Must not / Impossible for social or moral reasons
This grammar indicates that while something might be physically possible, one cannot do it due to social norms, responsibility, or specific circumstances. It combines 'wake' (reason) and 'ikanai' (cannot go/proceed).
Memory Tip: Think: 'With this reason (wake), things simply cannot go (ikanai) in that direction.'
Example: 明日は大事な試験があるから、休むわけにはいかない。(あしたはだいじなしけんがあるから、やすむわけにはいかない)
-Since there is an important exam tomorrow, I cannot afford to be absent.
}

夜更かし-
{
夜更かし (よふかし) - Staying up late
This is a noun derived from the verb 夜更かす, referring to the act of staying awake late into the night. It is most commonly used with the verb する (to do).
Memory Tip: Combine 夜 (night) with 更 (to grow late/renew). You are staying awake as the night 'grows late' or pushes 'further'.
Example: 昨夜は試験のために夜更かしをした。 (さくやはしけんのためによふかしをした。)
-I stayed up late last night for the exam.
}

世に出る-
{
世に出る (よにでる) - To be released to the public; to become famous; to succeed in life
This idiom literally means "to go out into the world," used for creative works being published or individuals achieving recognition.
Memory Tip: Imagine a hidden gem finally coming "out" (出る) into the "world" (世) for everyone to see.
Example: その新製品は来月世に出る。 (そのしんせいひんはらいげつよにでる。)
-That new product will be released to the world next month.
}

焦り-
{
焦り (あさり) - Impatience / Panic
The noun form of the verb 焦る (aseru), it describes the feeling of being flustered or rushed under pressure.
Memory Tip: When you are in too much of a hurry, you might scorch (焦) your food.
Example: 焦りは禁物だ。 (あせりはきんもつだ。)
-Haste is forbidden.
}

取り分け-
{
取り分け (とりわけ) - Especially/Above all
An adverb used to single out one item as being particularly noteworthy among others.
Memory Tip: Combination of 'tori' (take) and 'wake' (divide); imagine taking one piece and setting it apart because it's special.
Example: 彼は取り分け数学が得意だ。 (かれはとりわけすうがくがくといだ。)
-He is especially good at mathematics.
}

暮れる-
{
暮れる (くれる) - To grow dark/to end
An intransitive verb used primarily for the day ending (sunset) or the passage of a season/year.
Memory Tip: The kanji has 'sun' (日) at the bottom, setting beneath a thicket or roof of time.
Example: 日が暮れる (ひがくれる)
-The sun goes down / The day ends
}

最悪-
{
最悪 (さいあく) - Worst
A noun or na-adjective indicating the lowest possible quality or the most terrible situation imaginable.
Memory Tip: Combining 'most' (最) and 'bad' (悪) to mean the absolute worst.
Example: 今日は最悪の一日だった。 (きょうはさいあくのいちにちだった。)
-Today was the worst day.
}

折れる-
{
折れる (おれる) - To break/To be folded
An intransitive ichidan verb used for objects snapping or being folded.
Memory Tip: The left side is 扌 (hand) and the right is 斤 (axe); a hand uses an axe to break something.
Example: 枝が折れる。 (えだがおれる。)
-The branch breaks.
}

従兄弟-
{
従兄弟 (いとこ) - Male cousin
A noun specifically referring to a male cousin, combining 'obey/follow' (従) with 'brothers' (兄弟).
Memory Tip: These are the 'brothers' (兄弟) who 'follow' (従) from a different branch of the family tree.
Example: 従兄弟と遊ぶ (いとことあそぶ)
-Play with my male cousin
}

姿-
{
姿 (すがた) - Figure / Appearance / Form
Refers to the physical shape or appearance of someone or something as it is perceived.
Memory Tip: Look at the next (次) woman (女) to see her graceful figure.
Example: 彼の後ろ姿を見た。 (かれのうしろすがたをみた)
-I saw his figure from behind.
}

眼-
{
眼 (め) - Eye, vision
A noun for the eye, often used in medical, technical, or literary contexts compared to the simpler 目.
Memory Tip: The "eye" (目) radical is paired with a part meaning "stop/steady," suggesting a fixed gaze or eyeball.
Example: 眼を閉じて。 (めを とじて。)
-Close your eyes.
}

買う-
{
買う (かう) - 
A transitive Godan verb meaning to purchase or buy items.
Memory Tip: The bottom part of the kanji is 貝 (shell), which was used as ancient currency.
Example: 新しい車を買うつもりだ。 (あたらしいくるまをかうつもりだ。)
-I intend to buy a new car.
}

殺す-
{
殺す (ころす) - Kill, Murder
A transitive Godan verb meaning to kill or murder.
Memory Tip: The right side radical resembles a weapon or tool used to strike or kill.
Example: クモを殺さないで。 (くもをころさないで。)
-Don't kill the spider.
}

〜みたい-
{
〜みたい (みたい) - Like / Similar to / Resembling
An auxiliary adjective used to describe something that resembles something else, or to make an inference based on appearances. Unlike the more formal ~yō da, this is common in daily conversation.
Memory Tip: Think of the verb miru (to see). It looks like (looks mi-) something else.
Example: 彼はプロの歌手みたいだ。 (かれはぷろのかしゅみたいだ。)
-He is like a professional singer.
}

～てしまう-
{
～てしまう (～てしまう) - To finish completely / To regret
Attached to the -te form of verbs; often contracted to 〜ちゃう in casual Japanese.
Memory Tip: Focus on the "regret" aspect of something happening beyond your control.
Example: 全部食べてしまいました。(ぜんぶたべてしまいました)
-I ended up eating it all.
}

無くなる-
{
無くなる (なくなる) - To be lost; to run out
This verb describes physical items going missing or resources like time or money being depleted. It is the intransitive result of something becoming 'nothing' (naku).
Memory Tip: Combine the concepts of 'nothing' (naku) and 'to become' (naru) to visualize something vanishing.
Example: 自信が無くなる。 (じしんがなくなる。)
-To lose self-confidence.
}

柄-
{
柄 (がら) - Pattern; design
Refers specifically to the visual design on surfaces like fabric or paper. It can also figuratively refer to a person's character or physique.
Memory Tip: The tree (木) radical reminds us of the natural patterns found in wood grain or bark.
Example: 派手な柄の服。 (はでながらのふく。)
-Clothes with a flashy pattern.
}

続ける-
{
続ける (つづける) - To continue; to keep up
A transitive verb used when a person maintains an activity without stopping.
Memory Tip: The left radical 糸 (thread) suggests a continuous, unbroken line of action.
Example: 努力を続ける。 (どりょくをつづける。)
-To continue putting in effort.
}

間-
{
間 (あいだ) - Between / interval
This kanji represents the space or time separating two points. It is often used with the particle 'の' to describe location.
Memory Tip: Look for the SUN (日) shining through the GAP in the middle of the GATE (門).
Example: AとBの間にあります。 (えーとびーのあいだにあります。)
-It is between A and B.
}

間もなく-
{
間もなく (まもなく) - Soon / shortly
This adverbial phrase literally means "without an interval." It is frequently used in formal announcements such as at train stations or airports.
Memory Tip: If there is "no" (なく) "interval" (間), then the event is happening right now.
Example: 電車が間もなく参ります。 (でんしゃがまもなくまいります。)
-The train will arrive shortly.
}

間に合う-
{
間に合う (まにあう) - To be in time
An intransitive verb meaning to make it within the allotted time. It combines the concepts of 'time interval' and 'to fit/match'.
Memory Tip: You and the deadline "match" (合う) inside the same "interval" (間) of time.
Example: 会議に間に合いました。 (かいぎにまにあいました。)
-I was in time for the meeting.
}

尚-
{
尚 (なお) - Furthermore/Still
A formal adverb used to add information or to state that a condition continues.
Memory Tip: Looks like a small altar where a flame is still burning.
Example: 尚、詳細は後ほど。 (なお、しょうさいはのちほど。)
-Furthermore, details will follow later.
}

夜-
{
夜 (よる) - Night / evening
A common noun for the period of darkness between sunset and sunrise. It can also be read as 'ya' in compounds like 'yakyuu' (baseball).
Memory Tip: When it is "Yoru" (night), it is time to "Roll" into bed under the covers.
Example: 夜は冷えますね。 (よるはひえますね。)
-It gets cold at night, doesn't it?
}

着る-
{
着る (きる) - To wear (upper body)
An ichidan verb used specifically for clothing put on over the torso, such as shirts, sweaters, or jackets.
Memory Tip: You use a "Key" (Ki) to open your closet and "wear" your favorite shirt.
Example: 上着を着ます。 (うわぎをきます。)
-I will put on a jacket.
}

不燃ゴミ-
{
不燃ゴミ (ふねんゴミ) - Non-combustible garbage
A compound noun consisting of "not" (不), "burn" (燃), and "trash" (ゴミ).
Memory Tip: Think of the "fire" (火) radical in 燃; adding 不 makes it "not fire-friendly" or unburnable trash.
Example: 不燃ゴミは金曜日に出してください。 (ふねんゴミは きんようびに だしてください。)
-Please put out the non-combustible garbage on Friday.
}

日の出-
{
日の出 (ひので) - Sunrise
A compound noun formed by 日 (sun), the particle の, and the noun form of 出る (to exit/come out).
Memory Tip: Think of it literally as the "Sun's (日の) Exit (出)" onto the stage of the sky.
Example: 日の出は五時です。(ひのではごじです。)
-Sunrise is at five o'clock.
}

中々-
{
中々 (なかなか) - Quite; considerably; not easily
An adverb that intensifies the degree of something. In positive contexts, it means 'fairly/quite'; with negative verbs, it means 'not easily/not readily'.
Memory Tip: Repeating the character for 'middle' (中) suggests that something is well beyond the average or expected level.
Example: 中々難しい問題だ。 (なかなかむずかしいもんだいだ。)
-It is quite a difficult problem.
}

娘-
{
娘 (むすめ) - Daughter
A noun used to refer to one's own daughter or a young woman in general contexts.
Memory Tip: A "good" (良) "woman" (女) in the family is your daughter.
Example: 娘は大学生です。(むすめはだいがくせいです。)
-My daughter is a university student.
}

過ぎる-
{
過ぎる (すぎる) - To pass, to exceed
A ru-verb that can stand alone or act as a suffix to adjectives and verbs to mean "too much."
Memory Tip: The movement radical (辶) shows someone walking past and exceeding a limit.
Example: 食べ過ぎました。(たべすぎました。)
-I ate too much.
}

空間-
{
空間 (くうかん) - Space/Room
A noun describing physical space, a void, or the atmosphere of a place. It combines 'sky/empty' (空) and 'interval/between' (間).
Memory Tip: Physical space is the 'empty' (空) 'interval' (間) that exists between objects.
Example: この部屋は空間が広い。(このへやはくうかんがひろい)
-This room has a lot of space.
}

記述-
{
記述 (きじゅつ) - Description, account
Used as a noun or suru-verb to denote writing down facts or details in an objective, descriptive manner.
Memory Tip: Combining 'record/scribe' (記) and 'state/narrate' (述) to describe something in writing.
Example: 彼の記述は非常に正確だ。 (かれのきじゅつはひじょうにせいかくだ。)
-His description is very accurate.
}

得る-
{
得る (える) - To obtain, to gain
A basic Ichidan verb used for acquiring knowledge, permission, or benefits. It can also be read as 'uru' in more formal or literary contexts.
Memory Tip: The left radical means 'road' or 'walking', suggesting you go out to get or obtain what you need.
Example: 知識を得る。(ちしきをえる)
-To gain knowledge.
}

軟らかい-
{
軟らかい (やわらかい) - Soft / Tender
Specifically describes materials that yield easily to pressure, often used for food texture or leather.
Memory Tip: The radical on the left is 'car' (車); think of a very soft, cushioned car seat.
Example: このお肉はとても軟らかいです。 (このおにくはとてもやわらかいです。)
-This meat is very tender.
}

脅し-
{
脅し (おどし) - Threat / Intimidation
The noun form of 'odosu', referring to an act or statement meant to frighten or coerce someone.
Memory Tip: Three 'power' (力) radicals grouped together represent overwhelming force used to threaten others.
Example: それはただの脅しだ。 (それはただのおどしだ。)
-That is just a threat.
}

賭ける-
{
賭ける (かける) - To wager; to bet; to risk
An Ichidan verb used for gambling or for metaphorically risking one's life or reputation.
Memory Tip: The kanji includes 貝 (shell), which was an ancient form of money used for betting.
Example: 命を賭けて戦う。 (いのちをかけてたたかう。)
-Fight risking one's life.
}

上昇-
{
上昇 (じょうしょう) - Rise, ascent
This noun frequently acts as a suru-verb to describe something moving upward, such as prices, temperature, or physical altitude.
Memory Tip: Combining 'up' (上) and 'rising sun' (昇), it creates an image of a steady upward movement.
Example: 物価が急激に上昇した。 (ぶっかがきゅうげきにじょうしょうした。)
-Prices rose sharply.
}

占い-
{
占い (うらない) - Fortune-telling, divination
The noun form of the verb 占う, encompassing various methods like astrology, palmistry, or tarot.
Memory Tip: Imagine looking for what is 'Ura' (hidden/behind) using a 'nai' (knife/tool) of insight.
Example: 占いで今年の運勢を調べた。 (うらないでことしのうんせいをしらべた。)
-I checked this year's fortune through fortune-telling.
}

元パートナー-
{
元パートナー (もとぱーとなー) - Former partner, ex-partner
Combines the prefix 元 (moto), meaning 'former', with the loanword 'partner'.
Memory Tip: Use 'Moto' for anything 'Ex'—think of your 'original' (original source) partner.
Example: 元パートナーに偶然会った。 (もとぱーとなーにぐうぜんあった。)
-I ran into my former partner by chance.
}

詰まる-
{
詰まる (つまる) - to be blocked, to be stuffed, to be clogged
An intransitive verb describing a state where something is packed too tightly or obstructed.
Memory Tip: Imagine objects being squeezed until they are 'tsu' (tightly) packed inside a space.
Example: 鼻が詰まっている。 (はながつまっている。)
-My nose is stuffed up.
}

去る-
{
去る (さる) - To leave / To pass away
Refers to departing a place or a specific time/event passing into the past.
Memory Tip: It looks like a person walking away from a specific ground or base.
Example: 彼は町を去った。 (かれはまちをさった。)
-He left the town.
}

折角-
{
折角 (せっかく) - with trouble, at great pains, long-awaited
Used to express that an opportunity is precious because it was rare or required significant effort to realize.
Memory Tip: Combining "fold" (折) and "angle" (角); imagine the effort of folding every corner of origami perfectly.
Example: 折角来たのだから。 (せっかくきたのだから。)
-Since you went to the trouble of coming.
}

解く-
{
解く (とく) - To solve, to untie, to unfasten
Used for solving puzzles/math or literally untying a knot. It implies taking something complex and breaking it down.
Memory Tip: Using a knife (right side) to separate horns/corners (left side) to solve a problem.
Example: 数学の問題を解く。(すうがくのもんだいをとく。)
-To solve a math problem.
}

事件-
{
事件 (じけん) - Incident / Case
Refers to an event, often of a criminal or troublesome nature, that requires investigation.
Memory Tip: A combination of 'matter' (事) and 'item' (件) creates a specific incident to handle.
Example: 警察がその事件を調べている。 (けいさつがそのじけんをしらべている。)
-The police are investigating the incident.
}

積もる-
{
積もる (つもる) - To pile up; to accumulate
A Godan verb primarily used for physical things like snow or dust, or abstract things like stress.
Memory Tip: To pile up "Two" (Tsu) "More" (Mo) things on the "Roof" (Ru).
Example: 雪が五センチ積もった。 (ゆきがごせんちつもった。)
-Snow piled up five centimeters.
}

我々-
{
我々 (われわれ) - We; us
A formal or humble plural first-person pronoun often used in speeches or to represent a company/group.
Memory Tip: The kanji for "self" (我) is doubled with the repetition symbol (々) to mean "many selves."
Example: 我々の意見は一致している。 (われわれのいけんはいっちしている。)
-Our opinions are in agreement.
}

身-

身 (み) - Body / Self / Status
Refers to the physical body, the flesh of a fish, or one's social standing/personal station.

唯-
{
唯 (ただ) - Only / Merely
Often used to emphasize that something is nothing more than what is stated.

-We are only friends

競う-
{
競う (きそう) - To compete, vie
A Godan verb used when two or more parties struggle or contest for superiority or a prize.
Memory Tip: Two 'stand' (立) radicals side-by-side suggest two people standing up to challenge each other.
Example: 二人は足の速さを競った。 (ふたりはあしのはやさをきそった。)

見詰める-
{
見詰める (みつめる) - To gaze/stare
A compound verb of "見" (to see) and "詰める" (to pack/stuff). It means to fix one's eyes steadily on something.
Memory Tip: "See" and "stuff" your entire focus onto a single point.
Example: 彼は静かに海を見詰めた (かれはしずかにうみをみつめた)
-He gazed quietly at the sea.
}

表情-
{
表情 (ひょうじょう) - Facial expression
Combines 'surface appearance' (表) with 'feeling/emotion' (情). It describes how feelings manifest on the face.
Memory Tip: Emotions (情) being expressed on the surface (表) of your face.
Example: 彼女の表情が明るくなった。 (かのじょのひょうじょうがあかるくなった。)
-Her facial expression brightened.
}

維持する-
{
維持する (いじする) - To maintain
The verb form of the noun '維持', used to describe the action of preserving a condition.
Memory Tip: Simply perform (suru) the act of holding (持) with ties (維).
Example: 体重を維持する。 (たいじゅうをいじする。)
-To maintain one's body weight.
}

身振り-
{
身振り (みぶり) - Gesture, body motion
Combines 身 (body) and 振り (shaking/movement), describing physical expressions used to communicate.
Memory Tip: Your body (身) doing the shaking or moving (振り) to tell a story.
Example: 彼は身振り手振りで説明した。(かれはみぶりてぶりでせつめいした。)
-He explained with gestures and hand movements.
}

我が国-
{
我が国 (わがくに) - Our country
A formal and literary term where '我が' (my/our) precedes '国' (country). It is frequently used in political speeches or news reports.
Memory Tip: 'Waga' is like 'Wagging' a finger to claim 'Our country' for the group.
Example: 我が国の経済は安定している。(わがくにのけいざいはあんていしている。)
-Our country's economy is stable.
}

迷わす-
{
迷わす (まよわす) - To perplex, to bewilder, to seduce
The causative form of 迷う (to be lost), used when someone or something causes another to lose their way or mental focus.
Memory Tip: Think of 'Mayo' (迷) making you lose your way in a 'wasu' (words) maze.
Example: 彼女の香水の香りが男たちを迷わす。 (かのじょのこうすいのかおりがおとこたちをまよわす。)
-The scent of her perfume bewilders the men.
}

裁判-
{
裁判 (さいばん) - trial, judgement
Combines "judge" (裁) and "distinguish" (判). Specifically relates to legal court proceedings.
Memory Tip: Two different kanji for judging combined to form a legal trial.
Example: 裁判官が判決を下した。(裁判官がはんけつをくだした。)
-The judge handed down the verdict.
}

眺める-
{
眺める (ながめる) - To gaze at / To stare at / To admire the view
An ichidan verb describing the act of looking at something (usually scenery) for a long time or with interest.
Memory Tip: Starts with 'Naga' (long); think of taking a 'long' look at a beautiful view.
Example: 海を眺める。 (うみをながめる。)
-To gaze at the sea.
}

編集-
{
編集 (へんしゅう) - Editing / Compilation
A noun referring to the process of organizing and preparing media for publication.
Memory Tip: Imagine weaving (糸/thread) together gathered (集) pieces of information into a book.
Example: 彼は映像の編集が上手だ。 (かれはえいぞうのへんしゅうがじょうずだ。)
-He is good at video editing.
}

ねだる-
{
ねだる - To coax/To pester/To beg for something
A verb used when someone persistently asks for something, especially a child asking a parent.
Memory Tip: 'Nedaru' sounds like 'nag-daru' — to nag someone until they give you what you want.
Example: 子供はおもちゃをねだった。 (こどもはおもちゃをねだった。)
-The child pestered (their parent) for a toy.
}

とびだす-
{
とびだす - To jump out/To dash out
A verb describing the sudden action of leaping or rushing out of somewhere unexpectedly.
Memory Tip: 'Tobi' (fly/jump) + 'dasu' (to put out) — to 'fly yourself out' of a place suddenly.
Example: 猫が茂みからとびだした。 (ねこがしげみからとびだした。)
-The cat jumped out of the bushes.
}

ふせる-
{
ふせる - To lie face down/To crouch low
A verb describing the act of pressing oneself flat against the ground, often to hide or take cover.
Memory Tip: 'Fuseru' — imagine 'fusing' yourself to the floor, pressing down as flat as possible.
Example: 彼は物音を聞いてふせた。 (かれはものおとをきいてふせた。)
-He heard a sound and crouched down low.
}

たたずむ-
{
たたずむ - To stand still/To linger quietly
A verb describing the act of standing quietly in place, often with a pensive or contemplative mood.
Memory Tip: 'Tatazumu' — imagine someone standing so still they become like a 'statue-zumu'.
Example: 彼女は窓の前にたたずんでいた。 (かのじょはまどのまえにたたずんでいた。)
-She stood quietly before the window.
}

存在-
{
存在 (そんざい) - Existence
A noun combining 存 (preserve/exist) and 在 (be at/location).
Memory Tip: To preserve (存) a person in a specific location (在) is to acknowledge their existence.
Example: 彼の存在は大きいです。(かれのそんざいはおおきいです)
-His existence is significant.
}

存在する-
{
存在する (そんざいする) - To exist
A suru-verb formed by adding 'suru' to the noun 'existence'.
Memory Tip: Take the noun for existence and add the 'doing' verb to make it an active state of being.
Example: 幽霊は存在すると思いますか？(ゆうれいはそんざいするとおもいますか)
-Do you think ghosts exist?
}

募集中-
{
募集中 (ぼしゅうちゅう) - Recruiting, now hiring
This term combines 募集 (recruitment) with the suffix 中, which indicates an ongoing state or being in the middle of an action.
Memory Tip: The kanji 中 (middle) means they are right in the middle of a hiring process.
Example: スタッフ募集中です。(すたっふぼしゅうちゅうです。)
-Staff are being recruited.
}

何故なら-
{
何故なら (なぜなら) - Because, the reason is
A formal conjunction used at the start of a sentence to provide the reason for a previous statement, often ending in 'からだ'.
Memory Tip: 'Naze' (Why) + 'Nara' (If it is) = 'If you ask why, it is because...'
Example: 傘を持ってきた。何故なら雨が降るからだ。 (かさをもってきた。なぜならあめがふるからだ。)
-I brought an umbrella. The reason is that it will rain.
}

クモの巣-
{
クモの巣 (くものす) - Spider web
A compound noun combining 'kumo' (spider) and 'su' (nest/home).
Memory Tip: Literally 'The spider's nest'; think of the web as the spider's base of operations.
Example: クモの巣に引っかかった (くものすにひっかかった)
-I got caught in a spider web.
}

ハチの巣-
{
ハチの巣 (はちのす) - Beehive / Wasp nest
A compound noun combining 'hachi' (bee/wasp) and 'su' (nest/hive).
Memory Tip: Literally 'The bee's nest'; refers to the physical structure bees live in.
Example: 木の上にハチの巣がある (きのうえにはちのすがある)
-There is a beehive in the tree.

統一-
{
統一 (とういつ) - Unity/unification
Refers to bringing separate elements together into a single, cohesive whole or a standardized system.
Memory Tip: 統 (ruling/governing) + 一 (one) = Governing many things into a single one.
Example: 精神を統一する。 (せいしんをとういつする。)

蛍 (ほたる) - Firefly

顔付き-

顔付き (かおつき) - Facial expression, look
This noun combines 顔 (face) and the suffix -付き (state/appearance) to describe the specific look or countenance on someone's face.

澄ます (すます) - To clear; to be poised/affect
This verb means to make something clear (like water) or to look cool/composed. It is also used in the idiom 'mimi o sumasu' (to strain one's ears).
Memory Tip: The 'water' radical (氵) is on the left; imagine making water 'clear' by letting the sediment settle.

身体 (からだ) - Body

落ち-
{
落ち (おち) - Fall, drop, punchline
The noun form of 'ochiru' (to fall). In the context of jokes or Rakugo storytelling, it refers to the final punchline.
Memory Tip: The 'fall' of the story is where the joke finally lands.
Example: その話には落ちがない (そのはなしにはおちがない)
-That story has no punchline.
}

浜-
{
浜 (はま) - Beach / Seashore
Refers to the sandy area along the coast or a lake.
Memory Tip: Water radical (氵) next to soldiers (兵). Think of soldiers landing on a beach.
Example: 浜辺で貝を拾う。 (はまべでかいをひろう。)
-Pick up shells at the beach.
}

事情-
{
事情 (じじょう) - Circumstances, reasons, situation
Refers to the underlying facts or conditions of a particular matter.
Memory Tip: A 'matter' (事) combined with 'feelings/conditions' (情) explains the situation.
Example: 複雑な事情があります。 (ふくざつなじじょうがあります。)
-There are complicated circumstances.
}

銃-
{
銃 (じゅう) - Gun, firearm
Specifically refers to handheld firearms and appears in many compound words like 拳銃 (handgun).
Memory Tip: The metal (金) radical on the left represents the material of the firearm.
Example: 彼は銃を持っています。(かれはじゅうをもっています)
-He has a gun.
}

狙い-
{
狙い (ねらい) - Aim/Objective
The noun form of the verb "nerau," meaning the target or the intended goal.
Memory Tip: The animal radical on the left suggests a hunter's aim at prey.
Example: 彼の狙いは的中した。 (かれのねらいはてきちゅうした。)
-His aim was right on the mark.
}

宜しい-
{
宜しい (よろしい) - Good, all right (polite)
This is the formal version of the adjective 良い (ii), used frequently in polite business interactions or formal requests.
Memory Tip: The kanji 宜 signifies 'best suited.' Think of 'Yo-ro-shii' as 'Your-rosy-choice'—the most appropriate option.
Example: お名前を伺っても宜しいですか？ (おなまえをうかがってもよろしいですか？)
-May I ask your name?
}

中国製-
{
中国製 (ちゅうごくせい) - Made in China
This compound noun consists of 中国 (China) and the suffix 製 (manufactured/produced).
Memory Tip: Look for 'China' followed by the complex kanji for manufacturing on product tags.
Example: これは中国製のスマホです。 (これはちゅうごくせいのすまほです。)
-This is a smartphone made in China.
}

飾り-
{
飾り (かざり) - decoration, ornament
The noun form of the verb 'kazaru' (to decorate), used for aesthetic or festive items.
Memory Tip: Think of 'Kazari' as fancy items used to make a room 'Zari' (radiant) and decorated.
Example: クリスマスの飾りを片付ける。 (くりすますのかざりをかたづける。)
-To put away the Christmas decorations.
}

姫-
{
姫 (ひめ) - Princess
A noun used for daughters of noble families or in traditional folklore.
Memory Tip: The radical for woman (女) is paired with a character for a high-ranking subject (臣).
Example: 姫は美しいドレスを着ている。 (ひめはうつくしいどれすをきている。)
-The princess is wearing a beautiful dress.
}

張る-
{
張る (はる) - To stretch / To tighten / To put up
This verb covers physical tension, such as stretching a string or sticking a poster onto a flat surface.
Memory Tip: Imagine playing a 'Harp' (Haru); you must stretch the strings tight to make music.
Example: テントを張る。 (てんとをはる。)
-To pitch (stretch out) a tent.
}

震える-
{
震える (ふるえる) - To shiver / To shake / To tremble
Describes involuntary shaking due to cold, fear, anger, or even excitement.
Memory Tip: 'Furu' sounds like 'Brrr'—the sound people make when they are shivering from the cold.
Example: 寒さで手が震える。 (さむさでてがふるえる。)
-My hands are shaking from the cold.
}

未だ-
{
未だ (まだ) - Still; yet
Indicates that a state continues or an action has not occurred yet. Usually written in kana.
Memory Tip: The kanji 'mi' (not yet) represents a tree with a shorter top branch, not yet fully grown.
Example: 彼は未だ寝ています。 (かれはまだねています。)
-He is still sleeping.
}

天の川-
{
天の川 (あまのがわ) - The Milky Way
Literally translated as 'River of Heaven,' central to the Japanese Tanabata festival lore.
Memory Tip: Heaven (天) + Possessive (の) + River (川). It is the river in the sky.
Example: 天の川が綺麗だ。 (あまのがわがきれいだ。)
-The Milky Way is beautiful.
}

群れ-
{
群れ (むれ) - Herd, flock, crowd
A noun used for groups of animals or people. It emphasizes a mass or collection of individuals acting as one.
Memory Tip: 'Mure' sounds like 'More'—when you have more and more animals, you get a herd.
Example: 羊の群れが見える。(ひつじのむれがみえる。)
-I can see a flock of sheep.
}

避ける-
{
避ける (さける) - To avoid
This verb refers to avoiding situations, people, or physical obstacles. It can also be read as 'yokeru' for physical evasion.
Memory Tip: Use the 'Road' (辶) radical to remember avoiding obstacles in your path.
Example: 渋滞を避けるために裏道を行く。 (じゅうたいをさけるためにうらみちをいく。)
-Go through the back streets to avoid traffic congestion.
}

落ち着く-
{
落ち着く (おちつく) - To calm down, settle
A compound verb combining 落ち (to fall) and 着く (to arrive/attach).
Memory Tip: Imagine your high energy falling and finally arriving at a stable spot to settle down.
Example: 深呼吸をして落ち着いて。 (しんこきゅうをしておちついて。)
-Take a deep breath and calm down.
}

判断-
{
判断 (はんだん) - Judgment, decision
This noun combines the kanji for 'judge' (判) and 'cut/sever' (断) to mean a final decision.
Memory Tip: You need to 'hand down' (handan) a final judgment.
Example: 彼の判断は正しい。(かれのはんだんはただしい。)
-His judgment is correct.
}

判断する-
{
判断する (はんだんする) - To judge, to decide
The verb form of 'judgment', created by adding the helper verb 'suru' to the noun.
Memory Tip: Just take the noun 'handan' and 'do' (suru) the action of judging.
Example: 状況を判断する。(じょうきょうをはんだんする。)
-To judge the situation.
}

勿論-
{
勿論 (もちろん) - Of course / Certainly
An adverb used to express that something is natural or goes without saying. It is often written in kana.
Memory Tip: The first kanji (勿) means "not," and the second (論) means "argument"; there is no argument needed, it's obvious.
Example: 勿論、私も行きます。 (もちろん、わたしもいきます。)
-Of course, I am going too.
}

撮影禁止-
{
撮影禁止 (さつえいきんし) - Photography prohibited
A compound noun often found on signs in museums, theaters, or private properties to forbid taking pictures or filming.
Memory Tip: 撮影 (filming/photography) + 禁止 (prohibition). Literally: 'filming forbidden.'
Example: このエリアは撮影禁止です。 (このえりあはさつえいきんしです。)
-Photography is prohibited in this area.
}

承知-
{
承知 (しょうち) - Consent / Knowledge
Often used in formal business settings to indicate that a request has been understood and accepted.
Memory Tip: Combine 'accept' (承) with 'know' (知) to mean you accept the information into your knowledge.
Example: その件は承知しました。(そのけんはしょうちしました)
-I have understood and accepted that matter.
}

性-
{
性 (せい) - nature, gender, character
Often used as a suffix to indicate a specific property or a quality of something.
Memory Tip: Radical for heart (忄) plus life (生). Your nature is the life within your heart.
Example: 性格は変えられる。(せいかくはかえられる。)
-Your personality can be changed.
}

墓-
{
墓 (はか) - grave, tomb
Refers to the physical burial site or headstone.
Memory Tip: Grass (艹) over the sun (日) and the ground (土). Buried deep in the dirt.
Example: 祖父の墓参りに行く。(そふのはかまいりにいく。)
-I'm going to visit my grandfather's grave.
}

炎-
{
炎 (ほのお) - Flame
A noun describing a large flame or blaze, often used figuratively to describe burning passion or desire.
Memory Tip: It consists of two 'fire' (火) kanji stacked on top of each other, creating a bigger flame.
Example: 炎が空高く上がった。 (ほのおがそらたかくあがった。)
-The flames rose high into the sky.
}

意外-
{
意外 (いがい) - Unexpected/Surprising
A na-adjective used when something happens outside of one's initial expectations or thoughts.
Memory Tip: 'Thought/Intent' (意) plus 'Outside' (外). Literally 'outside of what you thought'.
Example: 意外に難しかった。 (いがいにむずかしかった。)
-It was unexpectedly difficult.
}

際-
{
際 (きわ) - Edge, brink, side
Refers to the physical boundary of an object or the critical moment just before an event.
Memory Tip: The left radical is a wall/hill; imagine standing on the wall's 'kiwa' (edge) looking at a festival (祭).
Example: 窓の際に立たないで。 (まどのきわにたたないで。)
-Don't stand by the edge of the window.
}

一体-
{
一体 (いったい) - (What) on earth/The heck
Used as an adverb to add emphasis to a question, expressing surprise, confusion, or impatience.
Memory Tip: Asking how all the pieces fit into 'one body' (一体) of a mysterious situation.
Example: 一体何が起きたのですか？ (いったいなにがおきたのですか？)
-What on earth happened?
}

立場-
{
立場 (たちば) - Standpoint / Position
Refers to one's social status or mental point of view in a specific situation.
Memory Tip: A combination of 'to stand' (立) and 'place' (場) – the place where you stand is your perspective.
Example: 相手の立場になる (あいてのたちばになる)
-Put yourself in the other person's position
}

錦市場-
{
錦市場 (にしきいちば) - Nishiki Market
A famous historical food market in Kyoto, often called 'Kyoto's Kitchen.'
Memory Tip: Nishiki means 'brocade' (beautiful fabric), hinting at the rich and colorful variety of food.
Example: 錦市場で買い物をする。 (にしきいちばでかいものをする。)
-Shopping at Nishiki Market.
}

奪う-
{
奪う (うばう) - To snatch / To take by force
A transitive verb indicating that something valuable has been taken or stolen.
Memory Tip: Radical for big (大) + bird (隹) + hand (寸) – a big hand reaching out to snatch a bird away.
Example: 自由を奪う (じゆうをうばう)
-To take away freedom
}

訪れる-
{
訪れる (おとずれる) - To visit; to arrive
Used for visiting a place or the arrival of abstract concepts like seasons or luck.
Memory Tip: To visit is to bring the sound (oto) of your voice to a new place.
Example: ついに春が訪れた。 (ついはるがおとずれた。)
-Spring has finally arrived.

一応-
{
一応 (いちおう) - for the time being, tentatively
An adverb used when something is done 'just in case' or to a basic degree of satisfaction.
Memory Tip: Ichi (one) + Ou (response) - giving at least 'one response' for now.
Example: 一応確認します。 (いちおうかくにんします。)
-I will check just in case.

散る-
{
散る (ちる) - To scatter / To fall
An intransitive verb specifically used for petals, leaves, or people dispersing in many directions.
Memory Tip: The right side of the kanji looks like something being struck and breaking into pieces.
Example: 桜の花が散る (さくらのはながちる)
-Cherry blossoms scatter.

地上-
{
地上 (ちじょう) - above ground, surface
A noun referring to the surface of the earth or the area above the soil level.
Memory Tip: Earth (地) + Above (上) = Above the ground.
Example: 地上の星。 (ちじょうのほし。)
-Stars on the ground.
}

脇-
{
脇 (わき) - Side/Armpit
A noun referring to the side of the human torso or the side of an object/road.
Memory Tip: The left part is 'flesh' (月), and the right represents the ribs or power on the side of the body.
Example: 彼は脇に荷物を抱えている。 (かれはわきににもつをかかえている。)

覆う-
{
覆う (おおう) - To cover/hide
A godan verb used for physically covering a surface or metaphorically concealing something.

Example: 雪が地面を覆っている。 (ゆきがじめんをおおっている。)
-Snow is covering the ground.

納得-
{
納得 (なっとく) - Consent/Understanding/Agreement
A noun or suru-verb meaning to be personally convinced or to accept an explanation as valid.
Memory Tip: 納 (settle/supply) + 得 (gain). You 'gain' a 'settled' feeling in your mind after understanding.
Example: 彼の説明に納得した。 (かれのせつめいになっとくした。)
-I was convinced by his explanation.

竜-
{
竜 (りゅう) - Dragon
A noun referring to the mythical creature, often associated with water and power in East Asia.
Memory Tip: This simplified kanji looks like a standing creature with a crown and a long tail.
Example: 伝説の竜が現れた。 (でんせつのりゅうがあらわれた。)
-A legendary dragon appeared.
}

における-
{
における (における) - In; at; as for
A formal particle-like expression used to specify a location, time, or field of activity, equivalent to 'ni oite'.
Memory Tip: Think of it as 'ni' (in) + 'oku' (to place), indicating where something is 'placed' or situated.
Example: 数学における天才 (すうがくにおけるてんさい)
-A genius in mathematics
}

自殺-
{
自殺 (じさつ) - Suicide
A compound noun referring to the act of intentionally taking one's own life.
Memory Tip: The act of KILLING (殺) one's own SELF (自).
Example: 自殺を防止する (じさつをぼうしする)
-To prevent suicide
}

構える-
{
構える (かまえる) - To set up / to take a stance
Used for physical stances in martial arts or for setting up a business or household.
Memory Tip: Think of a "Camera" (Kamae) being "set up" on a tripod to take a shot.
Example: 銃を構える。 (じゅうを かまえる。)
-To ready/aim a gun.
}

退く-
{
退く (しりぞく) - To retreat / step back
To withdraw from a position, a competition, or a professional role.
Memory Tip: "Shiri" means back/butt; think of moving your "shiri" away from the front line.
Example: 第一線を退く。 (だいいっせんを しりぞく。)
-To retire from the front line.
}

偶然-
{
偶然 (ぐうぜん) - Coincidence/By chance
An adverbial noun referring to unexpected events. 偶 (even/pair) and 然 (state) imply things happening in a pair by nature.
Memory Tip: Think of finding an 'even' pair 'naturally' without looking for it; that is a coincidence.
Example: 偶然、彼に会った。 (ぐうぜん、かれにあった。)
-I met him by chance.
}

外れる-
{
外れる (はずれる) - To be disconnected / To miss
An intransitive verb used when something comes off its place or a prediction/aim is incorrect.
Memory Tip: When something goes to the 'outside' (外) of its target or slot, it has missed or come off.
Example: ボタンが外れました。 (ぼたんがはずれました。)
-The button came off.
}

早速-
{
早速 (さっそく) - Immediately / at once
This is an adverb used to describe doing something without any delay. It is often used when starting an action promptly.
Memory Tip: Early (早) and fast (速) combine to mean doing something right away.
Example: 早速始めましょう。 (さっそくはじめましょう。)
-Let's start right away.
}

大した-
{
大した (たいした) - Great / significant / (with negative) not a big deal
An attributive word that precedes a noun. In negative sentences, it means something is trivial or unimportant.
Memory Tip: Think of something "Big" (大) that was "done" (した), making it significant.
Example: 大した問題ではない。 (たいしたもんだいではない。)
-It is not a big problem.
}

現場-
{
現場 (げんば) - On-site / the scene (of an event)
A noun referring to the actual location where an event takes place, such as a construction site or crime scene.
Memory Tip: The actual (現) place (場) is the scene where things happen.
Example: 現場に急行する。 (げんばにきゅうこうする。)
-To rush to the scene.
}

巻く-
{
巻く (まく) - To wind/roll
A transitive godan verb used for rolling items like rugs, scarves, or bandages.
Memory Tip: Picture rolling up a scroll or a wrap with your hands.
Example: マフラーを首に巻きました。 (まふらーをくびにまきました。)
-I wrapped a scarf around my neck.
}

不幸-
{
不幸 (ふこう) - Unhappiness/Misfortune
A noun or na-adjective formed by adding the negative prefix "fu" to "happiness."
Memory Tip: Simply the opposite of happy; "not" (不) "happy" (幸).
Example: 彼は不幸な事故に遭いました。 (かれはふこうなじこにあいました。)
-He met with an unfortunate accident.
}

表現-
{
表現 (ひょうげん) - expression, presentation
'Hyou' (surface/show) + 'gen' (appear/actual). It refers to manifesting internal thoughts or feelings into an external form.
Memory Tip: To show (hyou) what has appeared (gen) in your mind.
Example: 感情を表現するのは難しい。 (かんじょうをひょうげんするのはむずかしい。)
-Expressing emotions is difficult.
}

正確-
{
正確 (せいかく) - accurate, precise, correct
'Sei' (correct) + 'kaku' (certain/firm). This na-adjective is used when something matches the truth or standard perfectly.
Memory Tip: When something is correct (sei) and certain (kaku), it is precise.
Example: 正確な時間を教えてください。 (せいかくなじかんをおしえてください。)
-Please tell me the exact time.

本気-
{
本気 (ほんき) - seriousness, earnestness
'Hon' (real/origin) + 'ki' (spirit/energy). It describes a state of being completely serious or putting one's true spirit into an action.
Memory Tip: Use your real (hon) spirit (ki) when you are serious about a goal.
Example: 彼は本気で怒っている。 (かれはほんきでおこっている。)
-He is seriously angry.

戦闘-
{
戦闘 (せんとう) - Battle, combat
A noun used for tactical engagements or fights, frequently seen in historical texts or video games.
Memory Tip: Both 戦 (war) and 闘 (struggle) represent conflict, doubling the intensity of the fight.
Example: 戦闘が始まった。 (せんとうがはじまった。)
-The battle started.
}

支える-
{
支える (ささえる) - To support
An ichidan verb meaning to prop up physically or to provide emotional or financial support.

-My family supported me.

勢い-
{
勢い (いきおい) - Momentum/Force/Vigor
Describes the physical force of movement or the general trend/energy of a situation.

Example: 水がすごい勢いで流れている。(みずがすごいいきおいでながれている。)
-The water is flowing with great force.

殺人-
{
殺人 (さつじん) - Murder/Homicide
A direct compound of "kill" (殺) and "person" (人).

怒鳴る-
{
怒鳴る (どなる) - To shout/To yell
To yell or bark at someone in anger. Includes the "mouth" (口) radical on the right.

-I heard the teacher's shouting voice.

狂う-
{
狂う (くるう) - To go crazy/To go haywire
Can describe a person losing their mind or a machine/plan failing to function correctly.

Example: 予定が狂ってしまった。(よていがくるってしまった。)
-My plans went haywire.

〜ってわけ-
{
〜ってわけ (〜ってわけ) - It means that...; so that's why...
A colloquial contraction of "〜というわけ", used to explain a reason or conclusion.
Memory Tip: "Wake" (わけ) means reason; "tte" links the conclusion to the context.
Example: 忙しいってわけね。(いそがしいってわけね。)
-So it means you're busy, huh?

〜わけで-
{
〜わけで (〜わけで) - For that reason; such being the case
Uses "wake" (reason) plus the particle "de" to indicate circumstances or logical follow-through.
Memory Tip: Think of it as "with that reason being..."
Example: そういうわけで、遅れました。(そういうわけで、おくれました。)
-For that reason, I was late.
}

婦人-
{
婦人 (ふじん) - Lady/Woman
A formal term for an adult woman, combining 'wife/lady' (婦) and 'person' (人).
Memory Tip: A lady (婦) is a person (人) who traditionally managed the household.
Example: 婦人服売り場は三階です。 (ふじんふくうりばはさんがいです。)
-The ladies' clothing department is on the third floor.
}

棒-
{
棒 (ぼう) - Pole, rod, stick
A noun for long, cylindrical objects typically made of wood or metal.
Memory Tip: The wood radical (木) indicates its material, while the right side suggests a "tribute" (奉) held up on a staff.
Example: 彼は棒で地面に円を描いた (かれはぼうでじめんにえんをかいた)
-He drew a circle on the ground with a stick.
}

に過ぎない-
{
に過ぎない (にすぎない) - Nothing more than, merely
A grammar expression meaning a situation does not exceed (sugiru) a certain limit.
Memory Tip: Literally "does not pass/exceed" (sugi-nai), so it stays at a low or simple level.
Example: それは単なる噂に過ぎない (それはたんなるうわさにすぎない)
-That is nothing more than a mere rumor.
}

絡む-
{
絡む (からむ) - To entangle, involve, pick a fight
Can describe physical tangling of strings or social involvement/entanglement with others.

Example: 糸が絡む。 (いとがからむ。)
-The threads are entangled.

異常-
{
異常 (いじょう) - abnormality, strangeness
A noun/na-adjective combining 'different/strange' (異) and 'normal/always' (常).
Memory Tip: When something is different (異) from what is always (常) there, it is an abnormality.
Example: 機械に異常が発生した。(きかいにいじょうがはっせいした。)
-An abnormality occurred in the machine.

責任-
{
責任 (せきにん) - responsibility, duty
Composed of 'blame/liability' (責) and 'duty/entrust' (任).
Memory Tip: You are entrusted (任) with a task, but you get blamed (責) if you don't take responsibility.
Example: 彼は責任感が強い。(かれはせきにんかんがつよい。)
-He has a strong sense of responsibility.
}

殴る-
{
殴る (なぐる) - to strike, to hit
A Godan verb specifically used for hitting someone or something with a fist or blunt force.
Memory Tip: The left side suggests a weapon being swung with power to strike someone.
Example: 彼は壁を殴った。(かれはかべをなぐった。)
-He punched the wall.

務める-
{
務める (つとめる) - to serve, to fill a role
Used when performing a specific duty, task, or social role (like a chairperson).
Memory Tip: Using your power (力) to perform a task (务) as your official service.
Example: 司会を務める。(しかいをつとめる。)
-To serve as the master of ceremonies.
}

要求-
{
要求 (ようきゅう) - Demand / Requirement
A noun describing a firm request for something necessary or desired.
Memory Tip: Combining the kanji for essential (要) and seeking (求) creates a demand.
Example: 要求を受け入れる。 (ようきゅうをうけいれる。)
-To accept a demand.
}

要求する-
{
要求する (ようきゅうする) - To demand
The suru-verb form of the noun 'yokyu,' indicating the active process of making a demand.
Memory Tip: Combine 'essential' (要) and 'request' (求) with the action verb 'to do' (する).
Example: 彼は謝罪を要求した。 (かれはしゃざいをようきゅうした。)
-He demanded an apology.
}

寄せる-
{
寄せる (よせる) - To bring near / To push aside
A transitive verb used for moving something closer to a location or gathering things to one side.
Memory Tip: 'Yo' (you) 'seru' (sell) things by bringing them closer to customers.
Example: 車を路肩に寄せる。 (くるまをろかたによせる。)
-Pull the car over to the side of the road.
}

穏やか-
{
穏やか (おだやか) - Calm / Peaceful
A na-adjective used to describe a tranquil state of mind, weather, or a quiet atmosphere.
Memory Tip: Think of a calm day where you order (oda) yak (yaka) tea.
Example: 穏やかな海ですね。 (おだやかなうみですね。)
-It's a calm sea, isn't it?
}

崩れる-
{
崩れる (くずれる) - To collapse / To crumble
An intransitive Ichidan verb describing a structure or even a plan falling apart.
Memory Tip: When a mountain (山) loses its support, its two halves (朋) fall and crumble.
Example: 天気が崩れる。 (てんきがくずれる。)
-The weather is breaking down (turning bad).
}

余裕-
{
余裕 (よゆう) - Room, leeway, margin
This noun refers to physical, temporal, or mental space. It often describes a state of being relaxed because one has extra capacity.
Memory Tip: Combine 'surplus' (余) and 'abundant' (裕); when resources are surplus and abundant, you have leeway.
Example: 時間に余裕がある。 (じかんによゆうがある。)
-I have some extra time.
}

余計-
{
余計 (よけい) - Excessive, unnecessary, spare
As a Na-adjective or adverb, it describes something that is more than needed or uncalled for. It often carries a negative nuance of being 'too much'.
Memory Tip: 'Surplus' (余) + 'plan/measure' (計). A plan with surplus measures is often unnecessary or uncalled for.
Example: 余計な心配はしないで。 (よけいなしんぱいはしないで。)
-Don't worry unnecessarily.
}

手前-
{
手前 (てまえ) - This side, in front of
It can refer to a physical location closer to the speaker or a social 'face/reputation' (keeping appearances).
Memory Tip: 'Hand' (手) + 'front' (前). Something located right in front of your hand.
Example: 駅の手前で車を止める。 (えきのてまえでくるまをとめる。)
-Stop the car just before the station.
}

大いに-
{
大いに (おおいに) - Greatly/Very much
An adverb used to emphasize the scale or degree of an action or state. It is the adverbial form of the archaic adjective 'ooi.'
Memory Tip: Take the kanji for big (大) and add 'ini' to turn a big thing into a 'great' action.
Example: 大いに楽しんでください。 (おおいにたのしんでください。)
-Please enjoy yourself greatly.
}

姿勢-
{
姿勢 (しせい) - Posture/Attitude
A noun used for physical posture or a mental attitude toward a situation. It combines 'figure' and 'force.'
Memory Tip: The shape (姿) of your physical energy (勢) determines your posture.
Example: 彼は姿勢が良い。 (かれはしせいがよい。)
-He has good posture.
}

否定-
{
否定 (ひてい) - Denial/Negation
A noun used to indicate that something is not true or to refuse a request.
Memory Tip: To 'fix' (定) a 'no' (否) into a formal stance of negation.
Example: 彼の否定は非常に強かった。(かれのひていはひじょうにつよかった)
-His denial was very strong.
}

否定する-
{
否定する (ひていする) - To deny/negate
The suru-verb form of 否定, meaning to contradict or declare a statement false.
Memory Tip: Take the noun for 'denial' and add 'suru' (to do) to turn the concept into an action.
Example: 彼はその事実を否定した。(かれはそのじじつをひていした)
-He denied that fact.
}

患者-
{
患者 (かんじゃ) - Patient
A noun used in a medical context for a person receiving care.
Memory Tip: A person (者) who is suffering from a sickness (患) that affects their heart (心).
Example: 医師は患者を診察した。(いしはかんじゃをしんさつした)
-The doctor examined the patient.
}

幸い-
{
幸い (さいわい) - Happiness, good fortune, luckily
An adjectival noun used to express gratitude or a fortunate situation, often in formal letters.
Memory Tip: The top part looks like a cross and the bottom like shackles; finding happiness despite being bound.
Example: ご連絡いただければ幸いです。(ごれんらくいただければさいわいです。)
-I would appreciate it if you could contact me.
}

組織-
{
組織 (そしき) - Organization, structure, tissue
Refers to social entities, biological structures, or the systematic arrangement of components.
Memory Tip: Both kanji feature silk (糸); organizing threads into a weave or a structured group.
Example: 彼は新しい組織を作った。(かれはあたらしいそしきをつくった。)
-He created a new organization.
}

唯一-
{
唯一 (ゆいいつ) - Only, sole, unique
A noun or no-adjective used to emphasize that there is absolutely only one of something.
Memory Tip: Combining 'solely' (唯) with 'one' (一) literally translates to the only one.
Example: これが私の唯一の希望だ。(これがわたしのゆいいつのきぼうだ。)
-This is my only hope.
}

訴える-
{
訴える (うったえる) - to sue, to complain of, to appeal to
This verb is used for legal actions, reporting physical pain, or making an emotional appeal. It implies bringing a grievance to someone's attention.
Memory Tip: The radical for words (言) suggests you are "speaking" your case to a judge or doctor.
Example: 彼は会社を訴えた。 (かれはかいしゃをうったえた。)
-He sued the company.
}

破壊-
{
破壊 (はかい) - Destruction
A noun or Suru-verb used for physical demolition. Both kanji carry meanings of breaking or damaging.
Memory Tip: A 'rock' (石) hits a 'skin' (皮) to break it (破), leading to total destruction (壊).
Example: 建物が地震で破壊されました。 (たてものがじしんではかいされました。)
-The building was destroyed by the earthquake.
}

眉-
{
眉 (まゆ) - Eyebrow
A noun referring to the hair growing on the ridge above the eye sockets.
Memory Tip: The kanji contains 'eye' (目) at the bottom with a hairy cover on top.
Example: 彼は眉をひそめた。 (かれはまゆをひそめた。)
-He knitted his eyebrows.
}

詩-
{
詩 (し) - Poem, poetry
A noun referring to literary verse or individual poems.
Memory Tip: Words (言) spoken at a Temple (寺). Ancient temple chants were often beautiful poetry.
Example: 彼女は詩を書くのが好きだ。 (かのじょはしをかくのがすきだ。)
-She likes writing poems.
}

真剣-
{
真剣 (しんけん) - Serious, earnest
A Na-adjective derived from the word for a 'real sword', indicating high stakes and focus.
Memory Tip: A True (真) Sword (剣). Fighting with a real blade requires being deadly serious.
Example: 彼は真剣に私の話を聞いた。 (かれはしんけんにわたしのはなしをきいた。)
-He listened to my story seriously.
}

頼る-
{
頼る (たよる) - To rely on / To depend on
An intransitive verb indicating reliance on someone's strength, help, or financial support.
Memory Tip: Think of 'requesting' (頼) help from someone's 'head' (頁).
Example: 彼は親に頼っている。 (かれはおやにたよっている。)
-He relies on his parents.
}

決心-
{
決心 (けっしん) - Determination / Resolution
A Sino-Japanese noun or suru-verb meaning to firmly make up one's mind.
Memory Tip: 'Deciding' (決) something deep within your 'heart' (心).
Example: 留学を決心しました。 (りゅうがくをけっしんしました。)
-I have decided to study abroad.
}

美人-
{
美人 (びじん) - A beautiful person
A noun composed of 美 (beauty) and 人 (person), typically used to refer to a beautiful woman.
Memory Tip: Simply 'beauty' plus 'person' equals a beautiful person.
Example: 彼女は有名な美人だ。 (かのじょはゆうめいなびじんだ。)
-She is a famous beauty.
}

爆発-
{
爆発 (ばくはつ) - Explosion
A noun/suru-verb combining 爆 (bomb/explode) and 発 (discharge/emit).
Memory Tip: A bomb (爆) emitting (発) fire and energy results in an explosion.
Example: 火山が爆発した。 (かざんがばくはつした。)
-The volcano exploded.
}

感心-
{
感心 (かんしん) - Admiration / Impression
A noun or na-adjective used when you are impressed by someone's noble behavior, skill, or attitude.
Memory Tip: When a feeling (感) hits your heart (心) directly, you are filled with admiration.
Example: 彼の努力に感心した。 (かれのどりょくにかんしんした。)
-I was impressed by his effort.
