形容動詞-
{
形容動詞 (けいようどうし) - Adjectival verb (na-adjective)
A part of speech in Japanese that functions like an adjective but conjugates similarly to a verb/copula. It literally translates to "describing-verb."
Memory Tip: Think of it as a hybrid: 形容 (describing) + 動詞 (verb); it describes things but needs "da" or "na" to function.
Example: 「静かだ」は形容動詞です。 (「しずかだ」はけいようどうしです。)
- "Shizuka da" is an adjectival verb.
}

活用形-
{
活用形 (かつようけい) - Conjugated form
A linguistic term describing the various forms a declinable word (verb/adjective) takes.
Memory Tip: 活用 means "practical use" and 形 means "shape/form." It is the "shape" a word takes to be "used" in a sentence.
Example: 動詞の活用形を一覧表にする。 (どうしかつようけいをいちらんひょうにする。)
-Make a table of verb conjugated forms.
}

燃え付く-
{
燃え付く (もえつく) - To catch fire / to ignite
A compound verb combining 燃える (to burn) and 付く (to attach). It refers to the moment fire starts or takes hold of something.
Memory Tip: Moe (burning) + Tsuku (sticks). The fire finally "sticks" to the wood and starts burning.
Example: 枯れ葉がすぐに燃え付いた。(かれはがすぐにもえついた。)
-The dry leaves caught fire immediately.
}

誓い-
{
誓い (ちかい) - Oath, vow, pledge
The nominalized form of the verb 誓う, often used in serious contexts like marriage vows, legal oaths, or personal pledges.
Memory Tip: To make a vow, you must speak (言) words that 'break' (折) your old self or past ways.
Example: 永遠の愛を誓い合った。 (えいえんのあいをちかいあった)
-They pledged eternal love to each other.
}

薦め-
{
薦め (すすめ) - Recommendation, advice, encouragement
The noun form of the verb 薦める, used when endorsing a course of action or suggesting something to another person.
Memory Tip: Beneath the grass (艹) canopy, I suggest or 'recommend' a hidden path to you.
Example: 先生の薦めで留学を決めた。 (せんせいのすすめでりゅうがくをきめた)
-I decided to study abroad on my teacher's recommendation.
}

励ます-
{
励ます (はげます) - To encourage, to cheer up
A transitive verb used when one gives support, hope, or verbal encouragement to someone who is struggling.
Memory Tip: Visualize giving someone 'ten thousand' (万) units of 'power/effort' (力) to help them overcome a cliff (厂).
Example: 友人が落ち込んでいる私を励ましてくれた。 (ゆうじんがおちこんでいるわたしをはげましてくれた)
-My friend cheered me up when I was feeling down.
}

除いて-
{
除いて (のぞいて) - except for, excluding
The te-form of the verb 除く (nozoku - to remove/exclude). It functions like a preposition in English to set something apart.
Memory Tip: Think of 'nozoku' as 'no-zoku'—as in, they are no longer part of the 'zoku' (group/tribe).
Example: 日曜日を除いて毎日働く。 (にちようびをのぞいてまいにちはたらく。)
-I work every day except Sunday.
}

紛れもない-
{
紛れもない (まぎれもない) - Unmistakable / Indisputable / Certain
This phrase combines 'magire' (confusion/entanglement) and 'nai' (none), literally meaning there is no room for confusion or being mistaken for something else.
Memory Tip: Think of 'No (ない) Mix-up (紛れ)'. If there is no possible mix-up, the truth is unmistakable.
Example: それは紛れもない事実だ。 (それはまぎれもないじじつだ。)
-That is an unmistakable fact.
}

尾-
{
尾 (お) - Tail, End
Refers to the tail of an animal or the rear end of an object. In modern Japanese, 'shippo' is more common for physical tails, while 'o' or the suffix '-bi' is used in formal, literary, or compound contexts.
Memory Tip: The top radical (尸) represents a body, and the bottom part (毛) means hair or fur. Think of the 'furry part' attached to the end of a 'body.'
Example: その犬は忙しく尾を振っている。 (そのいぬはいそがしくおをふっている。)
-That dog is wagging its tail busily.
}

擦る-
{
擦る (こする) - To rub/scrub
A transitive verb indicating the action of applying friction to a surface.
Memory Tip: The left side is the hand radical (扌), suggesting an action done with your hands like rubbing.
Example: 目を擦る (めをこする)
-Rub one's eyes
}

〜漬け-
{
〜漬け (〜づけ) - Pickled / Immersed in
A suffix derived from the verb 'tsukeru' (to soak), used for food or metaphors of being constantly involved in something.
Memory Tip: The kanji 漬 contains the water radical (氵) because you need liquid to soak or pickle things.
Example: 彼は仕事漬けの毎日だ。 (かれはしごとづけのまいにちだ。)
-He is immersed in work every single day.
}

沿岸-
{
沿岸 (えんがん) - Coast, shore
Combines 沿 (along) and 岸 (bank/shore), referring to the land specifically along the water's edge.
Memory Tip: Walking 'along' (沿) the 'bank' (岸) where the ocean meets the land.
Example: 沿岸をドライブするのが好きだ。(えんがんをどらいぶするのがすきだ。)
-I like driving along the coast.
}

増す-
{
増す (ます) - To increase / to grow
Refers to an increase in volume, degree, amount, or intensity.
Memory Tip: Water (氵) plus Earth (土) plus Sun (日). Plants increase in size when they have all three.
Example: 不安が増している。 (ふあんがましている。)
-The anxiety is increasing.
}

飢え-
{
飢え (うえ) - Hunger, starvation, famine
The noun form of the verb 'ueru'. It can refer to physical hunger or a metaphorical craving/starvation.
Memory Tip: The left side is the 'food' radical (食). When it's paired with 'desk/table' (几), the table is empty, leading to hunger.
Example: 飢えに苦しむ。 (うえにくるしむ。)
-To suffer from hunger.
}

始める-
{
始める (はじめる) - 
A transitive Ichidan verb meaning to start or begin an action.
Memory Tip: Features the 'woman' and 'mouth' radicals; think of a woman speaking her first word to start a conversation.
Example: 明日から日本語を勉強し始める。 (あしたからにほんごをべんきょうしはじめる。)
-I will start studying Japanese tomorrow.
}

欠け-
{
欠け (かけ) - Chip / Gap / Fragment
The noun form of the verb kakeru (to chip/lack), used to describe a missing piece.
Memory Tip: A visual 'gap' or 'lack' (欠) in an object.
Example: 茶碗に欠けがある。 (ちゃわんにかけがある。)
-There is a chip in the tea bowl.
}

相手-
{
相手 (あいて) - Partner; opponent; the other party
Formed from 相 (mutual) and 手 (hand). It refers to the person with whom you are interacting, whether as a collaborator or an adversary.
Memory Tip: A 'mutual hand' represents the person you are shaking hands or competing with.
Example: 相手の目を見る。 (あいてのめをみる。)
-To look into the other person's eyes.
}

〜間-
{
〜間 (かん) - Interval; period of time
A suffix used to denote a specific duration of time (e.g., hours, days, years).
Memory Tip: Visualize the sun (日) shining through the gap in a gate (門), marking the passage of time.
Example: 二時間待った。 (にじかんまった。)
-I waited for two hours.
}

嘘吐き-
{
嘘吐き (うそつき) - Liar
A noun derived from 嘘 (uso - lie) and 吐く (haku - to spit/breathe out).
Memory Tip: A person who 'spits out' (tsuki/haki) 'lies' (uso) is a liar.
Example: 彼は嘘吐きだ。(かれはうそつきだ。)
-He is a liar.
}

跡-
{
跡 (あと) - Mark / trace / tracks
This noun refers to the remains or footprints left behind. The kanji is composed of the 'foot' radical (足) and 'also' (亦).
Memory Tip: Your "foot" (足) leaves a "trace" (跡) on the ground as you walk.
Example: 足跡が見つかりました。 (あしあとがみつかりました。)
-Footprints were found.
}

事-
{
事 (こと) - Thing, matter
A noun used for intangible things, events, or abstract concepts, distinguishing it from physical objects (物).
Memory Tip: The kanji looks like a tall flagpole representing an important event or matter to attend to.
Example: 大事な事があります。(だいじなことがあります。)
-There is an important matter.
}

呼ぶ-
{
呼ぶ (よぶ) - To call, to invite
A transitive u-verb used for calling someone's name, summoning a taxi, or inviting guests.
Memory Tip: You use your mouth (口 radical) to yell "Yo, Boo!" to call your friend.
Example: タクシーを呼ぶ。(たくしーをよぶ。)
-To call a taxi.
}

値-
{
値 (あたい) - value, price, numerical value
A single kanji representing worth or a mathematical result.
Memory Tip: A person (亻) standing next to a direct (直) line to measure their direct worth.
Example: この変数の値は何ですか？(このへんすうのあたいはなんですか？)
-What is the value of this variable?
}

人-
{
人 (ひと) - Person
A basic noun and radical representing a human being; its shape is a simplified pictograph of a person standing.
Memory Tip: Visualize a side profile of a person with two legs braced and walking forward.
Example: 公園にたくさんの人が集まっています。 (こうえんにたくさんのひとがあつまっています。)
-Many people are gathering in the park.
}

お茶-
{
お茶 (おちゃ) - Tea
This word combines the honorific prefix 'o' with the kanji for tea 'cha', commonly referring to green tea in Japan.
Memory Tip: The kanji for tea (茶) depicts grass (艹) on top of a person (人) over a tree (木), like someone harvesting leaves.
Example: お茶を一杯いかがですか。 (おちゃをいっぱいいかがですか。)
-Would you like a cup of tea?
}

蜂-
{
蜂 (はち) - Bee, wasp
A noun representing any stinging insect from the Apoidea or Vespoidea families.
Memory Tip: The 'insect' (虫) radical on the left with a 'peak' (夆) suggesting a sharp stinger point.
Example: 庭で蜂の巣を見つけた。 (にわではちのすをみつけた。)
-I found a beehive in the garden.
}

に伴って-
{
に伴って (にともなって) - along with; as; accompanying
A grammar structure indicating that one change happens simultaneously or in proportion with another.
Memory Tip: The kanji 伴 means 'companion'; events change together like companions walking together.
Example: 人口の増加に伴って、ごみが増えた。 (じんこうのぞうかにともなって、ごみがふえた。)
-As the population increased, the amount of trash increased along with it.
}

〜のもあって-
{
〜のもあって (〜のもあって) - Partly because / Due in part to
Used to mention one of several reasons for a particular outcome, implying other factors exist.
Memory Tip: No (fact) + Mo (also) + Atte (being), literally "the fact that ... also being a reason."
Example: 雨が降っているのもあって、外出をやめた。(あめがふっているのもあって、がいしゅつをやめた)
-Partly because it was raining, I decided not to go out.
}

第一弾-
{
第一弾 (だいいちだん) - The first installment / The first round
Used to describe the first part of a series, campaign, or project rollout.
Memory Tip: Order prefix (第) + One (一) + Bullet (弾). The very first bullet fired in a sequence.
Example: キャンペーンの第一弾が始まる。 (きゃんぺーんのだいいちだんがはじまる)
-The first round of the campaign is starting.
}

〜氏-
{
〜氏 (〜し) - Mr./Ms. (formal suffix)
A formal honorific used in news, writing, and business to refer to individuals politely but with distance.
Memory Tip: The kanji 氏 depicts a person holding a ceremonial object, marking them as a person of title.
Example: 田中氏がスピーチを行った。(たなかしがすぴーちをおこなった)
-Mr. Tanaka gave a speech.
}

散らし-
{
散らし (ちらし) - Scattering/Leaflet/Flyer
Derived from the verb 散らす (to scatter), it refers to advertising papers or food (like chirashizushi) scattered over a surface.
Memory Tip: Think of 'scattering' (散) information to the public in the form of a flyer.
Example: 新聞に散らしが入っていた。 (しんぶんにちらしがはいっていた。)
-There was a flyer in the newspaper.
}

魔-
{
魔 (ま) - Demon; evil spirit; obstacle
Refers to a malevolent being or an evil influence that tempts or interferes with human paths.
Memory Tip: The kanji features "hemp" (麻) over "ghost/demon" (鬼) — a demon hiding in the brush.
Example: 魔が差した。 (まがさした。)
-I was tempted / I had a momentary lapse in judgment.
}

実り-
{
実り (みのり) - Ripening/Harvest
The noun form of the verb "minoru." It describes the ripening of fruit or the successful results of labor.
Memory Tip: The "fruit" (実) is ready for harvesting (ri).
Example: 今年の秋は豊かな実りがあった (ことしのあきはゆたかなみのりがあった)
-There was a bountiful harvest this autumn.
}

武装-
{
武装 (ぶそう) - Armament/armed
Refers to the act of equipping oneself with weapons or protective gear, either literally or figuratively.
Memory Tip: 武 (warrior) + 装 (attire) = The attire or gear of a warrior.
Example: 兵士が武装する。 (へいしがぶそうする。)
-The soldiers arm themselves.
}

託す-
{
託す (たくす) - To entrust/commit
This transitive verb involves handing over a task, hope, or responsibility to someone else for safekeeping or completion.
Memory Tip: The radical 言 (speech) plus 託 (consign) suggests giving your word to leave something in another's care.
Example: 夢を後輩に託す。 (ゆめをこうはいにたくす。)
-I entrust my dreams to my juniors.
}

祈願-
{
祈願 (きがん) - Prayer, supplication
A formal noun used primarily in religious or serious contexts when asking for a specific outcome.
Memory Tip: Focus on the kanji: pray (祈) for a wish (願) to come true.
Example: 合格を祈願する (ごうかくをきがんする)
-To pray for passing the exam.
}

〜殿-
{
〜殿 (〜どの) - Lord / Mr. (formal honorific)
An archaic or highly formal honorific used for lords, or in modern official documents and certificates.
Memory Tip: Picture a 'Dono' standing in front of his Dojo or castle.
Example: 織田殿からの手紙。 (おだどのからのてがみ。) -[A letter from Lord Oda.]
}

問う-
{
問う (とう) - To ask / To question
A formal Godan verb often used in serious contexts, like legal responsibility or philosophical inquiries.
Memory Tip: A mouth (口) positioned at a gate (門) to ask someone for entry or information.
Example: 責任を問う。 (せきにんをとう。)
-To hold someone responsible (literally: to question responsibility).
}

突く-
{
突く (つく) - To poke / To strike
A godan verb used for physical poking, stabbing, or striking a point of interest.
Memory Tip: Imagine a dog (represented in 突) suddenly rushing out of a hole (穴) to poke its nose at you.
Example: 指でつつく。(ゆびでつく)
-To poke with a finger.
}

妙-
{
妙 (みょう) - Strange, odd, exquisite
A na-adjective that can mean weird or mysterious, but can also imply something exceptionally fine or skillful.
Memory Tip: Radical 女 (woman) + 少 (few/small); a rare and 'exquisite' beauty is something slightly unusual.
Example: 妙な音がしました。 (みょうなおとがしました。)
-There was a strange sound.
}

牧師-
{
牧師 (ぼくし) - Pastor/Clergyman
A noun referring to a Christian minister, combining 'shepherd/pasture' (牧) and 'teacher' (師).
Memory Tip: A master teacher (師) who acts as a shepherd (牧) for the people.
Example: 牧師が話を始めた。 (ぼくしがはなしをはじめた。)
-The pastor began to speak.
}

吉-
{
吉 (きち) - Good luck / Fortune
A noun representing luck, frequently encountered on fortune-telling slips (omikuji) at Japanese shrines.
Memory Tip: A scholar (the top radical) speaking (the mouth radical below) words of wisdom brings good luck.
Example: おみくじを引いたら吉だった。 (おみくじをひいたらきちだった。)
-I drew a fortune and it was good luck.
}

舞う-
{
舞う (まう) - To dance; to flutter
Specifically refers to a spinning or circling motion, often in traditional dance or falling leaves.
Memory Tip: The complex kanji resembles a dancer with long sleeves or many legs moving in circles.
Example: 花びらが風に舞う (はなびらがかぜにまう)
-Flower petals flutter in the wind.
}

旨-
{
旨 (むね) - Gist / Purport
Commonly used in formal or business contexts to summarize the main point or intention of a message.
Memory Tip: The kanji shows a spoon in the mouth; you are tasting the gist or essence of the matter.
Example: 承知した旨を伝える。 (しょうちしたむねをつたえる。)
-Convey the message that I have understood.
}

電気柵-
{
電気柵 (でんきさく) - Electric fence
A compound of "electricity" (電気) and "fence" (柵), often used in farming.
Memory Tip: Electricity + a fence made with wooden posts (tree radical).
Example: 電気柵に触れないでください。 (でんきさくにふれないでください。)
-Please do not touch the electric fence.
}

第一段-
{
第一段 (だいいちだん) - First step; first stage
A compound noun formed by 第 (ordinal marker), 一 (one), and 段 (step/level/column).
Memory Tip: "Dai" (big) "Ichi" (number one) "Dan" (level) — the very first level of a process.
Example: 計画の第一段を実行する。 (けいかくのだいいちだんをじっこうする。)
-Execute the first stage of the plan.
}

鍛治屋-
{
鍛治屋 (かじや) - Blacksmith/Smithy
A noun for either a blacksmith as a person or the workshop where metal is forged and shaped.
Memory Tip: 'Kaji' (metalworking) + 'ya' (shop/person) — the shop or person who does the metalworking.
Example: 鍛治屋で剣を作ってもらった。 (かじやでけんをつくってもらった。)
-I had a sword made at the blacksmith's.
}

王国-
{
王国 (おうこく) - Kingdom
A noun for a country or realm ruled by a king or queen.
Memory Tip: 'Ō' (king) + 'koku' (country) — the king's country. Simple and direct!
Example: その王国は百年間平和だった。 (そのおうこくはひゃくねんかんへいわだった。)
-The kingdom was at peace for a hundred years.
}

城壁-
{
城壁 (じょうへき) - Castle wall/Rampart
A noun for the thick defensive walls surrounding a castle or fortified city.
Memory Tip: 'Jō' (castle) + 'heki' (wall) — the wall of the castle. What stands between you and the enemy.
Example: 城壁の上から敵を見張った。 (じょうへきのうえからてきをみはった。)
-They watched for enemies from atop the castle wall.
}

味方-
{
味方 (みかた) - Ally/One's own side
A noun for a person or group that is on your side, supporting you in conflict or competition.
Memory Tip: 'Mi' (one's own) + 'kata' (person/side) — 'my person', someone who stands with you.
Example: 彼は最後まで味方でいてくれた。 (かれはさいごまでみかたでいてくれた。)
-He remained my ally until the very end.
}

頻りに-
{
頻りに (しきりに) - Frequently, repeatedly
This is an adverb emphasizing the high frequency or constant nature of an action. It often implies that something is happening almost without pause.
Memory Tip: 'Shiki' sounds like 'seek' - if you seek something constantly, you are doing it 'shikirini'.
Example: 彼は頻りに時計を見ている。(かれはしきりにとけいをみている。)
-He is constantly looking at his watch.
}

〜貫-
{
〜貫 (かん) - Counter for pieces of sushi
A specific counter used for individual pieces of nigiri sushi. Historically, it was also a unit of weight or currency.
Memory Tip: Visualize a 'string' (radical within) of sushi pieces being counted like old coins on a thread.
Example: 寿司を五貫注文した。(すしをごかんちゅうもんした)
-I ordered five pieces of sushi.
}

没-
{
没 (ぼつ) - Rejection, death, sinking
Commonly used in publishing for rejected ideas or as a shorthand for the death of a person.
Memory Tip: The water radical (氵) suggests something sinking out of sight or being discarded.
Example: その企画は没になった (そのきかくはぼつになった)
-That plan was rejected.
}

まくる-
{
まくる (まくる) - To roll up / To do intensely
Originally meaning to roll up sleeves, it is often added to the stems of other verbs to mean doing something recklessly or vigorously.
Memory Tip: Roll up your sleeves and 'mark' the competition by doing the task intensely.
Example: 腕をまくる。 (うでをまくる。)
-Roll up one's sleeves.
}

限定販売-
{
限定販売 (げんていはんばい) - Limited edition sale
A term used for products sold in restricted quantities, specific locations, or for a short duration.
Memory Tip: Combine limit (限定) and sale (販売) to remember exclusive "Gentei" items.
Example: これは期間限定販売です。 (これはきかんげんていはんばいです。)
-This is a limited-time sale.
}

病棟-
{
病棟 (びょうとう) - Hospital ward
A compound of 病 (illness) and 棟 (building/wing), used to specify sections of a hospital.
Memory Tip: The part of the building (棟) dedicated to those with an illness (病).
Example: 彼は東病棟に入院している (かれはひがしびょうとうににゅういんしている)
-He is hospitalized in the east ward.
}

富む-
{
富む (とむ) - to be rich in; to be wealthy
Describes an abundance of something, whether it be material wealth, natural resources, or abstract qualities.
Memory Tip: Under the roof radical (宀) is a jar/vessel (畐) overflowing with wealth.
Example: この国は資源に富んでいる。 (このくにはしげんにとんでいる。)
-This country is rich in resources.
}

酷-
{
酷 (こく) - Cruel; severe; harsh
The root of the adjective 'hidoi'. It emphasizes extreme intensity or lack of mercy.
Memory Tip: The 'alcohol' radical next to 'report'; imagine someone reporting a crime committed while severely drunk.
Example: 酷い雨が降っている。 (ひどいあめがふっている。)
-It is raining severely.
}

凝る-
{
凝る (こる) - To be absorbed in/To get stiff
An intransitive verb meaning to be fanatically devoted to a hobby or to experience muscle stiffness, particularly in the shoulders.
Memory Tip: The ice radical (冫) suggests your focus or your muscles have 'frozen' or solidified in one state.
Example: 彼は写真撮影に凝っている。(かれはしゃしんさつえいにこっている)
-He is really into photography.
}

欄-
{
欄 (らん) - Column; section; field
Refers to a specific space, box, or margin on a page or digital form for information.
Memory Tip: Look for the wood (木) radical—like the wooden frames of old newspaper columns.
Example: 氏名欄に名前を書く。 (しめいらんになまえをかく。)
-Write your name in the name field.
}

茶の湯-
{
茶の湯 (ちゃのゆ) - Tea ceremony
A traditional Japanese cultural activity involving the ceremonial preparation of matcha.
Memory Tip: Literally 'tea' (茶) 's' (の) 'hot water' (湯), emphasizing the core elements of the ritual.
Example: 茶の湯を体験する (ちゃのゆをたいけんする)
-To experience the tea ceremony
}

募る-
{
募る (つのる) - To invite/solicit/grow violent
This verb is used for recruiting people or donations, but can also describe an emotion or storm intensifying.
Memory Tip: 募 (recruit) contains the radical for power/effort (力), implying effort spent to gather things together.
Example: 参加者を募る。 (さんかしゃをつのる。)
-To invite participants.
}

思わず-
{
思わず (おもわず) - Unintentionally, spontaneously
An adverb formed by the verb 'omou' (to think) and the classical negative suffix 'zu'.
Memory Tip: Literally 'without thinking' (omowazu), used when your body acts before your brain.
Example: 思わず笑ってしまった。(おもわずわらってしまった。)
-I laughed without thinking.
}

流石-
{
流石 (さすが) - As expected / typical of
Used to express admiration when someone lives up to their reputation or high standards.
Memory Tip: Kanji literally means 'flow' (流) and 'stone' (石). Think of a master so skilled they can make stones flow like water—as expected of them!
Example: 流石ですね。 (さすがですね。)
-As expected of you (impressive).
}

岡山城-
{
岡山城 (おかやまじょう) - Okayama Castle
A proper noun for the historic castle in Okayama, known for its black exterior.
Memory Tip: The Castle (城) on the Hill (山) in the Okayama district.
Example: 岡山城へ行きました。 (おかやまじょうへいきました。)
-I went to Okayama Castle.
}

報道-
{
報道 (ほうどう) - News report/information
Refers to the process of reporting news via mass media such as TV, newspapers, or the internet.
Memory Tip: 報 (report) + 道 (way/path) = The path through which a report reaches the public.
Example: 事件がテレビで報道された。 (じけんがてれびでほうどうされた。)
-The incident was reported on television.
}

叶う-
{
叶う (かなう) - To come true / to be realized
Specifically used when hopes, dreams, or wishes are fulfilled.
Memory Tip: Mouth (口) plus Ten (十). When ten people say a wish together with their mouths, it comes true.
Example: 夢が叶いました。 (ゆめがかないました。)
-My dream came true.
}

海軍-
{
海軍 (かいぐん) - navy
A compound noun referring to the branch of the military that operates on the sea.
Memory Tip: The "sea" (海) "military" (軍) tells you exactly what this force is.
Example: 彼は海軍の将校です。 (かれはかいぐんのしょうこうです。)
-He is a naval officer.
}

藍-
{
藍 (あい) - Indigo
Refers to both the plant and the deep blue dye derived from it.

意識-
{
意識 (いしき) - Consciousness, awareness
A compound noun where '意' represents thoughts/intent and '識' represents knowing or discerning. It refers to both clinical consciousness and social awareness.

-He lost consciousness in the accident.

煩い-
{
煩い (うるさい) - Noisy / Annoying

宴-

宴 (うたげ) - Banquet / Feast

達する-
{
達する (たっする) - To reach; to attain
An irregular verb used for reaching a physical destination, a numerical limit, or a personal goal.

Example: 目標に達する。 (もくひょうにたっする。)
-To reach a goal.

兼ねる-
{
兼ねる (かねる) - To serve two functions, to combine
A ru-verb used when one object or person holds multiple roles or uses.
Memory Tip: The kanji shows two stalks of grain being grasped together by a single hand, representing "combining."
Example: この部屋は寝室と書斎を兼ねている。 (このへやは しんしつと しょさいを かねている。)
-This room serves as both a bedroom and a study.

闇-
{
闇 (やみ) - Darkness
Refers to physical darkness or a metaphorical state of secrecy.

-A light is visible in the darkness.

禁じる-

禁じる (きんじる) - To forbid/prohibit

狼-

狼 (おおかみ) - Wolf
A noun referring to the wild animal, often found in folklore.

-The wolf is howling.

崩壊-
{
崩壊 (ほうかい) - collapse, crumbling

生じる-
{
生じる (しょうじる) - to result from, to arise
This is an ichidan verb derived from the character for life/birth, often used for abstract developments like problems or friction.
Memory Tip: When "birth/life" (生) is being "performed" (じる), a new situation arises.

至る-
{
至る (いたる) - To reach / To arrive
A formal verb used for arriving at a physical destination or reaching a certain state or conclusion.

間抜け-
{
間抜け (まぬけ) - Fool / idiot
A Na-adjective/noun meaning 'missing the beat.' It literally means the 'ma' (interval/timing) is 'nuke' (dropped/missing).
Memory Tip: If your 'Ma' (timing) is 'Nuke' (missing), you look like a total fool.
Example: そんな間抜けなミスをするなんて。 (そんなまぬけなみすをするなんて。)
-To make such a stupid mistake.

諸〜-
{
諸〜 (しょ〜) - Various/many
A prefix used before nouns to indicate multiple items or several different types of something.

自ら-
{
自ら (みずから) - Oneself / personally / voluntarily
A formal adverbial form emphasizing that an action is taken by the person themselves rather than by others.

我が〜-
{
我が〜 (わが〜) - My, our
A formal or literary possessive prefix derived from the classical Japanese particle 'ga'. It is used to express ownership or belonging to one's self or group.
Memory Tip: Combine 'Ware' (I/self) with the old possessive 'ga' to get 'of me' or 'our'.
Example: 我が家へようこそ。 (わがやへようこそ。)
-Welcome to my home.

極めて-
{
極めて (きわめて) - Extremely, exceedingly

態と-

態と (わざと) - On purpose / Intentionally

蔵-
{
蔵 (くら) - Storehouse/Warehouse
This noun refers to a traditional Japanese storehouse used for storing rice, liquor, or valuables. It is often found in historical contexts or as a suffix in family names.

敢えて (あえて) - Dare to/Deliberately

堪える-

偏り-

偏り (かたより) - Bias, imbalance, leaning

A compound of 'nothing' (無) and 'word/speech' (言).
Memory Tip: When there are 'no' (無) 'words' (言), there is only silence.
Example: 彼は無言で部屋を出た。 (かれはむごんでへやをでた。)
-He left the room in silence.
}

縁-
{
縁 (えん) - fate, bond, edge
This word refers to a karmic connection between people or the physical edge/rim of an object.
Memory Tip: Imagine a thread (糸) of destiny connecting people at the very edge (豕/彖) of the world.
Example: 彼とは不思議な縁がある。(かれとはふしぎなえんがある。)
-I have a strange bond with him.

意志-
{
意志 (いし) - Will/Intent
Refers to a person's determination or purpose. Both kanji contain the 'heart' radical (心), emphasizing internal resolve.
Memory Tip: Combining 'thought' (意) and 'ambition' (志) into one strong heart-driven will.
Example: 彼は意志が強い。 (かれはいしがつよい。)
-He has a strong will.
}

誠に-
{
誠に (まことに) - Truly / Sincerely
This is a formal adverb used to express deep sincerity, often used in business correspondence and apologies.
Memory Tip: Sincerity is represented by speech (言) that is complete (成).
Example: 誠にありがとうございます。 (まことにありがとうございます。)
-Thank you very much.
}

杉-
{
杉 (すぎ) - Cedar / Cryptomeria
A noun representing a common evergreen tree in Japan. It features the tree radical (木) on the left.
Memory Tip: The tree (木) that grows 'too' (sugi) tall is a cedar.
Example: この辺りは杉が多い。 (このあたりはすぎがおおい。)
-There are many cedars around here.

貴族-
{
貴族 (きぞく) - Noble / Aristocrat
Combines 貴 (noble/precious) and 族 (tribe/family). It refers to the hereditary social class of nobility.
Memory Tip: A family (族) that is precious (貴) belongs to the nobility.
Example: 彼は貴族の出身だ。 (かれはきぞくのしゅっしんだ。)
-He comes from a noble family.

撃つ-
{
撃つ (うつ) - To shoot
A transitive verb used for firing a gun, shooting an arrow, or attacking. It is phonetically identical to 'utsu' (to strike) but uses a specific kanji.
Memory Tip: Imagine a hand (radical) pulling a trigger to launch an attack from a chariot.
Example: 彼は銃で的を撃った。 (かれはじゅうでまとをうった。)

筋-
{
筋 (すじ) - Muscle/Plot/Logic
A versatile noun referring to physical muscle fibers, the thread of a story, or the logical consistency of an argument.

井戸-
{
井戸 (いど) - Well
Composed of 井 (well/grid) and 戸 (door), referring to a traditional water well.

放つ-
{
放つ (はなつ) - To release, to set free, to emit

密か-
{
密か (ひそか) - secret, private, stealthy

裂く (さく) - To tear, to split

覗き込む-

覗き込む (のぞきこむ) - To peer into, to look into

突っ込む-

突っ込む (つっこむ) - To thrust into / To plunge

新た-
{
新た (あらた) - New, fresh

逃れる-
{
逃れる (のがれる) - To escape, evade

A godan verb indicating compliance with rules, laws, or following a person.

薦める-
{
薦める (すすめる) - to recommend
This transitive verb is used for suggesting things, people, or actions to others based on a favorable opinion.

本来-
{
本来 (ほんらい) - originally / by nature

誠-

伝-
{
伝 (つて) - Connection/Intermediary

恵む (めぐむ) - To bless, to show mercy, to give

This title is used specifically for an Emperor or Empress. The kanji mean 'steps' (陛) and 'below' (下), referring to one who stands below the steps of the throne out of respect.

好奇心-
{
好奇心 (こうきしん) - Curiosity

Memory Tip: Having a 'heart' that 'likes' 'strange' or unusual things is the essence of curiosity.
Example: 彼は好奇心が旺盛だ (かれはこうきしんがおうせいだ)
-He is full of curiosity
}

暗闇-
{
暗闇 (くらやみ) - Darkness
A combination of two kanji for dark (暗 and 闇), emphasizing total absence of light.
Memory Tip: The sun is blocked in '暗' and something is hidden inside the gate in '闇', creating total darkness.
Example: 暗闇の中で鍵を探す (くらやみのなかでかぎをさがす)
-Searching for keys in the dark
}

操る-
{
操る (あやつる) - To manipulate, to pull strings
This verb refers to controlling a tool, a puppet, or even a person with great skill or dexterity.
Memory Tip: Use your HAND (扌) to manage a complex operation (操) like a puppet master.
Example: 彼は巧みに言葉を操る。 (かれはたくみにことばをあやつる。)
-He manipulates words skillfully.
}

師匠-
{
師匠 (ししょう) - Master, mentor
It describes a master in traditional arts, crafts, or martial arts who takes on apprentices.
Memory Tip: A combination of a TEACHER (師) and an ARTISAN (匠) who masters his craft.
Example: 彼は私の料理の師匠です。 (かれはわたしのりょうりのししょうです。)
-He is my cooking mentor.
}

淡い-
{
淡い (あわい) - Faint, pale, fleeting
Used for light colors, delicate flavors, or vague, short-lived emotions.
Memory Tip: Adding WATER (氵) to a FLAME (炎) makes the light become pale and weak.
Example: 彼は淡い色のシャツを着ている。 (かれはあわいいろのしゃつをきている。)
-He is wearing a pale-colored shirt.
}

関わる-
{
関わる (かかわる) - To be involved with/to affect
An intransitive verb often used with the particle 'ni' to indicate involvement in a matter or relationship.
Memory Tip: Passing through the gate (門) to connect or intertwine with what is inside.
Example: 彼はその事件に関わっている。(かれはそのじけんにかかわっている。)
-He is involved in that incident.
}

隙-
{
隙 (すき) - Gap/Opening/Vulnerability
Can refer to a physical space between objects or a mental lapse in one's defense or attention.
Memory Tip: Imagine a small space in a wall (阝) where you can see the sun and a small gap.
Example: 隙を見て逃げ出した。(すきをみてにげだした。)
-He saw an opening and escaped.
}

指揮-
{
指揮 (しき) - Command/Direction
A noun representing leadership or conducting, often used with 'suru' in musical or military contexts.
Memory Tip: Use your 'finger' (指) to 'wield' (揮) the orchestra's baton.
Example: 彼はオーケストラを指揮した。 (かれはおーけすとらをしきした。)
-He conducted the orchestra.
}

幕-
{
幕 (まく) - Curtain/Act
Used for theater curtains or as a counter for acts in a performance.
Memory Tip: A cloth 'curtain' (幕) hanging over the 'market' (radical inside).
Example: 第一幕が終わった。 (だいいちまくがおわった。)
-The first act ended.
}

指摘-
{
指摘 (してき) - Pointing out/Identification
Identifying or calling attention to a specific point, fact, or error.
Memory Tip: Using your 'finger' (指) to 'pluck' (摘) out the specific mistake.
Example: 彼は間違いを指摘した。 (かれはまちがいをしてきした。)
-He pointed out the mistake.
}

指摘する-
{
指摘する (してきする) - To point out
This is a suru-verb combining 'point' (指) and 'pluck/expose' (摘). It is used for identifying errors or facts.
Memory Tip: Use your finger (指) to pluck (摘) out a specific detail or mistake.
Example: 彼は私の間違いを指摘した。(かれはわたしのまちがいをしていした。)
-He pointed out my mistake.
}

復讐-
{
復讐 (ふくしゅう) - Revenge
A formal noun or suru-verb. '復' means return/redo and '讐' means adversary or retribution.
Memory Tip: Returning (復) a blow to your enemy (讐) to settle a score.
Example: 彼は復讐を誓った。(かれはふくしゅうをちかった。)
-He swore revenge.
}

作用-
{
作用 (さよう) - Action / Effect / Function
Combines 'make/produce' (作) and 'use/service' (用). It refers to a physical or chemical process having an effect.
Memory Tip: The way something is made (作) to be used (用) determines its natural effect.
Example: 薬の副作用を調べる。(くすりのふくさようをしらべる。)
-Investigate the side effects of the medicine.
}

仏-
{
仏 (ほとけ) - Buddha / Deceased person
Refers to the enlightened one, a Buddhist statue, or a person who has passed away.
Memory Tip: A person (亻) who is no (厶) longer a simple human being.
Example: 仏のような人だ。 (ほとけのようなひとだ。)
-He is a person like a Buddha (very kind).
}

非難-
{
非難 (ひなん) - Blame/Criticism
A noun used to describe the act of finding fault or censuring someone. The kanji mean "non/fault" and "blame."
Memory Tip: "Non-stop" (非) "blame" (難) leads to heavy criticism.
Example: 彼は非難を浴びた。(かれはひなんをあびた。)
-He was showered with criticism.
}

非難する-
{
非難する (ひなんする) - To criticize/blame
The verb form of the noun 非難 (criticism) created by adding the helper verb suru.
Memory Tip: To "do" (する) the act of "non-stop blame" (非難).
Example: 彼は政府を非難した。(かれはせいふをひなんした。)
-He criticized the government.
}

大臣-
{
大臣 (だいじん) - Government minister
A title for a high-ranking cabinet official, literally meaning "great" (大) "servant/retainer" (臣).
Memory Tip: The "big" (大) "retainer" (臣) who serves the prime minister.
Example: 外務大臣が訪米した。(がいむだいじんがほうべいした。)
-The Foreign Minister visited the US.
}

処理-
{
処理 (しょり) - Processing, dealing with, disposal
A Suru-verb used for systematic handling of tasks, data, or physical waste. It implies a logical or administrative resolution.
Memory Tip: To 'manage/dispose' (処) using 'logic/reason' (理) is to process something effectively.
Example: 彼は大量のデータを処理した。 (かれはたいりょうのでーたをしょりした。)
-He processed a large amount of data.
}

評価-
{
評価 (ひょうか) - Evaluation, appraisal, assessment
A Suru-verb or noun formed by 評 (criticism/judgement) and 価 (value/price).
Memory Tip: Using words (言) to judge (評) the price or value (価) of something.
Example: その映画の評価は高い。 (そのえいがのひょうかはたかい。)
-The evaluation of that movie is high.
}

塊-
{
塊 (かたまり) - Lump, mass, clod, cluster
A noun used for a concentrated mass of something, like earth, snow, or even a group of people.
Memory Tip: A demon (鬼) hiding inside a lump of earth (土).
Example: 雪の塊を投げる。 (ゆきのかたまりをなげる。)
-Throw a lump of snow.
}

無意識-
{
無意識 (むいしき) - unconscious, involuntary
Formed by adding 無 (none) to 意識 (consciousness). It is used as a noun or a na-adjective/no-adjective.
Memory Tip: When you have no (無) consciousness (意識) of an action, it is unconscious.
Example: 無意識にため息をついた。 (むいしきにためいきをついた。)
-I sighed unconsciously.
}

浪人-
{
浪人 (ろうにん) - Masterless samurai, student waiting for another chance
Originally used for samurai without a master, it now specifically refers to students who have failed entrance exams and are studying for a retry.
Memory Tip: A person (人) who is wandering like a wave (浪) without a school or master to anchor them.
Example: 彼は一浪して大学に入った。(かれはいちろうしてだいがくにはいった。)
-He entered university after one year as a ronin.
}

理屈-
{
理屈 (りくつ) - Logic, reason, pretext
Refers to the underlying logic or theory of a situation. It often carries a negative nuance of "quibbling" or "making excuses."
Memory Tip: Logic (理) that is bent or crouched (屈) to fit an excuse rather than the truth.
Example: 理屈はいいから、やってみて。(りくつはいいから、やってみて。)
-Never mind the logic, just try it.

強烈-
{
強烈 (きょうれつ) - Intense, strong
An adjective describing something with a very powerful impact or fierce intensity.
Memory Tip: Combining Strength (強) with Burning Heat (烈) creates an intense feeling.
Example: 彼には強烈な印象を受けた。 (かれにはきょうれつないんしょうをうけた。)
-He left a strong impression on me.

係わる-

係わる (かかわる) - To be involved in, to affect

-To be involved in that incident.

把握-
{
把握 (はあく) - Grasp; understand; catch

Example: 状況を把握する。 (じょうきょうをはあくする。)

舞 (まい) - Dance

名誉 (めいよ) - Honor, prestige, credit

哀れ-

哀れ (あわれ) - Pity / sorrow / pathetic

獲物-
{
獲物 (えもの) - Prey / Game / Catch

現に (げんに) - actually, really

快い (こころよい) - Pleasant, agreeable

説得する (せっとくする) - To persuade

嘆く-

夫妻-

夫妻 (ふさい) - Married couple, husband and wife
A formal compound noun combining the kanji for husband (夫) and wife (妻).
Memory Tip: Visualize the Husband (夫) and Wife (妻) standing side-by-side as a formal pair.
Example: 田中夫妻がパーティーに来た。 (たなかふさいがぱーてぃーにきた。)
-Mr. and Mrs. Tanaka came to the party.
}

観念-
{
観念 (かんねん) - Idea, notion, resignation
Combines 観 (view) and 念 (thought). It can refer to a philosophical concept or the act of giving up.
Memory Tip: When you observe (観) a final thought (念), you reach a conclusion or resignation.
Example: 彼はついに観念した。(かれはついにかんねんした)
-He finally gave up.
}

永久-
{
永久 (えいきゅう) - Eternity, permanence
Consists of 永 (eternal) and 久 (long time). It describes something that lasts forever.
Memory Tip: Both kanji emphasize long duration; when combined, they represent forever.
Example: 永久に愛することを誓います。(えいきゅうにあいすることをちかいます)
-I swear to love you forever.
}

高度-
{
高度 (こうど) - Altitude, high-level, advanced
Formed from 高 (high) and 度 (degree). It can mean physical height or a high degree of sophistication.
Memory Tip: A high (高) degree (度) of either elevation or technical skill.
Example: 高度な技術が必要です。(こうどなぎじゅつがひつようです)
-Advanced technology is necessary.
}

拒否-
{
拒否 (きょひ) - Refusal/Denial
This verb/noun expresses a formal or firm rejection of an offer, proposal, or request.
Memory Tip: Use your hand (扌) to 'reject' (拒) and say 'no' (否) to the proposal.
Example: 彼らはその要求を拒否した。 (かれらはそのようきゅうをきょひした。)
-They refused that demand.
}

策-
{
策 (さく) - Measure/Plan/Strategy
A noun used for formal policies, countermeasures, or a clever scheme to achieve a goal.
Memory Tip: Visualize a strategic plan written on bamboo (竹) slips in ancient times.
Example: 良い策を考え出す必要がある。 (よいさくをかんがえだすひつようがある。)
-It is necessary to come up with a good plan.
}

深刻-
{
深刻 (しんこく) - Serious/Grave
An adjective used for critical situations or deep emotions. It combines "deep" (深) and "carve" (刻).
Memory Tip: A deeply (深) carved (刻) scar represents a very serious or grave situation.
Example: 事態は非常に深刻だ。 (じたいはひじょうにしんこくだ。)
-The situation is extremely serious.
}

大胆-
{
大胆 (だいたん) - Bold/Daring
A na-adjective combining 大 (big) and 胆 (gallbladder/courage). Traditionally, a large gallbladder was linked to bravery.
Memory Tip: Someone with a "big (大) liver/gall (胆)" has the guts to be bold.
Example: 彼女は大胆な決断を下した。 (かのじょはだいたんなけつだんをくだした。)
-She made a bold decision.
}

悲劇-
{
悲劇 (ひげき) - Tragedy
Combines 悲 (sad) and 劇 (drama/play). It refers to both theatrical tragedies and tragic real-life events.
Memory Tip: A sad (悲) theatrical play (劇) is a tragedy.
Example: その事故は大きな悲劇だった。 (そのじこはおおきなひげきだった。)
-That accident was a great tragedy.
}

首相-
{
首相 (しゅしょう) - Prime Minister
This noun combines the kanji for "head/neck" (首) and "minister" (相) to denote the head of government.
Memory Tip: The "Head" (首) "Minister" (相) leads the country.
Example: 首相が演説を行う。 (しゅしょうがえんぜつをおこなう。)
-The Prime Minister gives a speech.
}

錯覚-
{
錯覚 (さっかく) - Optical illusion / Hallucination
A noun or suru-verb consisting of "confused/mixed" (錯) and "sense/perception" (覚).
Memory Tip: When your "senses" (覚) are "mixed up" (錯), you see an illusion.
Example: それはただの錯覚だ。 (それはただのさっかくだ。)
-That is just an illusion.
}

〜層-
{
〜層 (〜そう) - Layer / Stratum / Social class
A suffix used for geological layers or segments of a population based on specific criteria.
Memory Tip: The kanji contains "earth/soil" (土) at the bottom, suggesting layers of ground or classes.
Example: 若年層に人気がある。 (じゃくねんそうににんきがある。)
-It is popular among the younger generation.
}

班-
{
班 (はん) - Group / Party / Squad
A noun often used for small organizational units, such as cleaning squads or study groups.
Memory Tip: Two "kings" (王) are split by a "knife" (刂) into separate groups.
Example: ４人１組の班を作る。 (よにんひとくみのはんをつくる。)
-Form groups of four people.
}

唐突-
{
唐突 (とうとつ) - Abrupt/Sudden
Used to describe an action or event that happens unexpectedly and without warning.
Memory Tip: Imagine a 'Tang' (唐) dynasty warrior 'colliding/breaking through' (突) a wall suddenly.
Example: 彼は唐突に部屋を出て行った。 (かれはとうとつにへやをでていった。)
-He left the room abruptly.
}

絶叫-
{
絶叫 (ぜっきょう) - Scream, shout, exclamation
Combines 絶 (discontinue/extreme) and 叫 (shout). It describes a shout of extreme intensity.
Memory Tip: Imagine a shout so loud that it 'cuts off' (絶) all other sounds in the room.
Example: 観客は興奮して絶叫した。 (かんきゃくはこうふんしてぜっきょうした。)
-The audience screamed in excitement.
}

残酷-
{
残酷 (ざんこく) - Cruel/Harsh
A na-adjective where 'zan' means leftover/ruthless and 'koku' means severe. It describes extreme lack of mercy.
Memory Tip: A ruthless person leaves a severe and cruel impression on others.
Example: その映画は残酷なシーンが多い (そのえいがはざんこくなしーんがおおい)
-That movie has many cruel scenes.
}

築く-
{
築く (きずく) - To build/construct
A godan transitive verb used for physical structures or abstract concepts like trust or wealth.
Memory Tip: You kick up dust to build something from the ground up.
Example: 二人は幸せな家庭を築いた (ふたりはしあわせなかていをきずいた)
-The two of them built a happy home.
}

収める-
{
収める (おさめる) - To store/achieve/obtain
An ichidan transitive verb used for putting things away, paying (taxes), or achieving (success).
Memory Tip: Putting things inside a box (the radical) to store them or finalize a goal.
Example: 彼は大きな成功を収めた (かれはおおきなせいこうをおさめた)
-He achieved great success.
}

脆い-
{
脆い (もろい) - Fragile/Brittle
An i-adjective describing something that breaks or crumbles easily, physically or emotionally.
Memory Tip: The left radical 肉 (meat/flesh) suggests that human bodies and emotions are easily hurt.
Example: このガラスは非常に脆い (このがらすはひじょうにもろい)
-This glass is extremely fragile.
}

砕ける-
{
砕ける (くだける) - To break/To smash/To be crushed
An intransitive verb meaning to shatter into small pieces; also used for informal language.
Memory Tip: The kanji features 石 (stone), implying the result of a stone being smashed against something.
Example: 氷が粉々に砕けた (こおりがこなごなにくだけた)
-The ice shattered into pieces.
}

勘-
{
勘 (かん) - Intuition/Hunch
A noun representing a sixth sense or instinctive feeling. It is often used with 'ataru' (to hit/be right) or 'hataraku' (to work).
Memory Tip: On the right is 'power' (力); think of it as the 'power' of your gut feeling.
Example: 勘が当たりました (かんがあたりました)
-My hunch was correct.
}

継ぐ-
{
継ぐ (つぐ) - To succeed/inherit
A transitive verb used for taking over a business, family line, or legacy. It implies continuity.
Memory Tip: The 'thread' radical (糸) on the left represents the continuous string connecting generations.
Example: 彼は父の跡を継ぎました (かれはちちのあとをつぎました)
-He succeeded his father (took over the legacy).
}

派遣-
{
派遣 (はけん) - Dispatch, sending (on a mission)
Combines 派 (faction/group) and 遣 (send). It is common in business for temporary staffing or military deployment.
Memory Tip: 'Ha' (send) + 'Ken' (authority); sending a person with specific authority to represent a group.
Example: 調査員を派遣する。 (ちょうさいんをはけんする。)
-Dispatch an investigator.
}

囚人-
{
囚人 (しゅうじん) - Prisoner
Formed by 囚 (captured) and 人 (person). It refers to someone serving time in a correctional facility.
Memory Tip: Look at the kanji 囚: it is a person (人) trapped inside a four-walled box (囗).
Example: 囚人が脱走した。 (しゅうじんがだっそうした。)
-A prisoner escaped.
}

捻る-
{
捻る (ひねる) - To twist/To wring
A godan verb that describes twisting a physical object (like a cap) or metaphorically twisting one's mind to think hard.
Memory Tip: Imagine using your fingers to twist (捻) a small dial.
Example: 足首を捻った。 (あしくびをひねった。)
-I twisted my ankle.
}

愚か-
{
愚か (おろか) - Foolish
A na-adjective used for behavior or decisions that lack wisdom or common sense.
Memory Tip: The kanji shows a "Brain/Head" above a "Monkey" (禺) and "Heart" (心), suggesting a foolish mindset.
Example: そんなことをするのは愚かだ。 (そんなことをするのはおろかだ。)
-It is foolish to do such a thing.
}

片隅-
{
片隅 (かたすみ) - Corner/Nook
A noun indicating a remote corner or a small, inconspicuous spot.
Memory Tip: A "single-side" (片) "corner" (隅) emphasizes an isolated or small space.
Example: 部屋の片隅に机を置く。 (へやのかたすみにつくえをおく。)
-Place a desk in the corner of the room.
}

拒む-
{
拒む (こばむ) - To refuse, to reject
A transitive godan verb used for firm refusals or resisting an action.
Memory Tip: Use your hand (扌) to hold back a giant (巨) and say no.
Example: 彼は要求を拒んだ。 (かれはようきゅうをこばんだ。)
-He refused the demand.
}

王妃-
{
王妃 (おうひ) - queen / princess (consort)
Refers specifically to the wife of a king rather than a reigning queen (who would be 女王).
Memory Tip: The King (王) and his official woman/consort (妃) rule together.
Example: 王妃は美しかった。(おうひはうつくしかった。)
-The queen was beautiful.
}

無邪気-
{
無邪気 (むじゃき) - innocent / simple-minded
Used to describe a pure, guiltless nature, especially in children.
Memory Tip: Literally 'without (無) evil (邪) spirit (気)'.
Example: 彼は無邪気に笑った。(かれはむじゃきにわらった。)
-He laughed innocently.
}

化ける-
{
化ける (ばける) - To transform, to take another form
An Ichidan verb often used for supernatural transformations, like foxes or ghosts.
Memory Tip: The 'change' (ka) radical represents a person flipping or transforming.
Example: 狐が人間に化ける (きつねがにんげんにばける)
-A fox transforms into a human.
}

株-
{
株 (かぶ) - Stock/Share/Stump
A versatile noun referring to either the stump of a tree or a share in a company.
Memory Tip: A tree (木) cut down to its red (朱) core remains as a stump or a 'foundation' (share) of the tree.
Example: 彼は株でたくさん儲けた。 (かれはかぶでたくさんもうけた)
-He made a lot of money with stocks.
}

朱-
{
朱 (しゅ) - Vermilion, cinnabar red
Explanation: A traditional, bright orange-red color often associated with Shinto shrines and red ink seals.
Memory Tip: The kanji looks like a tree with a marker; imagine a tree stump painted bright vermilion red.
Example: 朱色の鳥居が見える。 (しゅいろのとりいがみえる。)
-I can see a vermilion torii gate.
}

呆気-
{
呆気 (あっけ) - Blank amazement, taken aback
Explanation: Usually found in the idiom 呆気に取られる (to be stunned). 呆 means dazed or dumbfounded.
Memory Tip: When you are dazed (呆), your spirit/air (気) is taken away by shock.
Example: 彼の早業に呆気に取られた。 (かれのはやわざにあっけにとられた。)
-I was taken aback by his quick work.
}

胴-
{
胴 (どう) - Torso/Trunk
Refers to the main part of the human body or the body of an object/instrument. It features the body part radical (月).
Memory Tip: The body (月) part that stays the same (同) width from top to bottom is the torso.
Example: 胴が長い犬ですね。(どうがながいいぬですね。)
-That is a dog with a long torso.
}

和尚-
{
和尚 (おしょう) - Buddhist priest
This term is typically used for high-ranking Zen priests. It combines '和' (harmony) and '尚' (esteem).
Memory Tip: A priest brings Harmony (和) and should be Esteemed (尚).
Example: 和尚がお経を唱える。 (おしょうがおきょうをとなえる。)
-The priest recites the sutra.
}

破片-
{
破片 (はへん) - Fragment, splinter, shard
Combines 破 (break) and 片 (one-sided/piece). It refers to a small piece of a broken object.
Memory Tip: When you break (破) something, a small piece (片) is all that's left.
Example: 皿の破片を片付ける。(さらのはへんをかたづける。)
-Clean up the shards of the plate.
}

踏み込む-
{
踏み込む (ふみこむ) - To step into, to penetrate
A compound verb combining "fumu" (to step) and "komu" (to go into), implying movement into a deeper or specific space.
Memory Tip: Think of "fuming" as you "step" (fumu) "into" (komu) a restricted area.
Example: 彼は問題の核心に踏み込んだ。 (かれはもんだいのかくしんにふみこんだ。)
-He stepped into the heart of the problem.
}

不吉-
{
不吉 (ふきつ) - Ominous, unlucky
A na-adjective consisting of "fu" (not) and "kitsu" (good luck/auspicious).
Memory Tip: Think of "Kitsu" as a lucky fox, but "Fu" makes it "not" lucky.
Example: カラスが鳴くのは不吉だ。 (からすがなくのはふきつだ。)
-A crow cawing is ominous.
}

襲撃-
{
襲撃 (しゅうげき) - Attack, raid
A noun referring to a sudden, violent assault or charge.
Memory Tip: "Shuu" sounds like a "swoop" and "geki" means to strike or hit.
Example: 基地が襲撃を受けた。 (きちがしゅうげきをうけた。)
-The base came under attack.
}

襲撃する-
{
襲撃する (しゅうげきする) - To attack, to raid
The verb form of the noun "shūgeki," used to describe the act of carrying out a raid.
Memory Tip: Add the action verb "suru" to "raid" to carry out the assault.
Example: 賊が村を襲撃した。 (ぞくがむらをしゅうげきした。)
-The bandits attacked the village.
}

静寂-
{
静寂 (せいじゃく) - Silence, stillness
A formal noun describing a profound or serene lack of sound, often in nature.
Memory Tip: A quiet (静) and lonely or mellow (寂) atmosphere creates deep silence.
Example: 森は静寂に包まれていた。 (もりはせいじゃくにつつまれていた。)
-The forest was wrapped in silence.
}

甚だ-
{
甚だ (はなはだ) - Exceedingly, very
A formal adverb used to emphasize an extreme degree, often for undesirable situations.
Memory Tip: The kanji 甚 represents an extreme or excessive amount.
Example: 甚だ遺憾に思います。 (はなはだいかんにおもいます。)
-I find it extremely regrettable.
}

露-
{
露 (つゆ) - Dew
Represents the water droplets that form on surfaces during the morning.
Memory Tip: Rain (雨) that settles on the path (路) as tiny drops of dew.
Example: 草の葉に露が降りている。 (くさのはにつゆがおりている。)
-There is dew on the leaves of the grass.
}

捕虜-
{
捕虜 (ほりょ) - Prisoner of war
Combines 'catch' (捕) and 'captive' (虜), specifically used for military captives.
Memory Tip: Someone caught (捕) and held as a captive (虜) in a cage.
Example: 彼は捕虜として捕まった。 (かれはほりょとしてつかまった。)
-He was taken as a prisoner of war.
}

浸る-
{
浸る (ひたる) - To soak, to be immersed
This intransitive verb describes being physically submerged in liquid or deeply absorbed in a memory or feeling.
Memory Tip: The water radical (氵) next to the broom/hand suggests cleaning or dipping something into water.
Example: 思い出に浸る (おもいでにひたる)
-To soak in memories
}

秘める-
{
秘める (ひめる) - To hide / To keep to oneself
An Ichidan verb used for keeping feelings or secrets hidden deep inside.
Memory Tip: Related to 'secret' (秘密 - himitsu); it's the action of keeping a secret in the heart.
Example: 彼女は心に決意を秘めている。 (かのじょはこころにけついをひめている。)
-She hides a resolution in her heart.
}

誘拐-
{
誘拐 (ゆうかい) - Kidnapping / Abduction
A noun/suru-verb combining 'invite/entice' (誘) and 'kidnap' (拐).
Memory Tip: Someone who 'entices' (誘) you away to 'kidnap' (拐) you.
Example: 彼は誘拐事件に巻き込まれた。 (かれはゆうかいじけんにまきこまれた。)
-He was involved in a kidnapping case.
}

軌道-
{
軌道 (きどう) - Orbit/Track
Combines 軌 (rut/track) and 道 (road/way). Refers to satellite paths or train rails.
Memory Tip: A vehicle (車) traveling on a specific road (道) makes a track.
Example: 衛星が軌道に乗った。(えいせいがきどうにのった。)
-The satellite entered orbit.
}

推定-
{
推定 (すいてい) - Estimation/Presumption
A noun/suru-verb formed by 推 (infer) and 定 (decide), used when making an educated guess based on evidence.
Memory Tip: To make an estimate, you must "infer" (推) information to "fix" (定) a value.
Example: 被害額は一億円と推定される。(ひがいがくはいちおくえんとすいていされる。)
-The damage is estimated to be 100 million yen.
}

哲学-
{
哲学 (てつがく) - Philosophy
Composed of 哲 (wisdom) and 学 (study), this word was coined during the Meiji era to translate the Western concept.
Memory Tip: Philosophy is the "study" (学) of "wisdom" (哲).
Example: 彼は大学で西洋哲学を専攻した。(かれはだいがくでせいようてつがくをせんこうした。)
-He majored in Western philosophy at the university.
}

顔面-
{
顔面 (がんめん) - Face/Surface of the face
Combining 顔 (face) and 面 (surface), it is a more formal or anatomical term than the common "kao".
Memory Tip: This refers specifically to the frontal "surface" (面) of the "face" (顔).
Example: 彼はボールを顔面に受けた。(かれはぼーるをがんめんにうけた。)
-He took a ball to the face.
}

飢える-
{
飢える (うえる) - To starve/To thirst for
A verb that can mean physical starvation or a strong metaphorical craving for something like love or power.
Memory Tip: The left side of 飢 is the food radical; without it, you are starving.
Example: 彼は愛に飢えている。(かれはあいにうえている。)
-He is starving for love.
}

駒-
{
駒 (こま) - Chess piece/Pawn
Originally referred to a horse, now commonly used for pieces in Shogi or metaphorically for a person being used.
Memory Tip: The kanji contains the "horse" (馬) radical, as pieces move across the board like horses.
Example: 彼は重要な駒として使われた。(かれはじゅうようなこまとしてつかわれた。)
-He was used as an important pawn.
}

犠牲者-
{
犠牲者 (ぎせいしゃ) - Victim/Casualty
Composed of 犠牲 (sacrifice) and 者 (person). It refers to those killed or injured in accidents or war.
Memory Tip: Both 犠 and 牲 contain the "cow" (牛) radical, representing ancient animal sacrifices.
Example: その事故で多くの犠牲者が出た。(そのじこでおおくのぎせいしゃがでた。)
-There were many victims in that accident.
}

砕く-
{
砕く (くだく) - To smash, to break, to crush
A transitive verb used for physically breaking something hard or metaphorically simplifying a difficult concept.
Memory Tip: The kanji contains 石 (stone) and 九 + 十 (many pieces); imagine smashing a stone into many bits.
Example: 氷を砕く。 (こおりをくだく。)
-To crush ice.
}

墓地-
{
墓地 (ぼち) - Graveyard, cemetery
A compound noun consisting of 'haka' (grave) and 'chi' (land/ground).
Memory Tip: Earth (土) and grass (艹) cover a sun (日) that has set forever in the ground.
Example: 彼は墓地で祈った。 (かれはぼちでいのった。)
-He prayed at the cemetery.
}

盗賊-
{
盗賊 (とうぞく) - Thief, bandit
A formal term for a robber, combining the kanji for 'steal' (盗) and 'rebel/bandit' (賊).
Memory Tip: A thief (盗) belongs to a dangerous tribe or group (賊).
Example: 盗賊が宝を奪った。 (とうぞくがたからをうばった。)
-The bandit stole the treasure.
}

会釈-
{
会釈 (えしゃく) - A slight bow / A nod
Refers to the shallowest of the three common Japanese bows, usually around 15 degrees, used for casual greetings.
Memory Tip: Meeting (会) and Explaining (釈) — a bow used when you meet and acknowledge someone's presence.
Example: 彼女は軽く会釈した。 (かのじょはかるくえしゃくした。)
-She gave a slight bow.
}

枠-
{
枠 (わく) - Frame / Border / Limit / Category
Refers to a physical frame (like a window) or an abstract boundary/quota in a system.
Memory Tip: The 'wood' radical (木) on the left shows it originally referred to a wooden frame.
Example: 窓の枠を直す。 (まどのわくをなおす。)
-Fix the window frame.
}

膜-
{
膜 (まく) - Membrane, film, thin layer
A noun used in biological or technical contexts to describe a thin skin or coating.
Memory Tip: The flesh radical on the left suggests it covers the body like a thin curtain.
Example: 表面に薄い膜がある。(ひょうめんにうすいまくがある。)
-There is a thin film on the surface.
}

論理-
{
論理 (ろんり) - Logic
A noun representing the principles of reasoning and valid inference.
Memory Tip: Using reason (理) to construct a sound argument (論).
Example: 彼の論理は一貫している。(かれのろんりはいっかんしている。)
-His logic is consistent.
}

衝突-
{
衝突 (しょうとつ) - Collision, conflict, clash
Used for physical crashes between objects or metaphorical clashes between opinions.
Memory Tip: A heavy impact (衝) that happens suddenly (突).
Example: 意見が衝突した。(いけんがしょうとつした。)
-Our opinions clashed.
}

本能-
{
本能 (ほんのう) - Instinct
This word combines 'origin' and 'ability'. It refers to an innate, unlearned biological urge or behavior found in animals and humans.
Memory Tip: An ability (能) that is built into your very origin or base (本) from birth.
Example: 鮭は本能で自分が生まれた川に戻る。(さけはほんのうでじぶんがうまれたかわにもどる。)
-Salmon return to the river where they were born by instinct.
}

賢明-
{
賢明 (けんめい) - Wise / Prudent
An adjective (na-type) used to describe a person's judgment or actions as sensible and highly intelligent.
Memory Tip: A person who is 'wise' (賢) usually has a 'bright' or clear (明) mind.
Example: それは非常に賢明な判断だ。(それはひじょうにけんめいなせんたくだ。)
-That is an extremely wise decision.
}

神聖-
{
神聖 (しんせい) - Sacred
Formed by the kanji for 'god' and 'holy', used to describe things of religious or spiritual significance.
Memory Tip: A god (神) who is also a saint (聖) must be sacred.
Example: 神聖な儀式が行われた (しんせいなぎしきがおこなわれた)
-A sacred ceremony was held.
}

編集者-
{
編集者 (へんしゅうしゃ) - Editor
Composed of 'compile' + 'gather' + 'person', describing someone who edits media.
Memory Tip: The person (者) who gathers (集) and compiles (編) stories into a book.
Example: 彼は雑誌の編集者として働いている (かれはざっしのへんしゅうしゃとしてはたらいている)
-He is working as a magazine editor.
}

比較的-
{
比較的 (ひかくてき) - Relatively, comparatively
This combines 'comparison' (比較) with the suffix '-like' (的). It functions as a -na adjective or an adverb to describe a degree relative to something else.
Memory Tip: Compare (比) two things (較) to find the target (的) state.
Example: 今日は比較的暖かいです。 (きょうはひかくてきあたたかいです。)
-It's relatively warm today.
}

爽やか-
{
爽やか (さわやか) - Refreshing, fresh
A -na adjective used to describe pleasant weather, a clear voice, or a refreshing personality. The kanji depicts a person with open space around them.
Memory Tip: The four 'X' marks in the kanji (爽) look like windows letting in a fresh breeze.
Example: 爽やかな秋の朝ですね。 (さわやかなあきのあさですね。)
-It's a refreshing autumn morning, isn't it?
}

建築-
{
建築 (けんちく) - Architecture, construction
A formal term combining 'to build' (建) and 'to construct/pile up' (築). It is used for both the act of building and the study of architecture.
Memory Tip: Establish (建) the plan and then pile up (築) the materials.
Example: 彼は大学で建築を学んでいます。 (かれはだいがくでけんちくをまなんでいます。)
-He is studying architecture at university.
}

所属-
{
所属 (しょぞく) - Affiliation, membership
A compound noun often used with the verb 'suru' to indicate being part of a group or organization.
Memory Tip: Think of a specific 'Place' (所) where you are 'Attached/Connected' (属).
Example: 彼は野球部に所属している。 (かれはやきゅうぶにしょぞくしている。)
-He belongs to the baseball club.
}

愚痴-
{
愚痴 (ぐち) - Complaint, grumble
Often used with the verb 'kobosu' (to spill or vent). It combines the kanji for 'foolish' and 'ignorant'.
Memory Tip: Think of a foolish (愚) person spilling their silly (痴) complaints to everyone.
Example: 彼はいつも仕事の愚痴をこぼしている。 (かれはいつもしごとのぐちをこぼしている。)
-He is always complaining about his work.
}

国境-
{
国境 (こっきょう) - National border
A compound word consisting of 'country' and 'boundary/border'.
Memory Tip: It marks the boundary (境) between one country (国) and the next.
Example: 電車で国境を越える。 (でんしゃでこっきょうをこえる。)
-To cross the border by train.
}

遺産-
{
遺産 (いさん) - Inheritance, legacy, heritage
遺 (bequeath) plus 産 (property). Used for both financial assets and cultural history.
Memory Tip: Leaving things behind on the "road" (辶) of life as your "production" (産).
Example: 祖父から遺産を相続した。(そふからいさんをそうぞくした。)
-I inherited an estate from my grandfather.
}

惜しむ-
{
惜しむ (おしむ) - To value, to grudge, to regret
A transitive verb expressing reluctance to waste or lose something precious.
Memory Tip: Your heart (忄) feels for the old (昔) value and hates to see it go.
Example: 彼は努力を惜しまない。(かれはどりょくをおしまない。)
-He does not spare any effort.
}

〜症-
{
〜症 (しょう) - Sickness / illness / syndrome
A productive suffix added to nouns to specify a particular medical condition or symptom.
Memory Tip: The 'sickness' radical (疒) on top signals it's always related to health issues.
Example: 彼は重い不眠症に悩んでいる。 (かれはおもいふみんしょうになやんでいる。)
-He is suffering from severe insomnia.
}

暖炉-
{
暖炉 (だんろ) - Fireplace
A specific noun referring to a hearth used for warming a room.
Memory Tip: 'Warmth' (暖) plus 'Hearth/Furnace' (炉) equals a fireplace.
Example: 暖炉のそばで本を読む。 (だんろのそばでほんをよむ。)
-I read a book by the fireplace.
}

沢-
{
沢 (さわ) - Mountain stream, marsh, swamp
Refers to small streams or wetlands, often used in geographical names or mountain climbing contexts.
Memory Tip: The water (氵) radical combined with the shape of gatherers in a low valley area.
Example: 沢で魚を釣った。(さわでさかなをつった)
-I caught fish in the mountain stream.
}

茂み-
{
茂み (しげみ) - Thicket, bush, shrubbery
A noun derived from the verb 'shigeru' (to grow thick), referring to a dense cluster of plants.
Memory Tip: The grass (艹) radical on top indicates 'overgrowth' in a specific place (み).
Example: 猫が茂みに隠れた。(ねこがしげみにかくれた)
-The cat hid in the thicket.
}

快感-
{
快感 (かいかん) - Pleasant sensation, pleasure
A combination of 'pleasant' (快) and 'feeling' (感), often describing a physical rush of pleasure.
Memory Tip: A 'Pleasant' 'Feeling' that makes your heart (忄) feel light.
Example: 走った後の快感は格別だ。(はしったあとのかいかんはかくべつだ)
-The pleasure after running is exceptional.
}

資金-
{
資金 (しきん) - Funds/Capital
Refers to the money needed for a specific purpose or business, combining 'resource/asset' (資) and 'money' (金).
Memory Tip: Money (金) that serves as your primary resource (資).
Example: 新しい事業の資金を集める。 (あたらしいじぎょうのしきんをあつめる。)
-To raise funds for a new business.
}

信徒-
{
信徒 (しんと) - Believer/Layperson
A term for a follower or believer of a religion, especially a layperson rather than clergy. 'Shin' is trust/believe, 'to' is follower.
Memory Tip: A person who believes (信) becomes a disciple (徒).
Example: 彼は熱心な仏教の信徒だ。 (かれはねっしんなぶっきょうのしんとだ。)
-He is a devoted Buddhist believer.
}

拷問-
{
拷問 (ごうもん) - Torture
This is a noun/suru-verb referring to the act of inflicting physical or mental pain for interrogation or punishment.
Memory Tip: The first kanji 拷 has the "hand" (扌) radical, suggesting physical force used to "ask/question" (問).
Example: 彼は拷問を受けた。 (かれはごうもんをうけた。)
-He was subjected to torture.
}

引き裂く-
{
引き裂く (ひきさく) - to tear up, to rip apart, to sever
A compound verb combining 引く (to pull) and 裂く (to rip), implying a forceful separation.
Memory Tip: Pull (Hiki) it until it rips (Saku). Imagine pulling a paper from both ends until it snaps.
Example: 手紙を二つに引き裂いた。 (てがみを ふたつに ひきさいた。)
-I tore the letter into two.
}

塗装-
{
塗装 (とそう) - coating, painting (surfaces)
Combines 塗 (paint/smear) and 装 (attire/decoration). Refers to the technical act of painting structures.
Memory Tip: To (Toe) + Sou (Sew) — Imagine putting a protective "coating" on your toe before sewing.
Example: 壁の塗装が剥げている。 (かべの とそうが はげている。)
-The paint on the wall is peeling off.
}

荒々しい-
{
荒々しい (あらあらしい) - Rough, wild, fierce
A reduplicative i-adjective that emphasizes the quality of being coarse or violent in nature.
Memory Tip: Repeating 'rough' (荒) twice doubles the intensity of a storm or someone's wild behavior.
Example: 荒々しい波が岸に打ち寄せる。(あらあらしいなみがきしにうちよせる。)
-Rough waves wash up against the shore.
}

平静-
{
平静 (へいせい) - Calm, serenity, composure
A na-adjective or noun composed of 平 (even/flat) and 静 (quiet), describing internal mental state.
Memory Tip: When your mind is flat (平) and quiet (静), you have achieved true composure.
Example: 彼は平静を装った。(かれはへいせいをよそおった。)
-He feigned composure.
}

侮辱-
{
侮辱 (ぶじょく) - Insult, affront
A noun or suru-verb consisting of 侮 (scorn/despise) and 辱 (humiliate/shame).
Memory Tip: A person (亻) showing scorn that results in a shameful (辱) situation for the victim.
Example: それはひどい侮辱だ。(それはひどいぶじょくだ。)
-That is a terrible insult.
}

久しい-
{
久しい (ひさしい) - Long-time, long-continued
An i-adjective typically used in formal or literary contexts to describe a long duration of time since something happened.
Memory Tip: The kanji 久 represents a person with an elongated stroke, signifying a long time passing.
Example: 彼に会うのは久しい。(かれにあうのはひさしい。)
-It has been a long time since I met him.
}

放棄-
{
放棄 (ほうき) - Abandonment, renunciation
A formal suru-verb used for discarding rights, duties, or physical items, combining "release" (放) and "discard" (棄).
Memory Tip: Imagine releasing (放) a grip and discarding (棄) a duty you no longer want to carry.
Example: 彼は権利を放棄した。(かれはけんりをほうきした。)
-He renounced his rights.
}

本質-
{
本質 (ほんしつ) - Essence, nature
A noun composed of "origin/book" (本) and "quality/substance" (質).
Memory Tip: The origin (本) quality (質) of an object is its true essence.
Example: 問題の本質を理解する。(もんだいのほんしつをりかいする。)
-Understand the essence of the problem.
}

法廷-
{
法廷 (ほうてい) - Courtroom
A noun describing the specific room or arena where law (法) is administered in court (廷).
Memory Tip: Focus on the place where the Law (法) is king in the Court (廷).
Example: 彼は法廷で証言した。(かれはほうていでしょうげんした。)
-He testified in the courtroom.
}

容疑者-
{
容疑者 (ようぎしゃ) - Suspect (person)
A legal term for someone suspected of a crime; contains 'appearance' (容) and 'doubt' (疑).
Memory Tip: A person (者) whose appearance/actions (容) lead to doubt (疑).
Example: 警察は容疑者を逮捕した。 (けいさつはようぎしゃをたいほした。)
-The police arrested the suspect.
}

輪郭-
{
輪郭 (りんかく) - Outline/contour
Refers to the external border of an object, especially a face or drawing.
Memory Tip: Wheel (輪) + outer wall (郭) suggests the outer circular boundary of a shape.
Example: 山の輪郭がはっきりと見える。 (やまのりんかくがはっきりとみえる。)
-The outline of the mountain is clearly visible.
}

荒らす-
{
荒らす (あらす) - To ruin, to devastate, to break into
A transitive verb used when a place is left in a mess, raided, or damaged.
Memory Tip: 'Ara' (wild) sounds like 'arashi' (storm); a storm 'ruins' the garden.
Example: 猿が畑を荒らす。 (さるがはたけをあらす。)
-Monkeys ruin the fields.
}

滅びる-
{
滅びる (ほろびる) - To perish/be ruined
An intransitive verb describing the downfall or extinction of a species, kingdom, or culture.
Memory Tip: Fire (火) and water (氵) are elements that cause civilizations to perish (滅).
Example: 古代の文明が滅びる。(こだいのぶんめいがほろびる)
-Ancient civilizations perish.
}

実在-
{
実在 (じつざい) - Real existence
This word refers to something that actually exists in reality, as opposed to fiction or imagination.
Memory Tip: Real (実) existence (在) is about things that are actually there.
Example: その物語の主人公は実在の人物だ。(そのものがたりのしゅじんこうはじつざいのじんぶつだ)
-The protagonist of that story is a real person.
}

不倫-
{
不倫 (ふりん) - Adultery/Affair
This noun combines "un-" (不) and "ethics/morals" (倫), describing behavior that deviates from social morality.
Memory Tip: Think of it as "No (不) Ethics (倫)" in a romantic relationship.
Example: 彼は不倫の末に離婚した。 (かれはふりんのすえにりこんした。)
-He divorced after an affair.
}

色彩-
{
色彩 (しきさい) - Color/Hue
A noun referring to colors or coloring, often used in artistic, technical, or formal contexts.
Memory Tip: Combine 'color' (色) with 'vividness/coloring' (彩) to remember it refers to specific hues.
Example: 自然の色彩は美しい。 (しぜんのしきさいはうつくしい。)
-The colors of nature are beautiful.
}

琴-
{
琴 (こと) - Koto
A traditional Japanese stringed musical instrument, similar to a horizontal harp or zither.
Memory Tip: The top looks like two 'kings' (王), which historically represented jade or precious strings on an instrument.
Example: 彼女は琴を弾くのが上手だ。 (かのじょはことをひくのがじょうずだ。)
-She is good at playing the koto.
}

拍子-
{
拍子 (ひょうし) - Beat / Rhythm / Momentum
This noun refers to musical time or the chance moment something happens.
Memory Tip: The rhythm of a clap (拍) made by a small part/child (子).
Example: 拍子に合わせて踊る。 (ひょうしにあわせておどる。)
-Dance to the beat.
}

懲りる-
{
懲りる (こりる) - To learn by experience, to have enough of, to be discouraged by
An ichidan verb used when a negative experience makes someone want to avoid repeating the same mistake. It implies learning a lesson the hard way.
Memory Tip: The kanji includes 'punishment' and 'heart'—your heart learns after being punished by a mistake.
Example: 失敗したが、彼はまだ懲りていない。 (しっぱいしたが、かれはまだこりていない。)
-He failed, but he hasn't learned his lesson yet.

陰謀-
{
陰謀 (いんぼう) - Conspiracy, plot, intrigue
Refers to a secret plan to do something illegal or harmful. It uses 'shadow/secret' (陰) and 'strategy/scheme' (謀).
Memory Tip: A "Scheme" (謀) hatched in the "Shadows" (陰).
Example: 彼は陰謀に巻き込まれた。 (かれはいんぼうにまきこまれた。)
-He was caught up in a conspiracy.
}

承諾-
{
承諾 (しょうだく) - Consent, acceptance, approval
A formal noun/suru-verb often used in business or legal contexts for agreeing to a request.
Memory Tip: 承 (to receive/accept) and 諾 (agreement). Formally receiving and agreeing to terms.
Example: 彼はその条件を承諾した。 (かれはそのじょうけんをしょうだくした。)
-He accepted those conditions.
}

脅迫-
{
脅迫 (きょうはく) - Threat, intimidation
A noun/suru-verb referring to coercion or threatening someone with harm.
Memory Tip: The kanji 脅 contains 'power' (力) under three 'mouths', suggesting forceful words used to intimidate.
Example: 彼は脅迫を受けた。 (かれはきょうはくをうけた。)
-He was threatened.
}

悲惨-
{
悲惨 (ひさん) - Miserable/Tragic
A na-adjective combining 悲 (sad) and 惨 (wretched/cruel). It describes a state of extreme misery or a tragic situation.
Memory Tip: A feeling of sadness (悲) mixed with a cruel (惨) reality.
Example: その事故の現場は悲惨だった。 (そのじこのげんばはひさんだった。)
-The scene of that accident was tragic.

乏しい-
{
乏しい (とぼしい) - Scarce, meager, lacking
An i-adjective used for resources, wealth, or experience that is in short supply.
Memory Tip: When things are 'too' (to) low, the 'bowl' (bo) is empty and resources are 'shee' (shii) - scarce.
Example: 彼は経験が乏しい。 (かれはけいけんがとぼしい。)
-He lacks experience.

噴き出す-
{
噴き出す (ふきだす) - To blow out, to spurt out, to burst into (laughter)
A compound verb consisting of 噴 (erupt/spew) and 出す (to put out).

Example: 彼は突然笑い噴き出した。(かれはとつぜんわらいふきだした。)
-He suddenly burst out laughing.

峠-
{
峠 (とうげ) - Mountain pass, ridge, climax
A Kokuji (Japanese-made kanji) that refers to the highest point of a mountain road.
Memory Tip: Look at the radicals: Mountain (山) + Up (上) + Down (下). It's the point where you stop going up and start going down.
Example: 山の峠を越えるのは大変だ。(やまのとうげをこえるのはたいへんだ。)

徹する-
{
徹する (てっする) - To sink in, to devote oneself to, to stay up (all night)
An intransitive verb meaning to go through or maintain a specific role/state completely.

鎮める-
{
鎮める (しずめる) - To calm, to suppress, to appease
A transitive verb used for quieting down anger, riots, or intense pain.

揺さぶる-
{
揺さぶる (ゆさぶる) - To shake, stir up
A transitive verb used for physically shaking an object or emotionally shaking someone's heart or confidence.

無縁-
{
無縁 (むえん) - unrelated / having no connection
A noun or na-adjective formed by 無 (none) and 縁 (connection/fate). It implies something is irrelevant or outside of one's circle.
Memory Tip: 'Mu' means 'no' and 'en' is the 'fate' that connects people; hence, no fate connects you.
Example: 私はギャンブルとは無縁だ。 (わたしはぎゃんぶるとはむえんだ。)
-I have nothing to do with gambling.

揺らぐ-
{
揺らぐ (ゆらぐ) - To shake, waver
This intransitive verb describes either a physical swaying or an abstract loss of stability in one's heart or status.

Example: 自信が揺らぐ。 (じしんがゆらぐ。)
-My confidence is wavering.

肯定-
{
肯定 (こうてい) - Affirmation / positive
Formed by 肯 (agreement) and 定 (determine). It is the opposite of 否定 (negation) and indicates saying "yes" to a proposal or fact.
Memory Tip: "Determining" (定) that you are in "agreement" (肯).
Example: 彼は私の意見を肯定した。 (かれはわたしのいけんをこうていした。)
-He affirmed my opinion.

掲載-
{
掲載 (けいさい) - Publication / appearance (in print/media)
A noun referring to the placement of text or images in a newspaper, magazine, or website.

-The article appeared on the front page.

掲載する-
{
掲載する (けいさいする) - To publish / to post
The verb form of 掲載, specifically meaning the action of putting information into a medium.

扇-
{
扇 (おうぎ) - Folding fan
A noun for a traditional Japanese folding fan, distinct from a flat 'uchiwa' fan.
Memory Tip: The kanji shows a door (戸) and feathers (羽). Imagine feathers moving like a swinging door to create a breeze.
Example: 彼女は扇を広げて顔を隠した。 (かのじょはおうぎをひろげてかおをかくした。)
-She spread her fan and hid her face.

偽-
{
偽 (にせ) - Fake / counterfeit
A noun or prefix used to describe something that is not genuine or is a deception.

願望-
{
願望 (がんぼう) - Desire/Wish
Consists of 願 (request/petition) and 望 (hope/view). Describes a strong inner yearning or aspiration.

従来-

従来 (じゅうらい) - Conventional/Hitherto
Combines 'follow/obey' (従) and 'come' (来). It refers to how things have been done up until the present.

嫁ぐ-
{
嫁ぐ (とつぐ) - To marry (of a woman)
A specific verb used for a woman getting married and joining her husband's household.

費やす-
{
費やす (ついやす) - To spend, to consume, to waste
A transitive verb used for the expenditure of time, money, or resources.

突如-
{
突如 (とつじょ) - Suddenly, unexpectedly
An adverb used to describe an abrupt or unforeseen event, often in written or formal style.
Memory Tip: Something stabbing (突) out of the darkness just like (如) a surprise.
Example: 突如として雨が降り出した。 (とつじょとしてあめがふりだした。)

莫大-
{
莫大 (ばくだい) - Enormous, vast, immense
This na-adjective is used to describe abstract but massive quantities, such as wealth, costs, or impact.
Memory Tip: 莫 (nothingness/huge) + 大 (big) = So big it defies simple measurement.
Example: 莫大な費用がかかる。 (ばくだいなひようがかかる。)
-It costs a vast amount of money.

頻繁-
{
頻繁 (ひんぱん) - Frequent, often
A formal na-adjective or adverb (with に) indicating a high frequency of occurrence.
Memory Tip: 頻 (frequency) + 繁 (luxuriance/busy) = Busy with a high frequency of events.
Example: 彼は頻繁にここに来る。 (かれはひんぱんにここにくる。)
-He comes here frequently.
}

由来-
{
由来 (ゆらい) - Origin, derivation, source
Refers to the historical background or the root from which something (like a word or custom) originated.
Memory Tip: 由 (reason) + 来 (come) = The reason why it came to be.
Example: この地名の由来は何ですか。 (このちめいのゆらいはなんですか。)
-What is the origin of this place name?
}

幾度-
{
幾度 (いくど) - How many times / Frequently
An adverbial noun combining "how many" (幾) and "degree/times" (度). It sounds more formal than 何度 (nando).
Memory Tip: Think of asking "how many" (幾) "degrees" (度) a wheel has turned.
Example: 幾度も彼に尋ねた (いくどもかれにたずねた)
-I asked him many times.

胴体-
{
胴体 (どうたい) - Torso / Body / Fuselage
A noun combining "trunk/torso" (胴) and "body" (体). It refers to the main central part of a person, animal, or aircraft.

Example: 飛行機の胴体は長い (ひこうきのどうたいはながい)
-The airplane's fuselage is long.

交互-
{
交互 (こうご) - Alternation / Mutual / Reciprocal

蓄える-
{
蓄える (たくわえる) - To store / To save up / To grow (a beard)

Example: 冬に備えて食料を蓄える (ふゆにそなえてしょくりょうをたくわえる)
